definition: , aor. and , inf. n. A^abonN , He made him an object of imputation, or suspected him: and he found fault with him, or blamed him: (M:) or he cast a foul, or an evil, imputation upon him. (IAar, T.)...

A^abonN , He made him an object of imputation, or suspected him: and he found fault with him, or blamed him: (M:) or he cast a foul, or an evil, imputation upon him. (IAar, T.) You say, A^abanahu bi$aYo'K , (S, K,) or bi$~arK (as in one copy of the S,) or bixayorKwa$~arK , (Lh, M,) aor. as above, (Lh, S, M, K,) and so the inf. n., (Lh, M,) He made him an object of imputation, or suspected him, (Lh, S, M, K,) of a thing, (S, K,) or of evil, (S, accord. to one copy,) or of good, and evil: (Lh, M:) and ↓ A^b~nhu signifies the same. (M.) And bixayorK ↓ fulaAnN yuw^ab~anu , or bi$~arK , Such a one is made an object of imputation, or suspected, of good, or of evil: (AA, * Lh, T [as in the TT; but perhaps yuw^ab~anu is a mistranscription for yuw^obanu ; for it is immediately added, fahuwa maA^obuwnN :]) when, however, you say yw^bn [i. e. yuw^obanu or ↓ yuw^ab~anN ] alone, it relates to evil only. (AA, T. [But see 2.]) And fulaAnN yaw^abanu bika*aA , or ↓ yuw^ab~anu , Such a one is evil spoken of by the imputation of such a thing. (S, accord. to different copies.) And it is said respecting the assembly of the Prophet, fiyhi AlHuramu , ↓ laA tuw^ab~anu , (T, and so in a copy of the S,) or lA tuw^obanu , (so in some copies of the S,) i. e. Women (T) shall not be mentioned in an evil manner therein: (T, S:) or shall not have evil imputations cast upon them, nor be found fault with, nor shall that which is foul be said of them, nor that which ought not, of things whereof one should be ashamed. (IAar, T.) ― -b2- Also, and ↓ A^b~nhu , (M, K,) inf. n. taA^obiynN , (K,) He found fault with him, or blamed him, to his face; (M, K;) and he upbraided him, or reproached him. (M.)

definition: A knot in wood, or in a branch;
sourceDefinition: A knot in wood, or in a branch; (S, M, K;) or in a staff, or stick; (T;) and in a bow, (TA,) [i. e.] the place of the shooting forth of a branch in a bow, (M,) which is a fault therein; (TA;) and in a rope, or cord: (M in art. Avl :) pl. A^ubanN . (T, S.) ― -b2- Hence, (M,) (tropical:) A fault, defect, or blemish, (T, M, K, TA,) in one's grounds of pretension to respect, (T, TA,) and in speech, or language. (M, TA.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) Particularly The enormity that is committed with one who is termed maA^obuwn . (TA.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) Rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite: (K, TA:) and enmity: pl. as above. (TA.) You say, bayonahumo A^ubanN (tropical:) (S, TA) Between them are enmities. (S.) ― -b5- Also The [ part called ] galoSamap [meaning the epiglottis ] of a camel. (M, K.)

definition: The time of a thing;
sourceDefinition: The time of a thing; (T, S, M, K, and Msb in art. Ab ;) the season of a thing; (Msb in that art.;) the time of the preparing, or making ready, of a thing; (Mgh in that art.;) as, for instance, of fruit, (S, Mgh, Msb,) of the fresh ripe dates, and of the gathering of fruits, and of heat or cold: (T.:) or the first of a thing. (M, K.) You say, A^axa*a Al$~aYo'a biA_ib~aAnihi He took the thing in its time: or in, or with, the first thereof. (M.) The n is radical, so that it is of the measure fiE~aAlN ; or, as some say, augmentative, so that it is of the measure fiEolaAnN . (TA.) [See art. Ab .]

You say, haAlaniY A^aziyzu Alr~aEodi [ The sounding of the thunder terrified me ]: and Sad~aEaniY A^aziyzu Alr~aHaY [ The sounding of the mill-stone made my head to ache ]. (TA.) ― -b3- A^az~ahu , (A, TA,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. A^az~N , (S, TA,) He put him in motion; disquieted him; (A,* TA;) stirred up, roused, or provoked, him; and incited, urged, or instigated, him; (S,* A,* TA;) EalaY ka*aA to do such a thing. (S, TA.) Or A^az~N signifies The inciting a man to do a thing by artifice, or cunning, and gentleness. (El-Harbee.)

sourceDefinition: Dirt, or filth; as also ↓ A^uf~apN : (S:) you say, A^uf~aA lahu , and ↓ A^uf~apF , Dirt, or filth, to him; in which the tenween is for the purpose of rendering them indeterminate; (S;) and A^uf~a lahu wa tuf~N ; (T;) and watuf~apF ↓ A^uf~apF ; and A^uf~aA watuf~aA ; (T, S;) the latter of which is an imitative sequent: (S:) or A^uf~N signifies the dirt of the ear; and tuf~N , the dirt of the nails; (As, T, M, K; but in the last, of the nail; ) the phrases mentioned above being used on the occasion of deeming a thing dirty or filthy, and afterwards on the occasion of experiencing annoyance or disgust at anything; (As, T, M,* TA;) and ↓ A^afafN , also, has the former of these two meanings: (TA:) or A^uf~N signifies the dirt around the nail; (M;) or the dirt of the nail; (K;) and tuf~N , the dirt in the nail: (M:) or the former, a paring of the nail: and a piece of stick, or a reed, which one takes up from the ground: (K:) in these various senses they are explained as used in the saying, A^uf~aA lahu watuf~aA : (TA:) or the former signifies stink: (Zj, TA:) or paucity; (T, M, K) as also ↓ A^afafN ; (M;) or from ↓ A^afafN signifying a thing little in quantity; (T; and the same meaning is assigned to this word in the K;) and tuf~N is an imitative sequent, (T, M, K,) of the same meaning. (M.) ― -b2- A^uf~ , also, is a word expressive of vexation, distress of mind, or disgust; (M, Mgh;) or of dislike, displeasure, or hatred; (K;) and has six forms; (T, S;) mentioned by Akh; (S;) or ten; (M;) or forty; (K;) or more; (TA;) as follow: A^uf~i and A^uf~a and A^uf~u and A^uf~K and A^uf~aA and A^uf~N (T, S, M, K) and A^uf~i and A^ufa and A^ufu and A^ufK and A^ufFA and A^ufN (K) and A^ufo (M, K) and A^uf~o and ↓ A^uf~aY , pronounced with imáleh, (M, K,) i. e. with pure imáleh, and ↓ A^uf~aY with intermediate imáleh, and ↓ A^uf~aY without imáleh, the alif [written Y ] in these three denoting the fem. gender, and ↓ A^uf~iY , with kesr to the f , (K,) i. e., as a prefixed noun with its complement, [the latter being the pronoun of the first pers.,] (TA,) and ↓ A^uf~uwoho , (K,) with damm to the A^ and f , which latter is with teshdeed, and with the w and h quiescent, (TA,) and ↓ A^uf~apo [in a copy of the M ↓ A^uf~apF ] and ↓ A^ufiho and ↓ A^uf~uho (K) and ↓ A_ifo and ↓ A_if~o and ↓ A_ifi and ↓ A_ifK and ↓ A_ifFA and ↓ A_ifN and ↓ A_if~K and ↓ A_if~F and ↓ A_if~N and ↓ A_if~u , with damm to the f , which is with teshdeed, [in a copy of the M ↓ A_if~a ,] and ↓ A_if~aA , like A_in~aA , and ↓ A_if~aY , pronounced with imáleh, and ↓ A_if~iY , with kesr, (K,) i. e., prefixed to the pronoun of the first person, (IAmb,) and ↓ A^afo and ↓ A^af~i (K) and ↓ A^af~K or ↓ A^afK and ↓ A=fi , or ↓ A=f~i , and ↓ A=fK , or ↓ A=f~K , (accord. to different copies of the K,) [all these forms, making the number (forty) mentioned by the author of the K, I have drawn from a comparison of three copies of that work, and I believe them to be correct: some other forms are mentioned by SM as perhaps indicated in the K; but I see no good reason for this: he then adds,] and ↓ A^afaho and ↓ A^afuwho and ↓ A^af~aho , the last mentioned by IB on the authority of IKtt. (TA.) A^uf~i , [with its variants,] in its primary sense, denotes one's blowing at a thing that falls upon him, such as dust or ashes; or at the place, to remove therefrom what is annoying; therefore people say, at anything that they deem troublesome, or displeasing, or hateful, A^uf~i lahu [as though meaning A puff, or blast of breath, to it ]: (Kt, T:) or [rather] it is a word imitative of a sound; [like ugh in English, both in sound and meaning; and in meaning like our interjections foh and faugh; ] (Bd on the ex. in the Kur which will be found below, and TA;) denoting vexation, or distress of mind, or disgust; (Bd ubi suprà) or denoting contempt: (TA:) or it is a verbal noun, meaning I am vexed, or distressed in mind, or disgusted: (Bd ubi suprà:) or it is an imperative verbal noun [denoting disgust or abhorrence, like out, and away ]: (IJ, M:) or he who says A^uf~aA laka uses it in the manner of an imprecation, like as one says wayolFA lilokaAfiriyna ; and he who says A^uf~N laka puts it in the nom. case because of the l , like as one says wayolN lilokaAfiriyna ; and he who says A^uf~K laka puts it in the gen. case likening it to words imitative of sounds. (IAmb.) It is said in the Kur [xvii. 24], walaA taqulo lahumaA A^uf~i , (T, S, TA,) or A^uf~K , (TA, [in which other readings also are mentioned,]) [ And say not thou to them (i. e. to thy father and mother) Ugh, &c.,] meaning, do not thou deem anything of their affairs burdensome, nor be contracted in bosom thereby, nor be rough, or harsh, or coarse, to them: (Kt, T:) or do not thou say to them anything expressive of the least disgust, when they have become old, but take upon thyself their service; A^uf~i signifying stink. (Zj, T.)

sourceDefinition: as signifying He was, or became, worthy, or deserving, of it, or he merited it, or he had a right, or just title or claim, to it, is not allowable: (Msb, * MF:) not only does J disallow it, but the generality of those before him do so; saying that it is not chaste: in the Fs it is said to be of weak authority; and the expositors thereof confirm this assertion, saying that it occurs, but is inferior to other words in chasteness; and El-Hareeree asserts it to be erroneous: (MF:) or it is good in this sense; and J's disallowance of it is of no account: (K:) Az and Z and Sgh and others assert it to be good: and Az says, in the T, some have asserted the saying fulaAnN yasotaA^ohilu A^ano yukorama A^awo yuhaAna , as meaning [ Such a one ] is worthy, or deserving, [ of being treated with honour, or of being held in light estimation, ] to be erroneous; and AlAisotiy^ohaAlu to be only from AlA_ihaAlapu ; but I do not disallow it, nor charge with error him who says thus; for I have heard the verb thus used by a chaste Arab of the desert, of the BenooAsad, and there was present a number of Arabs of the desert who did not disapprove his saying: and this is confirmed by the saying in the Kur [lxxiv. 55], huwa A^aholu Alt~aqoway wa A^aholu Almagofirapi [explained below: see A^aholu ]. (T.) -A2- AstA^hl , (JK, K,) or AstA^hl AlA^ahaAlapa , (Msb,) He took the A_ihaAlapa : (JK, K:) or he ate the AhAlp : see this word below. (Msb, TA.)

definition: [The people of a house or dwelling, and of a town or village, and of a country: and the family of a man:] a man's cohabitants of one dwelling or place of abode, (Er-Rághib, Kull p.
sourceDefinition: [The people of a house or dwelling, and of a town or village, and of a country: and the family of a man:] a man's cohabitants of one dwelling or place of abode, (Er-Rághib, Kull p. 84,) and of one town or country: (Er-Rághib:) afterwards applied to a man's fellow-members of one family or race, and of one religion, and of one craft or art or the like: (Er-Rághib, Kull:) or, as some say, relations, whether they have followers or dependents, or not; whereas A=lN signifies relations with their followers or dependents: (Kull:) or it originally signifies relations: and sometimes is applied to followers or dependents: and signifies also the A^ahol [i. e. people, or inhabitants, or family,] of a house or tent: (Msb:) or a man's nearer, or nearest, relations by descent from the same father or ancestor; or his kinsfolk; his relations: (K:) or, accord. to [the Imám] Mohammad, a man's wife [or wives] and his children and household who are the objects of his expenditure; and thus, any brother and sister, or paternal uncle and son of a paternal uncle, or strange or distantly-related child, whom a man feeds or sustains in his abode: the most particular, or most special, dependents, or the like, of a man: on the authority of El-Ghooree: (Mgh:) [J indicates some of these meanings merely by saying that it signifies] the A^ahol of a man, and the A^ahol of a house; as also ↓ A^aholapN : (S:) [see also A=lN ; in the explanations of which, certain distinctions between it and A^aholN will be found mentioned:] the pl. is A^aholuwna , [like A^aroDuwna , a form sometimes used for A^araDuwna ] (Mgh, Msb, K,) and A^ahaAlK , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) with an additional Y [implied by the tenween, and expressed in the accus. case, and when the word is determinate, as in AlA^ahaAliY ,] (S,) contr. to rule, (S, Mgh,) like layaAlK , pl. of layolN , (S,) [and like A^araAD , respecting which and lyaAlK and A^ahaAlK , see A^aroDN ,] and A=haAlN , (S, K,) a pl. [of pauc.] sometimes occurring in poetry, (S,) [like A=raADN ,] and A^aholaAtN and A^ahalaAtN [as though pls. of A^aholapN ]. (S, K.) ― -b2- A^aholu Albayoti The [ people or] inhabitants [or family] of the house or tent. (Mgh, K.) But A^awoSaY lA^aholi bayotihi means the same as AwSY lijinosihi , i. e. He left by will, of his property, to the children of his father, [or his kindred by the father's side,] exclusively of all relations of the mother. (Mgh in art. jns .) [See also A^aholu Alr~ajuli , below.] ― -b3- A^ahola AlquraY The [people or] inhabitants of the towns or villages. (TA.) And A^aholu Albaladi The settled, or constant, inhabitants of the country or town. (Msb.) sourceDefinition: , aor. yabow^usu , (S, M, Msb, K,) inf. n. baA^osN , (S, Msb, K,) or baA^osapN ; (M; [so I find in a copy of the M, but perhaps it is a mistranscription for baA=sapN ;]) and bay^isa , [aor. yaboA^asu ,] inf. n. baA^osN ; (M;) He was, or became, mighty, or strong, in war or fight; (K;) courageous, or valiant: (M, Msb, K:) or very mighty or strong in war or fight. (AZ, S.) -A2- bay^osu , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor. yaboA^asu (S, M, K) and yaboy^isu , the latter extr., like yanoEimu aor. of naEima , (M,) [and some other instances, (see Hasiba ,)] inf. n. buw^osN (S, Msb, * K) and buw^uwsN and buw^osaY (K) and baA^osN (TA) and bay^ysN , (S, K,) [in measure] like A^amiyrN , (TA,) [accord. to the CK biy^osN , which is a mistake,] and bay^iysaY , (TS, TA,) incorrectly written in the copies of the K biy^osay ; (TA;) or baw^usa ; (A;) or both these forms; (M;) He was, or became, in a state of distress; straitened in his means of subsistence, or in the conveniences of life; (M, Msb;) in a state of poverty: (M, A, Msb, * TA:) or in a state of pressing want: (S, K, TA:) and baw^usa , inf. n. baA=sapN and bay^iysN , whence the subst. baw^osaY , he was, or became, in a state of trial, or affliction: (M:) and [in like manner,] ↓ A^aboA^asa , (inf. n. A_iboA=sN ,S,) distress, or poverty, or misfortune, or calamity, ( AlbaA^osaA='u ,) befell him. (IAar, S, * M, TA.) -A3- biy^osa , also written bay^isa and biy^isa and baA^osa , (S, K,) is a word of dispraise or blame, (S,) implying all kinds of dispraise or blame, (TA,) [or superlative dispraise or blame; signifying, Very evil or bad is he, or it: or superlatively evil or bad is he, or it: ] contr. of niEma : (S, M, TA:) a pret. verb, imperfectly inflected, (S, K,) like niEoma , (S,) [having only one variation of form, namely, the fem. biy^osato , though the masc. is more commonly used even when the agent is fem. or pl.,] because it is translated from its original application, (S, K,) i. e. from bay^isa fulaAnN signifying A^aSaAba buw^osFA [he found, met with, or experienced, distress, &c.], to signify dispraise or blame. (S, TA.) When it is accompanied by a gen. n. without the article Al , this is always in the accus. case: but when the n. has the article Al , it is always in the nom. case: (TA:) you say, biy^osa rajulFA zayodF [ Very evil or bad, or superlatively evil or bad, as a man, is Zeyd; rjlA being a specificative]: (K:) and biy^osa Alr~ajulu zayodN [ Very evil, &c., is the man, Zeyd ]; and biy^osati AlmaroA^apu hinodN [or more commonly biy^osa AlEayoru in this case also, Very evil, &c., is the woman, Hind ]. (S.) Some argue that it is a noun, from the saying, niEoma Als~ayoru EalaY biy^osa AlEayoru , because it has a prep.; but this is explained as elliptical, and meaning, niEama Als~ayoru EalaY EayorK maquwlK fiyhi biy^osa AlEyoru [ Excellent is the journeying upon an ass of which it is said Very evil, &c., is the ass ]. (I 'Ak p. 232.) (I 'Ak ubi suprà.) [For further illustration, see niEoma .]

definition: (also written buwsN , with the suppressed, Msb) Distress;
sourceDefinition: (also written buwsN , with the suppressed, Msb) Distress; straitness of the means of subsistence, or of the conveniences of life; poverty: (M, Msb,* TA:*) or a state of pressing want: (S, K:) or misfortune; calamity: (A:) and ↓ buw^uwsN and ↓ buw^osaY (K, TA) and ↓ baA^osaA='u (M, A) and ↓ baA^osN (TA) and ↓ bay^iysN (S, K) and ↓ bay^iysaY (TA) and ↓ maboA^asapN (M, TA) [all of which, except ↓ baA^osaA='u and ↓ maboA^asapN , are said to be inf. ns. (see bay^isa )] signify the same as buw^osN : (S, M, A, K, TA:) ↓ buw^osaY and ↓ baA^osaA='u are both from buw^osN [with which they are syn. accord. to authorities indicated above]; (Zj, IDrd, TA;) the former is contr. of nuEomaY , (S, TA,) and in like manner the latter is contr. of naEomaA='u : (TA:) the latter is of the measure faEolaA='u without any A^afoEalu , because it is a subst.; like as A^afoEalu occurs among substs. without any faEalaA='u , as in the instance of A^aHomadu : (Akh, S:) or ↓ buw^osaY signifies a state of trial or affliction, and is a subst.; and ↓ bay^iysN and ↓ baA=sapN signify the same, but are inf. ns.: (M:) and ↓ baA^osaA='u is syn. with $id~apN [like buw^osN in the first of the senses explained above]; (S, TA;) and ma$aq~apN [meaning distress, or difficulty ]: (TA:) or it signifies misfortune, or calamity, (A, K,) like buw^osN ; (A;) and so A^abow^usN : (S, K:) or rather this last signifies misfortunes, or calamities; for it is pl. of ↓ baA^osN , i. e., a pl. of pauc.; not of buw^osN , as J asserts it to be; for the pl. of pauc. of buw^osN is A^aboA=sN : (IB, TA:) but A^abow^usN may be used as pl. of ↓ baA^osaA='u . (Fr, in S, voce Dar~aA='u , q. v.) [See exs. of these two pls. in what follows.] You say yawomu buw^osK wayawomu nuEomK [ A day of distress, or poverty, &c., and a day of ease and plenty ]. (S, TA.) And buw^osFA lahu [ May distress, or poverty, &c., befall him ]: a form of imprecation. (Sb, M, TA.) And buw^osa A@boni sumay~apa , app. an expression of pity [meaning Alas for the distress, &c., of Ibn-Sumeiyeh! ]. (TA, from a trad.) And EasaYa Alguwayoru A^abow^usFA Perhaps the little cave [ may be attended with ] calamities; not calamity, as in the S [and K]: (IB:) a prov.; (S;) originating from a cave's having collapsed upon some men in it; or from an enemy's having come to some men in a cave, and slain them; wherefore it is applied to anything whence evil is feared: (As, S, K, in art. gwr :) or it is applied to him who is suspected of a thing: (IAar, TA:) or Alguwayoru was the name of a certain water, which belonged to the tribe of Kelb, and the words of this prov. were said by Ez-Zebbà, when Kaseer turned aside from the plain road, and took the way to Alguwayoru : (Ibn-El-Kelbee, S, K, in art. gwr :) Abw^sA is in the accus. case by reason of yakuwnu understood. (Mughnee.) [See Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 94.] ElKumeyt also says, qaAluwA A^asaA='a banuw kurozK faqulotu lahumo EasaY Alguwayoru biA^aboA=sK waA^gowaAri [ They said, Benoo-Kurz have done evil: and I said to them, Perhaps the little cave may be attended with calamities and connected with other caves ]: A^aboA=s is here pl. of buw^os . (IB, TA.) [In the S, the last words are written biA_iboA=sK waA_iEowaArK , in one copy: in another, wA_igowaAri : both of which are app. wrong.] ― -b2- See also baAy^isN .

definition: , (T,) or AstbrA^ mina Albawoli , (Msb,) He took extraordinary pains, or the utmost pains, in cleansing the orifice of his penis from the remains of urine, by shaking it and pulling it and the like,...
sourceDefinition: , (T,) or AstbrA^ mina Albawoli , (Msb,) He took extraordinary pains, or the utmost pains, in cleansing the orifice of his penis from the remains of urine, by shaking it and pulling it and the like, until he knew that nothing remained in it: (T:) or he purified, or cleansed, himself from urine; syn. tanaz~ahu Eanohu : (Msb:) or AstbrA^ , (M,) or AstbrA^ Al*~akara , (K, TA,) signifies he took extraordinary pains, or the utmost pains, in cleansing the penis from urine; or he cleansed it entirely from urine; (M, * K, * TA;) and so AstbrA^ Alfaroja : and in like manner, AstbrA^ti Alfaroja said of a woman: (El-Munáwee, TA:) but the lawyers make a distinction between AsotiboraA='N and AisotinoqaA='N [which are made syn. in the M and K]: see the latter word. (TA.) ― -b2- And AstbrA^ AljaAriyapa , (T, S, Mgh,) or AlmaroA^apa , (M, Msb, K,) He abstained from sexual intercourse (T, M, K) with the girl whom he had purchased or whom he had taken captive, (T,) or with the woman, (M, K,) until she had menstruated (T, M, K) at his abode, once, and then become purified: (T:) the meaning is, (T,) he sought to find her free from pregnancy. (T, Mgh, Msb.) ― -b3- Hence, (Mgh,) AstbrA^ Al$~ayo'i , (Z, Mgh, Msb,) or AlA^amora , (TA,) He searched, searched out, or sought to find or discover, the uttermost of the thing, or affair, (Z, Mgh, Msb, TA,) in order that he might know it, (Mgh,) to put an end to his doubt. (Z, Mgh, Msb, TA.) You say, AisotaboraA^otu maA Einodaka [ I searched, or sought to find or discover, or I have searched, &c., the uttermost of what thou hast, of knowledge &c.]. (S, TA.) And AstbrA^ A^roDa ka*aA famaA wajada DaAl~atahu [ He searched the uttermost of such a land and found not his stray beast ]. (TA.) It is said in the Expos. of the Jámi' es-Sagheer that AisotiboraA='N is an expression denoting The seeking, or seeking leisurely and repeatedly, to obtain knowledge of a thing, until one knows it; considering it with the endeavour to obtain a clear knowledge of it; taking, in doing so, the course prescribed by prudence, precaution, or good judgment. (Mgh.)

definition: Free, (Msb,) minohu from it;
sourceDefinition: Free, (Msb,) minohu from it; namely a fault, defect, imperfection, blemish, or vice; (Mgh, Msb;) and, also followed by minohu , clear, or quit, of it; irresponsible for it; or in a state of immunity with respect to it; i. e. exempt from the demand thereof; namely a debt, (Msb,) or a claim, or due, or right; (Mgh;) as also ↓ baAriYN and ↓ baraA='N . (Msb.) You say, A^anaA bariYo'N minohu [ I am free from it, &c.]; (T, * S, M, K; *) and ↓ baraA='N , used alike as sing. and dual and pl. (Fr, T, S, M, K) and masc. and fem., (Fr, T, M, K,) because it is originally an inf. n.; (Fr, T, S;) and ↓ buraA='N : (S, M:) the pl. of bariYo'N is bariyw^uwna (T, S, K) and buraA^'u (T, S, M, K) and buraA='N , (T, M, K,) of the measure fuEaAlN , (T,) like ruxaAlN , (M, K,) of an extr. measure, disapproved by Suh, who says, in the R, that it is a contraction of buraA^'u , and has tenween because it resembles [words originally of the measure] fuEaAlN , and that the rel. n. formed from it is ↓ buraAwiY~N , (TA,) but it is mentioned by AAF as a pl. of bariYo'N , and as being like ruxaAlN , and Fr mentions buraA='u as a pl. of the same, imperfectly decl., with one of the two hemzehs suppressed, (M,) and biraA='N (S, M, K) and A^aboraA='N (S, K) and A^aboriy^aA='u , (T, S, K,) the last two anomalous: (TA:) the fem. of bariyo'N is bariyoy^apN ; pl. bariyoA=tN (T, S, M, K) and bariy~aAtN (Lh, M, K) and baraAyaA . (T, S, M, K.) You say, A^anaA bariYo'N minohu and xaliY~N minohu [ I am free from it; or, more commonly, I am clear, or quit, of it, or him ]; and minohu ↓ A^naA baraA='N and xalaA='N minohu ; (S;) and minohu ↓ A^anaA AlbaraA='u : (M:) and ↓ naHonu minoka AlbaraA='u and AlxalaA='u [ We are clear, or quit, of you ]; (Fr, T;) i. e., *awuw AlbaraA='i : so says Aboo-Is-hák; and As says the like of what Fr says. (T.) It is said in the Kur [xliii. 25], mim~aA taEobuduwna ↓ A_in~aniY baraA='N [ Verily I am clear of that which ye worship ]; (T, M;) or bariYo'N , or ↓ buraA='N ; accord. to different readers. (Bd.) bariYo'N occurs in several places in the Kur. (M.) Accord. to IAar, it signifies Clear of evil qualities or dispositions; shunning what is vain and false; remote from actions that occasion suspicion; pure in heart from associating any with God: and it signifies sound in body and intellect. (T, S, M, K.) You say, A^anaA bariYo'N minohu and xaliY~N minohu [ I am free from it; or, more commonly, I am clear, or quit, of it, or him ]; and minohu ↓ A^naA baraA='N and xalaA='N minohu ; (S;) and minohu ↓ A^anaA AlbaraA='u : (M:) and ↓ naHonu minoka AlbaraA='u and AlxalaA='u [ We are clear, or quit, of you ]; (Fr, T;) i. e., *awuw AlbaraA='i : so says Aboo-Is-hák; and As says the like of what Fr says. Accord. to IAar, it signifies Clear of evil qualities or dispositions; shunning what is vain and false; remote from actions that occasion suspicion; pure in heart from associating any with God: and it signifies sound in body and intellect. (T.) See also baAriy^N , in two places.

sourceDefinition: and ↓ bazorN , (S, Msb, K,) the former the more chaste, (T, S, Msb,) or the only form used by persons of chaste speech, (ISk, T, Msb,) The seed of herbs or leguminous plants, (S, A, Mgh, Msb,) and of other plants: (S, A, Msb:) or small seed or grain, such as that of herbs or leguminous plants and the like: (TA:) or any seed, or grain, that is sown (Kh, Msb, K) for vegetation; (K;) as also ba*orN [q. v.]: (Kh, Msb:) pl. buzuwrN . sourceDefinition: A piece of paper: (IAar, M, Sgh, TA:) in the K, AlHadaqapu is erroneously put for Alwaraqapu : (TA:) a ticket that is attached to a garment, or piece of cloth, (T, S, M, L, K,) bearing the mark, or inscription, of its price; (T, S, L, K;) or a ticket marked, or inscribed, with the weight, and the number, of a thing: (TA:) of the dial. of Egypt (T, S, L) and the neighbouring parts: (T, L:) so called, (K,) or said (by Sh, TA) to be so called, (S,) because it is tied by a twist, or thread, ( biTaAqapF ,) of the unwoven end of the cloth: (S, K:) but this is a mistake: (ISd, TA:) [in Greek, πιττάκιον , as observed by Freytag; and hence probably derived:] accord. to some, it is [ niTaAqapF ,] with n , because it tells ( tanoTiqu ) what is marked, or inscribed, thereon; but this is strange. (TA.) (TA.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. buTolN and buTuwlN and buTolaAnN , [of which the last seems to be the most common,] (S, Msb, K, KL, &c.,) It (a thing) was, or became, baATil , as meaning contr. of Haq~ ; (S;) [i. e.,] it was, or became, false, untrue, wrong or incorrect, fictitious, spurious, unfounded, unsound, (KL,) vain, unreal, naught, futile, worthless, useless, unprofitable, (KL, PS,) devoid of virtue or efficacy, ineffectual, null, void, of no force, or of no account; (Msb;) it went for nothing, as a thing of no account, (S, Msb, K,) or as a thing that had perished or become lost. (K.) [It is said of an assertion or allegation and the like, and of a deed, &c.] Hence the saying in the Kur [vii. 115], wa baTala maA kaAnuwA yaEomaluwna [ And what they were doing became vain, or null; or went for nothing, as a thing of no account ]. (TA.) And *ahaba damuhu buTolFA His blood went for nothing, [ unretaliated, and uncompensated by a mulet, ] as a thing of no account. (S, Msb.) And baTala damuhu [signifies the same; or] He was slain without there being obtained for him either blood-revenge or blood-wit. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b2- See also the inf. n. buTuwlN below, voce baT~aAlN . ― -b3- labaTula Alqawolu [ How false, untrue, wrong or incorrect, &c., is the saying! ] is said in wonder at that which is baATil . (TA.) ― -b4- baTala , (S, K,) or baTala mina AlEamali , (Msb,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. baTaAlapN (S, Msb, K, KL) and biTaAlapN , which is mentioned by one of the expositors of the Mo'allakát, and said to be the more chaste, and sometimes one says buTaAlapN , to make it accord with its contr. EumaAlapN , (Msb,) He (a hired man, or hireling,) was, or became, idle, unoccupied, or without work. (S, Msb, * K, KL. [See also 5.]) [Hence, yawomu baTaAlapK A day of idleness; a holiday. ] ― -b5- biTaAlapN , with kesr, also signifies The being diverted from that which would bring profit in the present life or in the life to come. (TA.) ― -b6- See also 2. ― -b7- baTala fiY Hadiyvihi , (K,) aor. ; so it seems to be from the context in the K, but correctly baTila , aor. , as in the Jm; (TA;) inf. n. baTaAlapN (K) [and app. buTuwlN also; see baT~aAlN ]; He jested, or joked, or was not serious or in earnest, in his discourse; as also ↓ AbTl . (K.) -A2- baTula , aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. baTaAlapN (S, Msb, K, KL) and biTaAlapN (Lth, Msb, TA) and buTaAlapN (TA) and buTuwlapN , (S, K, KL,) He (a man) was, or became, courageous, brave, or stronghearted, on the occasion of war, or fight; such as is termed baTalN , q. v.; (S, Msb, K, KL;) as also ↓ tbT~l : (K:) or this last signifies he affected courage, &c.; he made himself, or constrained himself to be, courageous, &c.; syn. ta$aj~aEa . (TA.) ― -b2- labaTula Alr~ajulu [ How courageous, &c., is the man! ] is said in wonder at Alt~abaT~ul [i. e. courage, &c., or the affecting of courage, &c.]. (TA.)

Hsn ;) applied to a man, Courageous, brave, or strong-hearted, on the occasion of war, or fight; [commonly used as a subst., meaning a man of courage or valour, a brave man, a hero; ] (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ baT~aAlN ; (K;) one whose wound goes for nothing, so that he does not care for it, (Lth, K,) and it does not withhold him from the exercise of his courage; (Lth, TA;) or the blood of whose adversaries goes for nothing with him, (K,) unrevenged: (TA:) or for this reason he is thus called; (TA;) or because life is annulled, or made to go for nothing, on the occasion of encountering him, and severe misfortunes are annulled by him, (Msb,) or by his sword, and made to be of no account: (TA:) and so ↓ baTalapN applied to a woman; (S, Msb, K;) accord. to one of the expositors of the Hamáseh; (Msb;) but AZ says that this is not allowable: (IDrd, TA:) the pl. of baTalN is A^aboTaAlN . (Msb, K.)

sourceDefinition: contr. of Haq~N ; (S, K;) i. e. False, untrue, wrong or incorrect, fictitious, spurious, unfounded, unsound, (KL,) vain, unreal, naught, futile, worthless, useless, unprofitable, (KL, PS,) devoid of virtue or efficacy, ineffectual, null, void, of no force, or of no effect; (Msb;) that proves, when inquired into, or investigated, to be false, wrong, unfounded, unsound, or not established; applying to a saying, and [sometimes] to a deed: (TA:) [ going for nothing, as a thing of no account, or as a thing that has perished or become lost: (see the verb, 1, first sentence:) often used as a subst., meaning a false, or vain, saying, or assertion, or allegation; a lie; a falsehood: and a false, or vain, deed, or action, or affair, or thing; &c.:] and ↓ buTolN is syn. therewith, (Ham p. 114,) and so are ↓ A^uboTuwlapN and ↓ A_iboTaAlapN : (K:) the pl. of baATilN is bawaATilu ; (Msb;) and buTulN occurs as a pl. of the same; (Ham p. 360;) or its pl. is A^abaATiylu , contr. to analogy, (S, Msb,) as though the sing. were A_iboTiylN ; (S;) or, accord. to AHát, this is pl. of ↓ A^uboTuwlapN , or, as some say, of ↓ A_iboTaAlapN , (Msb,) or, accord. to As and AHát and IDrd, of both these; (TA;) and signifies false, or vain, sayings and actions or deeds. (K in art. htr , &c.) You say, qado qulota baATilFA [ Thou hast said a false, or vain, saying; a lie; a falsehood ]; like as you say, qado qulota Haq~FA . (Ham p. 360.) And yaA^okuluwna A^amowaAla Aln~aAsi biAlbaATili [ They devour the possessions of men by false pretence ]. (Kur ix. 34.) And ↓ bayonahumo A^uboTuwlapN and ↓ A_iboTaAlapN [ Between them is false, or vain, speech, or discourse, &c.]; syn. baATilN . (K.) ― -b2- The belief in a plurality of Gods: so explained as occurring in the Kur xlii. 23. (TA.) ― -b3- See also baT~aAlN , in two places. [Hence,] baATilFA In play, or sport; acting unprofitably; or aiming at no profit. (Jel in iii. 188 and xxxviii. 26.) ― -b4- AlbaATilu Iblees: so in the Kur [xxxiv. 48], where it is said, maA yubodiy^u A@lobaATilu wa maA yuEiydu [explained in art. bdA^ ]: (Katádeh, K:) and again [xli. 42], where it is said, laA yaA^otiyhi A@lobaATilu mino bayona yadayohi wa laA mino xalofihi , [accord. to some,] meaning that Iblees shall not add to the Kur-án nor diminish therefrom: (TA:) ↓ baTalapN [is its pl., and] signifies devils: (A, TA:) or enchanters. (O, K.)

definition: both [properly] relate to the beginning of the day: (AZ, Msb:) the former of these verbs, (T, S, A,) aor.
sourceDefinition: both [properly] relate to the beginning of the day: (AZ, Msb:) the former of these verbs, (T, S, A,) aor. , inf. n. bukuwrN ; (T, S;) and ↓ bk~r , (T, S, A,) inf. n. tabokiyrN ; (T, S;) and ↓ Abkr , and ↓ Abtkr , (S, A,) and ↓ bAkr ; (S;) all signify the same; (S;) He (a traveller, A) went forth early in the morning, in the first part of the day; or between the time of the prayer of daybreak and sunrise; syn. xaraja fiY Albukorapi : (T, A:) or ↓ Abkr , inf. n. A_ibokaArN , signifies he entered upon that time: (T:) one should not say bakura nor bakira in the sense of bk~r [&c.]. (S.) ― -b2- You say also, bakara A_ilayohi , and Ealayohi , and fiyhi , inf. n. as above; and ↓ bk~r , and ↓ Abkr , and ↓ Abtkr ; and ↓ bAkrhu ; meaning A^ataAhu bukorapN [i. e. He came to him, or it, early in the morning, in the first part of the day; or between the time of the prayer of daybreak and sunrise: and he did it at that time: or bakara &c. with fiyhi following may be rendered he occupied himself at that time in doing it ]. (K.) ― -b3- And [hence,] bakara A_ilayohi , [and Ealayohi ,] aor. and inf. n. as above; (Msb;) and bakira Alyh , aor. ; (ISd, K; * [but see a remark respecting this verb above;]) and Alyh ↓ bkr , (S, Msb, TA,) and Elyh ; (TA;) and Alyh ↓ Abkr , (S, K,) and Elyh ; [and ↓ Abkrhu ;] and ↓ bAkrhu ; (TA;) signify also (assumed tropical:) He hastened [or betook himself early ] to it, or to do it, at any time, (S, Msb, K, TA,) morning or evening. (TA.) You say, bakarotu EalaY AlHaAjapi (assumed tropical:) [ I hastened to do, or accomplish, or attain, the thing needed ], inf. n. as above: and in like manner, EalaY Alwirodi ↓ A^abokarotu (assumed tropical:) [ I hastened to come to water ]: (AZ, S:) and Alwiroda ↓ Abkr , (TA,) and AlgadaA='a , (AZ, S, TA,) (assumed tropical:) He hastened to come to water, and to take the morning-meal. (TA.) Lebeed says, baAkarotu jaAjatahaA Ald~ajaAja bisuHorapK meaning (assumed tropical:) I hastened to be before the crowing of the cock, at the close of night, in obtaining what was wanted [ of it, namely, of wine,] by me: (TA:) HAjthA being for HaAjatiY A_ilayohaA , i. e., A_ilaY Alxamori . (EM p. 170: but the first word is there written baAdarotu .) [See also 2, below.] ― -b4- [It is also said that] bkr [app. bakira ,] inf. n. bkr , [app. bakarN ,] signifies (assumed tropical:) He possessed the quality of applying himself early, or of hastening; expl. by kaAna SaAHiba bukuwrK . (Msb.) [But see bakurN .]

You say also, bk~r A_ilaY AljumoEapi (tropical:) He went forth to the [ prayers of ] Friday at the commencement of the time thereof. (A.) And bk~r [alone], inf. n. as above, (tropical:) He came to prayer at the commencement of its time. (K, TA.) And bk~r biAlS~alaApi (tropical:) He performed the prayer at the commencement of its time: (A, Mgh, Msb, TA:) he was regardful of it, and performed it early. (TA.) And bak~iruwA biSalaApi Almagoribi (tropical:) Perform ye the prayer of sunset at the setting of the [ sun's ] disc. (S.) And bak~arati Aln~axolapu biHamolihaA (tropical:) [ The palmtree was early with its fruit ]. (A.) ― -b2- Also (tropical:) He was, or became, or went, before; preceded; had, or took, precedence; syn. taqad~ama ; and so ↓ Abkr and ↓ tbk~r . (K, TA.) (M, K.) ― -b2- See also 4. ― -b3- bk~r AlfaAkihapa : see 8.

sourceDefinition: (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ bukorN , (K,) but this latter is hardly to be found in any of the lexicons, (MF,) and ↓ bikorN , (ISd, TA,) A youthful he-camel; one in a state of youthful vigour: fem. with p ; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) and also bakorN , without p : (TA:) the term bakorN , applied to a camel, corresponds to fatFY , applied to a human being; and bakorapN , to fataApN ; and qaluwSN , to jaAriyapN ; and baEiyrN , to A_inosaAnN ; and jamalN , to rajulN ; and naAqapN , to maroA^apN : (AO, S:) or the offspring, or young one, of a she-camel; (K;) thus indefinitely explained: (TA:) or a camel in his sixth year ( vaniY~N ) [and] until he becomes a ja*aE : [but it seems that the reverse must be meant; for a j*E , of camels, is one in his fifth year:] or a camel in his second year [and] until he enters his sixth year: or a camel in his second year, or that has entered his third year, or that has completed his second year and entered his third year; syn. Aibonu labuwnK : (K:) and a camel that has just entered upon his fourth year: and a camel in his fifth year: (IAar, Az:) or a camel that has not entered his ninth year: (K:) and sometimes it is metaphorically applied to a human being; [meaning (tropical:) a young man; ] and bakorapN to (tropical:) a young woman: (TA:) the pl. (of pauc., S) is A^abokurN ; (S, K;) and ↓ A^ubayokiruwna occurs as pl. of the dim. of A^abokurN ; (S, TA;) and (pl. of mult., S, TA) bikaArN , (S, Msb,) like as firaAxN is pl. of faroxN ; (S;) or this is pl. of bakorapN ; (Msb, K;) and there are other pls. of bakorN , namely, bukoraAnN (K) and bikaArapN ; (S, Msb, K;) and [quasi-pl. n.] ↓ bakaArapN . (K.) Hence the well-known prov., (TA,) SadaqaniY sin~a bakorihi , and sin~u bakorihi , meaning He hath told me what is in his mind, and what his ribs infold: a saying originating from the following fact: a man bargained with another for a youthful camel ( bakor ), and said, “ What is his age ( sin~uhu )? ” the other answered, “ He is in his ninth year: ” then the young camel took fright and ran away: whereupon his owner said to him, hidaEo hidaEo ; and this is an expression by which are quieted young ones, (K,) of the camel; (TA;) so when the purchaser heard it, he said, SdqnY sn~ bkrh [ He hath told me truly the age, or as to the age, of his youthful camel: or the age of his youthful camel has spoken truly to me ]: if sn~ is in the accus. case, the meaning [of the verb] is Ear~afaniY , (K,) and sn~ is in the accus. case as a second objective complement; (TA;) or xabara sin~i is meant; [in the CK, erroneously, xabara ;] or fiY sin~i ; the prefixed noun [ xabara ] or the proposition [ fiY ] being suppressed [and sn~ being therefore in the accus. case]: but if sn~ is in the nom. case, veracity is attributed to the [animal's] age, by an amplification: (K:) or, as some say, the buyer said to the owner of the camel, “ How many years has he? ” and he told him; and he looked at the teeth of the camel, and found him to be as he had said; whereupon he said, SdqnY sin~u bkrh . (Har p. 95.)

sourceDefinition: A virgin; (S, K;) and a man who has not yet drawn near to a woman; (TA;) contr. of vay~ibN , applied to a man as well as to a female: (Mgh, Msb:) pl. A^abokaArN . (S, Msb, K.) ― -b2- And [hence,] (assumed tropical:) A pearl unpierced. (MF.) And (assumed tropical:) A bow when one first shoots with it. (TA.) And (tropical:) A cloud abounding with water: (K, TA:) likened to a virgin, because her blood is more than that of her who is not a virgin: and the phrase saHaAbN bikorN is sometimes used. (TA.) And naArN bikorN (tropical:) Fire not lighted from another fire. (As, A.) ― -b3- Also She that has not yet brought forth offspring: (AHeyth:) and a cow that has not yet conceived: (K:) or a heifer (K, TA) that has not yet conceived: (TA:) and a woman, (S, K,) and a she-camel, (As, K,) that has brought forth but once: pl. A^abokaArN and bikaArN : (TA:) or a she-camel in her first state or condition. (Ham p. 340.) ― -b4- And [hence,] (tropical:) A grape-vine that has produced fruit but once: (A, K:) pl. A^abokaArN . (A.) ― -b5- Also i. q. bakorN , q. v. (ISd, TA.) And [hence,] A^abokaAru AlA^awolaAdi (assumed tropical:) Young children. (TA, from a trad.) And A^abokaAru Aln~aHoli (assumed tropical:) Young bees. (TA.) Whence, Easalu A^abokaArK (tropical:) Honey produced by young bees: or this means honey of which the preparation has been superintended by virgin-girls. (A, * TA.) ― -b6- Also (tropical:) The first-born of his, or her, mother (S, Msb, K) and father; (Msb, K;) applied alike to the male and the female: (S:) and sometimes to that which is not the offspring of human beings; (TA;) the first-born of camels; (S;) and of a serpent: (TA:) pl. (A, TA.) ― -b9- DarobapN bikorN (tropical:) A cutting blow or stroke, (S, K,) that kills (K) at once, (TA,) not requiring to be struck a second time: (S, A:) pl. definition: (S, Msb, K) and ↓ bakarapN (Msb, K) The thing upon which [passes the rope wherewith] one draws water (S, Msb, K) from a well [or the like ];
sourceDefinition: (S, Msb, K) and ↓ bakarapN (Msb, K) The thing upon which [passes the rope wherewith] one draws water (S, Msb, K) from a well [or the like ]; (S;) [ i. e. the sheave of a pulley;] a round piece of wood, in the middle [of the circumference] whereof is a groove (K, TA) for the rope, and in the interior [or centre] whereof is an axis upon which it turns: (TA:) or a quick maHaAlap [or large sheave of a pulley ]: (M, K:) [but MF disapproves of this last explanation: sometimes, by a synecdoche, it is used to signify a pulley complete:] the pl. is ↓ bakarN , (S, Msb, K,) a pl. of the former, anomalous, like HalaqN pl. of HaloqapN , and HamaA^N pl. of HamoA^apN , (S,) or of the latter; (Msb;) or a coll. gen. n., of which bakarapN is the n. un.; (MF;) and bakaraAt , (S, Msb, K,) a pl. of the former [as well as of the latter]. (S, Msb.) ― -b2- Hence, app., the former signifies also (assumed tropical:) A small ring, like a bead, in the ornamental part of a sword: (Mgh:) [and the pl.] bakaraAtN signifies (assumed tropical:) the rings that are attached to the ornamental part [ of the scabbard ] of a sword, (K,) resembling the [ rings called ] qatax [ which are worn upon the fingers or toes ] of women. (TA.) ― -b3- [And hence, perhaps,] (assumed tropical:) An assembly, a company, or a congregated body. (IAar, K.) ― -b4- jaAw^uwA EalaY bakorapi A^abiyhimo is a prov., (TA,) meaning (tropical:) They came together, not one remaining behind, (S, TA;) they came all of them, (AA, IJ, A, TA,) without exception: (TA:) or they came in a multitude, and all together, none remaining behind: (TA:) or they came in succession, one after, or at the heels of, another: (AO:) or they came in one way, or manner: (As:) [accord. to some, from bkrp as explained in the next preceding sentence; and, if so, ElY is used in the sense of maEa , or mu$otamiliyna is understood before it: or it is from bkrp signifying “ a youthful she-camel; ” and thus implies that they were few: (see Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 312:) or] from bak~arotu fiY ka*aA meaning “ I was, ” or “ became, ” or “ went, ” “ before in such a thing; ” so that it signifies that they came from first to last: (IJ:) or from bkrp in the first of the senses explained in this paragraph; though in this case there is no bkrp in reality. (AO, S. *)

definition: and ↓ bakarN The early morning, or first part of the day;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ bakarN The early morning, or first part of the day; (Bd and Jel in xix. 12 and xxxiii. 41 and xlviii. 9, as relating to the former word; and K; *) between the time of the prayer of daybreak and sunrise; syn. gudowapN ; and ↓ A_ibokaArN is a subst. in the same sense, (K,) accord. to the lexicologists, as Sb says; but he adds that he holds it to be [only] the inf. n. of A^abokara : (TA: [and the like is said in the S with reference to its occurrence in the Kur iii. 36 and xl. 57: ]) pl. [of pauc.] of the first, A^abokaArN , and [of mult.] bukarN . (T, Msb.) You say, A^atayotuhu bukorapN (S, A, Msb) and ↓ bakarFA , (A,) meaning ↓ baAkirKA [ I came to him early in the morning, &c.]. (S, A, Msb.) But if you mean the bukorapN of a particular day, you say, A^atayotuhu bukorapa , making the noun imperfectly decl.; [meaning I came to him early in the morning, &c., of this day; ] and in this case it is not to be used otherwise than as an adv. n. of time. (S.) If you say ↓ baAkirFA , using this word as an epithet, you use baAkirap for the fem. (TA.) You say also, siro EalaY farasika bukorapF and ↓ bakarFA [ Go thou on thy horse early in the morning, &c.]; like as you say, saHarFA . (S, TA. [But in two copies of the S, for sro , I find siyra .])

sourceDefinition: , (T, K,) inf. n. taboyiY~N , (K,) I made the thing apparent, manifest, evident, clear, plain, or perspicuous. (As, T, K*) -A2- Also, (K, as in the TA,) or Al$~aY'a , ↓, tab~ayayotu (M, and so in several copies of the K,) [both confirmed by what follows,] i. q. taEam~adotuhu [meaning I directed myself, or my course, or aim, to, or towards, the thing; made for it, or towards it; made it my object; &c.]. (M, K.) ― -b2- In the saying, Hay~aAka A@ll~`hu wa bay~aAka , the phrase HyAk All~h means May God make thee to have dominion: (S, M:) or may God prolong thy life: (M:) and by~Ak means AiEotamadaka biAlt~aHiy~api [ may He bring thee prolongation of life; lit. may He direct himself to thee, or the like, with the gift of prolongation of life ]; (As, S;) or qaSadaka biAlt~aHiy~api [which is the same]: (IAar, T:) or AiEotamadaka biAlomuloki [ may He bring thee dominion ]; (M;) so too says IAar: (TA:) or may He make thy state, or condition, to be good: (TA:) or may He make thee to laugh: (T, S, M, K:) so some say, accord. to As: (T:) and it is related that these words were addressed to Adam, in consequence of his having remained a hundred years without laughing after his son had been slain: (T, S:) so says A'Obeyd, on the authority of Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr: (T:) or it means may He bring thee near [ unto Himself ]: (Aboo-Málik, As, T, M, K:) or may He bring thee: (IAar, S, M:) or may He prepare for thee an abode; i. q. baw~aA^aka , (K,) or baw~aA^aka manozilFA ; the verb being here altered in order to assimilate it to the preceding verb, Hay~aA : (El-Ahmar, T, S:) this explanation was approved by As: (S:) the meaning intended thereby is, may He lodge thee in an abode in Paradise: (TA:) or, as some say, the verb in this case is an imitative sequent to that preceding it: (A'Obeyd, S K: *) but this is naught: (K:) A'Obeyd says that in his opinion it is not an imitative sequent, because an imitative sequent is scarcely ever coupled with what precedes it by w . (S.) As an ex. of bay~aA in the sense of qar~aba , Aboo-Málik cites this verse: Aalokiboda waAlmaloHaA='a wa Als~anaAmaA bay~aA lahumo A_i*o nazaluwA AlT~aEaAmaA [ He brought near to them, i. e., placed before them, when they alighted, the food, namely, the liver, and the flesh of the back extending from the withers to the rump, and the hump ]. (T.) And IAar, explaining by~Ak as meaning qSdk bAltHy~p , cites the following verse: A^aEoTaY EaTaA='a All~aHizi All~ay^iymi A^abaA tamiymi ↓ lam~aA tab~ayayonaA (T.) Accord. to J, the meaning in this instances may be agreeable with the explanation of by~Ak by AEtmdk bAltHy~p [so that the verse may be rendered When we betook ourselves with salutation to the father of Temeem, or, as the verse is cited in the S, to the brother of Temeem ( A^axaA tmym ), he gave the gift of the niggardly, the mean ]: or it may mean we brought: and the verb admits of the same double rendering in other instances. (TA.) -A3- bay~ayotu baA='F HasanapF and HasanFA [ I made, or wrote, a beautiful b ]. (TA in bAb AlAlf Ally~np .)

definition: The low, ignoble, mean, or contemptible, man;
sourceDefinition: The low, ignoble, mean, or contemptible, man; as also ↓ Aibonu bay~aAna , (IAar, T, K) and Abn hay~aAna , (IAar, T,) and Abn baY~ , (K,) or haY~u bonu baY~ , and ↓ hay~aAnu bonu bay~aAna : (Lth, T:) or the last two signify he whose stock and branch are unknown: (M:) or the same two, he who is unknown, and whose father also is unknown: (K in art. hY ; and so the latter of them is explained in the S, both there and in the present art.:) and one says, maA A^adoriY A^aY~u haY~i boni baY~K huwa , meaning I know not what man he is. . (S.) Accord. to some, (Lth, T,) haY~u bonu baY~K was one of the sons of Adam, that went away in the earth when the rest of his children dispersed themselves, and no trace of him was afterwards perceived. (Lth, T, K.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , inf. n. tabaEN (S, Msb, K) and tabaAEapN , (S, K,) He followed; or went, or walked, behind, or after; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) him, (Mgh, Msb, K,) or it; namely, a people, or company of men: (S:) or [in the CK “ and ”] he went with him, or it, when the latter had passed by him: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) and ↓ Ait~abaEahu signifies the same; (Lth, S, K *) and so does ↓ A^atobaEahu : (Lth, Mgh, K:) or ↓ A^atobaEotuhumo signifies I overtook them, they having gone before me; (Fr, * A'Obeyd, S, Msb, * K;) as also tabiEotuhumo : (Fr, K:) Akh says that tabiEotuhu and ↓ A^atobaEotuhu signify the same: and hence the saying in the Kur [xxxvii. 10], $ihaAbN vaAqibN ↓ faA^atobaEahu [ and a shooting star piercing the darkness by its light overtaketh him ]: (S:) and the saying in the same [vii. 174], ↓ faA^atobaEahu Al$~ayoTaAnu and the devil overtook him: (TA:) and the saying in the same [xx. 81], firoEawonu ↓ faA^atobaEahumo bijunuwdihi and Pharaoh overtook them with his troops: or almost did so: (Ibn-'Arafeh, K:) or this signifies made his troops to follow them; (TA;) the b , accord. to some, being redundant: (Bd:) or ↓ A^atobaEahu signifies he followed his footsteps; and sought him, following him: (TA:) but ↓ Ait~abaEahumo signifies he went [ after them, or followed them, ] when they had passed by him; as also tabiEahumo , inf. n. tabaEN : you say, ↓ Hat~aY A^atobaEotuhumo ↓ maA zilotu A^at~abiEuhumo , i. e. [ I ceased not to follow them ] until I overtook them: (A'Obeyd:) Fr says that ↓ A^atobaEa is better than ↓ Ait~abaEa ; for the latter signifies he went behind, or after, him, when the latter person was going along; but when you say, ↓ A^atobaEotuhu , it is as though [you meant that] you followed his footsteps: (TA:) and ↓ fulaAnN fulaAnFA ↓ Ait~abaEa [as in the L and TA, but perhaps a mistake for ↓ A^atobaEa ,] signifies also he followed him, desiring to do evil to him; like as Pharaoh followed Moses: (L, TA:) some say, tabiEotu Al$~aYo'a , inf. n. tubuwEN , meaning I went after the thing: and tabiEa Al$~aYo'a , inf. n. tabaEN and tabaAEN , (assumed tropical:) [ he followed the thing ] in respect of actions: (L, TA:) you say, tabiEa AlA_imaAma (assumed tropical:) he followed the Imám [ by doing as he did ]: (Msb:) [but in this last sense, more commonly,] one says, ↓ Ait~abaEahu , meaning (assumed tropical:) he did like as he [another] did: (TA:) and AlquroA=na ↓ Ait~abaEa (assumed tropical:) he followed the Kurán as his guide; did according to what is in it: (TA:) and you say also, EalaY AlA^amori ↓ taAbaEahu ; (Msb;) or ElY ka*aA , inf. n. mutaAbaEapN and tibaAEN ; (S;) (assumed tropical:) [ he followed him, or imitated him, in the affair; ] (Msb;) he followed him, or imitated him, in doing such a thing: (PS:) [but this last phrase has another meaning: see 3.] In the saying, laA yutobaEu binaArK A_ilaY Alqabori , [in which the verb may be pass. of tabiEa or of ↓ A^atobaEa ,] or, accord. to one relation, ↓ lA yut~abaEu , each in the pass. form, [ Fire shall not be made to follow to the grave, though it may be rendered one shall not follow with fire to the grave, it is said that] the b is to render the verb transitive. (Mgh.) ― -b2- tabiEotu Alr~ajula biHaq~iY ; and bihi ↓ taAbaEotuhu , inf. n. mutaAbaEapN [and probably tbaAEN also]; and bh ↓ Ait~abaEotuhu ; I prosecuted, or sued, the man for my right, or due. (TA.) The saying in the Kur [ii. 173], biA@lomaEoruwfi ↓ faA@t~ibaAEN means [ Then ] prosecution for the bloodwit [shall be made with lenity ]. (TA.) ― -b3- tabiEa , of which the aor., yatobaE , occurs in a trad., [see 4,] (Mgh, TA,) pronounced by the relaters of trads. with teshdeed, [↓ yat~abiE ,] (TA,) also signifies (assumed tropical:) He accepted a reference from his debtor to another for the payment of what was owed to him. (Mgh, TA. *)

sourceDefinition: [and mutaAbaEapN , the inf. ns. of taAbaEa ,] i. q. wilaA='N [The making a consecution, or succession, of one to the other, bayona A^amorayoni between two things, or affairs: and the making consecutive, successive, or uninterrupted, in its progressions, or gradations, or the like: see 6]. (S, K.) It is said in a trad., taAbiEuwA bayona AlHaj~i wAlEumorapi [ Make ye a consecution between the Hj~ and the Emrp ; meaning make ye the performance of the Hj~ and that of the Emrp to be consecutive ]; (TA;) i. e. when ye perform the Hj~ , then perform ye the Emrp ; and when ye perform the Emrp , then perform ye the Hj~ : or when ye perform either of these, then perform ye after it the other, without any length of time [ intervening ]: but the former [meaning] is the more obvious. (Marginal note in a copy of the Jámi'-es-Sagheer of Es-Suyootee.) And you say, taAbiEo bayonanaA wabayonahumo EalaY AlxayoraAti (assumed tropical:) Make thou us to be followers, or imitators, of them in excellencies. (TA.) And tAbE AlA^agaAniY~a [ He sang songs consecutively, successively, or uninterruptedly ]. (S and K in art. jr .) And tAbE A_isoqaATahu [ He made it to fall, fall down, drop, drop down, or tumble down, in consecutive portions or quantities ]. (M and K in art. sqT : in the CK AasoqATahu .) And tAbE Alfarasu AljaroYa (assumed tropical:) [ The horse prosecuted, or continued, the course, or running, uninterruptedly ]. (K voce halaba ; &c.) sourceDefinition: : see 1, from the beginning nearly to the end. -A2- Also He made him to follow; or to overtake: (S, K:) he made him to be a follower: (Mgh, Msb:) or he urged him, or induced him, to be a follower. (Mgh.) You say, [making the verb doubly trans.,] A^atobaEotuhumo gayoriY [ I made them to follow, or overtake, another, not myself ]. (K.) And A^atobaEotuhu Al$~aYo'a fatabiEahu [ I made him to follow, or overtake, the thing, and he followed it, or overtook it ]. (S.) And A^atobaEotu zayodFA EamorFA I made Zeyd to be a follower of 'Amr: (Mgh, Msb:) or I urged, or induced, Zeyd to be a follower of 'Amr. (Mgh.) And A^atobaEahu nafosahu mutaHas~irFA EalaY maA faAta (assumed tropical:) [ He made his mind, or desire, to follow after it, regretting what had passed away ]. (TA in art. Ejz .) [See also 10.] It is said in a prov., (TA,) A^atobiEi Alfarasa lijaAmahaA [ Make thou its bit and bridle to follow the horse ]: or Aln~aAqapa zimaAmahaA [ her nose-rein, the she-camel ]: or Ald~alowa ri$aA='ahaA [ its rope, the bucket ]: used in bidding to complete a favour, or benefaction: (K, TA:) A'Obeyd says, I think the meaning of the first prov. to be, Thou hast liberally given the horse, and the bit and bridle are a smaller matter; therefore satisfy thou completely the want, seeing that the horse is not without need of the bit and bridle. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence the trad., mano A^utobiEa EalaY maliYo'K faloyatobaEo (tropical:) Whoso is referred, for the payment of what is owed to him, to a solvent man, let him accept the reference: (Mgh, TA: *) [see also 1, last meaning:] the verb being made trans. by means of ElY because it conveys the meaning of A_iHaAlapN . (Mgh.) You say [also], A^utobiEa fulaAnN bifulaAnK (tropical:) Such a one was referred, for the payment of what was owed to him, to such a one. (S, TA.) And A^atobaEahu Ealayohi (tropical:) He referred him, for the payment of what was owed to him, to him. (TA.) ― -b3- [See also A_itobaAEN , below.]

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. tatab~uEN , (Lth, S, Msb, * K,) for which ↓ Ait~ibaAEN is used by El-Kutámee, tropically, (S,) or, accord. to Sb, because the same in meaning; (TA;) and ↓ tbE~h , inf. n. tatobiyEN ; (S, K; *) He pursued it; investigated it; examined it; hunted after it; prosecuted a search after it; made successive, or repeated, endeavours to attain it, to reach it, or to obtain it; or sought it, sought for it, or sought after it, successively, time after time, or repeatedly, or in a leisurely manner, by degrees, gradually, step by step, bit by bit, or one thing after another, (Lth, S, * Msb, K, * TA,) following after it. (S.) Hence the saying of Zeyd Ibn-Thábit, respecting the collecting of the Kur-án, faEaliqotu A^atatab~aEuhu mina All~ixaAfi waAlEusubi [ And I set myself to seeking to collect it successively, &c., from the thin white stones and the leafless palm-branches upon which it was written]. (TA.) And ttb~E AlbilaAda yaxoruju mino A^aroDK A_ilaY A^aroDK [ He investigated the countries, going forth from land to land ]. (S and K in art. qrY .) And fulaAnN yatatab~aEu A^avara fulaAnK [ Such a one pursues, &c., the track of such a one ]. (TA.) And yatatab~aEu masaAwiYa fulaAnK [ He seeks successively, &c., to discover the vices, faults, or evil qualities or actions, of such a one ]. (TA.) And yatatab~aEu madaAq~a AlA^umuwri wanaHowa *`lika [ He pursues small, or little, affairs; and the like thereof: or he seeks successively, &c., to obtain a knowledge of the subtilties, niceties, abstrusities, or obscuri- ties, of things, or affairs; and the like thereof ]. (TA.) And ttb~E AlHabola [ He took successive holds of the rope ]: said of a man descending from a part of a mountain such as is termed $iyq , by means of a rope tied to that part, to a place in which honey was deposited. (TA in art. $yq .)

A poet says, zamana Alt~aqaH~umi waAlmajaAEaho A^akalato Haniyfapu rab~ahaA ↓ suwo'a AlEawaAqibi waAlt~ibaAEaho lamo yaHo*aruwA mino rab~ihimo [ Haneefeh ate their lord, in the time of experiencing dearth, or drought, or sterility, and hunger: they did not fear, from their lord, the evil of the results, and the consequence of their action]: for they had taken to themselves a god consisting of Hayos , [i. e. dates mixed with clarified butter and the preparation of milk called A^aqiT , kneaded together,] and worshipped it for some time; then famine befell them, and they ate it. (S.) And one says, maA Ealayohi mina A@ll~`hi fiY h`*aA tabiEapN , and ↓ tibaAEapN , There is not, against him, on the part of God, in this, any claim on account of wrong-doing. (TA.)

definition: [One who is prosecuted, or sued, for a right, or due;
sourceDefinition: [One who is prosecuted, or sued, for a right, or due; of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , from tabiEotuhu biHaq~iY ;] one who owes property to another, (S, K, TA,) and whom the latter prosecutes, or sues, for it. (TA.) -A2- The young one of a cow in the first year; (S, Msb, K;) so says Aboo-Fak'as El-Asadee: (TA:) or that is a year old; (Az, Mgh, TA;) not so called until he has completed the year; erroneously said by Lth to signify a calf ripening to his perfect state: (Az, TA:) thus called because he yet follows his mother; (Mgh, Msb;) the word in this sense being of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure faAEilN : (Msb:) and ↓ tiboEN signifies the same: (TA:) fem. of the former with p : (S, Msb, K:) pl. tibaAEN and tabaAy^iEN ; (AA, S, O, K;) both pls. of tabiyEN ; (AA, S, O;) or the former is pl. of tabiyEapN ; (Msb;) and the pl. of tabiyEN is A^atobiEapN [a pl. of pauc.]; (L, Msb;) and A^ataAbiEu and A^ataAbiyEu , the latter of which is extr., are pls. of A^atobiEapN : (L:) the pl. of ↓ tiboEN in the abovementioned sense is A^atobaAEN . (TA.) Accord. to EshShaabee, (IF,) One whose horns and ears are equal [ in length ]: (IF, K:) but this is a judicial explanation; not deduced from the rules of lexicology. (IF.) ― -b2- I. q. ↓ taAbiEN [as signifying One who prosecutes, or sues, for a right, or due; and particularly for blood-revenge]. (S, K.) Hence the saying in the Kur [xvii. 71], vum~a laA tajiduwA lakumo EalayonaA bihi tabiyEFA Then ye shall not find for you any to prosecute for blood-revenge, nor any to sue, against us therein: (Fr. S, K:) or ye shall not find for you any to sue us for the disallowing of what hath befallen you, nor for our averting it from you: (Zj:) [or any aider against us; for] tabiyEN also signifies an aider; and especially against an enemy. (Lth, K.) ― -b3- See also taAbiEN , latter half.

definition: An appellation of each of the Kings of El-Yemen (S, K) who possessed Himyer and Hadramowt, (K, TA,) and, as some add, Sebà;
sourceDefinition: An appellation of each of the Kings of El-Yemen (S, K) who possessed Himyer and Hadramowt, (K, TA,) and, as some add, Sebà; (TA;) but not otherwise; (K, TA;) and the like of this is said in the 'Eyn: (TA:) so called because they followed one another; whenever one died, another took his place, following him in his course of acting: (TA:) pl. tabaAbiEapN , (S, K,) with p added as having the meaning of a rel. n.; [as though it were pl. of tub~aEiY~N , like as HanaAbilapN is pl. of HanobaliY~N ;] erroneously written in some of the copies of the K ttAbEp : (TA:) the tbAbEp of Himyer were like the A^akaAsirap of the Persians and the qayaASirap of the Romans. (Lth.) In the Kur xliv. 36, it is said in a trad. to mean a particular king, who was a believer, and whose people were unbelievers. (Zj.) ― -b2- And hence, (TA,) A species of the yaEaAsiyb [or kings of the bees ], (K,) the greatest and most beautiful thereof, whom the other bees follow: (TA:) pl. tabaAbiyEu ; (K;) in the L, tataAbiEu [which is probably a mistranscription for tabaAbiEu ]. (TA.) ― -b3- A species of Tayor [which means any flying things, as well as birds; and may therefore, perhaps, be meant to indicate what next precedes]. (S.) ― -b4- The shade, or shadow; (S, K;) because it follows the sun; as also ↓ tub~uEN . (K.) A poet says, (S,) namely, Soadà El-Juhaneeyeh, (TA,) or Selmà El-Juhaneeyeh, (marginal note in a copy of the S,) bewailing her brother, As'ad, yaridu AlmiyaAhu HaDiyrapN wanafiyDapF wiroda AlqaTaApi A_i*aA A@somaA^al~a Alt~ub~aEu (S) [ He comes to the waters when people are dwelling, or staying, there, (but see HaDiyrapN ,) and when no one is there, as the bird called katáh comes to water ] when the shade has become contracted at mid-day: or, accord. to Aboo-Leylà, the meaning is, the shade of night; i. e., this man comes to the waters in the last part of the night, before any one: though it means also the shade of day-time: (TA:) or, accord. to Aboo-Sa'eed Ed- Dareer, the meaning here is [ the star, or asterism, called ] Ald~abaraAn ; and this is very probably correct; for the bird above mentioned comes to the waters by night, and seldom by day; and hence the saying, A^adal~u mino qaTaApK . (Az, TA.) See taAbiEN . ― -b5- See also tiboEN . ― -b6- maA A^adoriY A^aY~u tub~aEK huwa I know not who of men he is. (Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ― -b7- tub~aEN is also a pl. of taAbiEN [q. v.]. (TA.)

definition: A certain wind, (K, TA,) also called Aln~ukayobaA='u , (TA,) which blows (K, TA) in the early morning, (TA,) with the rising of the sun, (K, TA,) from the direction of the wind called AlS~abaA ,...
sourceDefinition: A certain wind, (K, TA,) also called Aln~ukayobaA='u , (TA,) which blows (K, TA) in the early morning, (TA,) with the rising of the sun, (K, TA,) from the direction of the wind called AlS~abaA , unaccompanied by rising clouds, (TA,) and veers round through the various places whence winds blow until it returns to the place from which blows the wind called AlSbA , (K, TA,) whence it commenced in the early morning: (TA:) the Arabs dislike it. (Z, TA.)

definition: Following; a follower: (TA:) and ↓ tabaEN also signifies the same as taAbiEN ; (K;) a thing that follows in the track of a thing; (Lth, Az;) or that is at the kinder, or latter, part of anything;...
sourceDefinition: Following; a follower: (TA:) and ↓ tabaEN also signifies the same as taAbiEN ; (K;) a thing that follows in the track of a thing; (Lth, Az;) or that is at the kinder, or latter, part of anything; (TA;) but is used alike as sing. and pl.: (S, Msb, K:) the pl. of taAbiEN is tub~aEN and tub~aAEN (TA) [and, applied to rational beings, taAbiEuwna ]: and the pl. of ↓ tabaEN is A^atobaAEN ; (S, K;) or this may be used as a pl. of tabaEN ; (Msb;) or it is pl. of taAbiEN , like as xadamN is pl. of xaAdimN , (Kr, Mgh,) and TalabN of TaAlibN , &c.; (K;) or, correctly speaking, it is a quasi-pl. n. (Sb, TA.) You say, ↓ AlmuSal~iY tabaEN lAimaAmihi [ The person praying is a follower of his Imám ]: and Aln~aAsu tabaEN lahu [ The people are followers of him ]. (Msb.) And it is said in the Kur [xiv. 24, and xl. 50], ↓ A_in~aA kun~aA lakumo tabaEFA [ Verily we were followers of you ]: (S, TA:) in which the last word may be a quasi-pl. n. of taAbiEN ; or it may be an inf. n., meaning *awiY tabaEK . (TA.) ↓ tabaEN is applied as an epithet to the legs of a beast: (Lth, T:) and is also used as [an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant,] signifying The legs of a beast. (K.) ― -b2- A jinnee, or genie, that accompanies a woman and follows her whithersoever she goes, (K, TA,) loving her: (TA:) and taAbiEapN a jinneeyeh, or female genie, that does the same to a man: (S, * K, TA:) or the p is added in the latter to give intensiveness to the signification, or to denote evilness of nature, or to convey the meaning of daAhiyapN , q. v.: the pl. is tawaAbiEu : and this means female associates. (TA.) ― -b3- A servant; as also ↓ tabiyEN . (TA.) A^awi Alt~aAbiEiyna gayori A^uwliY AlA_irobapi , in the Kur [xxiv. 31], accord. to Th, means Or the servants of the husband, such as the old man who is perishing by reason of age, and the aged woman. (TA.) ― -b4- See also tabiyEN . ― -b5- [Also One next in the order of time after the SaHaAbap ; like ↓ taAbiEiY~N . ― -b6- And in grammar, An appositive. ] ― -b7- taAbiEu Aln~ajomi [ The follower of the asterism; i. e., of the Pleiades; ] a name of Ald~abaraAn [ the Hyades; or the five chief stars thereof; or the brightest star among them, a of Taurus ]: this name being given to it as ominous of good; (K;) or as ominous of evil: (O:) or so called because it follows the Pleiades: (T:) also called Alt~aAbiEu , (T in art. dbr , Sh, IB, and others,) and ↓ tuwayobiEN , (K,) which is the dim., (TA,) or Alt~uwayobiEu , (T in art. dbr ,) and ↓ tub~aEN , (K,) or Alt~ub~aEu [q. v.], (Aboo-Sa'eed Ed-Dareer, T,) and ↓ Alt~abaEu , (IB, Z,) and Alt~aAliY , and AlHaAdiY , (IB,) or HAdY Aln~ujuwmi , (S in art. jdH ,) or HAdY Aln~ajomi . (Kzw and others.) [See also AlmijodaHu .] taAbiEiY~N : see taAbiEN .

sourceDefinition: in language is when one says the like of HasanN basanN (S, K) and qabiyHN $aqiyHN : (S:) The putting, after a word, an imitative sequent, i. e. another word similar to the former in measure or in its rawiY~ , by way of pleonasm, or for fulness of expression, and for corroboration; (Mz 28th nwE , and Kull p. 11;) the latter word being one not used alone, and having no meaning by itself, as in bsanNa HasanN ; or being one which has a meaning of its own, as in haniyoy^FA mariyoy^FA . definition: Firmness of heart in war.
sourceDefinition: Firmness of heart in war. (Msb, TA.) You say, lahu vabatN Einoda AlHamolapi He has firmness, or steadiness, on the occasion of the charge, or assault. (S, A.) And lahu vabatN Einoda AlHimaAmi He has firmness on the occasion of death. (L.) [See also vabaAtN .] ― -b2- Hence, (Msb,) A proof, and evidence, or a voucher. (S, Mgh, Msb, TA.) You say, laA A^aHokumu bika*aA A_il~aA bivabatK I will not decide so unless on the ground of proof, or evidence. (S.) And it is said in a trad. respecting the day of doubt, [i. e. the day of which one doubts whether it be the last of Shaabán or the first of Ramadán,] vum~a jaA='a Alv~abatu A^an~ahu mino ramaDaAna Then came the proof, or evidence, or voucher, that it was of Ramadán. (TA.) ― -b3- And hence, (Mgh,) applied to a man, (A, Mgh, [in which latter it is said to be tropical when thus applied, but not so in the A,]) and sometimes written ↓ vabotN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) One who is an authoritative evidence, or voucher, by reason of his trustworthiness in that which he relates: (A, TA:) or (tropical:) one who is trustworthy (Mgh, K *) in that which he relates: (Mgh: [in the K, only the pl. is mentioned:]) or (assumed tropical:) one who is just, or equitable, [in that which he relates,] and exact, or honest: (Msb:) pl. A^avobaAtN . (A, Mgh, Msb, K.) ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) An index, or a table of contents, in which a relater of traditions collects a list of what he has related from others, and of his sheykhs [ who are his authorities ]: said by some to be a conventional term of the relaters of traditions: perhaps tropical. (TA.)

definition: , aor. , (S, M, Msb, K,) inf. n. valovN , (TA,) He took the third of the goods, or property, of the people, or company of men. (S, M, Msb, K.) And vulivati Alt~arikapu The property left at death had...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, M, Msb, K,) inf. n. valovN , (TA,) He took the third of the goods, or property, of the people, or company of men. (S, M, Msb, K.) And vulivati Alt~arikapu The property left at death had a third of it taken. (A.) And valava , aor. , [but in this case it seems that it should be , as above,] is also said to signify He slew a third. (L.) ― -b2- valava Alqawoma , (T, S, K,) or AlAivonayoni , (Fr, T, M,) or Alr~ajulayoni , (Msb,) aor. , (S, M, Msb, K,) [thus distinguished from the verb in the first sense explained above,] inf. n. valovN , (TA,) signifies He was, or became, the third of the people, (T, S, K,) or a third to the two, (Fr, T, M,) or to the two men: (Msb:) or he made them, with himself, three: (T, S, K:) and similar to this are the other verbs of number, to ten [inclusive], except that you say, A^arobaEuhumo and A^asobaEuhumo and A^atosaEuhumo , with fet-h, because of the E . (S.) A poet says, (IAar, S,) namely, AbdAllah Ibn-Ez-Zubeyr El-Asadee, satirizing the tribe of Teiyi, (IB, TA,) faA_ino tavolivuwA narobaEo waA_ino yaku xaAmisN yakuno saAdisN Hat~aY yubiyrakumu Alqatolu [ And if ye make up the number of three, we will make up the number of four; and if there be a fifth of you, there shall be a sixth of us; so that slaughter shall destroy you ]: (IAar, S, IB:) he means, if ye become three, we will become four: or if ye slay three. (IB, TA.) ― -b3- Also; (S, M, TA;) in the K, “ or, ” but this is wrong; (MF, TA;) valava Alqawoma signifies He made the people, with himself, thirty; (A 'Obeyd, S, M, K;) they being twenty-nine: and in like manner one uses the other verbs of number, to a hundred [exclusive]. (A 'Obeyd, S.) And valava also signifies He made twelve to be thirteen. (T.) ― -b4- valava AlA^aroDa He turned over the ground three times for sowing, or cultivating. (A, TA.) ― -b5- See also 2. ― -b6- valava , (T, M, L, TA,) [as though intrans., an objective complement being app. understood,] or ↓ vl~v , (K, [but the former is app. the right reading, unless both be correct,]) said of a horse, He came [ third in the race; i. e., next ] after that which is called AlmuSal~iY : (T, M, L, K: [in the CK, Al*Y , after Alfarasu , should be omitted:]) then you say rabaEa : then, xamasa . (T, M, L.) And in like manner it is said of a man [as meaning He came third ]. (T.) ― -b7- laA yavoniY walaA yavolivu , (so in a copy of the M in art. vnY , but in the present art. in the same copy written lA yvniY wlA yvolivu ,) or ↓ laA yuvan~iY walaA yuval~ivu , (so in a copy of the A, [in the CK in art. vnY , and in Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 545, laA yuvan~aY walaA yuval~avu ,]) or ↓ laA yuvoniY walaA yuvolivu , (so in a copy of the K in art. vnY , [in the TA, in the present art. and in art. vnY , without any syll. signs,]) said of an old man, meaning He cannot rise, (M, A, TA,) when he desires to do so, a first time, nor can he (M, TA) the second time, nor the third. (M, A, TA.)

definition: He made it three;
sourceDefinition: He made it three; or called it three: (Esh-Sheybánee, and K in art. wHd :) tavoliyvN signifies the making [a thing] three [ by addition or multiplication or division ]; as also ↓ valovN [inf. n. of valava ]: and the calling [it] three. (KL.) ― -b2- [Hence, vl~v , inf. n. tavoliyvN , He asserted the doctrine of the Trinity. ] ― -b3- [Hence also,] fulaAnN yuvan~iY walaA yuval~ivu Such a one counts two Khaleefehs, namely, the two Sheykhs [Aboo-Bekr and 'Omar], and [ does not count three, i. e.,] rejects the other [that succeeded them]: and fulaAnN yuval~ivu walaA yurab~iEu Such a one counts three Khaleefehs, [namely, those mentioned above and 'Othmán,] and [ does not count a fourth, i. e.,] rejects ['Alee,] the fourth. (A, TA.) ― -b4- laA yuvan~iY walaA yuval~ivu : see 1. ― -b5- vl~v liA@moraA^atihi , or EinodahaA , He remained three nights with his wife: and in like manner the verb is used in relation to any saying or action. (TA voce sab~aEa .) ― -b6- vl~v binaAqatihi He tied, or bound, three of the teats of his she-camel with the SiraAr . (S.) ― -b7- val~avato said of a she-camel, and of any female: see 4. ― -b8- vl~v said of a horse in a race: see 1. ― -b9- vl~v Albusoru , (M, K,) inf. n. as above, (K,) The full-grown unripe dates became, to the extent of a third part of them, ripe, or in the state in which they are termed ruTab . (M, K.) ― -b10- tavoliyvN also signifies The watering seed-produce [ on the third day, i. e.,] another time baEoda Alv~unoyaA [which app. means after excepting, or omitting, one day ]. (M.) ― -b11- And The making [a thing] triangular [or trilateral ]. (KL.) ― -b12- [The making a letter three-pointed; making it to have three dots. ] ― -b13- The making [a thing] to be a third part. (KL.) ― -b14- The making the electuary, or confection, of aromatics, or perfumes, that is called muval~av . (KL.)

definition: and ↓ mavolavu (S, L, K) Three and three;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ mavolavu (S, L, K) Three and three; three and three together; or three at a time and three at a time; (L;) imperfectly decl. [because] changed from the original form of valaAvapN valaAvapN ; (K;) or because of their having the quality of epithets and deviating from the original form of valaAvapN : they are epithets; for you say, mararotu biqawomK mavonaY wavulaAva [ I passed by a party of men two and two, and three and three, together ]: (Sb, S:) or they are imperfectly decl. because they deviate from their original as to the letter and the meaning; the original word being changed as above stated, and the meaning being changed to valaAvapN valaAvapN : but the dim. is ↓ vulay~ivN , perfectly decl., like A^uHay~idN &c., because it is like Humay~irN [dim. of HimaArN ], assuming the form of that which is perfectly decl., though it is not so in the cases of A^aHosanu and the like, as these words, in assuming the dim. form, do not deviate from the measure of a verb, for maA A^uHayosinahu [How goodly is he!] is sometimes said. (S.) It is said in the Kur [iv. 3], faA@nokiHuwA maA TaAba lakumo mina Aln~isaA='i wavulaAva warubaAEa , i. e. Then marry ye such as please you, of women, two [ and ] two, and three [ and ] three, and four [ and ] four: [meaning, two at a time, &c.:] here mvnY &c. are imperfectly decl. because deviating from the original form of Aivonayoni Aivonayoni , &c., and from the fem. form. (Zj, T, L.) And one says ↓ mavolava mavolava , like vulaAva vulaAva . (T.) You say also, faEalotu Al$~aYo'a mavonaY wavulaAva warubaAEa , meaning I did the thing twice and twice, and thrice and thrice, and four times and four times. (L.) ― -b2- [ vulaAvN is app. fem. of vulaAvapN , a dial, var. of valaAvapN , of which the fem. is valaAvN : and hence,] *uw vulaAvK , with damm [to the initial v ], A camel's [ girth of the kind called ] waDiyn . (K.) You say, Ailotaqato EuraA *iY vulaAvihaA (tropical:) [lit., The loops of her girth met together ]; (A, TA; [but in a copy of the former, ↓ *Y valaAvihaA ;]) meaning, she was, or became, lean , or lank in the belly. (A. [See a similar saying voce biTaAnN .]) And a poet says, waqado Damarato Hat~aY badaA *uw vulaAvihaA [ And she had become lean, or lank in the belly, so that her girth appeared ]: but some say that *w vlAvhA [here] means her belly, and the two skins, [namely,] the upper, and that which is pared, or scraped off, after the flaying: (TA:) or, accord. to some, the phrase is Hat~aY A@rotaqaY *w vlAvhA , meaning, so that her fœtus rose to her back; the vlAv [here again in a copy of the A written with fet-h to the initial v , and in like manner vlAvhA ,] being the saAbiyaA=' and the salaA and the womb. (A, TA.) You say also ↓ Ealayohi *uw valaAvK , [so I find it written, but perhaps it should be *w vulaAvK ,] meaning, (tropical:) Upon him is a [ garment of the kind called ] kisaA=' made of the wool of three sheep. (A, TA. [In the latter without any syll. sign to show that vlAv here differs from the form in the exs. cited before.])

definition: , also written val`vapN , a noun of number, [i.
sourceDefinition: , also written val`vapN , a noun of number, [i. e. Three, ] is masc., (S, M, Msb,) and is also written and pronounced ↓ vulaAvapN , with damm: (IAar, M, TA:) the fem. is ↓ valaAvN , also written val`vN ; (S, M, Msb;) [and app. vulaAvN also, mentioned above, under the head of vulaAvu , but only as occurring with *uw prefixed to it.] You say vulaAvapu rijaAlK [ Three men ]: and nisowapK ↓ valaAvu [ three women ]. (Msb.) In the saying of Mohammad, ↓ rufiEa Alqalamu Eano valaAvK [ The pen of the recording angel is withheld from three persons] vlAv is for valaAvi A^anofusK . (Msb. [See art. rfE .]) [In like manner, ↓ valaAvN occurs in several trads. for valaAvu xiSaAlK ; as, for instance, in the saying,] valaAvN mano kun~a fiyhi HaAsabahu A@ll~`hu HisaAbFA yasiyrFA [There are three qualities: in whomsoever they be, God will reckon with him with an easy reckoning ]: these are, thy giving to him who denies thee, and forgiving him who wrongs thee, and being kind to him who cuts thee off from him. (El-Jámi' es-Sagheer.) The people of El-Hijáz say, A^atawoniY valaAvatahumo [ The three of them came to me ], and A^arobaEatahumo , and so on to ten [inclusive], with nasb in every case; and in like manner in the fem., ↓ A^atayonaniY valaAvahun~a , and A^arobaEahun~a : but others decline the word with the three vowels, making it like kul~uhumo : after ten, however, only nasb is used; so that you say, A^atawoniY A^aHada Ea$arahumo [and valaAvapa Ea$arahumo ], and A_iHodaY Ea$oratahun~a [and valaAva Ea$oratahun~a ]. (S.) The saying waladu Alz~inaA $arN Alv~alaAvapi means [ The offspring of adultery, or fornication, is the worst of the three ] if he do the deeds of his parents. (Mgh.) [It is said that when vlAvp means the things numbered, not the amount of the number, it is imperfectly decl., being regarded as a proper name; and so are other ns. of number. (See vumaAniypN .) See also sit~apN .] ― -b2- valaAvapa Ea$ara [indecl. in every case, meaning Thirteen, ] is pronounced by some of the Arabs valaAvapa Eo$ara : and [the fem.] Ea$orapa ↓ valaAva , thus in the dial. of El- Hijáz [and of most of the Arabs], is pronounced valaAva Ea$irapa in the dial. of Nejd. (S in art. E$r .)
