sourceDefinition: A servant; (S, * Mgh, * Msb, * K, * TA;) applied to a young man, (S, Mgh, Msb,) or a male: (K:) and, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) as also xaAdimapN , (Msb, K,) each in chaste Arabic, (TA,) but the latter rare, (Msb,) to a young woman, (S, Mgh, Msb,) or a female: (K:) and xad~aAmN [q. v.] is also used in the same sense as xaAdimN : (TA:) the pl. of xaAdimN is ↓ xadamN , (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) or rather this is a quasi-pl. n., (TA,) and xud~aAmN (JK, Msb, K) and xadamapN , and vulgarly xudomaAnN . (TA.) It is said in a trad., of 'Abd-Er-Rahmán, (TA,) Tal~aqa A@moraA^atahu famat~aEahaA bixaAdimK sawodaA='a , meaning [ He divorced his wife, and gave her on that occasion ] a black young woman [as a slave]. (Mgh, * TA.) In the saying fulaAnapu xaAdimapu gadFA , the word xAdmp is not properly an epithet: the meaning is, Such a woman will be a servant to-morrow; like as one says HaAy^iDapN gadFA . (Msb.)

(K.)

sourceDefinition: , (JK, S, Msb, K,) aor. , (JK, Msb,) inf. n. xazanN , (Msb,) He reposited it, stowed it, or put it, (S, Msb,) laid it up, kept it, preserved it, or guarded it, (JK, K,) in a xizaAnap , (JK, S,) or in a maxozin [or maxozan ]; (Msb;) namely, a thing, (JK, Msb,) or property; (S, K;) as also ↓ Axtznhu , (S, K,) and ↓ Astxznhu : or ↓ the second of these signifies he did so for himself. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence] the first (S, Msb) and ↓ the second, (S,) (assumed tropical:) He concealed it; namely, a secret. (TA.) Tarafeh says, vum~a laA yaxozanu fiynaA laHomuhaA A_in~amaA yaxozanu laHomu Almud~axiro [ Then the flesh thereof will not become stinking among us: only the flesh-meat of him who lays it up becomes stinking ]. (S, TA.)

definition: [One who reposits, stows, lays up, keeps, preserves, or guards, property, &c.
sourceDefinition: [One who reposits, stows, lays up, keeps, preserves, or guards, property, &c.; a treasurer ]: (K, TA:) pl. xaAzinuwna and xazanapN . (TA.) [The latter of these pls. is applied in the Kur. xxxix. 73 to The keepers, or guardians, of Paradise: and in xxxix. 71 and xl. 52 and lxvii. 8 to those of Hell.] maA A^anotumo lahu bixaAziniyna , in the Kur [xv. 22, accord. to some], means (assumed tropical:) Ye are not bearing it in mind with thankfulness. (TA.) ― -b2- (tropical:) The tongue; as also ↓ xaz~aAnN . (K, TA.) Hence the saying of Lukmán to his son, A_i*aA kaAna xaAzinuka HafiyZFA A^amiynapF ra$odota fiY A^amorayoka dunoyaAka waA=xiratika ↓ waxizaAnatuka , i. e. (tropical:) [ When ] thy tongue [ is such as keeps the secret confided to thee ], and thy heart [ is trustworthy, thou wilt follow the right way in respect of thy two states, thy state in the present world and thy state in the world to come ]. (TA.)

(Msb.) And He made anything double, putting one piece upon another; he faced it. (TA.) ― -b3- And [hence,] xaSafa EalaY nafosihi , (JK,) or xaSafa Alwaraqa EalaY badanihi , (S, * K,) aor. as above, (S, TA,) and so the inf. n.; (TA;) and ↓ AxtSf ; (S, K;) and ↓ AxSf ; (K;) and ↓ xS~f , inf. n. taxoSiyfN ; (TA;) (tropical:) He stuck [or sewed ] the leaves together, one to another, (S, K, * TA,) and covered his person with them, leaf by leaf, (K,) to conceal therewith his pudenda: (S, TA:) or the first phrase, (JK,) as also ↓ AxtSf , (Lth, JK,) signifies he (a naked man) put upon his pudenda wide leaves, (Lth, JK,) or the like: (Lth:) you say, bika*aA ↓ AxtSf [ he covered his pudenda with such a thing ]. (Lth, JK.) It is said in the Kur [vii. 21 and xx. 119], waTafiqaA yaxoSifaAni EalayohimaA mino waraqi Aljan~api ; and ↓ yaxiS~ifaAni , originally yaxotaSifaAni , by some pronounced ↓ yaxaS~ifaAni , (S, TA,) and by some, ↓ yaxoS~ifaAni , with two quiescent letters together; (TA; [but this appears to be incorrect; see 8 in art. xSm ;]) and ↓ yuxoSifaAni , from A^axoSafa ; and ↓ yuxaS~ifaAni , from xaS~afa ; (Ksh and Bd in vii. 21, and TA;) thus accord. to different readings; i. e. (tropical:) And they betook themselves to sticking [or sewing ] together, one to another, of the leaves of Paradise, to conceal therewith their pudenda. (S, TA.) And hence, also, the saying, in a trad., A_i*aA daxala A^aHadukumu AlHam~aAma faEalayohi biAln~a$iyri ↓ walaA yuxaS~ifo , i. e. (tropical:) [ When any one of you enters the bath, ] let him take the waist-wrapper, and not put his hand upon his pudendum: and like this in meaning is txS~fh [app. a mistranscription for ↓ yataxaS~afu , or ↓ yaxiS~ifu or the like, for yaxotaSifu : if not, it must be ↓ taxaS~afahu , meaning he put his hand upon it ]. (TA.) ― -b5- And xuSifati Alkatiybapu mino waraAy^ihaA bixayolK , i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ The body of troops ] was followed [ by horsemen ]. (S.) ― -b6- And xaSafa , aor. , inf. n. xaSofN , (assumed tropical:) He lied. (Munjid of Kr. (JK, TA.)

definition: A wound, (S, A, K,) or mutilation, (S,) for which there is no fine, or mulct, (A,) or for which there is no certain fine, or mulct;
sourceDefinition: A wound, (S, A, K,) or mutilation, (S,) for which there is no fine, or mulct, (A,) or for which there is no certain fine, or mulct; (S, K:) or what is below the bloodwit; as the cutting off of an arm or a hand, or of an car, and the like: (K:) or a wound, or mutilation, of any kind below slaughter and the bloodwit; such as amputation, or a wound; or a blow, or plunder, or a similar injury. (L.) It is related in a trad., that Keys Ibn-' Ásim collected his sons at his death, and said, kaAna bayoniY wabayona fulaAnK xumaA$aAtN fiY AljaAhiliy~ahi [ There were, between me and such a one, wounds, &c., in the Time of Ignorance ]. (L.) And you say, qado A^axa*otu xumaA$atiY mino fulaAnK I have retaliated upon such a one [ my wound, &c.]. (TA.) ― -b2- xumaA$aAtN , also, (S, TA,) or xumaA$aAtu *aHolK , (A, TA,) signifies (tropical:) Remains of *aHol [or desire of retaliation, or the like ]. (S, A, TA.)

definition: Wine; (S, K;) so called because of its oldness: (S:) or old wine: (TA:) [accord. to some,] derived from xadorasapN , a word not explained: (K:) by some said to be of the measure fanoEaliysN , so that...
sourceDefinition: Wine; (S, K;) so called because of its oldness: (S:) or old wine: (TA:) [accord. to some,] derived from xadorasapN , a word not explained: (K:) by some said to be of the measure fanoEaliysN , so that its radical letters are xdr ; because wine is muxad~ir [i. e. a cause of torpor or languor]: by some said to be from xarosN ; but to this it is objected that d is not augmentative: the truth is, that it is of the measure faEolaliylN , as Sb says: (MF:) by the author of the L and others, it is mentioned after art. xns : (TA:) or it is a Greek word, arabicized: (K:) [but I know not how this is, unless, as an epithet applied to wheat, (see what follows,) it be supposed to be from χόνδρος :] IDrd thought it to be an arabicized word: it may be an arabicized word from the Persian xanodaho riy$o , meaning “ having a laughing beard,” [or rather “one whose beard is laughed at,” i. e., “a laughing-stock,”] because he who makes use of it [namely of wine] has his beard laughed at. (TA.) ― -b2- You also say, HinoTap xanodariysN Old wheat: (IDrd, S, K:) and tamorN xanodariysN old dates. (TA.)

definition: , aor. yaxuwDu , inf. n. xawoDN (S, A, Msb, K) and xiyaADN , (S, A, K,) [ He waded, or forded, through the water; ] he passed through the water walking or riding: (S:) or he entered into the water;...
sourceDefinition: , aor. yaxuwDu , inf. n. xawoDN (S, A, Msb, K) and xiyaADN , (S, A, K,) [ He waded, or forded, through the water; ] he passed through the water walking or riding: (S:) or he entered into the water; (A, K;) as also ↓ xaw~aDahu , (K,) inf. n. taxowiyDN ; (TA;) [or this latter has an intensive signification, as it is said to have in a phrase below;] and ↓ AxtADhu : (K:) or he walked in, or through, the water; (Msb;) as also ↓ txw~Dhu : (TA:) or he entered into the water and walked in it, or through it. (TA.) You say also, xaADa biAlfarasi , meaning He brought the horse to the water; as also ↓ AxADhu , (K,) inf. n. A_ixaADahu ; (AZ;) and ↓ xAwDhu , (K,) or xAwDhu fiY AlmaA='i , inf. n. muxaAwaDapN , as in the A: (TA:) or ↓ AxADwA AlmaA='a signifies xaADuwhu bidawaAb~ihimo [ They waded or forded through the water, or entered into it, &c., with their beasts ]: and you say also, ↓ xaAwaDotuhumo fY AlmaA='i [ I waded or forded with them through the water; &c.; meaning with men, not with beasts]: (so I find in a copy of the A:) and Alqawomu ↓ AxAD signifies xaADato xayoluhumu AlmaA='a [ The people's horses waded or forded through the water ]. (S.) ― -b2- xaADati AlA_ibilu luj~a Als~araAbi (tropical:) [ The camels passed through the great expanse of mirage ]. (A.) ― -b3- xaADa Albaroqu AlZ~alaAma (tropical:) [ The lightning penetrated through the darkness ]. (A, TA.) ― -b4- xaADa A_ilayohi Alr~imaAHa Hat~aY A^axa*ahu (tropical:) [ He forced his way to him through the spears until he took him, or it ]. (A, TA. *) ― -b5- xaADa Alqawomu fiY AlHadiyvi , (S, A,) and fiyhi ↓ txAwDwA , (S, A, K,) (tropical:) The people, or company of men, entered [or waded ] together into discourse. (S, A, K.) ― -b6- xaADa AlgamaraAti , (S, K,) aor. as above, inf. n. xawoDN , (TA,) (tropical:) He plunged into the submerging floods of ignorance, or the like; syn. AiqotaHamahaA . (S, K, TA.) ― -b7- xaADa fiY AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) He entered [or plunged ] into the affair. (Msb.) ― -b8- In like manner you say, [ xaADa fiY AlbaATili and] AlbaATila ↓ AxAD (assumed tropical:) He entered [or plunged ] into false, or vain, discourse or speech: (Msb:) and xaADa , alone, signifies (tropical:) He said, or spoke, what was false. (A.) It is said in the Kur [lxxiv. 46], (TA,) wakun~aA naxuwDu maEa AlxaAy^iDiyna , i. e. fiY AlbaATili (tropical:) [ And we used to enter into false, or vain, discourse or speech, with those who entered thereinto ]; (Bd, Jel, K;) syn. na$oraEu : (Bd:) or and we used to follow the erring, &c. (O, K.) And again, [lii. 12,] Al~a*iyna humo fiY xawoDK yaloEabuwna (tropical:) [ Who amuse themselves in entering into false, or vain, discourse or speech ]; (TA;) fY AlbATl being here, again, understood. (Bd.) And again, [ix. 70,] waxuDotumo kaA@l~a*iY xaADuwA , i. e. kaxawoDihimo (tropical:) [ And ye have entered into false, or vain, discourse or speech, like their entering thereinto ]. (K.) And again, [vi. 67,] Al~a*iyna yaxuwDuwna fiY A=yaAtinaA (tropical:) [ Who enter into false, or vain, discourse or speech respecting our signs; meaning the Kur-án]. (TA.) xaADa fiyhi is also explained as signifying (assumed tropical:) He said what was false respecting it. (TA.) And xawoDN signifies (assumed tropical:) The confusing, or confounding, in an affair. (TA.) ― -b9- xaADa , (S, A, Mgh, K,) and ↓ xw~D , (A, TA,) also signify He mixed, (S, * K, TA,) and stirred about, (TA,) the beverage, or wine: (S, K, TA:) or he stirred about the sawiyq with the mixowaD . (A, Mgh. *) ― -b10- xaADahu biAls~ayofi (tropical:) He moved about the sword in him, having smitten him: (S, K, * TA:) or he put [or thrust ] the sword into the lower part of his belly, and then raised it upwards. (A, * TA.) ― -b11- xuDotu biqidoHK fiY AlqidaAHi , (A, TA,) inf. n. xiyaADN ; and AlqidaAHa ↓ xaAwaDotu , inf. n. xiwaADN ; (TA;) (tropical:) I put an arrow, (A, TA,) which I had borrowed, and by which I expected to have good luck, (TA,) among the [ other ] arrows (A, TA) used in the game called el-meysir: (TA:) see an ex. (a verse of Sakhr-el-Gheí) in art. xD .

sourceDefinition: and dijaAjN (S, A, Msb) and dujaAjN , (TA,) the first of which is more chaste than the second, (S, A, Msb, * TA,) and the second than the third; (TA;) a coll. gen. n.; (S, TA;) n. un. dajaAjapN (S, Mgh, K) and dijaAjapN (S, K) and dujaAjapN ; (K;) applied to the male and the female; (S, K;) A certain bird, (TA,) well known; (S, Msb, K;) [the common domestic fowl, both cock and hen; ] so called because of its [frequent] coming and going: (Towsheeh:) pl. dujujN , (Mgh, Msb,) and sometimes dajaAy^iju ; (Msb;) and pl. of the n. un. djAjAtN ; and dijaAjN may be regarded as a broken pl. of dijaAjapN , its kesreh and A being considered as the kesreh and A which make the pl. form, and as being not the kesreh and A which are in the sing.; or it may be a pl. of dujaAjapN with the augmentative letter A rejected, as though pl. of duj~apN . (TA.)

definition: [part. n. of 1]. You say jamaAEapN daAj~apN A party, or company, creeping along; i. e., going, or walking, leisurely, softly, or gently: (ISk, S:) or doing so with short steps: or coming and going....
sourceDefinition: [part. n. of 1]. You say jamaAEapN daAj~apN A party, or company, creeping along; i. e., going, or walking, leisurely, softly, or gently: (ISk, S:) or doing so with short steps: or coming and going. (TA.) And A^aqobala AlHaAj~u wa Ald~aAj~u (S, * K, * TA) The [ company of pilgrims to Mekkeh, and of the ] letters-out of camels &c., and the servants, or assistants, (S, K,) and the like attendants of the pilgrims, came: (TA:) the two words HAj~ and dAj~ , though sings., are used in the pl. sense: (TA:) or AldAj~ signifies also the merchants; (K;) or the merchants and others who go leisurely, or creep along, after the pilgrims. (TA.) AldAj~ has the same meaning in the words of a trad., h`w^ulaA='i Ald~aAj~u walayosuwA biAljaAj~i [ These are the lettersout of camels &c., and they are not the pilgrims ]: (S, K:) said by Ibn-' Omar, of a people whom he saw among the pilgrims, whose appearance he disliked: or it means, accord. to A 'Obeyd, those who are with the pilgrims, such as the hired men, and the camel-drivers, and the servants, and the like; and Ibn-' Omar meant that these were not pilgrims in the proper sense, but merely persons journeying and creeping along. (TA.) In the words of another trad., maA tarakotu mino HaAjapK walaA daAjapK A_il~aA A^atayotu , the word dAjp is without teshdeed, and is an imitative sequent to HAjp : (S:) [see art. dwj :] but accord. to one relation, it is mA trkt HaAj~apN walaA daAj~apN , meaning, accord. to El-Khattábee, [ I left not a company of ] pilgrims to Mekkeh, nor those returning. (TA.) One says also, A^amaA waHawaAj~i bayoti A@ll~`hi wa dawaAj~ihi laA^afoEalan~a ka*aA waka*aA [ Nay, by the pilgrims to the House of God, and those who journey thither for mercantile purposes, I will assuredly do such and such things ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, TA,) inf. n. dasoEN (S, Mgh, K) and dasiyEapN , (S, TA,) He impelled it, pushed it, thrust it, or drove it; and particularly so as to remove it from its place; propelled it, repelled it; pushed it, thrust it, or drove it, away, or back. (Z, L, TA.) And dasaEa fulaAnN baqiyoy^ihi Such a one cast forth his vomit. (TA.) And dasaEa alone, (Mgh, TA,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. dasoEN , (K,) He vomited: (K, TA:) or he vomited as much as filled his mouth. (Mgh.) And dasaEa AlbaHoru biAlEanobari The sea collected together the ambergris like foam, or scum, and then cast it aside. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence, also, (as appears from an explanation of dasiyEapN , q. v. infrà,)] dasaEa , aor. , (S, TA,) inf. n. dasoEN , (K,) (tropical:) He gave a large gift. (S, K, TA.) It is said in a trad., (S, TA,) that God will ask the son of Adam on the day of resurrection, (TA,) A^alamo A^ajoEaloka tarobaEu wa tadosaEu Did I not make thee to take the fourth part of the spoil, and to give largely? (S:) and on his answering “ Yes, ” that God will ask, “ Then where is [thy] gratitude for that? ” for the doing thus is the act of the chief. (TA.) ― -b4- And dasaEotu AlqaSoEapa , (Ibn- 'Abbád,) inf. n. dasoEN , (Ibn-'Abbád, K,) I filled the bowl. sourceDefinition: A kind of tree; (S, and so in some copies of the K;) the tree called the Eayovam [or EayovaAm ], (T,) or the gayovaAn [probably a mistranscription for EayovaAm ]: (M:) or the Sin~aAr or SinaAr [i. e. the plane-tree ]; (T, M, K, accord. to different copies; in some copies of the K explained as the SnAr ; in other copies, as a kind of tree, and the SnAr ;) which is most like to it [referring to the Eyvm ]; (T;) or which is most likely; (M;) a kind of great tree, (Mgh,) having neither blossom nor fruit, the leaves of which are serrated (M, Mgh) and wide, resembling those of the vine, (M,) called in Persian SinaAr [or rather JanaAro ]: (Mgh:) in the [Kitáb en-] Nebát, [or Book of Plants, of AHn,] the [ tree called ] SnAr , which is a Persian word that has become current in the language of the Arabs: it grows large and wide: and some say that it is called the EayovaAm : (TT:) accord. to Ibn-El-Kutbee, it is a great, well-known, tree, the leaves of which resemble those of the xirowaE [or palma Christi ], except in being smaller, and are bitter in taste, and astringent; having small blossoms: (TA:) [see also De Sacy's “ Abdallatif, ” p. 80: and his “ Chrest. (A.) -A2- Ald~ulobu [or, as in a copy of the T, accord. to the TT, Ald~alobu ,] A certain race of the blacks, (T, K,) of Es-Sind: [said to be] formed by transposition from Ald~ayobulu . (T.)

sourceDefinition: It (a sword) came forth (S, Msb, K) from its scabbard (Msb) without being drawn: (S, Msb, K:) or became loose, and so came forth, and came forth quickly: (TA:) and in like manner, its scabbard became slit, (S,) or it slit its scabbard, (K,) so that it came forth from it: (S, K:) or it fell from its scabbard, and came forth, without being drawn; (Har p. 386;) and so ↓ dalaqa , inf. n. duluwqN (TA, and Har ubi suprà) and daloqN : (TA:) which also signifies it (a thing) came forth, or issued, from its place of egress quickly: (TA:) and [in like manner] the former verb signifies it (a thing) came forth, or issued, from its place: (A 'Obeyd, K:) it (anything) came forth, or issued, or fell out. (S.) You say, TaEanahu faA@nodalaqato A^aqotaAbu baTonihi He pierced him, and the intestines of his belly came forth. (S.) And Andlqt Alxayolu (S, TA) The horses, or horsemen, came forth, or issued, and hastened: (TA:) and Alxayolu ↓ dalaqati The horses, or horsemen, came forth, or issued, consecutively, or uninterruptedly. (TA.) ― -b2- It (a torrent) came suddenly, or unawares, EalaY qawomK upon a people, or party: (S:) or rushed, or became impelled, or poured forth as though impelled, (K, TA,) EalayohimN upon them; (TA;) as also ↓ tdl~q : (K:) or came, or advanced: (Msb:) and [in like manner] EalayohimN ↓ dalaqa . (JK.) ― -b3- He preceded: (S:) or went before and away. (TA.) You say, Ainodalaqa mino bayoni A^aSoHaAbihi He went before and away from among his companions. (TA.) ― -b4- It was, or became, flabby and prominent; said of a belly; (TA in the present art.;) or, accord. to Naseer, said of the belly of a woman, like AndlE , meaning it became large and flabby. (TA in art. dlE .) ― -b5- It (a door) shut again ( AinoSafaqa ) when opened; would not remain open. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , a Persian word (S, Msb) arabicized, (S, Msb, K,) originally dalahN ; (Msb, K;) [ A species of weasel; accord. to some, app., the common weasel; ] a certain small beast ( duwayob~apN , S, Msb, K) like the sam~uwr [or sable ], (K,) or like the cat, having a long back, [ of the coat ] of which are made fur garments: some say that it is the [ animal called ] Aibon miqoraD [q. v.; and this is agreeable with the description of Kzw, who says that it is “ a certain wild animal, an enemy to pigeons, likened to the cat, which, when it enters a pigeonhouse, leaves not in it anything, and abundant in Egypt; ” a description altogether applicable to the common weasel, now generally called Aibon nimos ]: some say that it resembles the Eiros [or ichneumon ]: some, that it is the Greek ichneumon ( nimos ruwmiY~ ): (Msb in the present art.:) accord. to IF, the [ common ] nimos . (Msb in art. nms .) ― -b2- [Also, from the same Persian original, in post-classical times, but variously pronounced by moderns, dalaqN and ↓ daliqN and daloqN and (now generally by the vulgar) diloqN ; the third being perhaps a contraction of the first, like as $aEorN is of $aEarN , or, as also the fourth, of the second, like as katofN and kitofN are contractions of katifN ; A certain kind of garment; first probably applied to one made of the fur of the animal so called: then applied to a kind of garment formerly worn by the kádees and other 'ulamà and the khateebs of mosques, (see De Sacy's Chrest. Ar., 2nd ed., vol. ii. pp. 267-269,) and by other persons of religious orders: and lastly, to a kind of patched garment worn by many devotees, reputed saints, and darweeshes; also called muraq~aEapN (q. v.) and xiroqapN . It occurs in a piece of post-classical poetry, quoted in p. 45 of the Arabic text of the vol. of the Chrest. above referred to, necessarily with the l quiescent; probably by poetic license, or in conformity with the common vulgar pronunciation.]

definition: A sword that comes forth easily from its scabbard;
sourceDefinition: A sword that comes forth easily from its scabbard; as also ↓ daAliqN (S, K) and ↓ daliqN (IDrd, K) and ↓ daloqaA='u : (K:) [which last is strange, and requires consideration; being fem., whereas sayofN (a sword) is masc.:] all, applied to a sword, signify that comes forth from its scabbard without being drawn; and that which does so is the best of swords. (TA.) [For the pl., see what follows.] ― -b2- gaArapN daluwqN (S, K) and duluqN , (TA,) and xayolN duluqN and ↓ munodaliqapN , (S,) [ Horsemen making a sudden attack and engaging in conflict, or horsemen urging their horses, and simply horsemen, or horses, ] rushing vehemently: (S, K, TA:) duluqN is pl. of daluwqN and of ↓ daAliqN having the same signification. (TA.) -A2- Also, and ↓ daloqaA='u and ↓ diloqimN , with an augmentative m , (S, K,) like as one says daqoEaA='u and diqoEimN , and darodaA='u and dirodimN , (S,) and ↓ diloqamN , (TA,) A she-camel having her teeth broken by old age (S, K) so that she spirts out water [ after drinking ]. (S, TA.) A poet, cited by Yaakoob, says, laA sin~a lahaA ↓ $aArifN daloqaA='u taHomilu AlA^aEobaA='a mino Eahodi A_iramo [ Old and decrepit, having her teeth broken by old age so that water falls from her mouth when she drinks, having no tooth left, carrying burdens from the time of Irem, i. e. Aram the son of Shem the son of Noah]: and ↓ $aArifN daloqaA='u occurs in a trad. as meaning having the teeth broken so that water falls from her mouth when she drinks: (TA:) [but] AZ says that one applies to the she-camel, after what is termed buzuwlN , the epithet $aArifN ; then, Eawozamo ; then, liToliTN then, jaHomari$N ; then, jaEomaA='u ; and then, ↓ diloqimN , when having her teeth ( A^aDoraAs ) fallen out by reason of extreme old age. (S, TA.) [See also art. dlqm .]

[For the pl., see what follows.] ― -b2- gaArapN daluwqN (S, K) and duluqN , (TA,) and xayolN duluqN and ↓ munodaliqapN , (S,) [ Horsemen making a sudden attack and engaging in conflict, or horsemen urging their horses, and simply horsemen, or horses, ] rushing vehemently: (S, K, TA:) duluqN is pl. of daluwqN and of ↓ daAliqN having the same signification. (S, TA.) A poet, cited by Yaakoob, says, laA sin~a lahaA ↓ $aArifN daloqaA='u taHomilu AlA^aEobaA='a mino Eahodi A_iramo [ Old and decrepit, having her teeth broken by old age so that water falls from her mouth when she drinks, having no tooth left, carrying burdens from the time of Irem, i. e. (S, TA.) [See also art. dlqm .]

definition: A constant, or chronic, disease;
sourceDefinition: A constant, or chronic, disease; (S, M, K;) such as infects, or pervades, the person or the inside: or, as some say, any disease, whatever it be. (M.) -A2- Also, (S, M, K,) and ↓ danifN , (S, M, Msb, K,) the latter held by Sb to be a possessive epithet, as he disallowed the verb danifa , (M,) A man having a constant, or chronic, disease; (S, M, Msb, K;) such as infects, or pervades, his person or his inside: or, accord. to some, having any disease: or emaciated by disease so as to be at the point of death: and ↓ mudonafN and ↓ mudonifN signify the same: (M:) or these two signify rendered heavy by disease [ so as to be near to death, or at the point of death: see 1]: (S, Mgh, K:) [and Freytag adds ↓ daAnifN , explained as meaning “ interitui obnoxius, ” as from the Ham; in which I only find (p. 624) authority for danifN , signifying being at the point of death or destruction: ] danafN is used alike as masc. (Fr, T, S, M, K) and fem. (S, M, K) and sing. (Fr, T, S, M, K) and dual (S, M) and pl., (Fr, T, S, M, K,) as though it were an inf. n. used as an epithet: (M:) but if you say ↓ danifN , you vary it for the fem. and dual and pl., (T, * S, M, K,) saying AimoraA^apN danifapN , (S, M,) &c., (S,) i. e., saying also rajulaAni danifaAni , (TA,) and qawomN A^adonaAfN , (M,) or rijaAlN A^adonaAfN : (TA:) and sometimes danafN has a dual form and a pl.; (K;) [i. e.] one may say A^axawaAka danafaAni and A_ixowatuka A^adonaAfu . (Fr, T.) ― -b2- Applied to the sun, it means (tropical:) Near to setting, (M, TA,) and (TA) becoming yellow. (T, TA.) So in the saying (of El-'Ajjáj, T, TA), waAl$~amosu qado kaAdato takuwnu danafaA (tropical:) [ And the sun had almost become near to setting, and to turning yellow ]. (T, M, TA.) [See Q. 2 in art. zHlf .]

(T, K.) ― -b5- naHonu laA najomudu fiY AlHaq~i walaA na*uwbu fiY AlbaATili (tropical:) [ We will not be hard, or niggardly, in the case of truth, or right, nor will we be soft, or easily yielding, in the case of falsity, or wrong ]. (A.) ― -b7- *aAbati Al$~amosu [and ↓ Ast*Abt (as is shown by a phrase mentioned in the L in art. Sxd )] (tropical:) The sun became intensely hot. (M, K.) ― -b10- *Ab Ealayohi AlmaAlu (assumed tropical:) The property became, or proved to be, binding, obligatory, or incumbent, on him to render as a debt. (T.) And *Ab liY Ealayohi Haq~N (tropical:) A right, or due, was, or became, incumbent, or obligatory, on him to render to me, and established against him. (S, A, Mgh, K. *) And *Ab Ealayohi mina AlA^amori ka*aA , inf. n. *awobN , (assumed tropical:) Such a part of the thing, or affair, was, or became, incumbent, or obligatory, on him; like jamada and barada . definition: and ↓ *w~bhu He melted it, dissolved it, rendered it fluid or liquid, liquified it;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ *w~bhu He melted it, dissolved it, rendered it fluid or liquid, liquified it; (S, M, A, K;) or made it to flow. (Msb.) It is said in a prov., (S, TA,) respecting butter, (S,) maA yadoriY A^ayuxoviru A^amo yu*iybu [expl. in art. xvr ]. (S, M, TA.) [See also a verse of Bishr cited below in this paragraph.] ― -b2- [Hence,] the former [as meaning (tropical:) It dissolved him, or emaciated him, ] is said of anxiety, (A, TA,) and grief. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] A*Ab HaAjatahu , and ↓ Ast*AbhA , (tropical:) He matured, and fully accomplished, the object of his want. (A, TA.) And A*AbwA A^amorahumo (assumed tropical:) They put their affair into a good, sound, or right, state. (K.) ― -b4- A*AbwA EalayonaA , (S, M,) or Ealayohimo , (A, K,) inf. n. A_i*aAbapN , (S,) (tropical:) They made an inroad or incursion, or a sudden attack, urging their horses, upon us, or upon them, (S, M, A, K,) and took spoil [ from us, or them, or made, or left, our property, or theirs, to be taken as spoil ]. (A.) Hence the saying of Bishr (S) Ibn-Abee-Kházim, (TA,) fakaAnuw ka*aAti Alqidori lamo tadori A_i*o galato A^atatorukuhaA ma*omuwmapF A^amo tu*iybuhaA (S,) or wakunotumo , (M, TA,) and A^atonoziluhaA , (so in some copies of the S and M,) meaning (assumed tropical:) [ And they were, or and ye were, like her having the cookingpot, not knowing, when it boiled, whether she should leave it, or put it down from the fire, disapproved, or ] whether she should let it be taken as spoil: (S, TA:) so accord. to AZ: (S:) or the meaning is, [ whether she should put it down from the fire,] or make it to remain; i. e. tuvobituhaA , (S, TA,) or tuboqiyhaA ; (AHeyth, TA;) from *aAba liY Ealayohi Haq~N , expl. above, (S, TA,) or from maA *aAba fiY yadiY $aYo'N , also expl. above: (A Heyth, TA:) or, accord. to As, the meaning is, or whether she should melt it; from the prov. mentioned above in this paragraph: (S, TA:) i. e., whether she should leave it in a thick state, [ disapproved, ] or should melt it; fearing that the butter [in the cooking-pot] would spoil. (TA.) [In the TT, for ma*omuwmapF , I find madomuwmapF , which, applied to a cooking-pot, means smeared, or done over, with spleen, &c. See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 626 et seq.]

(S, Sgh, Msb) and and , (Sgh, Msb,) not, as is implied in the K, only, (TA,) [or rather, not only,] inf. n. as above, and rbAEp [most probably rbAEapN ] also, (L,) He took the fourth part of their spoil: (S, Sgh, Msb, K:) i. e., of the spoil of an army: this was done in the Time of Ignorance, but El-Islám reduced it to a fifth part; (K;) as is declared in the Kur viii. 42. (TA.) It is said in a trad., A^alamo A^ajoEaloka tarobaEu watadosaEu , (S, * TA,) mentioned [and explained] in art. dsE , q. v.: the meaning [intended] is, Did I not make thee an obeyed chief? (TA.) ― -b2- And rabaEahumo , (S, Sgh, Msb,) or rabaEa Alv~alaAvapa , (K,) aor. (S, Sgh, Msb, K) and and , (Sgh, Msb, K,) [inf. n., app., raboEN ,] He became the fourth of them; (S, Sgh, Msb;) or, the fourth of the three: (TA:) or he made the three to be four by [ adding to them ] himself. (K.) And rabaEahumo also signifies He made them, by adding himself to them, forty: or, four and forty. (K, * TA.) And He made them (namely thirteen) to be fourteen. (T in art. vlv .) ― -b3- rabaEahu , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. rabEN , (S,) He twisted it (namely a bow-string, S, TA, and a rope, or cord, K, TA) of four twists, or strands. (S, K.) -A2- rabaEat AlA_ibilu , (S, K,) aor. , inf. n. raboEN , (TA,) i. q. ↓ waradati Alr~iboEa ; (S, K;) i. e., The camels, having been kept from the water three days [ counting two portions of days as one of those days ], or four days [ counting two portions of days as two days (for the difference is only verbal)], and three [ whole ] nights, came to the water on the fourth day [ counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first ]. (K.) [See riboEN , below. Another meaning of this phrase will be found later in the present paragraph.] Hence, A^arobaEa AlmariyDa : see 4. (TA.) ― -b2- rabaEato Ealayohi AlHum~aY , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. raboEN ; (Msb;) and Ealayohi ↓ A^arobaEato , (S, Msb, K,) and ↓ A^arobaEatohu , but not rabaEatohu ; (IAar;) or the phrase used by the Arabs is Elyh AlHm~Y ↓ A^arobaEato : (Az, TA:) The fever seized him on one day and left him two days and then came again on the fourth day [ counting the day of the next preceding fit as the first ], (S, Msb, K,) and so on. (Msb.) And rubiEa , and ↓ A^orobiEa , (S, K,) and ↓ A^arobaEa is said to be also used in the same sense, (TA,) He had, or was seized by, a quartan fever; a fever of the kind described above. (S, K, TA.) ― -b3- rabaEa said of a horse, He came fourth in the race. (T, M, L, all in art. vlv .) -A3- rubiEa , said of a man, also signifies He was hit, or hurt, in the A^arobaAE , meaning regions, of his head. (TA.) -A4- rabaEa AlmaTaru AlA^aroDa [ The rain watered the earth and made it to produce herbage: see rabiyEN ]. (TA.) And rubiEati AlA^aroDu The land was watered by the rain in the season called rabiyE . (S.) And rubiEuwA They were rained upon by the rain of the season called rabiyE ; (K, * TA;) similar to qiyZuwA and SiyfuwA : (TA in art. qyZ :) and in like manner, rubiEati AlA_ibilu The camels were rained upon by that rain: and marobaEN may be an inf. n. thereof. (Ham p. 425.) ― -b2- Hence, i. e. from rabaEa AlmaTaruAlA^aroDa , the phrase, rabaEa Alfarasu EalaY qawaAy^imihi (assumed tropical:) The horse sweated in his legs. (TA.) ― -b3- And [hence also,] rabaEahu A@ll~`hu (tropical:) God restored him from a state of poverty to wealth or competence or sufficiency; recovered him from his embarassment or difficulty, or from a state of perdition or destruction. (TA.) -A5- rabaEa Alr~abiyEu , aor. , inf. n. rubuwEN , The [ season called ] rbyE commenced. (TA.) ― -b2- rabaEa biAlmakaAni , (K, TA,) aor. , inf. n. raboEN , (TA,) in its primary acceptation, signifies He remained, abode, or dwelt, in the place in the [ season called ] rabiyE ; (TA;) as also bihi ↓ ArtbE . (S, K.) ― -b3- And hence, (TA,) (tropical:) He remained, abode, or dwell, in the place, (K, TA,) in any circumstances, and at any time; (TA;) he took it as his home. (K.) ― -b4- Also He alighted and abode wherever he would, in the place, in abundance of herbage, and pasturage. (K, * TA.) ― -b5- rabaEati AlA_ibilu , (K,) aor. , inf. n. raboEN , (TA,) The camels fed by themselves in the pasturage, and ate as they pleased, and drank. (K.) [Another meaning of this phrase has been mentioned before.] ― -b6- rabaEa fiY AlmaA='a He (a man, TA) acted according to his own opinion or judgment, or did what he judged fit, with respect to the water. (K.) ― -b7- rabaEa , (K,) aor. , inf. n. raboEN , (TA,) said of a man, also signifies He had, or obtained, abundance of herbage (K, TA) [ arising ] from the [ season, or rain, called ] rabiyE . (TA.) ― -b8- Also, [app. from rabaEa biAlmakaAni in the second of the senses explained above, and if so, tropical, or doubly tropical,] aor. , (assumed tropical:) He (a man, ISk, S) paused, (ISk, S, K,) and acted, or behaved, with deliberation or in a leisurely manner, (K,) and withheld himself. (ISk, S, K.) And [hence,] rabaEa Ealayohi , (K,) inf. n. raboEN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He was affectionate, or pitiful, or compassionate, towards him: (K:) or he acted gently towards him. (TA.) And rabaEa Eanohu (K,) inf. n. raboEN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He restrained himself, refrained, abstained, or desisted, from it. (K.) The phrases AirobaEo EalaY nafosika and ArbE ElY ZaloEika (S, K) and ArbE Ealayoka (K) are from rabaEa in the sense of “ he paused, ” &c., (S, K,) as explained by ISk, (S,) [or in one of the senses following that,] meaning (assumed tropical:) Deal thou gently with thyself; moderate thyself; restrain thyself: (S, TA:) or behave thou with deliberation, or in a leisurely manner: or the second of these phrases may mean continue thou notwithstanding thy slight lameness: or it may be from rabaEa AlHajara , [q. v. infrà,] meaning take thou it, or reach it, notwithstanding thy slight lameness. (TA.) The phrase AirobaEiY binafosiki , or EalaY nafosiki , in the trad. of Subey'ah El-Aslameeyeh, accord. to two different relations, admits of two interpretations: one is, (assumed tropical:) Pause thou, and wait for the completion of the Eid~ap [q. v.] of decease; and this is accord. to the persuasion of those who say that her Ed~p is the more remote of the two periods, which is the persuasion of 'Alee and I'Ab: the second is, from rabaEa Alr~julu signifying “ the man had, or obtained, abundance of herbage, ” and the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) relieve thou thyself, and release thyself from the straitness of the Ed~p , and the evil of thy condition; and this is accord. to the persuasion of those who hold that her Ed~p is the nearer of the two periods; and hence 'Omar said, “ If she bring forth when her husband is on his bier, meaning, not buried, it is allowable for her to marry. ” (TA.) It is also said, in another trad., laA yarobaEu EalaY ZaloEika mano laA yuHozinuhu A^amoruka , i. e. (assumed tropical:) He will not restrain himself, and be patient with thee, whom thy case does not grieve. (TA.) And it is said in a prov., Had~ivi A@moraA^apF Hadiyvayoni faA_ino A^abato faA@robaEo , i. e. (assumed tropical:) Speak thou to a woman twice; and if she refuse, abstain thou: or, accord. to one relation, it is ↓ faA^arobiEo : and accord. to another, faA@robaEohu , i. e., then add; for she is very weak in understanding; if she understand not, then make thou the two speeches to be four: Aboo-Sa'eed says, faA_ino lamo tafohamo baEoda AlA^arobaEapi faA@lomirobaEap , i. e., [ and if she understand not after the four, then ] the stick [is to be used; or, then use thou the stick ]: the prov. applies to the hearing and answering in an evil manner. (TA.) You say also, rabaEato EalaY Eaqoli fulaAnK wakasara fiyhaA ribaAEahu , inf. n. ribaAEapN , (tropical:) [app. She behaved in a gentle and coaxing manner so as to get the better of the reason, or understanding, of such a one, and he sold his houses one after another to expend upon her; ] i. e., he expended upon her all that he possessed, so that he sold his dwellings. (TA. [The w before ksr is not in the TA; but as it seems to have been dropped by inadvertence, I have supplied it.]) -A6- rabaEa AlfaSiylu The young camel widened his stepping, and ran; as also ↓ ArtbE . (TA.) -A7- rabaEa AlHajara , (S, K,) aor. , inf. n. raboEN ; (TA;) and ↓ ArtbEhu ; (S;) He raised, or lifted, the stone, (S, K, TA,) with the hand; (K, TA;) or carried it; (TA;) for trial of strength. (K.) It is said in a trad., mar~a biqawomK yarobaEuwna HajarFA , [ He passed by a company of men raising, &c., a stone ]; and ↓ yarotabiEuwna [signifies the same]; (S;) and ↓ yatarab~aEuwna . (Z, TA.) ― -b2- rabaEa AlHimola , (S, K,) aor. , inf. n. raboEN (TA,) He put the [ staff, or small staff, called ] mirobaEap beneath the load, and took hold of one end of the former, while another took hold of the other end, and then raised it, (S, K,) with the help of his companion, (K,) upon the camel, (S,) or upon the beast. (K,) [See also 3.] -A8- rabiEa biEayo$ihi He (a man) approved his life; was satisfied, or content, with it. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. tarobiyEN , He made it four. (EshSheybánee, K voce waH~adahu .) ― -b2- He made it (a thing) murab~aE ; (S, K;) i. e. he made it to have four portions [or sides or faces or angles &c.]: or he made it of the form of a thing having four legs; or of the form of a quadruped. (TA.) ― -b3- fulaAnN yuval~ivu walaA yurabab~Eu Such a one counts three Khaleefehs, [namely, Aboo-Bekr and 'Omar and 'Othmán,] and [ does not count a fourth, i. e.,] rejects [' Alee,] the fourth. (TA in art. vlv .) ― -b4- rab~aEato She brought forth her fourth offspring. (TA in art. bkr .) ― -b5- rb~E liA@moraA^atihi , or EinodahaA , He remained four nights with his wife: and in like manner the verb is used in relation to any saying or action. (TA voce sab~aEa .) ― -b6- tarobiyEN also signifies [The watering of seed-produce on the fourth day, counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first; ] the watering of seed-produce that is [ next ] after the tavoliyv . (TA.) [You say, rb~E Alz~aroEa He watered the seed-produce on the fourth day, &c.]

sourceDefinition: The party of men (three in number, Msb) became four: (S, Msb, K: [but in the last of these, mentioned after another signification with which it is connected by the conjunction A^awo “ or ”]) or, became forty. (TA.) -A2- A^arobaEato Ealayohi AlHum~aY , and A^arobaEatohu , and A^urobiEa , and A^arobaEa : see rabaEato Elyh AlHm~Y , [which is from rabaEati AlA^ibilu ,] in three places; and rubiEa , in two places. ― -b2- A^agib~uwA fiY EiyaAdapi AlmariyDi waA^arobiEuwA , occurring in a trad., [ Come ye every third day, and every fourth day, counting the day of the next preceding visit as the first, in visiting the sick; or, which is the same, leave ye him one day, and ] leave ye him two days, and come to him on the third day, in visiting the sick; unless he be overcome [by his sickness]: (S, TA:) this is [in like manner] from the water-ing of camels termed riboEN . (TA.) You say also, A^arobaEa AlmariyDa He omitted visiting the sick man two days, and came to him on the third; (O, K;) or, as in the L, and in [some of] the copies of the S, on the fourth [ if counting the day of the next preceding visit as the first ]. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] ArbE Ealayohi Als~aAy^ilu The asker, or beggar, asked, or begged, then went away, and then returned. (Ibn-' Abbád, Sgh, K. *) ― -b4- And ArbE biAlomaroA^api He returned to the mujaAmaEap of the woman without langour: (L:) or ArbE alone, said of a man, multum coïvit. (Ibn-' Abbád, K.) ― -b5- And ArbE Alwirodu , (O, K,) i. e. A^arobaEati AlA_ibilu biAlowirodi , (TA,) The camels quickly returned to watering, (O, * K, * TA,) so that they came to water without any appointed time: (TA:) mentioned by A 'Obeyd as written with the pointed g , which is a mistranscription. (L, TA.) ― -b6- And ArbE said of the water of a well, It [ returned quickly so that it ] became abundant, or copious. (K.) ― -b7- Said of a man, it also signifies ↓ waradato A_ibiluhu ribogFA ; (S;) [meaning] He was, or became, one whose camels came in the state in which they are termed rawaAbiE [i. e. being watered on the fourth day, counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first: from rabaEati AlA_ibilu : whence, likewise, what next follows]. (TA.) ― -b8- ArbE AlA_ibila He watered the camels in the manner termed riboEFA [i. e. on the fourth day, counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first ]. (TA.) ― -b9- This last phrase, also, (K,) or ArbE AlA_ibila EalaY AlmaA='i , (As,) signifies He sent and left the camels to go to the water whenever they pleased. (As, K. *) [Another signification of the verb thus applied will be found below.] -A3- ArbE , (inf. n. A_irobaAEN , S, Msb) He (a sheep or goat, a bull, a solid-hoofed beast, and a camel,) became what is termed rabaAEK : i. e., he shed the tooth called rabaAEiyap : (S, Msb, K:) it is when they do this that the camel and the horse begin to be strong. (TA.) -A4- ArbE Alqawomu The people, or company of men, entered the [ season called ] rabiyE : (S, K:) or [app. a mistake for “ and ”] it has the first of the significations mentioned in this paragraph. (K.) ― -b2- And (so in the S, but in the K “ or ”) The people, or company of men, remained in the place where they had alighted and taken up their abode in the [ season called ] rabiyE , abstaining from seeking after herbage; (S, K, TA;) the rain having been general, they remained where they were, because of the general fertility, not needing to remove for seeking after herbage. (TA.) [See also rabaEa biAlmakaAni .] ― -b3- And The people, or company of men, came to, or arrived at, land of seed-produce and fruitfulness, and water. (TA.) ― -b4- ArbE Algayovu The rain caused the [ herbage called ] rabiyE to grow: (TA:) or the rain confined the people in their ribaAE [or dwellings ] by reason of its abundance. (Msb.) ― -b5- ArbEt AlA^aroDu The earth, or land, produced herbage. (Msb in art. jmd .) ― -b6- ArbE said of a man, (tropical:) He had offspring born to him in the prime of his manhood: (S, TA:) this being likened to the [season called] rabiyE (TA.) ― -b7- ArbE A_ibilahu bimakaAni ka*aA He pastured his camels in the [ season called ] rabiyE in such a place. (S.) ― -b8- ArbEt Aln~aAqapu The she-camel's womb was, or became, closed, ( Aisotagolaqato raHimuhaA ,) so that it did not admit the seminal fluid; (Lth, K;) [perhaps because this commonly takes place in the season called rabiyE , meaning either the spring or the season called rabiyEu AlkalaA^i ; the usual season of the coupling of camels being winter;] as also ↓ ArtbEt . (TA.) -A5- ArbE lahaA biA lkalaAmi He made an abominable request to her; mentioned in the T in art. E*m ; (TA;) meaning saA^alahaA AlwaTo'a fiY Ald~uburi . (TA in art. E*m .) -A6- See also a prov. mentioned in the latter part of the first paragraph.

definition: (S, K) [ He crossed his legs in his sitting;
sourceDefinition: (S, K) [ He crossed his legs in his sitting; i. e. he sat cross-legged; because a person who does so puts himself in such a posture as to occupy nearly a square space;] contr. of javaA and A^aqoEaY . (K.) -A2- trb~E said of a camel, (S, K,) and of a horse, (TA,) He ate the [ herbage called ] rabiyE (S, K, TA,) and in consequence became brisk, lively, or sprightly, (TA,) and fat; (K, TA;) and ↓ ArtbE signifies the same: (S, K:) or trb~EwA and ↓ ArtbEwA signify they lighted on, or found, [ herbage called ] rabiyE : or they lighted on it, or found it, and remained among it: and trb~Et AlA_ibilu bimakaAni ka*aA The camels remained, or abode, in such a place. (TA.) You say also, tarab~aEonaA fiY AlHazoni waAlS~am~aAni We pastured upon the herbs, or leguminous plants, during the winter, upon the rugged ground and the hard and stony ground by the side of sand. (TA.) ― -b2- trb~Et Aln~axiylu The palm-trees had their fruit cut off; (TA, and in some copies of the K;) [because this is done in the autumn, which is called Alr~biyE .] -A3- See also 1, near the end of the paragraph. ― -b2- [Hence,] trb~Et Aln~aAqapu sanaAmFA TawiylFA The she-camel carried a tall hump. (K.)

definition: A place where people remain, abide, or dwell, in the [ season called ] rabiyE ;
sourceDefinition: A place where people remain, abide, or dwell, in the [ season called ] rabiyE ; (K, TA;) as also ↓ marobaEN , (S, Msb, K,) and ↓ murotabaEN : (K, TA:) this is the primary signification: (TA:) and hence, (TA,) (tropical:) a place of alighting or abode, (Sh, S, Msb, K, TA,) of a people, or company of men; (Msb;) a settled place of abode; a place of constant residence; a dwelling; a home; whenever and wherever it be; as also ↓ marobaEN , and ↓ murotabaEN : (TA:) and (assumed tropical:) a house, wherever it be: (S, Mgh, K:) [in Egypt, a range of distinct lodgings over shops or magazines, separate from the shops or magazines, but generally having one common entrance and staircase: ] pl. [of mult.] ribaAEN and rubuwEN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and [of pauc.] A^arobaAEN and A^arobuEN : (S, Msb, K:) and the pl. of ↓ marobaEN is maraAbiEu . (S.) You say, maA A^awosaEa raboEa baniY fulaAnK (tropical:) How ample, or spacious, is the place of alighting, or abode, of the sons of such a one! (S, TA.) ― -b2- Hence, also, (tropical:) The people of a place of alighting or abode; (Sh, Msb, TA;) the people of a house or tent: (Aboo-Málik, TA:) a company of men or people: (K:) a large number: (IB:) pl. as above: (Msb:) rubuwEN signifies the people of places of alighting or abode: (Sh:) and also tribes. (TA.) You say, A^akavara A@ll~`hu raboEaka (tropical:) May God multiply the people of thy house or tent. (TA.) And humu Alyawoma raboEN (tropical:) They now, or to-day, [ are a large number; or] have become many, and have increased. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence, also,] (assumed tropical:) A bier; or a bier with a corpse upon it; syn. naEo$N . definition: The Zimo' [or interval between two water-ings, or keeping from water during that interval, ] which is meant in the phrase rabaEati AlA_ibilu [q.
sourceDefinition: The Zimo' [or interval between two water-ings, or keeping from water during that interval, ] which is meant in the phrase rabaEati AlA_ibilu [q. v.]; (S;) a certain Zimo' of camels, respecting which authors differ: (TA:) it is when camels are kept from the water three days [ counting two portions of days as one of those days ], or four days [ counting two portions of days as two days (for the difference is only verbal)], and three [ whole ] nights, and come to the water on the fourth day [ counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first ]; (K;) or [in other words] their coming to the water one day, and leaving it two days, and then coming to it on the fourth day; or a period of three [ whole ] nights and four days [ of which the first and last are incomplete ]; as is indicated in the K: or, as some say, [but this at variance with common usage,] their being kept from the water four [ nights (for the n. of number is here fem.)], and then coming to it on the fifth [ day (for the n. of number is here masc.)]. (TA.) You say, waradati AlA_ibilu Alr~iboEa : see rabaEati AlA_ibilu . (S, K.) And waradato A_ibiluhu riboEFA : see 4. (S.) And A^aworada AlA_ibila riboEFA i. q. A^arobaEa AlA_ibila [q. v.]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Also, for sayoru riboEK , A journey in which the camels are watered only on the first and fourth days. ] ― -b3- [In like manner,] with respect to fever, it signifies The seizing on one day and leaving two days and then coming again on the fourth day [ counting the day of the next preceding fit as the first ]. (S, K.) [The fever is termed] Hum~aY Alr~iboEi [ The quartan fever; ] the fever that occurs on one day and intermits two days and then comes again on the fourth, and so on. (Msb.) And you say, jaA='atohu AlHum~aY riboEFA , i. q. rabaEato Ealayohi AlHum~aY [q. v.]. (K.) ― -b4- Also The fourth young one, or offspring. (A in art. vlv .)

sourceDefinition: The beasts' collecting of themselves together in the [ season called ] rabiyE : [whence] a a country, or region, is said to be Tay~ibu Alr~iboEapi [ good for the beasts' collecting of themselves together &c.]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, app.,] tarakonaAhumo EalaY riboEatihimo We left them in their former, or first, or original, and right, or good, state, or condition. (TA.) ↓ rabaAEapN , also, and ↓ ribaAEapN , signify An affair, a business, or a concern, in which one continues occupied; or a case, a state, or a condition, in which one abides, or continues; (K, TA;) meaning a former, or first, affair, &c.; (TA;) and only relating to a good state or condition : (Yaakoob, K:) or one's way, course, mode, or manner, of acting, or conduct, or the like : (K:) or one's right, or good, state, or condition, (K, TA,) in which he has been before: (TA:) or his [ tribe such as is termed ] qabiylap : or [the portion thereof which is termed ] his faxi*a : (K:) or ↓ humo EalaY ribaAEatihimo , (S, K,) and ↓ rabaAEatihimo , and ↓ rabaAEihimo , and ↓ rabaEaAtihimo , and ↓ rabiEaAtihimo , and ↓ ribaEatihimo , (K,) means They are in their right, or good, state, or condition : (K, TA:) or they are occupied in their affair, or business, or concern, in which they were occupied before; or they are in their case, or state, or condition, in which they were before : (S, K:) or ↓ ElY rabaEaAtihimo , (S, K,) and ↓ rabiEaAtihimo , (Fr, S, K,) signifies in their right, or good, state, or condition, and in their former, or first, case; or in their right, or good, state, or condition, and occupied in their former, or first, affair, or business, or concern : (S:) or it means in their places of abode. (Th, K.) You say also, gayoru ↓ maAfiY baniY fulaAnK mano yaDobiTu ribaAEatahu fulaAnK i. e. [ There is not among the sons of such a one he who manages thoroughly, or soundly, ] his case, or affair, or business, or concern, in which he is occupied [ except such a one ]. (S.) And [hence,] qawomihi ↓ huwa EalaY ribaAEapi and huwa *uw ribaAEapi qawomihi He is the chief of his people. (Ham p. 313. [See also ribaAEapN below.])

(TA.) ↓ rabaAEapN , also, and ↓ ribaAEapN , signify An affair, a business, or a concern, in which one continues occupied; or a case, a state, or a condition, in which one abides, or continues; (K, TA;) meaning a former, or first, affair, &c.; (TA;) and only relating to a good state or condition : (Yaakoob, K:) or one's way, course, mode, or manner, of acting, or conduct, or the like : (K:) or one's right, or good, state, or condition, (K, TA,) in which he has been before: (TA:) or his [ tribe such as is termed ] qabiylap : or [the portion thereof which is termed ] his faxi*a : (K:) or ↓ humo EalaY ribaAEatihimo , (S, K,) and ↓ rabaAEatihimo , and ↓ rabaAEihimo , and ↓ rabaEaAtihimo , and ↓ rabiEaAtihimo , and ↓ ribaEatihimo , (K,) means They are in their right, or good, state, or condition : (K, TA:) or they are occupied in their affair, or business, or concern, in which they were occupied before; or they are in their case, or state, or condition, in which they were before : (S, K:) or ↓ ElY rabaEaAtihimo , (S, K,) and ↓ rabiEaAtihimo , (Fr, S, K,) signifies in their right, or good, state, or condition, and in their former, or first, case; or in their right, or good, state, or condition, and occupied in their former, or first, affair, or business, or concern : (S:) or it means in their places of abode. (Th, K.) You say also, gayoru ↓ maAfiY baniY fulaAnK mano yaDobiTu ribaAEatahu fulaAnK i. e. [ There is not among the sons of such a one he who manages thoroughly, or soundly, ] his case, or affair, or business, or concern, in which he is occupied [ except such a one ]. (S.) And [hence,] qawomihi ↓ huwa EalaY ribaAEapi and huwa *uw ribaAEapi qawomihi He is the chief of his people. (Ham p. 313. [See also ribaAEapN below.])

definition: Of, or relating to, the rabiyE ;
sourceDefinition: Of, or relating to, the rabiyE ; (S, Msb, K;) i. e., the season so called; [and the rain, and the herbage, so called; ] a rel. n. irregularly formed. (Msb.) ― -b2- Born in the [ season called ] rabiyE ; applied to a young camel: born in the beginning of the breeding-time; [which means the same;] so applied. (TA.) ― -b3- And hence, (TA,) (tropical:) A son born in the prime [or spring-time ] of his father's manhood; (S, * TA;) because the rbyE is the beginning, and the most approved part, of the breeding-time: (TA:) pl. riboEiy~uwna . (S, TA.) Saad Ibn-Málik says, (TA,) A_in~a baniY~a SiboyapN Sayofiy~uwno A^afolaHa mano kaAna lahu riboEiy~uwno [ Verily my sons are boys born in the summer of my age: happy is he who has sons born in the spring-time of his manhood. ] (S, TA.) ― -b4- A palm-tree ( siboTN , i. e. naxolapN ,) of which the fruit ripens in the end of the summer, or hot season; AHn says, because then is the time of the [rain called] wasomiY~ . (TA.) ― -b5- The Arabs say, SarafaAnapN riboEiy~aho tuSoramu biAlS~ayofi watuw^okalu biAl$~atiy~apo [ A hard kind of date that would ripen in the season called rabiyE (meaning autumn ) that is cut in the summer and eaten in the winter-season ]. (TA.) ― -b6- naAqapN riboEiy~apN A she-camel that brings forth [ in the season called rabiyE ,] before others. (TA.) ― -b7- riboEiy~apN [used as a subst., or as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant, for miyrapN riboEiy~apN ,] signifies The miyrap [or corn brought for provision, or the bringing thereof, ] in the beginning of winter : (S, K:) or the miyrap of the [ season called ] rabiyE ; which is the first myrp ; next after. which is the Sayofiy~ap ; and next after this, the dafay^iy~ap ; and next after this, the ramaDiy~ap . (TA.) [See art. myr .] ― -b8- Also, the same, [used in like manner, for EiyrN riboEiy~apN ,] Camels that bring provision of corn in the [ season called ] rabiyE ; or, which means the same, in the beginning of the year : pl. rabaAEiY~u . (TA.) ― -b9- And [used in the same manner, for gazowapN riboEiy~apN ,] A warring, or warring and plundering, expedition in the [ season called ] rabiyE . (TA.) ― -b10- riboEiY~N also signifies (tropical:) The first, or beginning, or former part, of anything; for instance, of youthfulness, or the prime of manhood; and of glory: and riboEiy~apN likewise, the beginning of breeding, and of summer. (TA.) ― -b11- riboEiY~u AlT~iEaAni (assumed tropical:) The sharpest kind of thrusting, or piercing. (Th, TA.)

definition: -A2- It has also a twofold application;
sourceDefinition: : see ruboEN , in two places. -A2- It has also a twofold application; to months and to seasons: and it has a twofold application to months; denoting Two months, (S, Msb, K,) [ next ] after SafarN ; (S, K;) and they say, (Msb,) one should only say, in speaking of them, $ahoru rabiyEK AlA^aw~alu and $ahoru rabiyEK AlA=xirN ; (S, Msb, K;) [but in the margin of the copy of the S which I have here followed, I find it stated that in the handwriting of the author the former is $hr rbyEi AlAwl (with a single kesreh, and with no syll. sign to AlAwl ); and in another copy of the S I find $hru rbyE AlAwli and $ahru rabyE AlA=xir ;] with the addition of $hr : but it is allowable to say also $ahoru rabiyEi AlA^aw~ali and $ahoru rabiyEi AlA=xiri : the word $hr is necessarily added in order to discriminate between the months thus called and the season called rbyE : Az says, the Arabs mention all the months without the word $hr except the two months of rbyE and the month of ramaDaAn : and they say also $ahoraA rabiyEK and A^a$ohuru rabiyEK and $uhuwru rabiyEK : (Msb:) these months were thus called because, when they received this name, they occurred in the season when the earth produced herbage. (Msb in art. jmd .) It has a twofold application also to seasons; Alr~abiyEu AlA^aw~alu being The season in which the truffles and the blossoms come, (S, Msb, K,) and this is [also called] rabiyEu AlkalaA^i [ the rabeea of the herbage, properly called the spring of Arabia ]; (S;) and Alr~abiyEu Alv~aAniY The season in which fruits ripen; (S, Msb, K;) [also called rabiyEu Alv~imaAri ;] but some people call this Alr~abiyEu AlA^aw~alu ; (S, TA;) and the season which follows the winter, and in which the truffles and the blossoms come, they call Alr~abiyEu Alv~aAniY ; but all of them agree that the xariyf [or autumn ] is called Alr~abiyEu : AHn says, the two divisions of the winter [by which he means the half-year commencing at the autumnal equinox ] are called rabiyEaAni ; the former being rabiyEu AlmaA='i waAlA^amoTaAr i [ the rabeea of the water and the rains, in which the rain called AlwasomiY~ , which is termed the first of the rains, commences]; and the second being rabiyEu Aln~abaAti [or rabiyEu AlkalaA^i the rabeea of the herbage ], because the herbage therein attains to its last stage: and he adds, that rabiyEN is applied by the Arabs to the whole winter, [meaning, again, the half-year commencing at the autumnal equinox, ] because of the moisture, or rain: (TA:) or the year consists of six seasons; (so in the K; but in the S, “ and I heard Abu-l-Ghowth say, the Arabs make the year to be six seasons; ”) two months thereof are called Alr~abiyEu AlA^aw~alu ; and two months, SayofN ; and two months, qayoZN ; (S, K;) and two months, rbyE AlvAnY , (so in a copy of the S,) or rabiyEN Alv~AnY , (so in another copy of the S, [but in the margin of this latter, I find it stated that in the handwriting of the author it is rbyEu AlvAnY , without tenween,]) or Alr~abiyEu Alv~aAniY ; (K;) and two months, xariyfN ; and two months, $itaA='N . (S, K.) Az relates, with respect to the seasons and divisions of the year, on the authority of Aboo-Yahyà Ibn-Kibáseh, who possessed very great knowledge thereof, that the year consists of four seasons; namely, Alr~abiyEu AlA^aw~alu , which the vulgar call Alxariyfu [ The autumn ]; then Al$~itaA='u [ the winter ]; then AlS~ayofu , which is Alr~abiyEu AlA=xiru [or Alv~aAniY , i. e. the spring ]; then AlqayoZu [ the summer, or hot season ]: all this is what the Arabs in the desert say: the rbyE which is with the Persians the xryf , he says, commences on the third of A^ayoluwl [ September O. S. ]; and the $itaA=' , on the third of kaAnuwn AlA^aw~al [December O. S.]; and the Syf which is with the Persians the rbyE . on the fifth of A=*aAr [ March O. S. ]; and the qyZ which is with the Persians the Syf , on the fourth of HaziyraAn [June O. S.]: and Aboo-Yahyà adds, the rbyE of the people of El-' Irák agrees with the rbyE of the Persians, which is after the $tA' [or winter ], and which is the season of the flowers, or roses, and is the most temperate of the seasons : the people of El-' Irák, he says, have rain in all the winter, and have abundance of herbage in the xryf , which the Arabs call AlrbyE AlAw~l : and Az says, the quarter of the xryf is called xryf because the fruits are gathered therein; and the Arabs call it rbyE because the first rain [which is called AlwasomiY~ ] falls therein. (TA.) The pl. of rbyE is A^arobiEapN [a pl. of pauc.] and A^arobiEaA='u [a pl. of mult.] (S, Msb, K) and ribaAEN ; (AHn, K;) or the first of these is pl. of rbyE AlklA^ (Fr, Yaakoob, S, Msb, K) and of the rbyE of the months; (Fr, Msb;) but the second is pl. of rbyE in the sense of jadowalN , to be explained below. (Fr, Yaakoob, S, Msb, K.) Hence the phrase in a supplication, mentioned in a trad., Aall~`hum~a A@joEali AlquroA=na rabiyEa qalobiY [ O God, make Thou the Kur-án to be the life, or ease, of my heart ]; because the heart of man becomes lively, or at ease, in the season called rabiyE . (TA.) Hence also, (TA,) A^abuw Alr~abiyEi The hudohud [or hoopoe ]; (K;) because it appears with the [season called] rbyE . (TA.) [See also, respecting the seasons &c., the word zamanN .] ― -b2- Also The rain in the [ season called ] rabyE [as meaning the half-year commencing at the autumnal equinox, (which includes what is really the spring of Arabia, called “ the rabeea of the herbage, ”) accord. to a statement of AHn cited above, and accord. to what is stated on the authority of AZ voce nawo'N ]: (S, K:) or [only, accord. to some,] the rain which is after the wasomiY~ , and after which is [ that called ] the Sayof , and then the Hamiym : or, accord. to AHn, rain whenever it comes : Az says, I have heard the Arabs call thus the first rain falling upon the earth in the days of the xariyf [or autumn ]: (TA:) the pl. [of pauc.] is A^arobiEapN and [of mult.] ribaAEN . (AHn, TA.) [See also, respecting the rains, the word zamanN .] ― -b3- Also Herbage; green herbage which the beasts eat; (TA;) [properly] the herbage that is produced by the first rain in the quarter which is called the rabiyE , and which is commonly called the xariyf [or autumn ], (Msb in art. zmn ,) [ continuing its growth during the winter-quarter, which is also called the rabiyE , and which includes, as stated above, what is really the spring of Arabia, called “ the rabeea of the herbage, ” wherein, as AHn says, the herbage attains to its last stage : it seems generally to mean the spring-herbage, which is earlier or later in different latitudes:] pl. A^aroibEapN . (TA.) [Hence,] a poet says, yadaAka yadN rabiyEu Aln~aAsi fiyhaA wafiY AlA^uxoraY Al$~uhuwru mina AlHaraAmi meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Thy two hands are such that ] one hand has in it the means of the plentiful subsistence of mankind, [ and in the other are the sacred months, i. e.] in the other is [ that which causes ] security, and safeguard, and the preservation of what is to be regarded as sacred and inviolable. (TA.) [Compare Proverbs iii. 16.] ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) A rivulet, or streamlet; (Msb, K;) i. q. jadowalN : (S, Msb, K:) or i. q. nahorN : (Mgh:) or nahorN SagiyrN : (Har p. 402:) (tropical:) a rivulet, or streamlet, that runs to palmtrees : and rabiyEu Als~aAqiY , a subst prefixed to its epithet, occurring in a trad., (assumed tropical:) the river [or rivulet ] that waters seed-produce : (TA:) pl. A^arobiEaA='u (Fr, Yaakoob, S, Msb, K) and riboEaAnN . (TA.) definition: Twisted of four twists, or strands;

definition: The beginning, or commencement, of a thing.
sourceDefinition: The beginning, or commencement, of a thing. (K.) And hence, (K,) ras~u AlHum~aY , and ↓ rasiysuhaA , The beginning, or commencement, (M, A, K,) or first touch, (S,) of fever, (S, M, A, K,) before it becomes vehement, or severe; (A;) i. e., when the person attacked thereby stretches on account of it, and becomes languid in his body, and relaxed, or heavy, sluggish, or torpid, or confused in his intellect: (M, TA:) or the first that a man feels of the touch of fever, before it takes him forcibly, and becomes apparent. definition: A rope, or cord: (S, M, Msb, K:) or [ a halter;
sourceDefinition: A rope, or cord: (S, M, Msb, K:) or [ a halter; i. e.] a rope, or cord, with which a camel [or a horse (see 1)] is led: (TA:) and such of the [ reins, or leading-ropes, termed ] A^azim~ap [pl. of zimaAmN ] as is upon the nose; (M;) [in other words,] such a zimaAm as is upon a nose: (K:) pl. A^irosaAnN (S, M, Msb, K) and A^arosunN , (M, Msb, K,) [both properly pls. of pauc.,] and sometimes they said rusunN ; (Msb;) or, accord. to Sb, it has no other pl. than A^arosaAnN ; (M, Msb;) [but perhaps he meant of pauc., for SM says,] Sb disallowed A^arosunN . (TA.) A poet says, (S,) namely, Ibn-Mukbil, (TA,) hariytN qaSiyru Ei*aAri Alil~jaAmi A^asiylN Tawiylu Ei*aAri Alr~as~no [ Wide-mouthed, short in the cheek-straps of the bridle (or headstall ): smooth and long in the cheek, long in the appertenance of the halter corresponding to the cheek-straps of the bridle or headstall; because this appertenance is longer than are the cheek-straps of the bridle or headstall]. (S, TA.) m~r~a AlS~aEaAliyki biA^arosaAni Alxayoli [ As the passing along of the robbers with the halters of the horses ] is a prov., applied to an affair, or event, that is quick and uninterrupted. (TA.) And one says, ramaY birasanihi EalaY gaAribihi [ He threw his leading-rope upon his withers ], meaning (assumed tropical:) he left his way free, or open, to him; so that God did not withhold him from that which he desired to do. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] rasanu AlbaAziY [ The leash of the hawk ]. (A in art. rwd .) -A2- [The pl.] A^arosaAnN also signifies Rugged and hard tracts of ground. (K, * TA.)

definition: and ↓ raTolN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) the former of which is the better known, (Msb, TA,) or the more chaste, (O, TA,) [but the latter is that which is now in common use,] A certain thing with which...
sourceDefinition: and ↓ raTolN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) the former of which is the better known, (Msb, TA,) or the more chaste, (O, TA,) [but the latter is that which is now in common use,] A certain thing with which one weighs, (Mgh, O, Msb,) or which one uses as a measure of capacity: (Mgh, Msb:) [or rather both: a pound-weight: and a pint-measure: and also a pound of anything: and a pint of anything:] the half of what is termed manFA : (S:) accord. to the standard of Baghdád, twelve ounces; the ounce ( A^uwqiy~ap ) being an A_isotaAr and two thirds of an AstAr ; and the AstAr being four mavaAqiyl and half of a mivoqaAl ; and the mvqAl being a diroham and three sevenths of a drhm ; and the drhm being six dawaAniq ; and the daAniq being eight Hab~aAt and two fifths of a Hab~ap ; so that the rTl is ninety mvAqyl ; i. e. a hundred and twenty-eight daraAhim and four sevenths of a drhm (Msb:) or, accord. to A 'Obeyd, a hundred and twenty-eight drAhm of the weight of seven ( wazona saboEapK [explained voce dirohamN ]): (Mgh:) or twelve ounces; the ounce ( A^uwqiy~ap , i. e. the ounce of the Arabs, TA,) being forty drAhm ; (Mgh, K, TA;) so that the whole is four hundred and eighty drAhm : (Mgh, TA:) this is the Syrian rTl : (TA:) and thus it is, accord. to El-Harbee, in the saying, Als~un~apu fiY Aln~ikaAHi riTolN [meaning The usage of the Prophet in the case of marriage was to give a rTl of silver]: (Mgh, TA:) so says Az in the T: (Mgh:) or, as is [also] said by Az, it is in this instance twelve ounces and a na$~ ; the n$~ being twenty [ drAhm ] so that the whole is five hundred drAhm ; as is related on the authority of 'Áïsheh: but in a trad. 'Omar, twelve ounces, without the mention of the n$~ : accord. to the lawyers, [however,] when the rTl is mentioned without restriction, what is meant thereby is the rTl of Baghdád: (TA:) [ as a measure of capacity, i. e. a pint, ] it is said in the A [&c.] to be the eighth part of the SaAE ; the half of the mud~ ; (TA;) [i. e.] the half of the man~ : and hence applied to one of the vessels of the vintner [app. because it contains a pint]: (Har p. 650:) pl. A^aroTaAlN . (Msb.) -A2- See also raTolN , in two places.

You say, raEayotu AlA_ibila , (S,) or AlmaA$iyapa , (Msb, K,) or Alganama , (MA,) aor. A^aroEaAhaA , (S, Msb,) inf. n. raEoYN (S, MA) [and riEaAyapN , as appears from a phrase mentioned below,] and riEoyapN , (MA,) or this last is a simple subst. from this verb, (K,) I [ kept, or tended, or] pastured, (MA, Msb,) or lead to pasture, (MA,) the camels, (S,) or the cattle, (Msb, K,) or the sheep or goats; (MA;) and ↓ ArEAhA signifies the same as raEaAhaA . (K.) And SinaAEatuhu riEaAyapu AlA_ibili [ His habitual work, or occupation, is the tending, or pasturing, of camels ]. (ISd, K.) And fulaAnN yaroEaY A^abiyhi [ Such a one tends, or pastures, for his father; ] i. e. yaroEaY ganamahu [ tends, or pastures, his father's sheep or goats ]. (S.) ― -b2- And hence, as also riEaAyapN , The keeping or guarding [a person or thing]; being mindful or regardful [of him or it]; and managing or ruling or governing [him or it]. (Er-Rághib, TA.) You say, raEayotuhu I kept, or guarded, him, as a ruler or governor, or a prince or commander, who manages, conducts, orders, or regulates, the affairs of the people: (Msb:) and raEaY AlA^amiyru raEiy~atahu [ The prince ruled, or governed, his subjects ], inf. n. riEaAyapN . (TA.) famaA raEawohaA Haq~a riEaAyatihaA , in the Kur [lvii. 27], means But they did not observe it with its right, or due, observance; were not mindful, watchful, observant, or regardful, of it, in the right, or due, manner of being so. (TA.) You say also, raEayotu Ealayohi Huromatahu , inf. n. riEaAyapN , (ISk, S,) i. e. 1 was mindful, regardful, or observant, of his Hrmp [meaning of what was entitled to reverence, respect, honour, or defence, in his character and appertenances ]: and in like manner, ↓ muraAEaApN AlHuquwqi , mentioned in the S, means The being mindful, regardful, or observant, of rights, or dues. (PS.) (ISd, K.) ― -b2- A^arEayotuhu samoEiY means I made my ear, or ears, to be mindful of his speech: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or I gave ear, hearkened, or listened, to him. (S, Msb.) You say, A^aroEiniY samoEaka , (Msb, K,) and ↓ raAEiniY , i. e. Hearken thou, or listen thou, to my speech. (K.) Hence ↓ raAEinaA in the Kur [ii. 98 and iv. 48]: Akh says that it is of the form faAEilonaA from AlmuraAEaApu , and means A^aroEinaA samoEaka ; the Y having gone away because it is an imperative: he says also that it is read raAEinFA , as an objective complement, from Alr~uEuwnapu : (S: [see art. rEn :]) the reading in Ibn-Mes'ood's copy of the Kur-án is raAEuwnaA . (TA.) You say also, huwa laA yuroEiY A_ilaY qawoli A^aHadK He will not pay any regard, or attention, to the saying of any one. (TA.) ― -b3- And A^aroEayotu Ealayohi I showed mercy to him [ by sparing him, or letting him live, or by pardoning him, or otherwise ]; had mercy on him; pitied, or compassionated, him; syn. A^aboqayotu Ealayohi and taraH~amotuhu . (S, K.) Aboo-Dahbal says, A_ino kaAna h`*aA Als~iHoru minoki falaA turoEiY EalaY~a wajad~idiY siHoraA [app. meaning If this enchantment be from thee, then spare me not, but renew enchantment ]. (TA. You say, AisotaroEayotu maAliYa Alqamara , meaning I left my cattle to pasture without a pastor to take care of them in the night: and [in like manner,] AstrEythu Al$~amosa , in the day. (TA in art. qmr .) ― -b2- AisotaroEayotuhu Al$~aYo'a (S, K *) I asked him, or desired him, to keep or guard, or be mindful of or regardful of, the thing. (K, * TA.) Hence the prov., mani A@sotaroEaY Al*~iy^oba faqado Zalama [ He who asks, or desires, the wolf to keep guard does wrong ]; (S, TA;) i. e. he who trusts in one who is treacherous puts trust in a wrong place. (TA.) [And hence also,] AisotaroEaY AlA^asomaAEa lixuTobatihi He asked, or desired, the ears [meaning the hearers ] to mind his discourse, or oration. (Har p. 361.)

definition: and ↓ maroEFY Pasture, or herbage;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ maroEFY Pasture, or herbage; (S, Mgh, K;) the food of beasts: (Msb:) pl. of the former A^aroEaA='N [meaning kinds, or sorts, of pasture or herbage ]: (K:) and of ↓ the latter maraAEK . (Msb.) It is said in a prov., walaA kaAls~aEodaAni ↓ maroEFY [ Pasture, but not like the sEdAn : see art. sEd ]. (S.) ― -b2- riEoYu AlHamaAmi waAlA_ibili A certain herb, having berries like myrtle-berries, in which is the least degree of sweetness; not injurious to the camels that feed upon it, but poison to [ venomous or noxious reptiles or the like, such as are termed ] hawaAm~ : the decoction thereof blackens the hair. (Ibn-Seenà, book ii. p. 252.)

sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of 1]. You say maA$iyapN raAEiyapN Cattle [ pasturing, or] pasturing by themselves: (Msb:) pl. rawaAEiY [a mistranscription for rawaAEK ]. (TA.) ― -b2- raAEiY AlbusotaAni and AlA^utuni ↓ raAEiyapu are names of Two species of janaAdib [or locusts ]; (K;) the latter mentioned by ISd: Sgh says that the former is a large junodab : and the latter is another species, that does not fly. (TA.) ― -b3- raAEK also signifies A keeper, or guarder, (TA,) or pastor, (Msb,) of cattle: (Msb, TA:) an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant: (TA:) pl. ruEaApN , (S, Msb, TA,) but this is said to be mostly used as pl. of raAEK in another sense as will be shown below, (TA,) and riEaA='N [and app. ruEaA='N (mentioned below)] and ruEoyaAnN ; (S, Msb, TA;) and ruEaApN has a pl., namely, ruEFY . (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence,] Alr~aAEiY is the name of The star [ a ] that is upon the head of AlHaw~aA=' [i. e. Ophiuchus ]: that which is upon the head of AlHAwY [a mistranscription in my MS. for AljaAviY , i. e. Hercules, the star a, ] being called kalobu Alr~aAEiY . (Kzw.) Also The star [ γ ] that is upon the left leg of Cepheus: between whose legs is a star [app. K ] that is called kalobu Alr~aAEiY : (Kzw:) [from their longitudes it seems that these two stars are the same as are meant by what here follows:] Alkalobu [or kalobu Alr~aAEiY ] is a certain star over against Ald~alow [or Aquarius, which latter is ] below; in the path of which is a red [or perhaps another ( A=xar instead of A^aHomar )] star, called Alr~aAEiY . (TA in art. klb .) [And accord. to Freytag, raAEiY AljawozaA='i is the name of A star otherwise called the Foot of Orion: and raAEiY Aln~aEaAy^imi , the name of The star λ in Sagittarius: see Ideler's “ Untersuch. über den Ursprung etc. der Sternnamen, ” to which he refers, pp. 213, 226, for the former; and p. 187 for the latter.] ― -b5- [And hence,] raAEK signifies also A ruler, or governor, (S, K,) or prince, or commander, (Msb,) who manages, conducts, orders, or regulates, the affairs of a people: (Msb, K:) and a ruler, or governor, of himself: (TA:) pl. ruEaApN and ruEoyaAnN , (K,) but it is said that the former is mostly used as meaning rulers, or governors, and the latter as pl. of raAEK in relation to sheep or goats [or the like], (TA,) and riEaA='N and ruEaA='N . (K.) It is said in a trad., kul~ukumo raAEK wakul~ukumo masow^uwlN Eino ↓ raEiy~atihi [ Every one of you is a ruler, or governor, and every one of you shall be questioned respecting those, or that, of which he is ruler or governor ]: such is the man in respect of his family, and in respect of the property of his father; and the servant in respect of the property of his master; and the wife is a raAEiyap in respect of the house, or tent, of her husband: and every one of these shall be questioned respecting his, or her, raEiy~ap . (ElJámi' es-Sagheer of Es-Suyootee.) And one says, kaAlr~aAEiY ↓ layosa AlmaroEiY~u [ The ruled, or governed, is not like the ruler, or governor ]. (S.) ― -b6- In the saying of El-Karkhee, baAEa TayorFA EalaY A^an~ahu raAEK , relating to [carrier-] pigeons, it is from Alr~iEaAyapu signifying AlwafaA='u ; [the saying meaning He sold birds on the condition of their being such as would be faithful to their charge; ] for pigeons in El- 'Irák and Syria are bought for high prices, and sent from distant points with letters of informations, and convey them, and bring back replies to them. (Mgh, JM.)

definition: A certain colour of camels;
sourceDefinition: A certain colour of camels; accord. to A 'Obeyd, a dun colour; i. e. a kNmotap [or brown hue ] so intense as to have in it a blackness: (S:) thus explained by As: (TA:) or, in the colours of camels, brownness; i. e. redness intermixed with blackness: (Kr, TA:) or a colour more dusky, or dingy, than that which is termed zuroqap [q. v.]: (Msb:) or the colour of ashes: (K:) or wuroqapN [which is a colour like that of ashes ] inclining to blackness: or, as some say, duwna Alwuroqapi [ less intense than what is termed warqp ]: (TA:) it sometimes has for its pl. rumukN , with two dammehs. (ISd, TA.)

definition: Of the colour termed rumokapN : (S, Msb, K:) applied to a camel: fem.
sourceDefinition: Of the colour termed rumokapN : (S, Msb, K:) applied to a camel: fem. ramokaA='u . (S, Msb.) The rmkA=' is said by Honeyf-el-Hanátim, who was one of the most skilled of the Arabs respecting camels, to be the most beautiful of she-camels. (TA.) The fem. is also applied, tropically, to a woman. (Th, TA.) ― -b2- A poet says, [applying it to dust,] waAlxayolu tajotaAbu AlgubaAra AlA^aromakaA [ And the horses, or horsemen, cleave the dark brown, or ash-coloured, &c., dust ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And it is said in a trad., [but to what it relates I know not,] The name of the higher, or highest, land is Alr~amokaA='u ; said by IAth to be fem. of AlA^aromaku . (TA.)

definition: -A2- ArAqhu , (Msb in art.
sourceDefinition: : see 2. -A2- ArAqhu , (Msb in art. ryq , and K in that and the present art.,) inf. n. A_iraAqapN , (S in the present art., and so in the K accord. to the TA,) He poured it out, or forth; (S, Msb, K;) namely, water and the like, (S,) or water and blood: (Msb:) and one says also haraAqahu , (Msb, TA,) changing the A^ into h , originally haroyaqahu , like daHorajahu , in measure, (Msb,) said by Lh to be of the dial. of El-Yemen, and afterwards to have spread among Mudar, (TA in art. ryq ,) aor. yuhariyquhu , (Msb, TA,) with fet-h to the h , imperative hariqo , originally haroyiqo , like daHorijo , (Msb,) inf. n. hiraAqapN ; (S and K in art. hrq ;) and A^ahoraAqahu , aor. yuhoriyquhu , (Msb, TA,) with the h quiescent, like yusoTiyEu aor. of A_isoTaAEa ; or, accord. to the T, A^ahoraqotu is wrong as being anomalous; and some say, haraqotuhu , aor. , inf. n. haroqN , as though the h were radical. (Msb.) It is said in a trad., A_in~a A@moraA^apF kaAnato tuharaAqu Ald~imaA='a or tuhoraAqu , the verb being in the pass. form, and the h either meftoohah or quiescent, and AldmA' being in the accus. case as a specificative; [so that the meaning is, Verily a woman used to pour forth with blood; for thrAq is equivalent to tariyqu ; but by rule the specificative should be without the article Al ;] or AldmA' may be in the nom. case, Ald~imaA='u being for dimaAw^uhaA [i. e. her blood used to pour forth ]. (Msb.) ISd says that A^araAqa is judged to be originally A^arowaqa because the medial radical letter of a verb is more commonly w than Y ; and because, when water is poured forth, its clearness appears, and it excites the admiration and approval of its beholder; [to which may be added, also because one says, humA yataraAwaqaAni AlmaA='a ;] though Ks states that raAqa AlmaA='u , aor. yariyqu , signifies The water poured out, or forth: IB says that A^araqotu AlmaA='a is from rAq AlmaA='u , aor. yariyqu , inf. n. rayoqN , signifying the water went to and fro upon the surface of the earth. (TA.) One says also, of a man, ArAq maA='a Zahorihi and haraAqahu and A^ahoraAqahu [meaning He poured forth his seminal fluid ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And A^ariqo Eanoka mina AlZ~ahiyrapi and hariqo meaning (assumed tropical:) Stay thou until the mid-day heat shall have become assuaged, and the air be cool; syn. A^aborido . (IAar, TA in art. fyH .) ― -b3- [See more in art. hrq .]
