definition: [an inf. n. of raAqa , used as an epithet,] Clear; applied to water &c. (IAar, K. [See also raAy^iqN .] ― -b2- [Hence, app., as a subst.,] Pure, or sincere, love. (K.) -A2- [Also, as an epithet...
sourceDefinition: [an inf. n. of raAqa , used as an epithet,] Clear; applied to water &c. (IAar, K. [See also raAy^iqN .] ― -b2- [Hence, app., as a subst.,] Pure, or sincere, love. (K.) -A2- [Also, as an epithet originally an inf. n.,] Inducing wonder, or admiration, and pleasure, or joy; exciting admiration and approval; pleasing, or rejoicing; (IAar, K;) as also ↓ raAy^iqN (JK) and ↓ ray~iqN . (IAar, TA.) And, applied to a horse, Beautiful in make, that induces wonder, or admiration, and pleasure, or joy, in his beholder; excites his admiration and approval; or pleases, or rejoices, him; as also ↓ ray~iqN . (K.) -A3- A horn (JK, S, K, TA) of any horned animal: (TA:) pl. A^arowaAqN . (S, TA.) [Hence,] rawoqu Alfarasi (assumed tropical:) The spear which the horseman extends between the horse's ears: (K:) [for] spears are regarded as the horses' horns. (Ham p. 90.) And daAhiyapN *aAtu rawoqayoni (tropical:) A great calamity or misfortune; (K, TA;) lit. twohorned. (TA.) And HarobN *aAtu rawoqayoni (tropical:) A vehement war. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) [ A ] courageous [ man ], with whom one cannot cope. (K.) ― -b3- (tropical:) A chief (IAar, JK, K) of men. (JK.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) A company, or collective body, (As, O, K,) of people: so in the saying, jaA='anaA rawoqN mino baniY fulaAnK (assumed tropical:) [ A company of the sons of such a one came to us: or, app., a numerous and strong company; for it is added that this is] like the saying raA^osu jamaAEapi Alqawomi [which means “ the numerous and strong company of the collective body of the people ”]. (As, O.) ― -b5- Also syn. with riwaAqN in several senses, as pointed out below: see the latter word in six places. ― -b6- Also (assumed tropical:) The foremost part or portion of rain, and of an army, and of a number of horses or horsemen. (TA.) And (tropical:) The first part of youth; as also ↓ ray~iqN , (S, O, K,) originally rayowiqN , (O, K,) and ↓ rayoqN , (S, O, K,) which is a contraction of ray~iqN : (O:) you say, faEalahu fiY rawoqi $abaAbihi and $bAbh ↓ ray~iqi and $bAbh ↓ rayoqi (tropical:) He did it in the first part of his youth: (S, TA: *) and maDaY mina Al$~abaAbi rawoquhu (tropical:) The first part of youth passed. (TA.) ― -b7- Also (assumed tropical:) The youth [itself] of a man. (TA.) ― -b8- And (assumed tropical:) Life; i. e. the period of. life: whence the saying, A^akala rawoqahu (assumed tropical:) [ He consumed his life; or] he became aged: (K:) or this saying means (assumed tropical:) his life became prolonged so that, or until, his teeth fell out, one after another. (S, O.) ― -b9- (assumed tropical:) A part, or portion, of the night: (S, K:) pl., accord. to IB, A^arowuqN : but accord. to Aboo- 'Amr Esh-Sheybánee, this is pl. of riwaAqN : (TA:) [or the pl. of rawoqN in this sense is A^arowaAqN .] You say, maDaY rawoqN mina All~ayoli (assumed tropical:) A part, or portion, of the night passed. (TA.) And A^arowaAqu All~ayoli means (tropical:) The folds ( A^avonaA=' ) of the darkness of night. (K, TA.) And A^arowaAqu AlEayoni (tropical:) The sides of the eye: so in the saying, A^asobalato A^arowaAqu AlEayoni (tropical:) The sides of the eye shed tears. (O, K, * TA.) ― -b10- Also (assumed tropical:) The body: (K, TA:) and [in like manner the pl.] A^arowaAqN signifies the (assumed tropical:) extremities and body, of a man: (TA:) and his self; (JK, * TA;) as also the singular. (JK, TA.) You say, ramawonaA biA^arowaAqihimo (assumed tropical:) They threw themselves upon us. (TA.) And A^aloqaY EalayonaA A^arowaAqahu (assumed tropical:) He covered us with himself [ by throwing himself upon us ]. (TA.) And ramaAhu biA^arowaAqihi (assumed tropical:) He threw his weight upon him. (TA.) And ramaY biA^arowaAqihi Eani Ald~aAb~api (assumed tropical:) He mounted the beast: and ramaY biA^arowaAqihi Eani Ald~aAb~api (assumed tropical:) He alighted from the beast. (O, K.) And A^aloqaY A^arowaAqahu (assumed tropical:) He remained at rest in a place; (S, O, K;) like as one says, A^aloqaY EaSaAhu : (S, O:) a meaning said in the K to be app. the contr. of what here next follows: but this requires consideration. (TA.) Also (assumed tropical:) He ran vehemently: (A 'Obeyd, S, O, K:) not known, however, to Sh, in this sense; but known to him as meaning (assumed tropical:) he strove, laboured, toiled, or exerted himself, in a thing. (TA.) [Agreeably with this last explanation, it is said that] rawoqN also signifies (assumed tropical:) A man's determination, or resolution; his action; and his purpose, or intention. (K, TA.) And hence the saying, A^aloqaY Ealayohi A^arowaAqahu [meaning (assumed tropical:) He devoted his mind and energy to it, or him ]: (TA:) [or] you say thus, and A^aloqaY Ealayohi $araA$irahu , meaning his loving it, or him, ( A^ano yuHib~ahu ,) vehemently [i. e. (assumed tropical:) he loved it, or him, vehemently; agreeably with explanations of the saying AlqY Elyh $rA$rh in art. $r , q. v.]. (Thus in the JM. [In my two copies of the S, and in the O and K, and hence in the TA, in the places of Ealayohi and yuHib~ahu we find Ealayoka and tuHib~ahu ; evidently mistranscriptions which have been copied by one lexicographer after another without due consideration: or, if we read Ealayoka , we should read yuHib~aka ; for in this case the meaning of the saying would certainly be he loved thee vehemently. Freytag, misled by the reading tuHib~ahu in the S and K, renders AlqY Elyk ArwAqh as meaning Magno amore erga ipsum te accendit. Golius gives, in its place, Drb AwrAqh Elyh (for ArwAqh ), as meaning Valde amavit eum. ]) ― -b11- You say also, A^aloqati Als~aHaAbapu A^arowaAqahaA , (JK, S, O, K,) or Alqt AlsHAbp EalaY AlA^aroDi ArwAqhA , (TA,) (tropical:) The cloud cast down its rain, and its vehement rain consisting of large drops, (S, O, K, TA,) upon the earth: (TA:) or persevered with rain, and remained stationary upon the land: (JK, TA:) or A^aloqati Als~amaA='u biA^arowaAqihaA The sky cast down all the water that was in it: (IAmb, O, TA:) or this saying, (O, TA,) or the former, (K,) means cast down its clear waters; (O, K, TA;) from raAqa AlmaA='u signifying “ the water was, or became, clear: ” but IAmb deems this improbable, because the Arabs did not say maA='N rawoqN and maAA=ni rawoqaAni and A^amowaAhN A^arowaAqN : (O, TA:) [i. e. they said rawoqN only, in all cases when they used it as an epithet meaning “ clear, ” because it is originally an inf. n., like EadolN &c.:] or, as some say, by bArwAqhA is meant its waters rendered heavy by the clouds: and one says, A^aroxati Als~amaA='u A^arowaAqahaA and EazaAliyhaA (assumed tropical:) [ The sky loosed, or let down, its spouts; the clouds being likened to leathern water-bags]: (TA:) [for] rawoqu Als~aHaAbi means (assumed tropical:) The masiyl [or channel by which flows the water ] of the clouds. (TA in another part of the art. [See also riwaAqN , as used in relation to clouds.]) -A4- rawoqN also signifies A substitute for a thing, (O, K,) accord. to [the JK and] Ibn-'Abbád. (O.) -A5- And Alr~awoqu means The breathing of [i. e. in ] the agony of death ( nafosu Aln~azoEi ). (O, K, TA. [In the CK and in my MS. copy of the K, nafosu Aln~azoEi , which means the agony of death itself. ])

(TA.) And ramaY biA^arowaAqihi Eani Ald~aAb~api (assumed tropical:) He mounted the beast: and ramaY biA^arowaAqihi Eani Ald~aAb~api (assumed tropical:) He alighted from the beast. (O, K.) And A^aloqaY A^arowaAqahu (assumed tropical:) He remained at rest in a place; (S, O, K;) like as one says, A^aloqaY EaSaAhu : (S, O:) a meaning said in the K to be app. the contr. of what here next follows: but this requires consideration. (TA.) Also (assumed tropical:) He ran vehemently: (A 'Obeyd, S, O, K:) not known, however, to Sh, in this sense; but known to him as meaning (assumed tropical:) he strove, laboured, toiled, or exerted himself, in a thing. (TA.) [Agreeably with this last explanation, it is said that] rawoqN also signifies (assumed tropical:) A man's determination, or resolution; his action; and his purpose, or intention. (K, TA.) And hence the saying, A^aloqaY Ealayohi A^arowaAqahu [meaning (assumed tropical:) He devoted his mind and energy to it, or him ]: (TA:) [or] you say thus, and A^aloqaY Ealayohi $araA$irahu , meaning his loving it, or him, ( A^ano yuHib~ahu ,) vehemently [i. e. (assumed tropical:) he loved it, or him, vehemently; agreeably with explanations of the saying AlqY Elyh $rA$rh in art. $r , q. v.]. (Thus in the JM. [In my two copies of the S, and in the O and K, and hence in the TA, in the places of Ealayohi and yuHib~ahu we find Ealayoka and tuHib~ahu ; evidently mistranscriptions which have been copied by one lexicographer after another without due consideration: or, if we read Ealayoka , we should read yuHib~aka ; for in this case the meaning of the saying would certainly be he loved thee vehemently. Freytag, misled by the reading tuHib~ahu in the S and K, renders AlqY Elyk ArwAqh as meaning Magno amore erga ipsum te accendit. Golius gives, in its place, Drb AwrAqh Elyh (for ArwAqh ), as meaning Valde amavit eum. ]) ― -b11- You say also, A^aloqati Als~aHaAbapu A^arowaAqahaA , (JK, S, O, K,) or Alqt AlsHAbp EalaY AlA^aroDi ArwAqhA , (TA,) (tropical:) The cloud cast down its rain, and its vehement rain consisting of large drops, (S, O, K, TA,) upon the earth: (TA:) or persevered with rain, and remained stationary upon the land: (JK, TA:) or A^aloqati Als~amaA='u biA^arowaAqihaA The sky cast down all the water that was in it: (IAmb, O, TA:) or this saying, (O, TA,) or the former, (K,) means cast down its clear waters; (O, K, TA;) from raAqa AlmaA='u signifying “ the water was, or became, clear: ” but IAmb deems this improbable, because the Arabs did not say maA='N rawoqN and maAA=ni rawoqaAni and A^amowaAhN A^arowaAqN : (O, TA:) [i. e. they said rawoqN only, in all cases when they used it as an epithet meaning “ clear, ” because it is originally an inf. n., like EadolN &c.:] or, as some say, by bArwAqhA is meant its waters rendered heavy by the clouds: and one says, A^aroxati Als~amaA='u A^arowaAqahaA and EazaAliyhaA (assumed tropical:) [ The sky loosed, or let down, its spouts; the clouds being likened to leathern water-bags]: (TA:) [for] rawoqu Als~aHaAbi means (assumed tropical:) The masiyl [or channel by which flows the water ] of the clouds. (TA in another part of the art. [See also riwaAqN , as used in relation to clouds.]) -A4- rawoqN also signifies A substitute for a thing, (O, K,) accord. to [the JK and] Ibn-'Abbád. (O.) -A5- And Alr~awoqu means The breathing of [i. e. in ] the agony of death ( nafosu Aln~azoEi ). (O, K, TA. [In the CK and in my MS. copy of the K, nafosu Aln~azoEi , which means the agony of death itself. ])

definition: (Lth, S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (Lth, S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ ruwaAqN (MA, K) and ↓ rawaAqN (MA) A bayot [or tent ] like the fusoTaAT [q. v.], (Lth, JK, O, Msb, K,) supported upon one pole in the middle thereof; (Lth, O, Msb;) as also ↓ rawoqN ; (K, * TA; expl. in the former as signifying a fusoTaAT ; and its pl. A^arowaAqN is expl. in the S as signifying fasaATiyTu ;) accord. to Lth: (TA:) or a roof in the front, or fore part, of a bayot [or tent ]; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ rawoqN : (S:) or a curtain that is extended below the roof; as also ↓ rawoqN ; which latter is expl. in the K as signifying simply a curtain: (TA:) or the riwaAq of a bayot [or tent] is the curtain of the front, or fore part, thereof, extending from the top thereof to the ground: (AZ, TA:) a [ piece of cloth such as is called ] kisaA=' let down upon the front, or fore part, of a bayot , from the top thereof to the ground: (Mgh:) ↓ rawoqN signifies the same as riwaAqN : (K:) and each signifies the $uq~ap [or oblong piece of cloth ] that is beneath the upper, or uppermost, $uq~ap of a bayot [or tent]: (Az, O, K:) or sometimes the rwAq is one such piece of cloth, and sometimes of two such pieces, and sometimes of three: (TA:) and, (Msb,) or as some say, (Mgh, TA,) riwaAqN signifies (assumed tropical:) the front, or fore part, of a bayot [or tent]; (Z, Mgh, Msb, TA;) as also ↓ rawoqN ; (JK, Z, K;) its hinder part being called its kifaA=' , and its two sides being called its xaAlifataAni ; (TA;) whence the saying, bayotihi ↓ qaEaduwA fiY rawoqi and riwaAqi bayotihi , i. e. (tropical:) [ They sat in ] the front or fore part [ of his tent ]: (Z, TA:) and ↓ rawoqN also signifies a tent; as in the saying, Daraba rawoqahu [ He pitched his tent ]: (S:) and [hence] the place of the huntsman [ in which he conceals himself to lie in wait ]; (K;) as being likened to the rwAq : (TA:) and rwAq signifies also a place that affords shelter in rain: (MA:) [and a portico; and particularly such as surrounds the court of a mosque; (see sud~apN ;) in some of the large collegiate mosques, as, for instance, in the mosque El-Azhar, in Cairo, divided into a number of distinct apartments for students of different provinces or countries, each of which apartments by itself is termed a riwaAq :] the pl. of rwAq is A^arowiqapN and ruwqN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) the former a pl. of pauc. and the latter of mult. (S, O.) ― -b2- [Hence, Alr~iwaAqu mina Als~aHaAbi , expl. in the TA as meaning mA dAr minohu kariwaAqi Albayoti : but dAr is here evidently a mistranscription for kaAna ; and the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) The part, of the clouds, that resembles the rwAq of the tent. See also rawoqu Als~aHaAbi , near the end of the paragraph commencing with rawoqN .] ― -b3- [Hence also,] riwaAqu All~ayoli (assumed tropical:) [ The curtain of night: and] the first part of night; and the greater, or main, part thereof. (ISd, K. [It is implied in the latter that one says also in this instance and in the next ruwaAq .]) You say, of night, mad~a riwaAqa Zulomatihi (assumed tropical:) [ It extended the curtain of its darkness ]: (S, Msb:) and A^aloqaY A^arowiqatahu (assumed tropical:) [ It let fall its curtains ]. (S.) [See also an ex. in a verse cited voce murim~N , in art. rm .] ― -b4- And riwaAqu AlEayoni (assumed tropical:) The eyebrow. (JK, K.) -A2- riwaAqu [imperfectly decl. as being a proper name and of the fem. gender, though it is implied in the K that it is Alr~iwaAqu and Alr~uwaAqu ,] is a name for The ewe, (O, K,) by which she is called to be milked, by the cry riwaAq riwaAq ; (O;) but not unless she be ↓ rawoqaA=' [app., if not a mistranscription for waroqaA=' , formed from this latter by transposition, and thus meaning dusky: see A^arowaqu ]. (O, K.)

definition: A clarifier, or strainer, (S, Msb, K,) syn.
sourceDefinition: A clarifier, or strainer, (S, Msb, K,) syn. miSofaApN , (S, K,) for wine or beverage: (S:) the naAjuwd [q. v.] with which wine, or beverage, is cleared, (Lth, JK, K, TA,) without pressing, or expressing: (TA:) and (sometimes, S) the [ kind of wine-vessel called ] baATiyap . (S, K.) Accord. to IAar, (O, TA,) who is said by Sh to differ herein from all others, (TA,) Alr~aAwuwqu signifies also The kaA^os [or drinking-cup, or cup of wine, ] itself. (O, K, TA.) sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. zaHofN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and zuHuwfN (Msb, K) and zaHafaAnN , (K,) He, or it, (an army, Mgh, Msb, * or a company of men, Msb) walked, marched, or went on foot, A_ilayohi [ to him, or it ]; (S, K;) and [generally] did so by little and little; (accord. to an explanation of zaHofN in the TA;) crept, or crawled, along; or went, or walked, leisurely, or gently: (Mgh:) and ↓ tzH~f A_ilayohi , (S, K,) as also ↓ AzdHf , (K,) i. q. tm$~Y , (S, K,) i. e. he walked [ with slow steps, or] heavily, with an effort, to him, or it: (TK:) and mi$oyapu zaHafaAnK means a gait in which is a heaviness of motion. (TA.) One says of a child, before he walks, (S, Msb, K,) or before he stands, (T, TA,) yazoHafu [ He drags himself along ] (S, Msb, K) EalaY AlA^aroDi [ upon the ground ], or EalaY A@sotihi [ upon his posteriors ]: (TA:) or zaHafa alone, said of a child, he went along slowly, by little and little, upon his posteriors: (Bd in viii. 15:) and to the zaHof of children is likened the marching of two bodies of men going to meet each other for fight, when each of them marches gently, or leisurely, towards the other, before they draw near together to smite each other: and one says likewise of a child, before he walks, EalaY ↓ yatazaH~afu AlA^aroDi , or, as in the T, EalaY baTonihi , i. e. he drags himself along [ upon the ground, or upon his belly ]. (TA.) ― -b2- zaHafa Ald~abaA [ The young locusts not yet winged ] went on, or forwards: (S, O, K:) ma$aY in this explanation in the K should be maDaY , as in the S and A. (TA.) ― -b3- zaHafa said of an arrow, (assumed tropical:) It fell short of the butt, and then slid along to it. (S, * Msb.) ― -b4- Also, said of a camel, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. zaHofN and zuHuwfN , and zaHafaAnN , (TA,) He became fatigued, and dragged his foot, or the extremity of his foot; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ A^azoHafu : (S, Mgh, Msb:) or this latter signifies he (a camel) became fatigued, (K, TA,) and stood still with his master: and raAHilatuhu mina AlA_iEoyaA='i ↓ A^azoHafato His saddle-camel stood still from fatigue: or, accord. to El-Khattábee, correctly, A^uzoHifato Ealayohi : (TA:) or this is a mistake, occurring in the Fáïk; and it is correctly with fet-h: (Mgh:) and accord. to the T, zaHafa signifies he (a camel) became fatigued, so that he stood still with his master: (TA:) or, as some say, zaHafa said of one walking, or marching, [i. e., of a man and of a beast,] (Msb, TA,) accord. to AZ, whether fat or lean, (Msb,) aor. , inf. n. zaHofN and zaHafaAnN , or, as AZ says, zaHofN and zuHuwfN , (TA,) signifies, (Msb,) or signifies also, (TA,) he became fatigued, (Msb, TA,) in walking, or marching. (TA.) ― -b5- And zaHafa Al$~ajaru (tropical:) The trees became in a state of gentle motion, by the influence of the wind. (TA.) -A2- zaHafa Al$~aYo'a , inf. n. zaHofN , He dragged the thing along gently. (TA.)

definition: [ He became furnished, or he furnished himself, with provisions for travelling or for a fixed residence;
sourceDefinition: [ He became furnished, or he furnished himself, with provisions for travelling or for a fixed residence; ] he took, or prepared, for himself provisions (S, * KL, TA) for travelling or for a fixed residence: (TA: [Golius makes it to be trans. by means of bi as on the authority of the KL; in which the only explanation, as that of the inf. n., is tw$h brGrftn :]) and he chose a thing as zaAd [or provision ] for himself. (Har p. 92.) You say, tazaw~ada min~aA fulaAnN [ Such a one was furnished, or such a one furnished himself, with provisions from us ]. (A.) And tzw~d lisafarihi [ He was furnished, or he furnished himself, with provisions for his journey ]. (Msb.) And see another ex. voce zaAdN . You say also, tazaw~ada mina Ald~unoyaA liloA=xirapi (tropical:) [ Take thou provisions from the present world, i. e. make thou provision in it, for the world to come ]. (A, TA.) And tazaw~ada mina AlA^amiyri kitaAbFA liEaAmilihi (tropical:) [ He provided himself with a letter from the commander, or governor, or prince, to his prefect ]. (A, TA.) And tazaw~ada min~iY TaEonapF bayona A^u*unayohi (tropical:) [ He got from me a stab, or spear-wound, or the like, between his ears ]. (A, TA.)

definition: Provisions, or a stock of provisions, for travelling (S, L, Msb, TA) and for a fixed residence: (L, TA:) pl.
sourceDefinition: Provisions, or a stock of provisions, for travelling (S, L, Msb, TA) and for a fixed residence: (L, TA:) pl. A^azowaAdN (L, Msb) and A^azowidapN ; the latter anomalous. (L.) ― -b2- And hence, as being likened thereto, (tropical:) Any deed, or acquirement, whether good or evil, whereby one becomes changed in state, or condition; (L;) [or rather, whereby one provides for a change of state, or condition, like as a traveller provides for a journey. ] It is said in the Kur [ii. 193], faA_in~a xayora Alz~aAdi ↓ watazaw~aduwA Alt~aqowaY (L) meaning, [as is implied in the L, (tropical:) And make ye provision; but verily the best acquirement whereby to provide for a change of state, or condition, is fear of God, or piety: or the meaning is] and prepare ye provisions for your journey; and verily the best provision is that whereby one provides against begging from others, &c. (Jel.) ― -b3- [It is also said to be used as meaning (assumed tropical:) Salutation and the returning of a greeting. (De Sacy's Chrest. Ar., ii. 415, q. v.)]

(TA.) ― -b2- [Hence also] sabagato quSayoraY Alfarasi The qSyry [app. here meaning the rib next the flank ] of the horse was of full length. (TA.) ― -b4- And sabagati Aln~iEomapu , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. as above, (S, Msb,) (tropical:) The benefit, or boon, was, or became, ample. (S, Msb, K, TA.) One says, AlHamodu lil~`hi EalaY subuwgi Aln~iEomapi Praise be to God for the ampleness of the benefit, or boon. (TA.) ― -b5- And sabaga libaladihi (assumed tropical:) He tended towards, and reached, his town, or country; (AA, * K;) inf. n. as above. (TA.)

definition: (JK, S, K) and tasobagapN and ↓ tasobigN and tasobagN , (JK, K,) the first of which is the most chaste, (TA,) I.
sourceDefinition: (JK, S, K) and tasobagapN and ↓ tasobigN and tasobagN , (JK, K,) the first of which is the most chaste, (TA,) I. q. migofarN [q. v.]: (JK:) or a portion of the mail of the coat of mail, that is conjoined to the helmet, and protects the neck: (JK, S, K:) for the helmet becomes lengthened ( tasobugu ) thereby; and but for it, there would be between it and the opening at the neck of the coat of mail an intervening space: (S:) or the mail composing the raforaf of the helmet, at the bottom thereof, with which the man protects his neck, and which is also called the migofar : or, accord. to “ the Book of the Coat of Mail and the Helmet, ” by AO, the raforaf of the helmet is other than its tasobigap ; for he says that, of helmets, there is that which has a raforaf , [consisting of] rings [or mail] encompassing the bottom thereof, so as to surround the back and other parts of the neck, and the two cheeks, and to reach to the maHojiraAni [q. v.] of the two eyes; and he afterwards says, but when it [the helmet] is not of plate, or expanded metal, but is [ a head-covering ] of mail, it is called migofarN and gifaArapN and tasobigapN : (TA:) [the pl. is tasaAbigu :] and the helmet [that has a tasobigap attached to it, accord. to those who mean by this term the mail attached to the bottom thereof,] is called ↓ saAbigN : (JK:) or, accord. to As, one says bayoDapN lahaA saAbigN , (S,) or lahaA tasaAbigu . sourceDefinition: : see sijonN . ― -b2- [In the Kur lxxxiii. 7,] A certain place in which is the record [ of the deeds ] of the wicked; (S, L, K;) or, as I 'Ab says, in which are their registers: AO says, it is of the measure fiE~iylN from Als~ijonu , like Alfis~iyqu from Alfisoqu : (S, L:) or a certain valley in Hell: or a certain stone, [or rock, ] (L, K,) beneath, (L,) or in, (K,) the seventh earth: (L, K:) [these explanations are given by those who hold that maA sij~iynN in the next verse is for maA kitaAbu sij~iynK :] or it there means a register comprising the deeds of the wicked, (Bd, Jel, *) of the jinn, or genii, and of mankind, (Bd,) or of the devils and the unbelievers: (Jel:) or mA sj~yn in the next verse is for mA ktAb sj~yn , and the meaning is the place, (Bd, Jel,) which is beneath the seventh earth, the abode of Iblees and his forces: (Jel:) IAth says, it occurs in a trad. with the article Al ; and without that article it is a proper name for the fire [ of Hell ], and hence the mention of it in the Kur lxxxiii. 7. (L.) [See also sij~iylN .] -A2- Also Anything hard: (L:) and hard, vehement, or severe; (S, L, K;) applied to a beating. (S, L.) ― -b2- And Continuing, lasting, or everlasting; syn. daAy^imN ; (L, K;) as also sij~iylN : so accord. to El-Muärrij. (L. [See, again, sij~iylN .]) -A3- And i. q. EalaAniyap : (L, K:) so in the saying, Eamila *`lika sij~iynFA [ He did that openly, or publicly ]. (L.) -A4- Also Palm-trees ( naxol ) such as are termed silotiyn (As, L, K) in the dial. of the people of El-Bahreyn; (As, L;) [app. meaning that the latter word is of that dial.; for it is said that] the Arabs [app. the Arabs in general] say sij~iyn in the place of silotiyn , which is not Arabic: (L:) the palm-trees thus termed are such as have trenches dug at their feet to conduct the water to them when it has not reached to them. (L, and K in art. sltn .)

definition: , aor , (K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , aor , (K,) inf. n. saHolN , (S, TA,) He pared it; peeled it; or stripped off, scraped off, rubbed off, abraded, or otherwise removed, its outer covering or integument, or superficial part: or he pared, peeled, or stripped, it off: (S, K, TA:) this is the primary signification: (S:) and he filed it. (TA.) It is said in a trad., fajaEalato tasoHaluhaA lahu , i. e. And she betook herself to paring off from it the flesh that was upon it for him: or, as some relate it, tasoHaAhaA , which means the same. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Alr~iyaAHu tasoHalu AlA^aroDa (tropical:) The winds strip off what is upon the earth, (K, TA,) or the surface of the earth. (TA: and the like is said in the S.) ― -b3- And saHalahu miAy^apa sawoTK , (S, K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He struck him a hundred lashes, or strokes of a whip, (S, K, TA,) and pared off his skin, (TA,) or as though he pared off his skin. (S.) ― -b4- And saHala fulaAnN (assumed tropical:) Such a one reviled [another], and blamed [him: like as you say, qa$ara biAll~isaAni ]. (K. [See misoHalN as meaning “ a tongue. ”]) One says, wajada Aln~aAsa yasoHaluwnahu (assumed tropical:) He found the people reviling him, (K, TA,) and blaming him, and speaking evil of him behind his back, or in his absence, or otherwise. (TA.) ― -b5- saHalotu Al$~aYo'a i. q. saHaqotuhu [ I bruised, brayed, or pounded, the thing: or pulverized it: &c.]. (S.) ― -b6- saHala Alv~iyaAba He washed the clothes, [ beating them in doing so, ] and removed [or rubbed off ] from them the soils. (TA.) ― -b7- saHalotu Ald~araAhima I made the pieces of money smooth. (S.) Accord. to ISk, I poured out, or forth, the pieces of money; as though I rubbed them, one against another. (S.) [Or] saHala Ald~araAhima , aor. as above, (K,) and so the inf. n., (TA,) i. q. AinotaqadahaA [which signifies He picked the pieces of money, separating the good from the bad; or examined them to do so: and also he received the pieces of money ]. (K.) And saHalotuhu miAy^apa dirohamK I paid him a hundred dirhems in ready money. (S.) [Or] saHala Algariyma miAy^apa dirohamK He paid the creditor a hundred dirhems in ready money. (K.) -A2- saHala Alv~awoba , (K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) He wove the garment, or piece of cloth, of spun thread not formed of two twists: (K:) or he wove it without having twisted its warp [i. e. without having made its warp to consist of threads of two twists ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And saHalotu AlHabola I formed the rope of a single twist; (S, TA;) and accord. to some, one says also ↓ A^asoHalotuhu , but the former is the chaste expression. (TA.) [Hence,] suHilato mariyrapu fulaAnK is said of one whose strength has become weakened; meaning (tropical:) His well-twisted rope, or rope of two twists, has become a rope of a single twist. (TA.) ― -b3- saHala AlqiraA='apa , inf. n. saHolN , He performed the reading, or recitation, in consecutive portions, continuously: and some relate it with j [i. e. sajala ]: saHolN is syn. with sarodN , signifying the making [a thing] to be consecutive in its parts, or portions. (TA.) ― -b4- baAtati Als~amaA='u tasoHalu layolatahaA (tropical:) The sky continued pouring forth water that night: (As, S, TA:) inf. n. as above. (TA.) ― -b5- And saHalati AlEayonu , (K,) aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. saHolN and suHuwlN , (tropical:) The eye wept; (K;) poured forth tears. (TA.) -A3- saHala , aor. (S, K) and , (K,) inf. n. saHiylN and suHaAlN , (S, * K, [the latter inf. n. erroneously written in the CK siHAl ,]) He (an ass) made a rolling sound in his chest; whence the ass of the desert is called ↓ misoHalN : (S: [see also saHiylN below:]) he (a mule, K, and an ass, TA) brayed. (K, TA.)

sourceDefinition: A white garment or piece of cloth: (Msb:) or a white, thin garment or piece of cloth: (TA:) or a white garment or piece o cloth, of cotton, (S, K,) of those of El-Yemen: (S:) pl [of mult.] suHuwlN and suHulN (S, Msb, K) and [of pauc.] A^asoHaAlN . (K. [See also viyaAbN saHuwliy~apN , below.]) ― -b2- And A garment, or piece of cloth, of which the spun thread is not composed of two twists; as also ↓ saHiylN : (K:) or, as some say, the latter is not applied to a garment, or piece of cloth; but to thread, in a sense expl. below: (TA:) or, accord. to Aboo-Nasr, it (the latter) is applied also to a garment, or piece of cloth, of which the spun thread is a single yarn: the muboram is that of which the spun thread is twisted of two yarns: and the mitoA=m is that of which the warp and the woof are each of two yarns. (S, TA.) ― -b3- Also, (K,) or ↓ saHiylN , (S,) or both, (TA,) A rope that is of a single strand; (K, TA;) or the latter, a rope that is twisted of one twist, like as the tailor twists his thread: the muboram is that which is composed of two twists twisted together into one: (Aboo-Nasr, S, TA:) such a rope is also termed ↓ masoHuwlN ; but not ↓ musoHalN , for the sake of [analogy to] muboramN ; (S, TA;) or the latter epithet is sometimes applied to it: (S, TA: [see also misoHalN :]) ↓ saHiylN likewise signifies thread not twisted; (Aboo-Nasr, S, TA;) or spun thread not composed of two twists. (TA.) -A2- Also Ready money: (S, TA:) an inf. n. used as a subst. [properly so termed]. (TA.)

definition: An implement for cutting, hewing, or paring, (Lth, K, TA,) of wood.
sourceDefinition: An implement for cutting, hewing, or paring, (Lth, K, TA,) of wood. (Lth, TA.) ― -b2- A file. (S, K.) ― -b3- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) The tongue, in an absolute sense: (K, TA:) [see miboradN : or as being an instrument of reviling,] from saHala “ he reviled. ” (TA.) J explains AlmisoHalu as meaning All~isaAnu AlxaTiybu , (K, TA,) and MF defends this as meaning The tongue that speaks well: (TA:) [and it is said in the Ham p. 683 to signify All~isaAnu Al~a*iY laA yataA^at~aY lilokalaAmi , app. meaning the tongue that does not prepare itself for speech; i. e, the ready tongue: ] but [F says that] the right reading is All~isaAnu waAlxaTiybu (K) [i. e.] ― -b4- misoHalN also signifies i. q. xaTiybN (assumed tropical:) [ A speaker, an orator, or a preacher; or a good speaker &c.]: and and eloquent xaTiyb ; (K, TA;) one who scarcely, or never, stops short in his speech; excelling such as is termed miSoqaEN . (TA.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) One who is skilled in the reading, or reciting, of the Kur-án: (K:) from saHolN meaning the “ making ” [a thing] “ to be consecutive in its parts, or portions; ” and the “ pouring forth ” [water &c.]. (TA.) ― -b6- A copious rain: (K:) from saHolN meaning the act of “ pouring forth. ” (TA.) ― -b7- A water-spout ( miyzaAb ) of which the water is not to be withstood [so I render laA yuTaAqu maAw^uhu , app. meaning, that pours forth its water with such violence that no obstruction will resist it ]. (O, K.) ― -b8- The mouth of a mazaAdap [or leathern water-bag ]. (O, K.) ― -b9- A brisk, lively, sprightly, or active, waterer, or cup-bearer. (O, K.) ― -b10- Extreme ( nihaAyapN ) in bounty, or munificence. (O, K.) ― -b11- A courageous man, who acts, ( yaEomalu , so in the M and K, TA,) or charges, or makes an assault or attack, ( yaHomilu , so in the O, TA,) alone, or by himself. (M, O, K.) ― -b12- The flogger who inflicts the castigations appointed by the law (O, K) before, or in the presence of, the Sultán. (O.) -A2- I. q. lijaAmN [as meaning The bridle, or headstall and reins with the bit and other appertenances ]; as also ↓ siHaAlN ; (K;) like as you say minoTaqN and niTaAqN , and miy^ozarN and A_izaArN : (TA:) or its faA^os ; (K;) which is the piece of iron that stands up in the mouth [from the middle of the bit-mouth]; as IDrd says in the “ Book of the Saddle and Bridle: ” (TA:) and two rings, (K, TA,) one of which is inserted into the other, (TA,) at the two extremities of the $akiym of the bridle, (K, TA,) which is [generally applied to the bit-mouth, but is here said by SM to be] the piece of iron that is beneath the lower lip: or, accord. to IDrd, the misoHal of the bridle is a piece of iron which is beneath the lower jaw; and the faA^os is the piece of iron that stands up in the $akiymap ; and the $akiymap is the piece of iron that lies crosswise in the mouth: and the pl. is masaAHilu : (TA:) or the misoHalaAni are two rings at the two extremities of the $akiym [or bit-mouth ] of the bridle, one of which is inserted into the other [ so that they occupy the place of our curb-chain ]: (S:) they are [also said to be] the xad~aAni [lit. two cheeks ] of the bridle: (TA:) the misoHal is beneath the part in which is the bridle, and upon it flow the foam and blood of the horse. (Az, TA voce qayoqabN . [See also lijaAmN and faA^osN .]) One says of a horse when exerting himself, and being quick, in his going, and thrusting forward therein his head, rakiba misoHalahu [ He bore upon his bridle, &c.]. (O, TA.) And hence, (TA,) this phrase means [also] (assumed tropical:) He (a man, TA) followed his error, not desisting from it: (K, TA:) misoHalN signifying (assumed tropical:) error: (K:) and [in like manner] TaEana fiY misoHali DalaAlatihi means (assumed tropical:) He hastened, and strove in his error. (TA.) Also, the former of these two phrases, (assumed tropical:) He resolved, or determined, upon the [or his ] affair, and strove, or exerted himself therein: (O, TA:) [for] misoHalN signifies also (assumed tropical:) decisive resolution or determination. (O, K, TA.) And (assumed tropical:) He went on with energy in his discourse, sermon, speech, oration, or harangue: (S, TA:) and so in his poetry. (A, TA.) ― -b2- Also, [from the same word as meaning the “ bridle, ” or “ headstall &c., ”] (tropical:) The side of the beard: [like as it is called Ei*aAr because it is in the place corresponding to that of the Ei*aAr of a horse or the like: ( jAnibi in the CK is a mistake for jaAnibu :)] or the lower part of each Ei*aAr [or side of the beard ], to the fore part of the beard; both together being called misoHalaAni : (K, TA: [ Aasofala in the CK is a mistake for A^asofalu :]) or the place of the Ei*aAr : (Az, TA:) or the temple; misoHalaAni meaning the two temples: (TA:) and (K) the EaAriD [or side of the cheek ] of a man. (Ibn- 'Abbád, O, K.) One says, $aAba misoHaluhu , meaning (tropical:) The side of his beard became white, or hoary. (TA.) -A3- A clean (O, K, TA) thin (TA) garment, or piece of cloth, of cotton. (O, K, TA. [See also saHolN .]) ― -b2- A rope, (K,) or string, or thread, (M, TA,) that is twisted alone: (K:) if with another, [i. e. with another strand,] it is termed muboramN , and mugaArN . (TA. [See, again, saHolN .]) ― -b3- A sieve. (O, K.) -A4- The wild ass: (S, TA:) [because of his braying:] see 1, last sentence: an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates. (TA.) ― -b2- A brisk, lively, sprightly, or active, ass. (O.) ― -b3- A low, vile, mean, or sordid, man. (O, TA.) ― -b4- A devil. (O, TA.) ― -b5- The name of The taAbiEap (S, O) or [familiar] jinnee or genie (K) of [the poet] El-Aashà. (S, O, K. [In the K it is implied that it is with the article Al : but accord. to the S and O and TA, it is without Al .])

definition: Cattle, or camels &c.
sourceDefinition: Cattle, or camels &c., pasturing, (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) or pasturing where they please, by themselves: (S, A, K:) or only such as are sent, or driven, forth [ to pasture ] in the morning, and brought, or driven, back in the evening to their nightly resting-place: (L:) an inf. n. used as a subst. (Mgh, Msb.) A'Obeyd says that saroHN and ↓ saAriHN and ↓ saAriHapN signify Cattle, or camels &c.: and Khálid Ibn-Jembeh says that ↓ saAriHapN means camels and sheep or goats: and a single beast; as well as a collection [ of beasts ]. (TA.) -A2- Also A certain kind of trees, of great size, (S, K, TA,) and tall, (S, TA,) not depastured, or seldom eaten by the camels &c., but used for their shade: they grow in Nejd, in plain, or soft, and in rugged ground, but not in sand nor upon a mountain; and have a yellow fruit: (TA:) n. un. with p : and it is said to be the same as the A=' : (S:) but this is a mistake; the fact being that it bears a kind of berry termed A=' , (K, TA,) resembling the olive: (TA:) or any trees without thorns: (K:) n. un. in this sense with p : (Fr, Ham p. 603, TA:) or any tall trees: (K:) or [ trees ] of the kind called EiDaAh , great, with spreading branches, beneath which men alight in the Sayof [or summer ]: (Ham ubi suprà:) accord. to AHn, the saroHap is a great tree with spreading branches, beneath which people often alight, widely extending; men alight beneath it in the Sayof [or summer ], and pitch tents, or build houses, beneath it; and its shade is good: accord. to information given to Az by an Arab of the desert not known by him to have uttered a lie, it has a dusty colour, is not so tall as the A^avol [a species of tamarisk], has small leaves, and lank branches, or twigs, and always grows slanting, its inclination among all the trees being towards the south ( Alyamiyn ): Lth says that the saroH are a kind of trees that have a fruit, and they are the A^alaA=' ( AlAlA=' [app. a mistranscription for AlA=' , i. e. the A=' ,]); but Az says that this is a mistake: Lth cites the saying of' Antarah, baTalN kaA^an~a viyaAbahu fiY saroHapK tuHo*aY niEaAlu Als~iboti layosa bitawo'ami (L,) i. e. He is a man of valour, tall of stature, as though his clothes were upon a great tree such as is called srHp ; sandals of sbt [q. v.] are cut and made for him, such as are worn by the kings; and he is not a twin; so that he has been well suckled: (EM p. 245:) thus he describes this person as tall of stature, showing that the srHp is a large tree: but the AlA=' [or A=' ] has no trunk nor tallness: IAar says that the saroH are *akowaAn that have become large; and the *kwAn are certain trees having beautiful [shoots such as are termed] EasaAliyj : the pl. is siraAHN . (L.) ― -b2- The n. un., saroHapN , is applied to signify (tropical:) A man's wife, (S, A,) by a metonymy. (S.) The Arabs are said by Az to term a woman, or wife, a saroHp growing over water, because in this case it is in the most beautiful condition. (TA.) ― -b3- [Accord. to Forskål, (Flora Aegypt. Arab. pp. cvi. and 68,) the name of srH is applied to a plant of the class pentandria, which he terms Cadaba farinosa, (described by him in p. 68,) growing in the lower region of the mountains of Wádee-Surdud, in Tihámeh.] -A3- Also The exterior court or yard of a house, (K,) or, as in the L, of a gate, or door. (TA.)

(TA.) -A2- Also A certain kind of trees, of great size, (S, K, TA,) and tall, (S, TA,) not depastured, or seldom eaten by the camels &c., but used for their shade: they grow in Nejd, in plain, or soft, and in rugged ground, but not in sand nor upon a mountain; and have a yellow fruit: (TA:) n. un. with p : and it is said to be the same as the A=' : (S:) but this is a mistake; the fact being that it bears a kind of berry termed A=' , (K, TA,) resembling the olive: (TA:) or any trees without thorns: (K:) n. un. in this sense with p : (Fr, Ham p. 603, TA:) or any tall trees: (K:) or [ trees ] of the kind called EiDaAh , great, with spreading branches, beneath which men alight in the Sayof [or summer ]: (Ham ubi suprà:) accord. to AHn, the saroHap is a great tree with spreading branches, beneath which people often alight, widely extending; men alight beneath it in the Sayof [or summer ], and pitch tents, or build houses, beneath it; and its shade is good: accord. to information given to Az by an Arab of the desert not known by him to have uttered a lie, it has a dusty colour, is not so tall as the A^avol [a species of tamarisk], has small leaves, and lank branches, or twigs, and always grows slanting, its inclination among all the trees being towards the south ( Alyamiyn ): Lth says that the saroH are a kind of trees that have a fruit, and they are the A^alaA=' ( AlAlA=' [app. a mistranscription for AlA=' , i. e. the A=' ,]); but Az says that this is a mistake: Lth cites the saying of' Antarah, baTalN kaA^an~a viyaAbahu fiY saroHapK tuHo*aY niEaAlu Als~iboti layosa bitawo'ami (L,) i. e. He is a man of valour, tall of stature, as though his clothes were upon a great tree such as is called srHp ; sandals of sbt [q. v.] are cut and made for him, such as are worn by the kings; and he is not a twin; so that he has been well suckled: (EM p. 245:) thus he describes this person as tall of stature, showing that the srHp is a large tree: but the AlA=' [or A=' ] has no trunk nor tallness: IAar says that the saroH are *akowaAn that have become large; and the *kwAn are certain trees having beautiful [shoots such as are termed] EasaAliyj : the pl. is siraAHN . (L.) ― -b2- The n. un., saroHapN , is applied to signify (tropical:) A man's wife, (S, A,) by a metonymy. (S.) The Arabs are said by Az to term a woman, or wife, a saroHp growing over water, because in this case it is in the most beautiful condition. (TA.) ― -b3- [Accord. to Forskål, (Flora Aegypt. Arab. pp. cvi. and 68,) the name of srH is applied to a plant of the class pentandria, which he terms Cadaba farinosa, (described by him in p. 68,) growing in the lower region of the mountains of Wádee-Surdud, in Tihámeh.] -A3- Also The exterior court or yard of a house, (K,) or, as in the L, of a gate, or door. (TA.)

definition: , of the measure fiEolaAnN , the n being an augmentative letter, (Sb, S,) from the verb saraHa , (TA,) The wolf;
sourceDefinition: , of the measure fiEolaAnN , the n being an augmentative letter, (Sb, S,) from the verb saraHa , (TA,) The wolf; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also siroHaAlN ; (Yaakoob, K;) fem. siroHaAnapN (Ks, S) and siroHaAlahN ; (TA;) and the lion, (S, O, Msb, K,) in the dial. of Hudheyl: (S, O:) pl. saraAHiynu (S, A, O, Msb, K) and saraAHK and siraAHN , (O, L, K,) but the last not remembered to have been heard by Az. (L.) It is said in a prov., saqaTa AlEa$aA='u bihi EalaY siroHaAni [ The evening-meal, or supper, (i. e. the seeking for it,) made him to fall, or light, upon a wolf ]: (S, Meyd:) accord. to A'Obeyd, it originated from a man's going forth to seek the eveningmeal, and falling upon a wolf, which devoured him: accord. to As, from the like accident to a beast: accord. to IAar, from a man's being slain by another man, named siroHaAn : it is applied to the seeking an object of want that leads one to destruction. (Meyd. [See Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 599: but the name there written “ Hasahah ” is huzolap ; accord. to Meyd, the father, but accord. to the O, the brother, of Sirhán.]) ― -b2- Hence, (Mgh, Msb,) i. e. from Als~iroHaAnu as meaning “ the wolf, ” or, as some say, “ the lion, ” (TA,) *anabu Als~iroHaAni The false dawn; (Mgh, O, K, TA;) i. e. the first [ dawn ]. (TA. [A term nearly agreeing with the Greek λυκόφως ]) ― -b3- Als~iroHaAnu , (O, K,) or siroHaAnN , (TA,) is also the name of A certain dog: and of a certain horse: and of another horse. (O, K.) -A2- Also The middle of a wateringtrough or tank: (O, K:) pl. as above. (K.)

sourceDefinition: a subst. from tasoriyHu AlmaroA^api ; (S, Msb, K;) [i. e., a subst.] signifying The dismissal of a wife by divorcement: (Bd in xxxiii. 28 [where it is used as a quasi-inf. n., as it is also in verse 48 of the same chap.]:) like TalaAqN and firaAqN , it signifies divorcement explicitly. (L.) ― -b2- [And Dismissal in a general sense. Hence,] it is said in a prov., Als~araAHu mina Aln~ajaAHi (tropical:) [i. e. Dismissal is a part of the accomplishment of one's want ]; (S, A, L;) meaning, when thou canst not accomplish a man's want, make him to despair; for thy doing so will be in his estimation an act that will stand him in lieu of thy helping him to accomplish it: (S, L: [in some copies of the former, for faA^ayoy^isohu , we find faA=yasotahu :]) or it is applied to a man who does not desire to accomplish the want [of another]; and means, it behooves thee to make him to despair if thou accomplish not his want. (Meyd. [See a similar prov. voce $araAHN .]) ― -b3- Also Haste, ex- pedition, or promptness. (TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) Ease: so in the saying, AifoEalo *`lika fiY saraAHK warawaAHK (TA) i. e. (tropical:) Do thou that in a state of ease (S and A and K in art. rwH ) and rest. (A in that art.) -A2- saraAHi [indecl.] like qaTaAmi , [app. as meaning The quick, or quick and easy in pace, like Als~uruHu ,] the name of a certain horse. (K.)

sourceDefinition: A carpenter's adz, or axe, (L,) or a large adz or axe, (M, L,) or a thing (S, L, K) of any kind, (K,) with which one hews, or shapes out, or pares, a thing; as also ↓ misofanN : (S, L, K:) or an adz with which palm-trunks are pared; as also safarN and $afarN . definition: A ship, or boat;
sourceDefinition: A ship, or boat; (M, L;) of the measure faEylapN in the sense of the measure faAEilapN ; (IDrd, S, M, L, Msb;) as though it pared the surface of the water; (IDrd, S, L, Msb;) or so called because it pares [meaning skims] the surface of the water; (M, L;) or because it pares the sands [by running aground] when the water is little [in depth]; or because [in that case] it sticks upon the ground; or it may be from safanN meaning “ a carpenter's adz or axe with which he hews &c., ” and, if so, having the meaning of the measure mafoEuwlapN : (L:) the pl. is safaAy^inu and sufunN (M, L, Msb, K) and [coll. gen. n.] ↓ safiynN : (S, M, L, Msb, K:) the first of these is a regular pl.: (Sb, M, L:) the second is pl. of the third, (Msb,) or it is as though it were pl. of the third: (Sb, M, L:) ↓ the third is anomalous, being of a class proper to created things, as in the instances of tamorapN and tamorN , and naxolapN and naxolN , and only heard in a few instances in the cases of things made by art; and some say that it is a dial. var. of safiynapN . (Msb.) [Hence,] Als~afiynapu (assumed tropical:) [ The constellation Argo; ] one of the southern constellations, of which the stars are five and forty, the bright great star upon the southern oar being sohayolN [i. e. Canopus ], accord. to Ptolemy, and it is the most remote star from the sfynp , in the south, and is marked on the astrolabe; but some of the Arabs say that the bright star at the extremity of the second oar [but what star is meant thereby I know not] is called suhayolN , without restriction. (Kzw.) ― -b2- [Also An oblong book: and a commonplace book: app. post-classical.]

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (M, K) and , (K,) inf. n. salotN , (M, TA,) He extracted, or made to come forth, [ the contents of ] the gut [ by compressing it ] with his hand. (M, K. [In both it is expl. by A^axorajahu biyadihi : but it seems that a fault has been accidentally committed by a copyist in the former or in its original, and thence passed into the latter; and that the words which I have supplied are necessary to explain the true meaning. That such is the case, appears from what here follows.]) It is said in the L that Als~alotu signifies The griping, with the hand, a thing that is contaminated by dirt, or filth, so that what is in it comes forth; and thus is done with a gut. (TA.) It is also said to signify The extracting, or causing to come forth, what is fluid, or moist, adhering to another thing. (MF, TA.) [Hence,] salata xamo$ahu i. e. muxaATahu Eano A^anofihi [ He cleansed his nose of the mucus that was in it by compressing it with his fingers ]: occurring in two trads.; in one of which, the Prophet is related to have been in the habit of doing this to El-Hoseyn when he used to carry him upon his shoulder. (TA.) [Hence, likewise,] it is said in a trad., fayanofu*u AljaHiymu A_ilaY jawofihi fayasolutu maAfiyhi , i. e. [ And the fire of Hell shall penetrate to his inside, and ] shall exscind and extirpate what is in it. (TA.) ― -b2- You say also, salata AlqaSoEapa , (S, A, K,) aor. , inf. n. salotN ; (S;) and ↓ AstlthA ; (K;) He cleansed the bowl by taking off with his finger what remained upon its sides; (S;) he wiped the bowl (A, K) with his fingers (A) or with his finger. (K.) And salatato xiDaAbahaA Eano yadihaA , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. salotN , (Msb,) She cast from her, or from her hand, the remains of her stuff for dyeing the hands or hair: (S, K:) or she put away, or removed, that stuff from her hand: (Msb:) or she wiped off, and cast away, that stuff from her hand: (TA:) or salata AlxiDaAba , aor. , he took away, and wiped off, the material for dyeing the hands or hair; and in like manner. a similar thing; and sweat; and blood. (Mgh.) salata Ald~ama EanohaA occurs in a trad. as meaning He removed the blood [ from her or it ]. (TA.) ― -b3- salata dama Albadanapi (M, K) means, accord. to Lh, He scraped off the blood of the bdnp [or beast brought to Mekkeh for sacrifice, or there sacrificed, ] with the knife: but [ISd says, (and in like manner halata dama Albadanapi is expl. in the L as on the authority of Lh,)] in my opinion the meaning is, he scraped off the skin of the bdnp with the knife so that he made its blood to appear. (M. [The explanation in the K is made up from the two different explanations in the M, being as follows: qa$arahu Hat~aY A^aZohara damahaA , as though meaning he scraped off the dried blood of the bdnp so that he made its fresh blood to appear: but in the copy of the K followed in the TA, Aln~adabap (i. e. the scar ) is put in the place of Albadanap , and the former of these two (i. e. Alndbp ) I regard as the right word.]) ― -b4- salata also signifies (assumed tropical:) He cut off a thing. (K. [This is said in the TA to be the primary meaning: but accord. to the A, the phrase here following, in which it has this meaning, is tropical.]) You say, salata A^anofahu , (S, M, A, K,) aor. and , inf. n. salotN , (M,) (tropical:) He cut off his nose (S, M, A, K) entirely (TA) with a sword. (S, A.) And salata yadahu biAls~ayofi (assumed tropical:) He cut off his hand, or arm, with the sword. (M.) And salata $aEarahu (assumed tropical:) He shaved off his hair. (M, K.) And salata raA^osahu (tropical:) He shaved his head. (As, S, L.) ― -b5- salatahu (assumed tropical:) He beat, struck, or smote, him: (K, TA:) and flogged him. (TA.) You say, salat~uhu miAy^apa sawoTK (assumed tropical:) I inflicted upon him a hundred strokes of the whip. (S, TA.) ― -b6- And salata bisaloHihi (assumed tropical:) He cast forth his excrement, or ordure. (K.)

sourceDefinition: A species of $aEiyr [or barley ], (Lth, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) having no hush, (Lth, S, Mgh, Msb,) A^ajoradu [which may mean either beardless or smooth ], (Lth,) [ in appearance ] as though it were wheat, (S,) growing in El-Ghowr and El- Hijáz; (Mgh, Msb;) the sawiyq [or meal of the parched grain ] whereof is employed as a cooling diet in the Sayof [or summer ]: (TA:) or i. q. $aEiyr [i. e. the common barley ]; (M, K;) as some say: (M:) or the sour ( HaAmiD ) sort of $Eyr : (M, K:) or a white $Eyr , without husk: or, as some say, a species of wheat; but the explanation next preceding this last is the more correct, for AlbayoDaA='u and Als~ulotu are mentioned in a trad. as distinct, each from the other, and by the former is meant wheat: (TA:) or a species of $Eyr with a thin husk and small grain: (IF, Msb:) or a grain between wheat and barley ( $Eyr ), not having a husk like that of the latter, and thus being like wheat in smoothness, and like barley ( $Eyr ) in its nature, or quality, and in its coolness: (Az, Msb:) accord. to Es-Seydelánee, like barley ( $Eyr ) in its form, and like wheat in its nature, or quality; but this is a mistake: (Ibn-Es-Saláh, Msb:) [ gymnocrithon (i. e. hordeum nudym ) of Galen: tragus of Diosc. (Golius.)]

sourceDefinition: [as an inf. n.] is syn. with qaSodN [in an intrans. sense], (S, * Msb,) and hudFY [in the sense of ra$aAdN ], and AisotiqaAmapN : (Msb:) or Husonu naHowK : (M, K:) you say, samata , aor. , (S, M, K,) and , (K,) or in this case the former only, (TA,) inf. n. samotN , (M, TA,) He pursued a right course; syn. qaSada : (S, TA:) or (assumed tropical:) he followed a good direction (M, K, * TA *) in the way of religion [&c.]. (TA.) Accord. to Khálid Ibn- Dabbeh, it signifies (assumed tropical:) The following the truth and the right way or direction, and being a good neighbour, and doing little harm. (TA.) [But more commonly, or primarily, it relates to the course that one pursues in journeying.] An Arab of the desert, of [the tribe of] Keys, says, sawofa tajuwbiyna bigayori naEoti taEas~ufFA A^awo h`ka*aA biAls~amoti i. e. [ Thou shalt traverse (addressing a woman), or, more probably, ye shall traverse (addressing camels or other beasts), a land without a description ], journeying without any sign of the way and without any track [ for guidance ], such being the meaning of tEs~fA , or thus, pursuing a right course, Als~amotu meaning AlqaSodu . (TA.) Accord. to Sh, Als~amotu signifies The seeking, searching, or inquiring, for, or after, the right way or direction. (TA.) ― -b2- Als~amotu also signifies qaSdu AlT~ariyqi [i. e. samotu AlT~ariyqi signifies The road's having a right, or direct, tendency ]: (M:) or [ samotu Al$~aYo'i ] signifies qaSodu Al$~aYo'i [i. e. The thing's having a right, or direct, tendency ]. (K.) [This last explanation has been misunderstood by the Turkish translator of the K; who has hence been led to assert that one says, samata Al$~aYo'a as well as samata naHowahu , meaning qaSadahu : it is tasam~atahu that (like samata naHowahu ) signifies qaSadahu ; not samatahu , for samata is always intrans.] ― -b3- Also The journeying (S, M, K) upon the road (M, K) [ guided only ] by opinion (S, M, K) and conjecture: (S:) or, as some say, the journeying by conjecture and opinion, not upon a [ known ] road. (TA.) A poet says, ↓ layosa bihaA riyEN lisamoti Als~aAmiti [ There is not, or was not, in it, a road of any kind (see riyEN ) for the journeying by opinion and conjecture of him who so journeys ]. (S, TA.) ― -b4- And The pursuing a course, or direction, [ of any kind, ] and [particularly] (assumed tropical:) in religion and in worldly affairs. (TA.) You say, huwa yasomutu samotahu (assumed tropical:) He pursues his [another's] way, or course, doing as he [the latter] does. (TA.) [ samotahu is here an absolute (not an objective) complement of yasomutu ; like sayorahu in the phrase huwayasiyru sayorahu . See also samotN below.] ― -b5- Also samata , aor. , inf. n. samotN , (assumed tropical:) He (a man) was, or became, grave, staid, steady, sedate, or calm. (Msb.) ― -b6- And samata lahumo , aor. , (Fr, K,) inf. n. samotN , (Fr, TA,) (assumed tropical:) He prepared, arranged, or disposed, for them, the mode, or manner, of speech, and of judging, or forming an opinion, (Fr, K, TA,) and of work, or action. (Fr, TA.)

definition: The keeping to the samot [i.
sourceDefinition: The keeping to the samot [i. e. road, &c.]. (K.) It is said in a trad., faA@noTalaqotu laA A^adoriY A^ayona A^a*ohabu A_il~aA A^an~aniY A^usam~itu , meaning [ And I departed, not knowing whither I should go, but ] I kept to the course, or direction, of the road: or as some say, I prayed to God. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) The mentioning of God, (S, M, A, Msb, K,) or, as in some copies of the S, the mentioning of the name of God, [like tasomiyapN , inf. n. of sam~aY ,] (TA,) upon, or over, a thing, (S, M, A, Msb, K,) or in any case. (TA.) One says, sam~ata EalaY AlT~aEaAmi (assumed tropical:) He mentioned the name of God upon, or over, the food. (TK.) ― -b3- And sm~t lahu and Ealayohi , inf. n. tasomiytN , (assumed tropical:) He prayed for what was good for him; prayed for a blessing upon him; as also $m~t . (L and TA in art. $mt , q. v.) In a trad. respecting eating, it is said, sam~uwA A@ll~`ha wadan~uwA wasam~ituwA , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Pronounce ye the name of God, and take what is next you of the food, or make your words to be near together, (see 2 in arts. dnw and smw ,) and, ] when ye have ended, invoke a blessing upon him at whose abode or table ye have eaten. (TA.) ― -b4- Alt~asoniytu also signifies, (M, K,) or tasomiytu AlEaATisi , (S, Msb,) (assumed tropical:) The praying for the sneezer; (M, Msb, K;) saying, hadaAka A@ll~`hu A_ilaY Als~amoti [ May God guide thee to the right, or good, course ]; because the person sneezing is disturbed and disquieted: so says AAF: (M, TA:) or the saying to him, yaroHamuka A@ll~`hu [ May God have mercy on thee ]: (Th, S, M:) or Alt~asomiytu signifies the saying baAraka A@ll~`hu fiyka [ May God bless thee ]: (ISh, TA:) it is with s and with $ : (S, M, Msb:) one says sam~atahu , (T, M, Msb,) i. e. sam~ata AlEaATisa , meaning He prayed for the sneezer, [ saying as above, ] (A,) and $am~atahu : (T, M, Msb:) Th says that the former is preferred, (S,) or is the original, (Msb,) being from Als~amotu signifying AlqaSodu , (S, M, Msb,) and AlhudaY , and AlAisotiqaAmapu , (Msb,) and AlmaHaj~apu , (S,) or AlT~ariyqu ; (M;) as though one made a person his object by this prayer; (M;) and that the s is changed [by some] into $ : (TA:) but A 'Obeyd says that the pronunciation with $ is of higher authority, and more common. (S, Msb.) The Prophet said, When any of you sneezes, let him say, AlHamodu lil~`hi [ Praise be to God ]; and he who prays for him ( Al~a*iY yu$an~ituhu [or yusam~ituhu ]), yaroHamuka A@ll~`hu ; and let him [i. e. the sneezer] say [in reply], yahodiykumu A@ll~`hu wayuSoliHu baAlakumo [ May God direct you aright, and render good your state, or condition, or case ]. (Har p. 250.)

(Har p. 250.)

sourceDefinition: , (M, L, K,) [aor. ,] inf. n. san~N , (M,) He (a man, M, L) bit him (another man, M, L) with his A^asonaAn [or teeth ]. (M, L, K: but in the K, with the A^asonaAn .) [Hence, app.,] sun~ati AlA^aroDu The herbage of the land was eaten. (L, K.) ― -b2- And, (M, L, in the K “ or, ”) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M, L,) He broke his (a man's, M, L) A^asonaAn [or teeth ]. (M, L, K.) ― -b3- sun~ati Albadanapu : and san~ahaA A@ll~`hu : see 4. ― -b4- Also, (accord. to the M and L, but accord. to the K “ or, ”) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M, L,) He pierced him, or thrust him, with the sinaAn [or spear-head ]. (M, L, K.) And san~ahu biAlr~umoHi He pierced him, or thrust him, with the spear. (L.) ― -b5- And He fixed, or mounted, upon it (i. e. the spear) the sinaAn [or iron head ]; (M, L, K;) and ↓ A^asan~ahu he put to it a sinaAn . (L.) ― -b6- Also, (S, M, L, Msb, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M, L, Msb,) He sharpened it, whetted it, or made it sharp-pointed, (S, M, L, Msb, K,) and polished it, (M, L, K,) namely, a thing, (M, L,) or a knife; (S, L, Msb, K;) and so ↓ sn~nhu : (M, L, K:) and san~a he sharpened, whetted, or made sharp-pointed, a spear-head upon the misan~ : (L:) and he rubbed, or grated, a stone upon a stone. (Fr, L.) ― -b7- [Hence,] san~aniY h`*aA Al$~aYo'u (assumed tropical:) This thing [ sharpened my appetite; ] made me desirous of food. (K.) The Arabs say [also] AlHamoDu tasun~u AlA_ibila EalaY Alxul~api (assumed tropical:) The [ plants, or trees, called ] HmD strengthen the camels [or sharpen their appetites ] for the [ plants, or trees, called ] xl~p , like as the whetstone strengthens [or sharpens ] the edge of the knife. (L.) ― -b8- [Hence also,] san~a A^aDoraAsahu , (M, L, K, *) [aor. and] inf. n. as above, (M, L,) He rubbed and cleaned his teeth with the stick used for that purpose; (M, L, K;) as though he polished them. (M, L.) ― -b9- And san~a AlA_ibila , (ISk, S, M, L,) or AlmaAla , (K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M, L,) He tended well, (K,) or pastured and tended well, (ISk, S, L,) or pastured, and rendered fat, or plump, (M, L,) the camels, (ISk, S, M, L,) or the cattle; (K;) [ so that they became in good condition, free from mange or the like; ] as though he polished them. (ISk, S, M, L, K.) ― -b10- And san~uwA AlmaAla They sent the cattle into the pasturage. (El-Muärrij, S, L, K. *) ― -b11- And san~a AlA_ibila , (M, L, K,) [aor. and] inf. n. as above, (M, L,) He drove the camels quickly: (M, L, K:) or, as some say, Als~an~u signifies Als~ayoru Al$~adiydu [i. e. the making to go vehemently; Als~ayoru being here syn. with Alt~asoyiyru ]: (M, L:) you say, sananotu Aln~aAqapa I made the she-camel to go ( sirotuhaA , S, or say~arotuhaA , L) vehemently. (S, L.) ― -b12- A_Kn~amaA A_unas~aY liA^asun~a , occurring in a trad., meaning I am made to forget only that I may drive men by directing to the right way, and show them what is needful for them to do when forgetfulness occurs to them, may be from san~a [expl. above as] meaning “ he pastured and tended well ” the camels. (L.) ― -b13- san~a Ealayohi AlmaA='a , [aor. and inf. n. as above,] He poured forth the water upon him, or it; (M, L, K;) as also ↓ Asn~hu : (Ham p. 611:) or he discharged the water gently upon him, or it. (M, L.) You say, sananotu AlmaA='a EalaY wajohiY , (S, L,) or EalaY Alwajohi , (Msb,) or san~a AlmaA='a EalaY wajohihi , (L,) or fiY wajohihi , (Mgh,) aor. as above, (Mgh, L,) and so the inf. n., (L,) I [or he ] discharged the water without scattering upon his face: if scattering it in pouring, you say, $ananotu : (S, L:) or I, or he, poured the water gently (Mgh, L, Msb) upon the face, (Msb,) or upon his face. (Mgh, L.) And san~a Alt~uraAba He poured the dust, or earth, gently upon the ground: (S, L:) and he put it gently upon a corpse. (L.) And san~ati AlEayonu Ald~amoEa , aor. and inf. n. as above, The eye poured forth tears. (M, L.) And Ausonuno quruwna farasika Make the [ issues of ] sweat to flow from thy horse by plying him hard, in order that he may become lean, or light of flesh: and sun~a lahu qaronN , and quruwnN , An issue, and issues, of his sweat, was, and were, made to flow. (L.) san~a Ealayohi Ald~iroEa , (S, M, L, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (S, M, L,) He put (lit. poured ) upon him the coat of mail. (S, M, L, K.) ― -b14- san~a AlfaHolu Aln~aAqapa The stallion threw down the she-camel ( kab~ahaA , in copies of the K [erroneously] rakibahaA ,) upon her face. (L, K. * [See also 3.]) ― -b15- san~a AlT~iyna He plastered pottery with the clay: (M, L:) or he made the clay into pottery. (M, L, K.) ― -b16- san~ahu , (S, L, K,) aor. as above, (S,) and so the inf. n., (S, L,) also signifies He formed it, fashioned it, or shaped it; (S, L, K;) namely, a thing: (K:) and some say, he made it long. (L.) ― -b17- And [from the former of these two meanings, app.,] He instituted, established, or prescribed, it, i. e. a custom, practice, usage, or the like, whether good or bad; set the example of it; originated it as a custom &c. to be followed by others after him. (L.) You say, sananotu lakumo sun~apF faA@t~abiEuwhaA [ I have instituted &c., for you an institute, a custom, a practice, a usage, or the like, to be followed, therefore follow ye it ]. (L.) And san~a fulaAnN TariyqFA mina Alxayori , aor. and inf. n. as above, Such a one originated [or instituted ] an act of goodness, or piety, [or a good, or pious, way of acting, ] which his people knew not, and which they afterwards followed, or pursued. (L.) And san~a A@ll~`hu sun~atahu liln~aAsi God manifested, or made known, his statutes, or ordinances, and commands and prohibitions, [i. e. his laws, ] to men: (M, L:) and san~a A@ll~`hu sun~apF God manifested, or made known, a right way [ of acting &c.]: (L:) [and in like manner one says of any one,] san~a AlA^amora He manifested, or made known, the thing, affair, or case. (K.) ― -b18- And san~a sun~apF , (M, L,) or TariyqapF , (K,) [aor. and] inf. n. as above, (M, L,) He pursued [ a way, course, rule, mode, or manner, of acting or conduct or life or the like ]; as also ↓ Astn~hA ; (M, L;) or ↓ Astsn~hA ; (so in the K;) and bihaA ↓ Astn~ : (K in art. syr :) and biTariyqK mina Alxayori ↓ Astsn~wA [ They followed, or pursued, a good, or pious, way of acting ]. (L.) It is said in a trad. respecting the Magians, A^aholi AlkitaAbi ↓ sun~uwA bihimo sun~apa , i. e. Pursue ye with them the way of the People of the Scripture, or Bible; act with them as ye act with these; granting them security on the condition of receiving [from them] the [tax called] jizoyap . (Mgh, L. *) -A2- sun~a is also expl. as meaning He, or it, became altered for the worse, or stinking: so in a trad. of Barwaa the daughter of Wáshik, where it is said, kaAna zawojuhaA sun~a fiY biy^orK [ Her husband had become altered for the worse, or stinking, having died, in a well which he had descended]: from the saying in the Kur mino HamaA^ masonuwnK : [see masonuwnN :] but some say that he [who used this phrase] meant [to say, or meant thereby,] A^asina , i. e. his head became affected with vertigo by reason of a foul odour that he smelt, and he swooned. (L.)

(ISk, S, M, L, K.) ― -b10- And san~uwA AlmaAla They sent the cattle into the pasturage. (El-Muärrij, S, L, K. *) ― -b11- And san~a AlA_ibila , (M, L, K,) [aor. and] inf. n. as above, (M, L,) He drove the camels quickly: (M, L, K:) or, as some say, Als~an~u signifies Als~ayoru Al$~adiydu [i. e. the making to go vehemently; Als~ayoru being here syn. with Alt~asoyiyru ]: (M, L:) you say, sananotu Aln~aAqapa I made the she-camel to go ( sirotuhaA , S, or say~arotuhaA , L) vehemently. (S, L.) ― -b12- A_Kn~amaA A_unas~aY liA^asun~a , occurring in a trad., meaning I am made to forget only that I may drive men by directing to the right way, and show them what is needful for them to do when forgetfulness occurs to them, may be from san~a [expl. above as] meaning “ he pastured and tended well ” the camels. (L.) ― -b13- san~a Ealayohi AlmaA='a , [aor. and inf. n. as above,] He poured forth the water upon him, or it; (M, L, K;) as also ↓ Asn~hu : (Ham p. 611:) or he discharged the water gently upon him, or it. (M, L.) You say, sananotu AlmaA='a EalaY wajohiY , (S, L,) or EalaY Alwajohi , (Msb,) or san~a AlmaA='a EalaY wajohihi , (L,) or fiY wajohihi , (Mgh,) aor. as above, (Mgh, L,) and so the inf. n., (L,) I [or he ] discharged the water without scattering upon his face: if scattering it in pouring, you say, $ananotu : (S, L:) or I, or he, poured the water gently (Mgh, L, Msb) upon the face, (Msb,) or upon his face. (Mgh, L.) And san~a Alt~uraAba He poured the dust, or earth, gently upon the ground: (S, L:) and he put it gently upon a corpse. (L.) And san~ati AlEayonu Ald~amoEa , aor. and inf. n. as above, The eye poured forth tears. (M, L.) And Ausonuno quruwna farasika Make the [ issues of ] sweat to flow from thy horse by plying him hard, in order that he may become lean, or light of flesh: and sun~a lahu qaronN , and quruwnN , An issue, and issues, of his sweat, was, and were, made to flow. (L.) san~a Ealayohi Ald~iroEa , (S, M, L, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (S, M, L,) He put (lit. poured ) upon him the coat of mail. (S, M, L, K.) ― -b14- san~a AlfaHolu Aln~aAqapa The stallion threw down the she-camel ( kab~ahaA , in copies of the K [erroneously] rakibahaA ,) upon her face. (L, K. * [See also 3.]) ― -b15- san~a AlT~iyna He plastered pottery with the clay: (M, L:) or he made the clay into pottery. (M, L, K.) ― -b16- san~ahu , (S, L, K,) aor. as above, (S,) and so the inf. n., (S, L,) also signifies He formed it, fashioned it, or shaped it; (S, L, K;) namely, a thing: (K:) and some say, he made it long. (L.) You say, sananotu lakumo sun~apF faA@t~abiEuwhaA [ I have instituted &c., for you an institute, a custom, a practice, a usage, or the like, to be followed, therefore follow ye it ]. (L.) A_isonaAnN , (Mgh, L, Msb,) said of a man, (S, M, L, Msb, K,) and of other than man, (Msb,) i. q. kabira [meaning He became advanced in age, or fullgrown ], (S, L, Msb,) or kabirato sin~uhu [which means the same]; (M, L, K;) as also ↓ Astsn~ : (K:) but Az says that AlA_isonaAnu in the case of an animal of the ox-kind and of the sheep or goat, is not the same as in that of a man: for in such animals it means [ the attaining to the age of ] the coming forth of the [ permanent ] vaniy~ap [or central incisor ]: (Msb:) or in such animals it means at least [ the attaining to the age of ] the shedding of the [ tooth called ] vny~p [which is generally said to be in the third year ]; and at the utmost in such animals, [ the attaining to the age of ] what is termed AlS~uluwg or Als~uluwg [which is in the sixth year ]; and at the utmost in camels, [ the attaining to the age of ] what is termed Albuzuwl [which is generally in the ninth year ]. (Mgh, L.) And Albadanapu ↓ sun~ati , a phrase mentioned by Kt, as meaning The teeth of the bdnp grew forth, is also a mistake [for A^asan~at ]. (L.) ― -b2- See also 1, in the former half of the paragraph, in two places.

definition: He rubbed and cleaned his teeth with the siwaAk [or piece of stick used for that purpose ];
sourceDefinition: He rubbed and cleaned his teeth with the siwaAk [or piece of stick used for that purpose ]; (S, M, L, K;) he made use of the siwaAk , passing it over his teeth. (L.) ― -b2- And He took, or seized, with the teeth. (KL.) -A2- Astn~t AlEayonu The eye poured forth its tears. (M, L.) ― -b2- Astn~ said of the blood of a wound made with a spear or the like, It issued in a gush. (AZ, L.) ― -b3- Said of the saraAb [or mirage], It was, or became, in a state of commotion, went to and fro, or quivered. (M, L, K.) ― -b4- Said of a horse, i. q. qamaSa [app. as meaning He pranced, leaped, sprang, or bounded ]: (S, K:) he frisked; or was brisk, lively, or sprightly: he ran, in his friskiness, briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness, in one direction: he ran, by reason of his friskiness, briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness, a heat, or two heats, without a rider upon him: (L:) he ran to and fro, by reason of briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness: from san~a as signifying “ he poured forth ” water, and as signifying “ he sharpened ” iron upon a whetstone. (Har p. 47.) It is said in a prov., Aisotan~ati AlfiSaAlu Hat~aY AlqaroEaY , (S, Meyd, L,) or AlfuSolaAnu , (Meyd,) i. e. The young weaned camels leaped, sprang, or bounded; (S * L;) even those affected with the small pustules called qaraE ; (Meyd, L;) which are small white pustules, the remedy for which is salt, and the butter ( jubaAb ) of camels' milk: (Meyd:) when the healthy young weaned camels do thus, those affected with such pustules do the like in imitation, but become disabled from doing it by weakness: the prov. is applied to the man who introduces himself among a people, or party, to whom he does not belong: (L:) or to him who speaks with one before whom he should not speak by reason of the greatness of his rank: and some related it differently, saying, AlqurayoEaY [which is the dim. of AlqaroEaY ]; (Meyd;) and AlquroEu [which is pl. of AlA^aqoraEu , q. v.]: and some say that Astn~t AlfiSaAlu signifies the young weaned camels became fat, or plump, and their skins became [ sleek ] like masaAn~ [or whetstones ]. (L.) And it is said in a trad. of 'Omar, raA^ayotu A^abaAhu yasotan~u bisayofihi kamaA yasotan~u Aljamalu , meaning [ I saw his father ] exulting with briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness, and brandishing his sword, [ like as the camel exults with briskness, and lashes with his tail. ] (L.) See also 5. ― -b5- [Also He took, held, or followed, the sanan , i. e., road, or way, or main and middle part thereof: and he, or it, was, or lay, in the way. Hence,] one says, xu*o maA A@sotan~a , meaning [ Take thou what lies in the way; ] what is easily attainable; what offers itself without difficulty. (AA, TA voce Ainotadaba .) ― -b6- See also 1, near the end of the paragragh, in two places.
