sourceDefinition: i. q. DirosN [as meaning A tooth; in which sense this latter word is often used; though it is frequently restricted to a molar tooth, or to any of the teeth except the central incisors]: (M, L, K:) [or, accord. to some, a single tooth; i. e. one that is not of the double, or molar, kind; as shown by a description in what follows:] of the fem. gender: (S, M, L, Msb:) pl. A^asonaAnN (S, M, L, Msb, K) and A^asin~apN and A^asun~N , (M, L, K,) the last of these mentioned by Lh, and this and the second anomalous; (M, L;) or the second is allowable as pl. of the first of these pls.; (S;) or it is pl. of the sinaAn of the spear; but may also be pl. of A^asonaAnN as pl. of sin~N applied to herbage upon which camels pasture, in an instance to be cited in what follows: (A'Obeyd, T, L:) the vulgar say A_isonaAn and A^usonaAn , which are wrong: (Msb:) the A^asonaAn of a human being consist of four vanaAyaA , and four rabaAEiyaAt , and four A^anoyaAb , and four nawaAji* , and sixteen A^aDoraAs : or, as some say, four vnAyA , and four rbAEyAt , and four AnyAb , and four nwAj* , and four DawaAHik , and twelve A^aroHaA=' : (Msb:) or the A^asonaAn and A^aDoraAs together make up the number of thirty-two; the vnAbA are four, two above and two below [in the middle]; next are the rbAEyAt , which are four, two above and two below; next are the AnyAb , which are four [likewise, two above and two below]; and next are the ADrAs , which are twenty, on each side five above and five below; and of these [last] the four that are next to the AnyAb are the DwAHk ; next to each nAb , above and below, is a DaAHik ; next to the DwAHk are the TawaAHin , also called the A^aroHaA=' , which are twelve, on each side [above and below] three; and next to these are the nwAj* , which are the last of the teeth in growth, and the last of the ADrAs , on each side of the mouth one above and one below: (Zj in his “ Khalk el-Insán: ”) the dim. of sin~N is ↓ sunayonapN , because it is fem. (S.) One says, laA A=tiyka sin~a AlHisoli , (S, M, L,) i. e. I will not come to thee as long as remains the tooth of the young one of the [ kind of lizard called ] Dab~ ; (M, L;) meaning, ever; (S, M, * L;) because the Hsl never sheds a tooth: (S, L:) or, as Lh relates it, on the authority of ElMufaddal, sin~aYo HisolK ; [using the dual form of sin~N ;] and [it may be rendered, accord. to the former reading, (assumed tropical:) during the life of the young one of the D~b , for] he says, they assert that the Db~ lives three hundred years, and that it is the longest-lived creeping thing upon the earth. (M, L.) A poet (Aboo-Jarwal El-Jushamee, whose name was Hind, L) says, describing camels taken as a bloodwit, fajaA='ato kasin~i AlZ~aboYi lamo A^ara mivolahaA bawaA='a qatiylK A^awo Haluwbapa jaAy^iEi [ And they came; (assumed tropical:) like the age of the gazelle was the age of every one of them: I have not seen the like of them for an equivalent of a slain person, or a milch camel of one hungry: (I have given a reading of this verse that I have found in the M and TA in art. ZbY , instead of that in the present art. in the S and L, in which snA='a and sanaA='a are put in the place of bawaA='a app. for sinaA='a , an inf. n. of saAnaAhu , and as such here meaning a soothing, or the like: )] he means that they were vunoyaAn , [pl. of vaniY~N ], because the vaniY~ is one shedding [or that has shed] his vaniy~ap , and the gazelle has no vaniy~ap [in the upper jaw], so that he is always [one that may be termed] a vaniY~ . (S, L.) It is said in a trad., A_i*aA saAfarotumo fiY AlxiSobi faA^aEoTuwA Alr~ukuba A^asin~atahaA , [expl. as] meaning When ye journey in the land abounding with herbage, enable ye the ridden beasts to take of the pasturage: (S, L:) but Az states that A'Obeyd says, I know not A^asin~ap except as pl. of the sinaAn of the spear; and if the trad. be [correctly] preserved in memory, it seems to be pl. of A^asonaAn ; for sin~N [sometimes] signifies the [ portion of ] herbage upon which camels pasture; and its pl. is A^asonaAnN ; one says, A^asonaAnN mina AlmaroEaY ; and the pl. of A^asonaAnN is A^asin~apN : Aboo-Sa'eed says that this last is pl. of sinaAnN , not of A^asonaAnN , and ↓ sinaAnN is applied to the [plants, or trees, called] HamoD , as meaning (assumed tropical:) a strengthener [i. e. a sharpener of the appetite ] of the camels for the [plants, or trees, called] xul~ap : [see a phrase in the earlier part of the first paragraph:] in like manner, also, [he says,] when they light upon what is termed sin~N mina AlmaroEaY [ a portion of pasturage ], this is termed EalaY Als~ayori ↓ sinaAnN [ a strengthener, or sharpener, for journeying ]: this explanation is approved by Az, and likewise that of A'Obeyd: it is also related, on the authority of Fr, that Als~in~u signifies the eating vehemently: [a signification mentioned in the K as well as in the L:] and Az says, I have heard more than one of the Arabs say, A^aSaAbati AlA_ibilu Alyawoma sin~FA mina AlmaroEaY [ The camels have obtained to-day a good portion of pasturage ] when they have eaten well of the best of the pasturage: Z says that ↓ A^aEoTuwA Alr~ukuba A^asin~atahaA means (assumed tropical:) Give ye to the ridden beasts what will prevent their being slaughtered; for when their owner pastures them well, they become fat, and goodly in his eye, and therefore he withholds himself, with niggardliness, from slaughtering them, and this [condition of them] is likened to A^asin~ap [as meaning “ spear-heads ”] pl. of sinaAnN : [see also A^axa*ato rimaAHahaA , said of camels, voce rumoHN :] or if the pl. of sin~N be intended by it, the meaning is, enable ye them [i. e. the ridden beasts ] to take of the pasturage; and hence the trad., A^aEoTuwA Als~in~a HaZ~ahaA mina Als~in~i , i. e. Give ye the possessors of the sin~ [meaning tooth ] their share of the sin~ which is the pasture. (L.) Als~in~u is also used for *awaAtu Als~in~i [ The possessors of the tooth ] as meaning the slave and horses and the like and other animals, [ collectively, in like manner as xuf~N and HaAfirN are used,] in a trad. of 'Omar. (L.) And it is said in a trad. of Ibn-Dhee-Yezen, laA^uwTiy^an~a A^asonaAna AlEarabi kaEobahu , for *awiY A^asonaAni AlEarabi , meaning [ I will assuredly make ] the great men and the nobles [ of the Arabs to tread upon his ankle ]. (L.) [But AsnAn in this instance may be pl. of sin~N in the sense here next following; so that *wY AsnAn may be rendered the advanced in age. ]) ― -b2- Hence, (L,) (tropical:) Life; (S, M, L, Msb;) metaphorically used in this sense as indicative of its length and its shortness; (L;) [for the teeth vary with the length of life;] the measure, (K,) or extent, of life; (Msb, K;) [the age attained; ] used in relation to human beings and others: (M, L, K:) of the fem. gender in this sense also, (M, L, Msb,) because meaning mud~apN : (Msb:) pl. A^asonaAnN , (M, L, K,) only. (M, L.) You say rajulN Hadiyvu Als~in~i , meaning (assumed tropical:) A young man. (S, Msb, K, all in art. Hdv .) And jaAwazotu A^asonaAna A^aholi bayotiY (assumed tropical:) [ I have exceeded ] the lives of the people of my house. (L.) And SadaqaniY sin~a bakorihi [and sin~u bakorihi , expl. in art. bkr ]. (L.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) A like, an equal, or a match, in age, of another; (M, L, K;) like tin~N ; (M, L;) as also ↓ saniynN , (M, L, K,) and ↓ siniynN , (L,) or ↓ sanynapN : (M, K:) in this sense also fem.; and [therefore] the dim. is ↓ sunayonapN ; (L;) one says, AiboniY sunayonapu A@bonika [ My son is the equal in age of thy son ]: (El-Kanánee, L:) and the pl. is A^asun~N and A^asonaAnN . (L.) ― -b4- Also (assumed tropical:) A tooth of a minojal [or reaping-hook ]: (M, L, K: *) pl. A^asonaAnN , signifying its A^u$ur . (L and K in art. A$r .) ― -b5- [And (assumed tropical:) A tooth of a comb.] The Arabs say kaA^asonaAni Almu$oTi meaning (assumed tropical:) [ Like the teeth of the comb ] in equality, in respect of any state, or condition: but if they mean equality in respect of evil, they say sawaAsiyapN kaA^asonaAni AlHimaAri [ Equals like the teeth of the ass ]; swAsyp being an anomalous pl. of sawaA='N . (Har p. 39.) ― -b6- And (assumed tropical:) The nib, i. e. the place of paring, of a writingreed: (S, L, K:) [and each lateral half of that part; for] the writing-reed has a right sin~ and a left sin~ : (TA in art. Hrf :) [and ↓ sin~apN occurs in the K voce jilofapN as meaning the point of a writing-reed.] One says, A^aTilo sin~a qalamika wasam~inohaA waHar~ifo qiT~ataka waA^ayominohaA [ Make long the nib, or pared portion, of thy writing-reed, and make it thick (lit. fat ), and make thy mode of cutting the extremity of the nib oblique, and make it to incline towards the right ]. (S, L. *) ― -b7- A tooth [or pin ] of a key [app. of the kind of wooden lock called Dab~ap , q. v.]. (MA.) ― -b8- See also sinosinN . ― -b9- Also, (M, K, and A and K in art. fS ,) or ↓ sin~apN , (S, JM,) A clove, ( faS~N , S and A as syn. with sin~N in art. fS , and JM in explanation of sin~apN in the present art., or faS~apN , S and L in explanation of sin~apN ,) or a Hab~ap [app. here meaning small distinct portion ] of the head [app. here meaning bulb], (M and L and K in explanation of sin~N ,) of garlic. (S, M, A, L, K, JM.) -A2- [Accord. to some,] one says, waqaEa fulaAnN fiY sin~i raA^osihi , meaning Such a one fell into [ what equalled ] the number of his hairs, of good, (M, * L, K, *) and of evil: (L:) or, as some say, into what he willed, or wished, and had authority to decide: (L, K:) but this is a mistranscription: (Meyd:) the correct saying is fiY siY~i raA^osihi , (Az, Meyd, L,) and sawaA='i raA^osihi , meaning he fell into a state of enjoyment, or welfare; (Meyd;) the former sometimes expl. as meaning, [ he lighted upon, or came upon, what equalled ] the number of the hairs of his head, of wealth, or good: (A'Obeyd, Meyd:) or what equalled [ the hairs of ] his head, of abundance of herbage, or of the goods, conveniences, or comforts, of life: (Az, L, and Meyd * on the authority of IAar:) the saying is a prov. (Meyd.) -A3- Als~in~u also signifies The wild bull. (L, K.)

definition: A way, course, rule, mode, or manner, of acting or conduct or life or the like;
sourceDefinition: A way, course, rule, mode, or manner, of acting or conduct or life or the like; syn. TariyqapN , (Mgh, L, Msb,) as also ↓ sananN , (S, L,) and siyrapN ; (S, M, L, Msb, K;) whence the saying, sun~uwA bihimo sun~apa A^aholi AlkitaAbi , expl. in the first paragraph of this art., last sentence but one, (Mgh,) and the saying of the Hudhalee [Khálid Ibn-Zuheyr] cited in the first paragraph of art. syr ; (S;) and this is [said to be] the primary signification; (L;) whether good, or bad; (M, L;) approved or disapproved: (Msb:) or, accord. to Sh, a way [ of acting &c.] that has been instituted, or pursued, by former people, and has become one pursued by those after them; and this, he says, is the primary signification: (L:) it signifies also [particularly] a way of acting &c. that is commended, or approved, and right; wherefore one says, fulaAnN mino A^aholi Als~un~api [ Such a one is of the people of the commended and right way of acting &c.; generally meaning, of those who follow the institutes, or ways, of the Prophet ]; and is from ↓ sananN signifying “ a way, ” or “ road; ” (T, L;) and is also syn. with sananN : (L:) and [the laws, i. e] the statutes, or ordinances, and commands and prohibitions, of God: (Lh, M, L, K:) [also a practice or saying, or the practices and sayings collectively, of Mohammad, or any other person who is an authority in matters of religion, namely, any prophet, or a Companion of Mohammad, (see Kull p. 203,) as handed down by tradition: ] when used unrestrictedly in matters of the law, Als~un~apu means only what the Prophet [ Mohammad ] has commanded, and what has been handed down from him by tradition, [or, as in the JM, and what he forbade, ] and what he has invited to do, by word or deed, of such things as are not mentioned in the Kur-án; wherefore one says, in speaking of the directions, or evidences, of the law, AlkitaAbu waAls~un~apu meaning the Kur-án and the Traditions: (L:) [thus used, it may be rendered the institutes of the Prophet; or his rule or usage: ] or in the law it signifies the way of acting &c. that is pursued in religion without being made obligatory, or necessary; it is what the Prophet persevered in doing, or observing, with omitting, or neglecting, [ it ] sometimes; and if the said persevering is in the way of religious service, it constitutes [ what are termed ] sunanu AlhudaY ; if in the way of custom, sunanu Alz~awaAy^idi : so that sun~apu AlhudaY [ the sun~ap of right direction ] is that of which the observance is a completion of religion, and it is that to the omission, or neglect, whereof attach blame and misdemeanour; and sun~apu Alz~awaAy^idi [ the sun~ap of supererogatory acts ] is that of which the observance is good, but to the omission, or neglect, whereof neither blame nor misdemeanour attaches, such as the ways of the Prophet in his standing and sitting and clothing and eating: (KT:) sunanN is the pl. (Msb.) sun~apu AlA^aw~aliyna , in the Kur xviii. 53, i. e. sun~atunaA fiY AlA^aw~aliyna [ The way pursued by us in respect of the former, or preceding peoples ], means the destruction decreed to befall them; (Jel;) or extirpation; (Bd;) or, as Zj says, their beholding punishment; ( A^an~ahumo EaAyanuwA AlEa*aAba ; [or, as expl. in the K, muEaAyanapu AlEa*aAbi ;]) for the believers in a plurality of gods said, [as is related in the Kur viii. 32,] O God, if this be the truth from Thee, then do Thou rain down upon us stones from heaven. (M, L.) ― -b2- Also Nature; natural, or native, disposition, temper, or other quality or property: (M, L, K:) pl. sunanN . (M, L.) ― -b3- And The face; (M, L, K;) because of its polish and smoothness: (M, L:) or the ball of the cheek ( Hur~u Alwajohi ): or the circuit ( daAy^irap ) of the face: or the form: (M, L, K:) or the form of the face: (S:) or the forehead and two sides thereof: (M, L, K:) all from the meaning of polish and smoothness and evenness: (M, L:) or the principal part of the face; the part thereof in which beauty is generally known to lie: (M in art. Am :) or the side of the cheek: pl. sunanN . (L.) You say, rajulN qabiayHu Als~un~api A man foul, or ugly, in respect of the form, and of what confronts one, of the face. (L.) And huwa A^a$obahu $aYo'K sun~apF waA^um~apF He is the most like thing in form, and face, and in stature. (L.) ― -b4- And The black line, or streak, on the back of the ass. (L.) -A2- Also, (S, K,) or ↓ sin~apN , (so in the L,) A sort of dates, of ElMedeeneh, (S, L, K,) well known. (L.)

definition: A way, or road: (T, L:) the main and middle part thereof;
sourceDefinition: A way, or road: (T, L:) the main and middle part thereof; (A'Obeyd, Mgh, L;) the beaten track, or part along which one travels, thereof; as also ↓ sunanN : (A'Obeyd, L:) the nahoj [i. e. plain, or open, track ] of the road; and so ↓ sunanN and ↓ sununN (M, L, K) and ↓ sinanN : (K:) and, all of these, the course, or direction, of the road: (M, L, K:) but ISd says, [in the M,] I know not ↓ sinanN on any other authority than that of Lh. (L.) One says, tanaH~a Eano sanani AlT~ariyqi (S, L, Msb) and ↓ sunanihi and ↓ sununihi [ Go thou away, or aside, from the main and middle part of the road, or from the beaten track thereof; &c.]: (S, L:) and Eano sanani Alxayoli (S, Msb) from the way of the horses, (Msb,) or from the course, or direction, thereof. (S.) And taraka fulaAnN laka sanana AlT~ariyqi and ↓ suanahu (Lh, M, L) and ↓ sununahu (L) and ↓ sinanahu (Lh, M, L) [respecting which last see what precedes] Such a one left, or has left, to thee the course, or direction, of the road. (Lh, M, L.) And AimoDi EalY sananika and ↓ sunanika (L) or ↓ sununika (M) Go along on thy course. (M, L.) sananN also signifies A way of acting or the like; syn. TariyqapN ; (S, L;) as also sun~apN : (Mgh, L, Msb: see the latter word, in the former half of the paragraph, in two places:) you say, AisotaqaAma fulaAnN EalaY sananK waAHidK [ Such a one went on undeviatingly in one way ]: (S, L, Msb: *) and [in like manner] ↓ jaA='ati Alr~iyHu sanaAy^ina The wind came in one way, (S, K,) in one course, or direction, and one way, (M, L,) not varying: (S, L:) and [similar to the former of these two phrases is the saying] banaY Alqawomu buyuwtahumo EalaY sananK waAHidK i. e. [ The people, or party, built their houses, or constructed their tents, ] in one mode, or manner. (M, L.) Also The aim, or intention, of a man. (ISh, M, * L.) [Accord. to Fei,] Als~ananu also signifies Alwajohu mina AlA^aroDi [by which may be meant The place, or tract, or quarter, of the land, towards which one goes; or it may mean the face, or surface, of the ground ]: and so ↓ sununN and ↓ sunanN . (Msb.) -A2- Als~ananu also signifies AlA_ibilu tasotan~u fiY EadowihaA [app. meaning The camels that leap, spring, or bound, in their running; (see 8;) or rather Als~ananu mina AlA_ibili has this meaning, as appears from what here follows]: (K:) or [a horse, or camel,] that perseveres in his running and advancing and retiring: and one says, jaA='a sananN mina Alxayoli , i. e. $awoTN [app. meaning There came a number of horses running a heat; for $wT in this explanation seems, from the phrase to which it relates and from what immediately precedes the mention of that phrase, to be an inf. n. used as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates, and therefore, agreeably with a common rule, applied to a pl. number as well as to a single individual]: (M, L:) and jaA='a mina Alxayolu sananN laA yurad~u wajohuhu [app. meaning, in like manner, There came, of the horses, a number running a heat, the course of which was not to be turned away ]; (S, L; not expl. in either;) and so, mina AlA_ibili [ of the camels ]. (L.) ― -b2- And Sh explains sananN as applied in a verse of El-Aashà to People, or a party, hastening to fight, or slay. (L.) -A3- Also, [as a quasi-inf. n.,] The leaping, springing, or bounding, [so I here render AisotinaAn , inf. n. of 8, which see for other, similar, meanings,] of camels and of horses. (L. [It is there mentioned in another place, and in the M, as a subst., meaning a quasi-inf.n., from Aisotan~a .])

definition: Cold, or coldness;

definition: Applied to a lion, it means Having his mouth tied, or bound;
sourceDefinition: : see the following paragraph. (Meyd, K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. $ajFA , He was choked; or his throat, or fauces, became obstructed; (S, K;) bihi by it; i. e. a bone or the like. (K.) One says, Ealayoka biAlkaZomi walawo $ajiyta biAlEaZomi [ Keep thou to self-restraint though thou be choked by the bone ]. (TA.) ― -b2- And, [hence, by a metaphor, (see Har p. 33,)] aor. and inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) He grieved, mourned, or lamented; or was sorrowful, sad, or unhappy: (S, Msb:) and he was, or became, anxious, or disquieted in mind. (S.) ― -b3- Also, aor. and inf. n. as above, said of a creditor ( gariym ), He went away, Eanohu [ from him ]. (K. [See 4.]) -A2- $ajaA bayonahumo It was, or became, an occasion of contention, or dispute, or of disagreement, or difference, between them. (K.) -A3- $ajaAhu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. $ajowN , (S, Msb,) [app. originally syn. with A^a$ojaAhu in the first of the senses assigned to the latter in the next paragraph: ― -b2- and hence,] (assumed tropical:) It (anxiety, Msb) grieved him; or caused him to mourn or lament, or to be sorrowful or sad or unhappy; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ A$jAhu . (K.) And, said of wealth ( AlginaY ), inf. n. $ajowN , It excited his griefs, mournings, &c., and his desire. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, and ↓ A$jAhu , (assumed tropical:) It caused him to be mirthful, (Ks, K, TA,) and excited him. (Ks, TA.) Thus each of these verbs has two contr. significations. (K.) But MF observes that Tar~abahu , the explanation here given in the K, is said by the author of the K [in art. Trb ] to denote a lightness arising from joy or grief. (TA.) [Generally, however, it means as rendered above.]

definition: (assumed tropical:) Grieving, mourning, or lamenting;
sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) Grieving, mourning, or lamenting; or sorrowing, sad, or unhappy; applied to a man; (S, Msb;) and $ajiyapN , of the measure faEilapN , applied to a woman: one says, wayolN lil$~ajiY mina AlxaliY~i [mentioned and expl. voce xaAlK , in art. xlw , where each of these epithets is written with teshdeed to the Y ; and likewise in another saying there mentioned]: (S:) or, in this saying, (TA,) it signifies occupied [ by anxiety or grief ]; (K, TA; [in the CK, Al$~ajA is erroneously put for Al$~ajiY ;]) and xaliY~ means “ free [therefrom]: ” so says AZ: and in this instance Al$~ajiY may mean occupied by a bone choking, or obstructing, his throat, or fauces, or by anxiety, and not having found a way of escape therefrom; or by his opponent, or adversary, whom he has been unable to withstand: (TA:) and sometimes one says ↓ $ajiY~N , like as one says HazinN and HaziynN ; though this is rare; (Msb;) it is mentioned in the 'Eyn; but $ajK is more known; and is said by Az to be the chaste form: (TA:) Mbr says, the Y of AlxlY is with teshdeed, and the Y of Al$~ajiY is without teshdeed, (S,) and sometimes this Y is with teshdeed in poetry; (S, K;) but if you make it to be from $ajaAhu , it is ↓ $ajiY~N only, syn. with ma$ojuw~N . (TA.)

definition: (S, O, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (S, O, Msb, K, &c.) and $isiEN (K) and ↓ $isoEan~N , so in some of the copies of the K, (TA,) [thus in my MS. copy of the K, and also in the O,] with an augmentative n , (O, TA,) The qibaAl of the sandal; (K;) [i. e.] the appertenance of the sandal that is attacked, or tied, to its zimaAm ; (S;) [meaning] one of the thongs, or straps, or strips of leather, of the sandal, being that which passes between two toes, of which the [ lower ] end enters the hole, or perforation, that is in the fore part of the sandal, and which is attacked [ at its upper end ] to the zimaAm [or, as it is also called, the $iraAk , a thong, or strap, or strip of leather, extending towards the ankle, and having two arms, (its EaDudaAni ,) which are attacked to the A^u*unaAni (q. v.), or pass through these and unite behind the foot ]: (IAth, TA:) a poet says, referring to camels, ↓ A^aHoduw bihaA munoqaTiEFA $isoEan~iY [ I urge them on by singing to them, with the interdigital thong of my sandal broken ]: (Lth, O, TA:) the pl. of $isoEN is $usuwEN (S, O, Msb, K, TA) and A^a$osaAEN : (O, K, TA:) ISd and Z affirm that it has only the former pl.; but AHei contradicts this: (TA:) the latter pl. [a pl. of pauc.] occurs in the saying of 'Obeyd Ibn-Eiyoob El- 'Amberee, yudiyru naEolayohi liy^al~aA tuEorafaA yajoEalu A^a$osaAEahumaA naHowa AlqafaA [ He turns round his sandals, in order that they may not be known by their prints upon the ground; putting the interdigital thongs thereof in the direction of the back of the neck ]. (O, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] qibaAlu Al$~isoEi signifies (assumed tropical:) The serpent; mentioned by IAar with qibaAlu Al$~ibori . (TA.) ― -b3- And $isoEN also signifies (assumed tropical:) The extremity of a place. (O, K.) One says, HalalonaA $isoEa Ald~ahonaA='i (assumed tropical:) [ We alighted in the extremity of the sandy desert, or of the desert called Ed-Dahnà ]. (O.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) A narrow tract of land. (O, K.) ― -b5- And (tropical:) Somewhat remaining of property or cattle. (IAar, O, K, TA.) And (K) (tropical:) A small quantity or number of property or cattle. (Mohárib, O, K, TA.) One says, lahu $isoEu maAlK (tropical:) He has a small quantity of property, or a small number of cattle; (Mohárib, O, K, TA;) or a small collection of camels and of sheep or goats: (K, TA:) and Fr adds maAlK ↓ $asiyEu [app. in the same sense: but see another explanation of $isoEu maAlK in what follows]. (O.) ― -b6- And (tropical:) The greater portion or number of property or cattle. (El-Mufaddal, O, K, TA.) Thus it has two contr. [?] significations. (K.) One says, *ahaba $isoEu maAlihi (tropical:) The greater portion of his property, or the greater number of his cattle, went, or passed, away. (El-Mufaddal, O, TA.) ― -b7- And fulaAnN $isoEu maAlK (tropical:) Such a one is a good manager of cattle or camels &c.; (S, O, K, TA;) one who keeps assiduously to the tending, or pasturing, thereof: (A, TA:) and Fr says, huwa maAlK ↓ $asiyEu , as syn. with $isoEu maAlK . (TA: [but see above.])

definition: One who scarcely ever, or never, sleeps;
sourceDefinition: One who scarcely ever, or never, sleeps; (S, M, L, K;) as also ↓ $aqi*N ; (S, M, K;) and who has a malignant eye, (S, M,) affecting, or hurting, others therewith; as also ↓ $aqi*N (S, M, K, in the TA $aqo*N ,) and ↓ $aqiy*N : (M:) or who has a strong, or powerful, eye, quickly affecting or hurting [ others therewith ]; (M, L, K;) as also ↓ $aqi*N and ↓ $aqiy*N : (M:) and AlEayoni ↓ $aqi*u one who scarcely ever, or never, sleeps; whom drowsiness does not overcome. (T, L.) ― -b2- Also Driven away, and remote; and so ↓ $aqi*N . (L.) ― -b3- And $aqa*aAnapN A light-spirited woman: (Th, M, L:) foul, or obscene, in her speech; clamorous, and foul-tongued. (T, L.) -A2- Also The male chameleon; (M, L, K;) and so ↓ $aqi*N and ↓ $iqo*N and ↓ $uqo*N : or all these words signify a slender and compact male chameleon, with a small head, that cleaves to the trunk of the kind of tree called EiDaAh : (M, L:) pl. $iqo*aAnN (M, L, K) and $aqaA*aY : (M:) the former pl. like kirowaAnN , pl. of karawaAnN ; (L;) and also used as a sing., meaning a male chameleon; (Th, M;) thus used by a poetess; (M:) also ↓ $iqo*N (S, M, L, K) and ↓ $uqo*N (M, L) and ↓ $uqa*N (M, L, K) and ↓ $aqo*N (K) the young one of a chameleon: (Lh, S, M, L, K:) pl. $iqo*aAnN (S, M, L, K) and $aqaA*aY : (M, L, K:) the former pl. like SinowaAnN , pl. of SinowN . (S.) A poet says, describing asses, raA^ati Al$~aqaA*aY taSoTaliY faraEato bihaA Hat~aY A_i*aA And they pastured therein until the heat became vehement and they saw the male chameleons thirsty, desiring to go to water, and repairing to the sun: some say, that $qA*Y here signifies moths, ( faraA$ ), but this is a mistake. (M, L.) $iqo*aAnN also signifies The animals called Dab~ and waral and TuHan and saAm~u A^aboraS and das~aAsap : and the sing. is ↓ $iqo*apN : (M, L:) or any small animals that creep or walk upon the earth, and venomous or noxious reptiles and the like: (M, L, K:) sing. ↓ $aqi*apN (M, L) and ↓ $iqa*N , (M,) or ↓ $aqi*N , (L,) and ↓ $uqa*N , (M,) or ↓ $aqa*N ; (L;) but it does not appear how ↓ $aqi*apN can be a sing. of $iqo*aAnN unless the augmentative letter be regarded as elided. (M, L.) ― -b2- Also The wolf; (M, L, K;) and so ↓ $aqo*aAnN (Th, M, L, K) and ↓ $uqo*N , (M, L,) or ↓ $iqo*N , (K,) or ↓ $aqo*N . (TA.) ― -b3- Also The hawk; syn. SaqorN ; (M, L;) and so ↓ $aqo*aAnN (Th, M, L) and ↓ $uqo*N , (M, L,) or ↓ $aqo*N . (TA.) ― -b4- And $iqo*aAnN [the pl.] also signifies The young ones of the kinds of birds called HbaAraY and qaTFA (M, L, K) and the like. (M, L.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, K,) aor. , inf. n. $an~N , (Mgh, TA,) He scattered the water; (S, K;) or poured it scatteringly; (Mgh;) or poured it and scattered it; or, as some say, poured it in a manner like that which is termed naDoHN [i. e. sprinkling ]; (TA;) EalaY Al$~araAbi [ upon the wine, or beverage ]: (S, K:) san~ahu signifies “ he poured it gently. ” (TA.) And $an~ati AlEayonu damoEahaA The eye poured forth its tears; (TA;) or sent forth [or shed ] its tears; like $al~at , (Lh, TA in art. $l ,) which is asserted by Yaakoob to be formed by substitution [of l for n ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And $an~a bisaloHihi (AA, S, * TA) He cast forth his excrement, or dung, in a thin [ and scattered ] state: and one says of the HubaAraY [or bustard] ta$un~u bi*aroqihaA [ It casts forth its dung in a thin and scattered state ]. (AA, TA.) ― -b4- And $an~a Ealayoihi diroEahu He put (lit. poured ) on him his coat of mail. (TA.) -A2- $an~a Aljamalu mina AlEaTa$i , [aor. accord. to general rule ,] The camel became dried up [ like a $an~ , q. v.,] from thirst. (TA.) And $an~ati Alxiroqapu The rag became dried up. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A skin, (Msb,) or a water-skin, (S, Mgh,) or a small water skin, (K,) or, as some say, any vessel made of skin, (TA,) applied by a poet to a dalow [or leathern bucket ], (Ham p. 602,) that is old, and worn out; (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA;) and so ↓ $an~apN ; (S, K;) but app. one that is small: (S: [in which this addition to the explanation seems to relate peculiarly to the latter word: see an ex. of this latter word in some verses cited in the first paragraph of art. sqY :]) or both signify an old water-skin; as also ↓ mi$an~N : (MA:) and ↓ $ananN , also, signifies an old, worn-out, water-skin: (TA:) pl. (Mgh.) A butt, at which one shoots or casts: probably because an old water-skin was sometimes used as a butt]: pl. as above. definition: A camel in a state between that of the lean, or emaciated, and that of the fat;
sourceDefinition: A camel in a state between that of the lean, or emaciated, and that of the fat; (S;) so called because some of his fatness has gone: (Aboo-Kheyreh, TA:) one says mahozuwlN ; then munoqK , when he has become a little fat; then $anuwnN ; then saAH~N ; and then muvaroTimN , when fat in the utmost degree: (Lh, TA:) so says Aboo-Ma'add El-Kilá- bee. (TA in art. sH .) [But it is said that] it signifies also Lean, or emaciated; (K;) applied to a beast: (TA:) and fat: thus having two contr. meanings. (K.) ― -b2- Also Hungry: (S, K:) applied in this sense by Et-Tirimmáh to a wolf, because this animal is not described as fat or lean. (S.)

sourceDefinition: A nature; or a natural, a native, or an innate, disposition or temper or the like; syn. TabiyEapN , (S, Mgh, K,) and xuluqN , (S,) and sajiy~apN : (TA:) and a custom, habit, or wont: (Mgh, K:) [pl. $anaA$inu .] One says fiyhi mino A^abiyhi $anaA$inu In him are habits [or natural dispositions inherited] from his father. (TA.) Hence, $ino$inapN A^aEorifuhaA mino A^axozamo [ A natural disposition, or a habit, which I know, as inherited from Akhzam ]: (S, Meyd, Mgh:) or, accord. to one relation, ni$oni$apN , which is app. formed by transposition from $ino$inapN : (Meyd:) a prov.: (Meyd, Mgh:) [of its origin there are different explanations: see Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 658, and Har pp. 591 and 596:] A^axozamu is the proper name of a man: (Meyd, Mgh, &c.:) or accord. to Lth, it is an epithet applied to a penis; one says kamarapN xazomaA='u “ a glans of a penis having a short frænum, ” and *akarN A^axozamu ; and $n$np means the dropping of water [i. e., in this case, of the seminal fluid]: (Meyd:) the prov. is applied in relation to nearness of resemblance. (Meyd, Mgh.) -A2- Also A bit of flesh-meat, as much as is chewed at once; syn. muDogapN : or a piece of flesh-meat; (K, TA;) and so ni$oni$apN : on the authority of AA. (TA.) ― -b2- And [the pl.] $anaA$inu signifies Bones; like sanaAsinu . (IAar, L in art. sn .)

sourceDefinition: is pl. of $awaApN : [or rather the former is a coll. gen. n. of which the latter is the n. un.:] the latter signifies The skin of the head: (S, TA:) so [accord. to some] in the Kur lxx. 16: (TA:) or the exterior of the skin of the head, in which grows the hair: (Aboo-Safwán, TA in art. b$r :) and some say, the exterior of all, or of any part, of the skin: (TA in the present art.:) and the former signifies the arms or hands and the legs or feet, or the fore and hind legs, (S, K,) and (K) the extremities (Msb, K) collectively, (K,) and the head of a human being, (S,) or the qiHof of the head [i. e. the bone above the brain, or a separate portion of the skull, or a distinct bone of the skull ], (K,) but of a horse the legs, not the head, because one says Eabolu Al$~awaY [i. e. thick in the legs ], for this cannot relate to the head of the horse, (S,) and any part that is not a [ vital ] place [i. e.] where a wound causes death (S, Msb, K) such [ for instance ] as the legs. (Msb.) vaAlibapu Al$~awaY means A woman having cracked, or chapped, feet. (S and K in art. vlb .) ― -b2- It is also a subst. [app. meaning a quasi-inf. n.] from A^a$owaAhu [q. v.] as said of a shooter or caster: (TA:) [and hence] the saying (S, TA) of the Hudhalee, (S, [accord. to the TA, Khálid Ibn-Zuheyr,]) faA_in~a mina Alqawoli Al~atiY laA $awaY lahaA A_i*aA zal~a Zahori All~isaAni A@nofilaAtuhu means (assumed tropical:) [ And, or for ] verily of speech is that sentence ( kalimap , a word understood,) which does not hit a place where a wound will not occasion death, [i. e. which does not miss its object, when its escaping from the upper surface of the tongue is quick, ] but which kills. (S, TA.) And $awFY is used [app. in like manner, as a quasi-inf. n.,] in the case of anything that has missed an object of aim, though there be to it [really] no place where a wound would occasion death nor anything that is [properly] termed $awFY [as meaning a place where a wound will not occasion death]. (TA.) And [hence] it signifies (assumed tropical:) A mistake; syn. xaTaA^N . (TA.) ― -b3- Also (tropical:) A thing, (S,) or an affair, (K,) that is paltry, mean, despicable, or of no account or weight or worth: (S, K, * TA:) in this sense, from the same word as signifying the “ extremities ” [of an animal]. (IAth, TA.) Hence, in a trad. of Mujáhid, kul~u maA A^aSaAba AlS~aAy^ima $awFY A_il~aA Algayobapa (tropical:) [ Everything that befalls the faster is a matter of no account, except absence of mind ]; i. e. nothing that befalls the faster annuls his fast except Algybp , for this does annul it. (TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) The worse, or viler, sort of cattle, (S, K, TA,) of camels, and of sheep or goats; and the small, or young, thereof. (TA.) [See also $uwaAyapN .] ― -b5- And (assumed tropical:) A remainder, or remaining portion. (TA.) [See, again, $uwaAyapN .] ― -b6- Also i. q. A_iboqaA='N (assumed tropical:) [The making, or causing, or suffering, to remain; or, perhaps, to continue in life, and if it mean thus, it may be from the same word in a sense expl. above, for the animal that one hits in a part that is not vital is suffered to continue in life]. (TA.)

definition: Having a loud cry or voice;
sourceDefinition: Having a loud cry or voice; as also ↓ Sad~aAHN ; both applied to a cock [meaning loudcrowing ]; (A;) [and to a crow as meaning loudcroaking ]; and so the former applied to an ass [meaning loud-braying ]; and so ↓ SayodaHN applied to a horse [meaning loud-neighing ]; (S, K;) [and app. also applied to a camel as meaning loudbraying, for] SayodaHu was the name of the she-camel of Dhu-r-Rummeh: (S, K:) or SaduwHN (L, K) and ↓ Sad~aAHN (L) and ↓ SayodaHN and ↓ SayodaAHN and ↓ miSodaHN (L, K) signify that raises his voice much in singing or otherwise; (L;) [app. thus applied to a bird, and (assumed tropical:) to a man; (see 1;)] or that cries out vehemently, or much; or has a loud, or strong, voice; (L, K;) and so ↓ SayodaHiY~N . (Ham p. 558.) [Hence,] ↓ qayonapN SaAdiHapN (tropical:) [ A loud-voiced female singer ]. (A, TA.) And ↓ HaAdK SayodaHN (tropical:) [ A loud-voiced man urging camels by his singing ]. (A, TA.) And ↓ mizoharN Sad~aAHN (tropical:) [ A loud-sounding lute ]. (S, A.)

definition: , (S, M, Msb,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Msb,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. SarFY , (M, Msb,) said of water, It remained, or stagnated, long: or it remained long, and became altered [ for the worse ]: (S, Msb:) or, said of water and of milk, it remained so that its flavour became altered [ for the worse ]: (M:) or, said of milk, it remained undrawn from the udder, so that its flavour became bad, or corrupt. (TA.) And SariYa Ald~amoEu The tears collected [ in the eye ] and did not run. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Sariyati Aln~aAqapu , (Fr, M, Msb, TA,) aor. as above, (Msb,) and so the inf. n.; (M, Msb, TA;) but Ibn-Buzurj says Sarat , aor. ; (TA;) The she-camel's milk became collected in her udder; (M, Msb, TA;) as also ↓ A^aSorat . (M, TA.) ― -b3- And SariYa fiY yadihi , (S, M, IKtt, TA,) with kesr; (S, TA;) or SaraY fiY yadihi ;) (thus accord. to the K;) He (a man) remained in his hand, as a pledge, (S, M, K, TA,) held in custody. (S, K, TA.) ― -b4- And SirYi [thus written without any syll. sign, app. SriY ,] i. q. AinoqaTaEa [ It, or he, became cut off, cut short, or stopped; &c.: quasi-pass. of SaraAhu in one of the senses of the latter]: from IAar. (TA.) -A2- SaraAhu , (IKtt, Msb, TA,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. SaroYN , (IKtt, Msb, TA,) He confined it, namely, water, in a resting-place or a vessel; and in like manner, milk, and tears: (IKtt, TA:) or he collected it, namely, water, and it remained long and became altered [ for the worse ], or remained or stagnated long; and in like manner, but in an intensive sense, ↓ Sr~Ahu . (Msb.) One says also of cows [and the like], taSoriY All~abana fiY DuruwEihin~a They confine and collect the milk in their udders. (TA.) And [of a man] one says, SaraY AlmaA='a fiY Zahorihi zamaAnFA He retained the mA' [i. e. sperma ] in his back a long time, (S, M, K, *) by abstaining from sexual intercourse. (M, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] SarayotuhaA , (M, Msb,) aor. , inf. n. SaroYN ; (Msb;) and ↓ Sar~ayotuhaA , (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. taSoriyapN , (S, Msb,) but the latter verb has an intensive meaning; (Msb;) and ↓ A^aSorayotuhaA ; (M;) namely, a ewe or she-goat, (S,) or a she-camel, (M, Msb,) and any other milch animal, (M,) I caused the milk to collect in her udder, (S, M, Msb,) by abstaining from milking her for some days. (S, M.) -A3- Also, i. e. SaraAhu , (M, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. SaroYN , (M,) i. q. qaTaEahu [ He cut it off, cut it short, or stopped it; &c.]; (M, K;) namely, a thing. (M.) You say, SaraY bawolahu , inf. n. as above, meaning qaTaEahu [ He, or it, cut short, or stopped, his urine ]. (S.) And Sarayotu AlmaA='a [app. I cut short, or stopped, the drawing of the water; for it is expl. as said] A_i*aA A@sotaqayota vum~a qaTaEota . (S.) And maA yaSoriyka min~iY A^aYo EabodiY , occurring in a trad., means What cuts short ( yaqoTaEu ) thine asking of Me [ O my servant ]? (TA.) ― -b2- And i. q. dafaEahu [ He repelled it ]. (M, K.) One says, SaraY A@ll~`hu Eanohu $ar~ahu i. e. dafaEa [ God repelled, or may God repel, from him his, or its, evil, or mischief ]. (S.) ― -b3- And i. q. manaEahu [ He prevented it, &c.]. (S, M, K.) Dhu-r-Rummeh says, wawad~aEona mu$otaAqFA A^aSabona fuw^aAdahu hawaAhun~a A_ino lamo yaSorihi A@ll~`hu qaAtiluho [ And they bade farewell to one affected with desire, whose heart they had smitten; the love of them, if God had not prevented it, had been his slayer ]. (S. [But this verse may be well rendered as an ex. of SaraAhu in the sense next following, which is also a meaning of manaEahu : in the M, it is cited as an ex. of SaraAhu in the sense of dafaEahu .]) ― -b4- Said of God, (M,) He protected, defended, guarded, or preserved, him: (M, K:) or (M) He saved him (M, K) from destruction, or perdition: (K:) or (M) He sufficed him: (M, K:) or He aided him. (TA.) ― -b5- SaraY bayonahumo , (K,) or SaraY maA bayonahumo , (S, M,) He decided [ between them, or the case between them ]; (S, K;) namely, persons who had applied to him as a judge: (S:) or he rectified, or adjusted, the case between them. (M.) -A4- SaraY also signifies EaTafa [ He bent, or inclined ]: (K, TA:) [app. intrans., or trans. by means of bi , for] a poet uses the phrase Sarayona biAlA^aEonaAqi [ They bent, or inclined, with the necks ]. (TA.) [But it is said in the TK that SaraAhu means EaTafahu He bent, or inclined, it. ] Accord. to Ibn-Buzurj, Sarati Aln~aAqapu EunuqahaA means The she-camel raised her neck by reason of the heaviness of the burden. (TA.) -A5- Also He preceded, or went before; syn. taqad~ama . (IAar, K.) [Accord. to the TK, one says SaraY Alqawoma , meaning taqad~amahumo He preceded, or went before, the people, or party. ] ― -b2- And [ the contr., i. e.] He receded, or retreated; or became, or remained, or lagged, behind; syn. taA^ax~ara . (IAar, K.) [Accord. to the TK, one says SaraY Eanohumo , meaning He receded, or retreated, from them; &c.]. ― -b3- Also He, or it, was, or became, high; syn. EalaA . (IAar, K.) ― -b4- And the contr., i. e. He, or it, was, or became, low; syn. safula . (IAar, K.)

definition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) an inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) an inf. n. used as an epithet, (Msb,) and ↓ SirFY , (S, M, K,) [and Freytag adds ↓ SurFY , as from the K, in which I do not find it,] Water remaining, or stagnating, long, accord. to Fr; (S;) or that has remained, or stagnated, long: (Msb:) or water remaining long, (K,) or that has remained long, and become altered [ for the worse ], (S, M, Msb,) accord. to AA. [And SalodN has a similar meaning.] You say, Saladati AlA^aroDu , and ↓ A^aSoladat , The land was, or became, hard: (K:) or (tropical:) so that it produced no plants, or herbage: (TA:) and Salada AlmakaAnu , and ↓ A^aSolada , (M, TA,) the place was, or became, hard: (TA:) or (assumed tropical:) produced no plants, or herbage. (M.) And Salada Ealayohi Aljabalu , aor. , inf. n. SalodN ; and Saluda , [aor. ,] inf. n. SalaAdapN and SuluwdapN and SuluwdN ; The mountain, or rock, baffled him, namely, a welldigger, [ by its hardness, ] and resisted his efforts. (M.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Salada Alz~anodu , (M, K, and so in some copies of the S,) aor. , inf. n. SalodN ; (M;) or Salida , with kesr to the l , aor. , inf. n. SuluwdN ; (AZ, S;) The znd [or piece of stick, or wood, for producing fire ] gave a sound without emitting fire; (S, M, K;) and ↓ ASld signifies [the same, or] it emitted no fire. (Ham p. 407.) ― -b3- And [hence,] Saladato zinaAduhu [lit. “ His pieces of stick, or wood, for producing fire, gave a sound without emitting fire ”] means (tropical:) He was, or became, niggardly, tenacious, penurious, or avaricious: (AA, L, TA:) and Saluda , alone, aor. , (M, A, K,) inf. n. SalaAdapN ; (M, A;) and Salada , (M, A,) aor. , (M,) or , (A,) inf. n. SalodN , (M,) or SuluwdN ; (A;) and ↓ Sl~d , inf. n. taSoliydN ; (K;) signify the same: (M, K:) or he was, or became, very niggardly &c. (A.) ― -b4- And Saladato SalaEatuhu , or SaloEatuhu , (accord. to different copies of the K, in the TA the former,) The bald place on the front of his head shone, or glistened. (K, TA.) Salada is also used in the same sense, in a trad., in relation to milk flowing forth. (TA.) ― -b5- And one says, jaA='a bimaraqK yaSolidu , and bilabanK yaSolidu , meaning He brought broth, and milk, containing little oily, or greasy, matter, and much water: for yaSolitu . (T in art. (K.) ― -b9- Salada , (M,) or Salada fiY Aljabali , (K,) aor. , inf. n. SalodN , said of a mountain-goat, (M,) He ascended the mountain. (TA.) -A2- Salada Als~aAy^ila (assumed tropical:) He gave nothing to the asker, or beggar. (L.)

definition: Hard and smooth;
sourceDefinition: Hard and smooth; (S, M, A, K;) as also ↓ SilodN (K) and ↓ SaluwdN (M) and ↓ SaliydN (A) and ↓ A^aSoladu ; (M;) applied to a stone; (S, M, A;) and so the first applied to land or ground ( A^aroD ); (S;) and to a solid hoof, as also ↓ SilodimN and ↓ SulaAdimN , which last is of the measure fuEaAlimN accord. to Kh, but fuEaAlilN accord. to others; (M;) and to a side of the forehead, (S, M,) or thus applied meaning smooth and tough; (L;) and to a head, as also ↓ SulaAdimN , (M,) or thus applied meaning (tropical:) upon which no hair grows: (A:) and ↓ SalawodadN , (M, K,) which is of an extr. form, (M,) has the first of the significations above, (K,) or signifies [simply] hard: (M:) the pl. of SalodN (M, L) and of ↓ SaluwdN (M) is A^aSolaAdN . (M, L.) ― -b2- Also applied to a place, ( makaAnN , M,) and SalodapN applied to land, ( A^aroDN , A,) (tropical:) That produces no plants, or herbage. (M, A.) And A^aSolaAdu Aljabiyni (tropical:) The part of the side of the forehead upon which is no hair: likened to smooth stone. (A Heyth.) ― -b3- [Hence,] HajarN SalodN and ↓ SaluwdN (tropical:) A stone that will not emit fire: (L, TA:) and ↓ zanodN SaluwdN (M, A) and ↓ SaAlidN and ↓ Sal~aAdN and ↓ miSolaAdN (M) [and ↓ muSolidN ] (tropical:) [ A piece of stick, or wood, for producing fire ] that gives a sound, (M,) not emitting fire: (M, A:) and ↓ EuwdN Sal~aAdN (tropical:) Wood, or a stick, from which fire cannot be produced. (T, L, K. *) ― -b4- And farasN SalodN (K) and ↓ SaluwdN (S, M, A, K) (tropical:) A horse that does not sweat: (S, A, K:) such a horse is discommended: (K:) or slow to sweat: or having little seminal fluid: and slow in impregnating. (M.) ― -b5- And rajulN SalodN (M) and ↓ SaluwdN (M, A) and ↓ A^aSoladu (S, M, A, K) (tropical:) A niggardly, tenacious, penurious, or avaricious, man: (S, M, K:) or a man very niggardly &c. (A.) ― -b6- And naAqapN SalodapN (tropical:) A hardy, strong, enduring she-camel. (K.) And xayolN SilaAdN (tropical:) Hard, hardy, or strong, horses. (A.) [And ↓ SilodaAmN , also, signifies Robust, or strong. (Freytag, from Jereer.)]

definition: A courageous lord or chief;
sourceDefinition: A courageous lord or chief; (S, L, K;) as also ↓ SinodidN : (K:) or a great, or big, and courageous, lord or chief: (A:) or a great, or big, and courageous, king: (M:) or the former, (As, IAar, L,) or ↓ the latter, (K,) a noble lord or chief: (As, L, K:) or a liberal, bountiful, munificent, or generous, lord or chief: or a clement, or forbearing, lord or chief: (IAar, L, K:) a defender of an army: (IAar, L:) jamaAEapu AlEasokari , by which the pl. AlS~anaAdiydu is expl. in the K, is a mistake for HumaApu AlEasokari , the words used by IAar: (TA:) a nobleman: a great man: (L:) or a great chief: (Kf:) one who presides over a people and their affairs of importance and things in general: or a lord, or chief, eminent among his people, possessing the qualities of courage and liberality or munificence or generosity, who overcomes those that act with hostility and opposition towards him: (MF:) pl. SanaAdiydu . (IAar, A, L.) Accord. to some, the n is augmentative; and the word is derived from AlS~ad~u , “ the act of turning away; ” and seems to have been formed to denote an intensive signification. (MF.) Also Overcoming, (K, TA,) and great. (TA.) daA='u AlS~anaAdiydi is The disease called *aAtu Aljanobi . (T in art. jnb .) ― -b2- Also A calamity; a misfortune; or a great, or formidable, event: (TA:) pl. as above. (S, M, A, K.) Hence the saying of El-Hasan, naEuw*u biA@ll~`hi mino SanaAdiydi Alqadari We seek protection by God from the calamities, &c., of destiny: (S, M: *) or from its great and overpowering afflictions. (L.) ― -b3- Also, (accord. to the TA,) or ↓ SinodidN , (accord. to the K,) An isolated ledge of a mountain. (K, TA.) ― -b4- riyHN SinodiydN (tropical:) Violent wind. (A, K.) ― -b5- barodN SinodiydN (tropical:) Vehement, or intense, cold. (A, K.) ― -b6- One says, mar~ato EalayonaA SanaAdiydu mino barodK (tropical:) Times of intense cold befell us. (A.) [See also another ex. voce SaxadaAnN .] ― -b7- And Har~N SinodiydN (tropical:) Vehement, or intense, heat. (A.) One says yawomN HaAmiY AlSinodiydi , (Th, M, L,) or AlS~anaAdiydi , (A, K,) A day of vehement, or intense, heat. (Th, M, A, L, K.) ― -b8- gayovN SinodiydN (tropical:) Rain consisting of large drops: (S, K:) or that falls in large quantity: pl. guyuwvN SanaAdiydu . (A.) And one says, ramati Als~amaA='u biSanaAdiydi Albaradi (tropical:) The sky cast down large hail-stones. (A.) ― -b9- AlS~anaAdiydu mina Als~aHaAbi (assumed tropical:) Great clouds: (M:) or clouds that pour forth much rain, in large drops. (L.)

sourceDefinition: A sign for the guidance of travellers, consisting of stones, (AA, S, IAth, Msb,) set up (IAth, Msb) in the way (Msb) in an unknown desert: (IAth:) or a stone that is a sign [ for guidance ] in the way: (M, K:) or an elevated sign of the way, set up in rugged ground: (M:) pl. SuwFY (AA, S, M, IAth, Msb) and pl. pl. A^aSowaA='N , (M, Msb, K,) the latter like A^aroTaAbN pl. of ruTabN , (Msb, TA,) or, as some say, this is a pl., not a pl. pl. (TA.) It is said in a trad., A_in~a liloA_isolaAmi SuwFY wamanaArFA kamanaAri AlT~ariyqi (assumed tropical:) [ Verily ElIslám has signs and marks of guidance like those of the way ]. (S.) ― -b2- Hence [the pl.] A^FSowaA='N is applied to signify Graves: (S:) occurring in a trad. in this sense. (TA.) ― -b3- And the sing., (S, K,) accord. to As, (S,) signifies Rugged and elevated ground, (S, K,) but inferior to a mountain: (S:) or an elevated and a rugged spot, upon which, sometimes, stones are set up in order that one may be directed thereby to the right way; like vuw~apN . (M in art. vw .) ― -b4- And A place of varying, or of coming and going, ( muxotalaf ) of the wind: (S, K:) a poet says, (namely, Imra-el- Keys, TA,) wahab~ato lahu riyHN bimuxotalafi AlS~uwaY [meaning, if the explanation be correct, and the citation appropriate, And a wind blew them (referring to the word jamor , i. e. live coals, in a verse immediately preceding) in the place of varying of the places of varying of the wind ]: (S:) but Aboo-Zekereeyà, in the margin of his book [or his copy of the S], throws doubt upon the word meaning “ wind ” [in this explanation]. definition: [seems to signify, properly, A disposition to bite ].
sourceDefinition: [seems to signify, properly, A disposition to bite ]. ― -b2- [Hence,] Aln~aAqapu bijin~i DiraAsihaA means (assumed tropical:) The she-camel is in the case of the recentness of her bringing forth, when she defends her young one; from the epithet DaruwsN ; (S, Meyd, O; but in the S and O, hiYa , referring to the she-camel, is put in the place of AlnAqp ;) and is a prov., applied to the man whose nature is evil on the occasion of his defending. (Meyd.) And one says, Ait~aqi Aln~aAqapa bijin~i DiraAsihaA , meaning (tropical:) Beware thou of the she-camel in the case of the recentness of her bringing forth, and of her evil disposition towards him who approaches her, by reason of her attachment to her young one. (A, TA.) [In the TA, in art. jn , this saying is mentioned with DiraAmihaA in the place of DiraAsihaA : the former may perhaps be another reading; but I rather think that it is a mistranscription for the latter. And in the present art. in the TA, it is added that Sgh has mentioned (app. in the TS, for he has not done so in the O,) El-Báhilee's having explained AlD~iraAsu as meaning siyomN lhm ; and that it is likewise explained in the T as meaning siyomN : but I know no such word as siyomN ; nor do I know any word of which it is likely to be a mistranscription, though I have diligently searched for such. This word siyomN has been altered by the copyist in each instance in the TA; so that it seems to have been indistinctly written by the author.] ― -b3- [Hence also] DiraAsu AlHarobi (assumed tropical:) The biting of war. (Ham p. 532.)

definition: The wild [ species of lote-tree called ] sidor [q.
sourceDefinition: The wild [ species of lote-tree called ] sidor [q. v.]: (S, O, K:) or such of the sidor as are watered only by the rain; (M, K:) the sidor of the mountains, which is thinner in its wood than that of the rivers: AHn says, it grows in the plain, or soft, tracts, and in the rugged; and the bow that is made of it, when it is pared, is pared so as to be thick, in order that it may be stronger, because of the lightness of its wood: (M:) n. un. with p . (S, M, O, K.) [See also EuboriY~N , and EumoriY~N .] ― -b2- Also Another species of tree; (M, K;) AHn says, it is a tree of the shrub-kind, found in the borders of El-Yemen, rising to the height of a cubit, in its manner of growth like the cypress, and having a yellow [ fruit of the sort called a ] baramap , of a very pungent odour, so that its odour comes to you before you reach it: it is not of the sidor thus called. (M.)

definition: , aor. , inf. n. TaboEN , He sealed, stamped, imprinted, or impressed; syn. xatama : (Msb:) [and, as now used, he printed a book or the like:] taboEN and xatomN both signify the making an impression...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. TaboEN , He sealed, stamped, imprinted, or impressed; syn. xatama : (Msb:) [and, as now used, he printed a book or the like:] taboEN and xatomN both signify the making an impression in, or upon, clay and the like: (S, Mgh, O, K:) or, as Er-Rághib says, the impressing a thing with the engraving of the signet and stamp: (TA in this art. and in art. xtm : [see more in the first paragraph of the latter art:]) and he says also that TaboEN signifies the figuring a thing with some particular figure; as in the case of the TaboE of the die for stamping coins, and the TaboE of coins [themselves]: but that it is more general in signification than xatomN , and more particular than naqo$N ; as will be shown by what follows: accord. to Aboo-Is-hák the Grammarian, TaboEN and xatomN both signify the covering over a thing, and securing oneself from a thing's entering it: and IAth says [in like manner] that they held TaboEN to be syn. with rayonN [inf. n. of raAna ]: but Mujáhid says that rayonN denotes less than TaboEN ; and TaboEN , less than A_iqofaAlN [or the “ closing with a lock: ” this he says with reference to a phrase in the Kur xlvii. 26]. (TA.) You say, TabaEa AlkitaAba , (Mgh, Msb,) and TabaEa EalaY AlkitaAbi , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, *) He sealed ( xatama , S, Mgh, Msb, K,) the writing, or letter. (S, Mgh, Msb.) And TabaEa He branded, or otherwise marked, the sheep, or goat. (O. [See TaAbaEN .]) And TabaEa A@ll~`hu EalaY qalobihi (tropical:) God sealed [or set a seal upon ] his [i. e. an unbeliever's] heart, so that he should not heed admonition, nor be disposed to that which is good; (Mgh;) or so that belief should not enter it: (O:) [and in like manner, xatama Ealayohi , q. v.:] in this, regard is had to the TaboE , and the TabiyEap , which is the natural constitution or disposition; for it denotes the characterizing of the soul with some particular quality or qualities, either by creation or by habit, and more especially by creation. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b2- Also He began to make, or manufacture, a thing: and he made [a thing] as in instances here following. (Mgh.) You say, TabaEa mina AlT~iyni jar~apF He made, [or fashioned, or moulded, ] of the clay, a jar. (S, O, K.) And TabaEa All~abina , (Mgh, TA,) and Als~ayofa , (S, Mgh, O, K,) and Ald~irohamu , (S, O, K,) He made (S, Mgh, O, K) [ the crude bricks, and the sword, and the dirhem ]: or TabaEa Ald~araAhima he struck (Mgh, Msb) with the die (Msb) [i. e. coined, or minted, ] the dirhems, or money. (Mgh, Msb.) And [hence] one says, Tabaqahu A@ll~`hu EalaY AlA^amori , aor. and inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) God created him with an adaptation, or a disposition, to the thing, affair, state, condition, or case; or adapted him, or disposed him, by creation, [or nature ], thereto. (TA.) And TubiEa EalaY Al$~aYo'i (assumed tropical:) He (a man, O, TA) was created with an adaptation, or a disposition, to the thing; or was adapted, or disposed, by creation [or nature ], thereto; syn. jubila , (IDrd, O, K, TA,) or fuTira . (Lh, TA.) ― -b3- Also, (aor. as above, TA, and so the inf. n., O, TA,) He filled (Er-Rághib, O, K, TA) a measure for corn or the like, (Er-Rághib, TA,) or a leathern bucket, (O, K, TA,) and a skin, (O, TA,) &c.; (O;) and so ↓ Tb~E , (S, O, K,) inf. n. taTobiyEN : (S, O:) because the quantity that fills it is a sign that prevents the taking a portion of what is in it [without the act's being discovered]. (Er-Rághib, TA.) ― -b4- And TabaEa qafaAhu , (IAar, O, K,) inf. n. as above, (IAar, O,) He struck the back of his neck with his hand; (IAar, O, K;) i. e. the back of the neck of a boy: if with the ends of the fingers, one says, qa*~a qafaAhu . (IAar, O.) ― -b5- maA A^adoriY mino A^ayona TabaEa means I know not whence he came forth; syn. TalaEa . (TA.) -A2- TabiEa , (aor. ,] inf. n. TabaEN , said of a sword, It was, or became, rusty, or overspread with rust: (S:) or very rusty, or overspread with much rust. (K, TA: from an explanation of the aor.: but this is written in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K, and in the O, yuTobaEu . [An explanation of TabaEN in the O and K confirms the reading yaTobaEu ; and another confirmation thereof will be found in what follows in this paragraph.]) ― -b2- Said of a thing, (Msb,) or of a garment, or piece of cloth, (TA,) inf. n. TabaEN , It was, or became, dirty; (Msb, TA;) and ↓ tT~bE is likewise said [in the same sense] of a garment, or piece of cloth. (M and TA voce raAna , in art. ryn .) ― -b3- Said of a man, (assumed tropical:) He was or became, filthy or foul [ in character ]. (S.) And (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, sluggish, lazy, or indolent. (S.) One says of a man, yaTobaEu , (O, K,) like yaforaHu , (K,) meaning (assumed tropical:) He has no penetrative energy, sharpness, or effectiveness, in the affairs that are the means, or causes, of attaining honour, like the sword that is overspread with much rust. (O, K.) -A3- TubiEa , (O, K,) inf. n. TaboEN , (O,) said of a man, (assumed tropical:) He was rendered [or pronounced ] filthy or foul [ in character ]; (O, K;) on the authority of Sh; (O;) and so TabiEa , like fariHa ; (TA as on the authority of Sh; [but this I think doubtful;]) and disgraced, or dishonoured: (K:) and ↓ Tub~iEa , (O, TA,) inf. n. taTobiyEN , (TA,) he was rendered [or pronounced ] filthy or foul [ in character ], (O, TA,) and blamed, or discommended. (O.)

definition: , originally an inf.
sourceDefinition: , originally an inf. n., (S,) signifies (assumed tropical:) A nature; or a natural, a native, or an innate, disposition or temper or the like; or an idiosyncrasy; syn. sajiy~apN (S, O, K, TA) or jibil~apN (Msb) and xaliyqapN ; (TA;) to which a man is adapted by creation; (S, O, Msb, K, TA;) [as though it were stamped, or impressed, upon him;] as also ↓ TabiyEapN ; (S, O, K, TA;) or this signifies his mizaAj [i. e. constitution, or temperament, or aggregate natural constituents ], composed of the [ four ] humours; (Msb; [see mizaAjN ;]) and ↓ TibaAEN ; (S, O, K, TA;) or this last signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (O,) with the article Al prefixed to it, what is, or are, constituted in us in consequence of food and drink &c. ( maA ruk~iba fiynaA mina AlmaToEami waAlma$orabi wagoyari *`lika [in which mTEm and m$rb are evidently used as inf. ns. agreeably with general analogy]), (O, K, TA,) by gyr *lk being meant such as straitness and ampleness [ of circumstances ], and niggardliness and liberality, (TA,) of the natural dispositions that are inseparable from us; (O, K, TA;) and this word is fem., (O, TA,) like TabiyEapN , as is said in the M; or it is sing. and masc. accord. to Abu-l-Kásim Ez-Zejjájee; and it is also pl. of TaboEN , as it is said to be by Az; (TA;) [and those who have asserted it to be fem. may have held it to be a pl.;] and ↓ TaAbiEN is syn. with TibaAEN [as a sing.]; (K, TA;) or, as Lh says, it is syn. with ↓ TabiyEapN ; of which the pl. is TabaAy^iEu . (TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) Model, make, fashion, or mould: as in the saying, AiDoribohu EalaY TaboEi h`*aA (assumed tropical:) [ Make thou it, fashion it, or mould it, according to the model, make, fashion, or mould, of this ]. (IAar, O, L, K, TA.)

definition: A river, or rivulet;
sourceDefinition: A river, or rivulet; (As, T, S, O, K, TA;) so called because first dug [ and filled ] by men; having the meaning of maTobuwEN , like qTofN in the sense of maqoTuwfN ; not applied to any of those cleft by God, such as the Tigris and the Euphrates and the Nile and the like thereof: (Az, TA:) pl. A^aTobaAEN [properly a pl. of pauc.,] (As, S, O,) or TubuwEN , as heard by Az from the Arabs, and TibaAEN : (TA:) or AlT~iboEu , as some say, is the name of a particular river: (S, O:) or it is also thus applied, i. e. to a particular river. (K.) ― -b2- And i. q. magiyDu maA='K [i. e. A place where water sinks, or goes away, into the earth; or where water enters into the earth; and where it collects ]: (O, K:) pl. A^aTobaAEN . (TA.) -A2- See also the next paragraph, in two places.

definition: A certain venomous duwayob~ap [or insect ]: (El-Jáhidh, O, K, TA:) or, (K,) as said to Az by a man of Egypt, an insect ( duwayob~ap ) (O) of the same kind as the qirodaAn [or ticks ], (O, K,) but (O) the bite of which occasions intense pain;
sourceDefinition: A certain venomous duwayob~ap [or insect ]: (El-Jáhidh, O, K, TA:) or, (K,) as said to Az by a man of Egypt, an insect ( duwayob~ap ) (O) of the same kind as the qirodaAn [or ticks ], (O, K,) but (O) the bite of which occasions intense pain; (O, K;) and sometimes, or often, he that is bitten by it becomes swollen [app. in the part bitten ], and is relieved by sweet things: Az says that it is with the Arabs [ called, or what is called, ] the nibor [which is expl. as meaning the tick; or an insect resembling the tick, which, when it creeps upon the camel, causes the track along which it creeps to swell; or as being smaller than the tick, that bites, and causes the place of its bite to swell; &c.]: (O:) [accord. to Dmr, as stated by Freytag, i. q. qamoqaAmapN , which is expl. as applied to a small tick; and a species of louse, that clings tightly to the roots of the hair, app. meaning a crab-louse: ] what is known thereof [or by this appellation] now is a thing of the form of a small emaciated tick, that sticks to the body of a man, and is hardly, or not at all, severed, except by the application of mercury. (TA.)

definition: [ The extinguisher of the live coals;
sourceDefinition: [ The extinguisher of the live coals; ] one of the [ seven ] days called A^ay~aAmu AlEajuwzi ; (S, O;) the fifth of those days; (K;) so in the M &c.: (TA:) or the fourth thereof: (O, K:) or the last thereof. (Har p. 295.) [Accord. to modern Egyptian almanacs, it is the fourth of those days on which the last of the three jamaraAt becomes extinct: see jamorapN : and see also EajuwzN ] ― -b2- muTofiy^apu Alr~aDofi (so in the M and O and L and in some copies of the K, in other copies of the K muTofiy^u , TA) A piece of fat which, when it falls upon the raDof [or heated stones ], melts, and quenches them. (Lth, O, K.) And in the M and L, it is said to signify A lean sheep or goat: the Arabs, as is related by Lh, used to say, Hadasa lahumo bimuTofiy^api Alr~aDofi (TA) i. e. He slaughtered for them a lean sheep or goat, which extinguished the fire and did not become thoroughly cooked: (M and L and K in art. Hds :) or a fat sheep or goat, (AO and T, TA in that art.,) which quenched the raDof by its fat. (T, TA ibid. [See also damaga .]) ― -b3- Also A serpent, the poison of which, as it passes by the raDof , extinguishes their fire: (O, K:) in a verse of El-Kumeyt, [for the sake of the metre,] the former word is [altered to] ↓ muTaf~iy^ap . (O.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) A calamity, or misfortune: (O, K, TA:) said by AO to mean originally such as has made one to forget that which was before it, and extinguished its heat. (O, TA.)

definition: He (a man) made his face to be displeasing, or odious;
sourceDefinition: He (a man) made his face to be displeasing, or odious; (M, L, TA;) he contracted it; or made it austere, or morose: and so Taromasa , and Talomasa , (L, TA,) and Tarosama . (TA in art. Tlms .) ― -b2- And He (a man) bent down his head; or lowered his eyes, looking towards the ground; or was, or became, silent; syn. A^aToraqa : and so Tarosama . (S in art. Trsm ; and TA.) ― -b3- [And, accord. to Golius, He receded, or drew back, from fight; followed by Eano : (one of the significations assigned in the K to Tarosama :) he mentions this as on the authority of J: perhaps he found it in a copy of the S in art. Trms (in which AlT~aromasapu is expl. as meaning AlAinoqibaADu and Aln~ukuwSu ), or in some other art. of that work in which I do not remember to have seen it. -A2- Also He sculptured, engraved, or inscribed, a thing with talismanic devices or characters. And He charmed, or guarded, or preserved, by means of a talisman. See what follows.]

definition: , (S, Mgh, Msb,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, Msb,) aor. , inf. n. TuluwqN , (Msb,) The she-camel was, or became, loosed from her bond, (S, Mgh, Msb,) or cord, by which her fore shank and her arm had been bound together. (S, Mgh.) And Talaqati Aln~aAqapu A_ilaY AlmaA='i [ The she-camel was, or became, loosed from her bond to repair to the water ]: (Msb:) or Talaqati AlA_ibilu (AZ, As, S, TA) A_ilaY AlmaA='i , (AZ, TA,) aor. as above, (As, TA,) inf. n. TaloqN (AZ, As, S, TA) and TuluwqN , (AZ, S, TA,) the camels were, or became, loosed to repair to the water, it being distant two days' journeys, (AZ, As, S, TA,) and were left to pasture while going thither: and the subst. is TalaqN [q. v.]. (AZ, S, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Talaqato , (IAar, Th, S, Mgh, O, Msb,) or Talaqato mino zawojihaA , (K,) aor. ; (Th, S, O, Msb, K;) and Taluqato also; (IAar, Th, Mgh, Msb;) the latter of which is preferable, but the former is allowable; (IAar, TA;) or the latter is the more common; (Th, TA;) but accord. to to Akh, the latter is not allowable; (S, O, TA;) inf. n. definition: He left, left alone, or let go, his she-camel.
sourceDefinition: He left, left alone, or let go, his she-camel. (TA.) See also 4, second sentence. ― -b2- [Hence,] Tl~q A@moraA^atahu , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. taToliyqN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) from TalaAqN [q. v.]; (O;) and ↓ ATlqhA , (K,) inf. n. A_iTolaAqN ; (TA;) (tropical:) [ He divorced his wife; ] he separated his wife from himself [ by a sentence of divorce ]. (K, TA.) [ Tl~q in this sense is opposed to raAjaEa : and hence the meanings of these two verbs in a verse of En-Nábighah which I have cited in art. n*r , (see conj. 6 in that art.,) and which is also cited in the S and O and TA in the present art.] ― -b3- And Tl~q AlbilaAda (tropical:) He left, or quitted, the country. (IAar, TA.) El-'Okeylee, being asked by Ks, A^aTal~aqota A@moraA^ataka [ Hast thou quitted thy wife? ], answered, naEamo waAlA^aroDa mino waraAy^ihaA (assumed tropical:) [ Yes, and the land behind her ]. (IAar, TA.) And one says, Tal~aqotu Alqawoma (assumed tropical:) I left, or quitted, the people, or party: and Tl~q AlEiyaAla (assumed tropical:) He left [or deserted ] the household, like as the man leaves [or divorces ] the woman, or wife. (TA.) And Tl~q AlEayoru EaAnatahu (assumed tropical:) The he-ass passed by, or beyond, his she-ass, and then left her: and Tal~aqatohu AlEaAnapu (assumed tropical:) The she-ass submitted herself [the verb which I thus render has been altered to Anqdt , for which I read A@noqaAdato ,] to him, after having been incompliant. (TA.) ― -b4- And Tul~iqa Als~aliymu (assumed tropical:) The person bitten by a serpent became rid of the pain: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or recovered himself, and his pain became allayed, (S, O, K,) after the paroxysm: (S, O:) inf. n. as above. (K.) ― -b5- Tal~aqa naxolahu : see 4, last sentence.

sourceDefinition: signifies The loosing, or setting loose or free, and letting go. (TA.) You say, ATlq Aln~aAqapa mino EiqaAlihaA , (S, O, Msb, TA,) or mina AlEiqaAli , i. e. And ATlq AlA^asiyra , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, TA,) and ATlq Eanohu , (O, TA,) He let go the captive; (S, O, K, TA;) and set him free; (TA;) he loosed the bond of the captive, and let him go: (Mgh, Msb:) and A^uToliqa Eanohu A_isaAruhu [ His bond was loosed from him ], namely, the captive. (S.) And ATlq xayolahu fiY AlHalobapi He made his horses to run [ in the race-ground ]. (TA.) And ATlq Aln~aAqapa He drove the she-camel to the water: (TA:) or A^aTolaqotu Aln~aAqapa A_ilaY AlmaA='i [ I loosed the she-camel from her bond to repair to the water ]: (Msb:) or A^aTolaqotu AlA_ibila (AZ, S, O, TA) A_ilaY AlmaA='i (AZ, S, * TA) I loosed the camels to repair to the water, it being distant two days' journeys, and left them to pasture while going thither. (AZ, S, O, * TA.) And ATlq Alqawomu means The people, or party, had their camels loosed to repair to the water, it being distant two days' journeys, and the camels being left to pasture while going thither. (S, K, * TA.) ― -b2- ATlq A@moraA^atahu : see 2, third sentence. ― -b3- ATlq Ald~awaA='u baTonahu The medicine loosened, or relaxed, his belly [or bowels ]; (Msb;) or moved his belly. TaloqN ; (TA;) (assumed tropical:) He opened his hand [ freely ] with good, (K, TA,) and with property. (TA.) sourceDefinition: [ Loosed from his bond, set loose or free, or], as expl. by IAar, let go; as also ↓ TaliyqN and ↓ muTolaqN : and a man not having anything upon him, as expl. by Ks: and Taloqu Alyadayoni a camel not having the fore legs bound. (TA.) You say, Hubisa TaloqFA , (so in the CK,) or ↓ TalaqFA , (K accord. to the TA, [and this is agreeable with the preceding context in the K, but it requires confirmation which I do not find,]) and with damm, [i. e. TuloqFA ,] accord. to the K, but correctly with two dammehs, [i. e. ↓ TuluqFA ,] (TA, and thus in the S,) He was imprisoned without shackle and without bond. (K, TA) See also TuluqN , first sentence. ― -b2- [Hence,] Taloqu All~isaAni , and ↓ Taliyqu AllsAn , (S, O, Msb, K,) and AllsAn ↓ Tiloqu , (K,) and AllsAn ↓ Tulaqu , (TA,) (tropical:) Eloquent, or chaste, in speech, and sweet therein: (Msb:) and All~isaAni ↓ munoTaliqu and ↓ mutaTal~iquhu (tropical:) [ free from impediment of the tongue; or] eloquent, or chaste in speech. (TA.) And lisaAnN TaloqN *aloqN , and *aliyqN , ↓ TaliyqN , and *uluqN ↓ TuluqN , and *ulaqN ↓ TulaqN , (S, O, K,) but the last two of these were unknown to As, and the latter of them was disallowed by IAar, (TA,) and *aliqN ↓ TaliqN , (O, K,) [expl. in the K as meaning A tongue having sharpness; but correctly] meaning (tropical:) a tongue free from impediment, or eloquent, or chaste in speech, ( *uw A@noTilaAqK ,) and sharp. (O, TA.) ― -b3- And Taloqu Alyadayoni , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) and Alydyn ↓ Tuluqu , (O, K,) and Alydyn ↓ Tuloqu , (O, TA,) and Alydyn ↓ Taliyqu , (L, TA,) (tropical:) Liberal, bountiful, munificent, or generous; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) applied to a man: (S, Mgh, O, Msb:) and in like manner, a woman: (TA:) [or] a woman is termed Taloqapu Alyadayoni : (S:) and so, accord to AZ, Taloqu Alwajohi ; which [generally] has another meaning, expl. in what follows. (TA.) And yaduhu TaloqN (tropical:) His hand is liberal; syn. bisoTN ; (TA in art. bsT ;) and so ↓ muTolaqapN : (S and K and TA in that art.:) or the latter signifies opened; and so ↓ maToluwqapN . (TA in the present art.) ― -b4- And Taloqu Alwajohi , (S, O, Msb, K,) and Alwjh ↓ Tiloqu , (IAar, O, K,) and ↓ Tuloqu Alwjh , (IAar, K,) and Alwjh ↓ Taliqu , (K,) and Alwjh ↓ Taliyqu , (S, O, K,) (tropical:) Laughing, or happy, or cheerful, and bright, in the face, or countenance: (K, TA:) or cheerful, or happy, displaying openness and pleasantness, in the face; and so TaloqN alone: (Msb:) and Alwjh ↓ Taliyqu open and pleasant, and goodly, in countenance: (AZ, TA:) and TaliyqN alone, joyful, and open or cheer- ful, in countenance. (TA. [And it is there said that the pl. of TaloqN is TaloqaAt : but this is app. a mistranscription for TuloqaAnN or TiloqaAnN .]) A^uwojuhN ↓ TawaAliqu is not allowable, except in poetry. (IAar, TA.) ― -b5- And yawomN TaloqN , (Lth, S, Mgh, O, K,) and layolapN TaloqapN (Lth, S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and TaloqN , (O, Msb, K,) (tropical:) A day, and a night, in which is neither heat nor cold: (Lth, Mgh, O, Msb, K:) or in which is no cold nor anything hurtful: (S:) or in which is no rain: or in which is no wind: or in which the cold is mild: (TA: [after which is added, mn AyAm TaloqAt : but the last word seems, as in an instance before mentioned, to be mistranscribed, or AyAm (i. e. A^ay~aAm ) may be a mistake for layaAlK :]) or layolapN TaloqN means a night in which is no cold: (AA, TA:) or in which the wind is still: (O, TA:) and layolapN TaloqapN sometimes means a moon-lit, or a light, or bright, night: (IDrd, O, TA:) and one says also ↓ layolapN TaAliqapN , (K, TA,) meaning a still, or calm, and light, or bright, night: (TA:) and ↓ layaAlK TawaAliqu , (K, * TA,) meaning pleasant nights in which is neither heat nor cold. (TA.) Er-Rá'ee says, falam~aA Ealatohu Al$~amosu fiY yawomi TaloqapK meaning yawomi layolapK TaloqapK [ And when the sun came upon him, or it, ] in a day of a night in which was neither cold nor wind; i. e., in a day after such a night; for the Arabs commence with the night, before the day: and the phrase fiY yawomi TaloqapK occurs in like manner in a verse of Dhu-r-Rummeh. (Az, TA.) ― -b6- For the epithet Taloqu Alyadi AlyumonaY , (applied to a horse, accord. to the K,) see TuluqN . ― -b7- And for other meanings assigned in the K to TaloqN , see TuluqN , in two places. -A2- TaloqN signifies also The pain of childbirth. (S, O.) One says, DarabahaA AlT~aloqu [ The pain of childbirth smote her ]. (O.) [See also Tuliqat , of which it is the inf. n.] -A3- And [it is said to signify] A sort of medicine. (S.) See TalaqN , latter half, in two places.

definition: ― -b2- Also the subst.
sourceDefinition: : see TaloqN , second sentence. ― -b2- Also the subst. from Talaqati AlA_ibilu : (AZ, S, TA: [see 1, second sentence:]) and [as such] signifying The journeying [of camels] during the night to arrive at the water in the next night, there being two nights between them and the water; the first of which nights is termed AlT~alaqu [or layolapu AlT~alaqi (see HawozN )]; the pastor loosing them to repair to the water, [in the CK yajolibuhA is put for yuxal~iyhaA ,] and leaving them to pasture while going thither: the camels after the driving, during the first night, are said to be ↓ TawaAliqu ; and in the second night, qawaAribu : (S, O, K, TA:) or AlT~alaqu signifies the first of two days intervening between the camels and the water; and Alqarabu , the second: and layolapu AlT~alaqi , the night in which the faces of the camels are turned towards the water and during which they are left to pasture; and layolapu Alqarabi , the second night: (As, TA:) but it has been said that layolapu AlT~alaqi means the second of the nights in which the camels repair to the water: Th says that AlT~alaqu signifies the second of two days during which the camels seek the water when it is two days distant from them; and Alqarabu , the first of those days: and it is said that layolapu AlT~alaqi means [ the night of ] the turning of the faces of the camels towards the water: but this explanation was not pleasing to ISd. (TA.) [See an ex. voce HawozN , in which it is used tropically.] ― -b3- Also A heat; i. e. a single run, or run at once, to a goal, or limit; syn. $awoTN ; (S, IAth, O, Msb, K, TA;) meaning a running, of a horse, without restraining himself, [or without stopping, ] to a goal, or limit: (Msb:) and the utmost extent to which a horse runs. (TA.) One says of a horse, EadaA TalaqFA or Talaqayoni [ He ran a heat or two heats ]. (S, O, Msb, K. [In the CK, erroneously, TaloqFA and Taloqayoni .]) ― -b4- And (hence, TA) (tropical:) A share, or portion, (Ibn-'Abbád, A, O, K, TA,) of property [&c.]. (A, TA.) -A2- Also A shackle, or pair of shackles, ( qayodN ,) of skins: (S, M, O, K, TA:) or a rope strongly twisted, so that it will stand up. (TA.) ― -b2- And sing. of A^aTolaAqN which signifies The [ intestines into which the food passes from the stomach, termed the ] A^amoEaA=' , or the A^aqotaAb of the belly; (IDrd, O, K; * [in some copies of the last of which, Alqunobu is erroneously put for Alqitobu as one of the words explaining AlT~alaqu ;]) so in one or more of the dialects: AO says, in the belly are A^aTolaAq , of which the sing. is TalaqN ; (O, TA;) meaning the lines, or streaks, ( TaraAy^iq ,) of the belly: and Talaqu AlbaToni is also expl. [in like manner] as meaning the jud~ap of the belly; pl. as above. (TA.) -A3- Also The [ plant called ] $uborum : [but what plant is meant by this is doubtful:] or a plant that is used in dyes: or this is a mistake: (K:) [or] accord. to Ibn-'Abbád, ↓ AlT~aloqu is what is used in dyes; and is said to be the $uborum : (O, TA: *) and (K) accord. to As, (O,) TalaqN signifies a sort of medicament, (O, K,) which, when one is anointed therewith, (K,) i. e. with the extract thereof, (TA,) prevents the burning of fire: (K:) or a species of plant: so says As: (O:) the appellation by which it is generally known is ↓ Taloq , with the l quiescent; (O, K;) or this pronunciation is incorrect: (K:) and AHát mentions, (K, TA,) on the authority of As, (TA,) its being termed ↓ TiloqN : (K, TA:) but it is not a plant: it is of the nature of stones, and of [ what are termed ] lixaAf [thin white stones]; and probably he [referring to As] heard that it is called kawokabu AlA^aroDi , and therefore supposed it to be a plant; for if it were a plant, fire would burn it; but fire does not burn it, unless by means of artful contrivances: (O, TA:) the word is arabicized, from talako : (K, TA: in the O written tilk :) [it is the well-known mineral termed talc: ] the Ra-ees [Ibn-Seenà, whom we call “ Avicenna, ”] says, (TA,) it is a brightlyshining stone, that separates, when it is bruised, into several laminæ and split pieces, of which are made maDaAwiY [correctly maDaAwiy^ , meaning small circular panes which are inserted in apertures to admit light, ] for the [ cupolas of ] hot baths, instead of glass: the best is that of El-Yemen; then that of India; then that of El-Undulus [or El-Andalus ]: the art employed in dissolving it consists in putting it into a piece of rag with some pebbles and immersing it in tepid water, then moving it about gently until it becomes dissolved and comes forth from the piece of rag into the water, whereupon the water is strained from it, and it is put in the sun to dry. (K, TA.)

sourceDefinition: is the inf. n. of Talaqat said of a woman: (Th, S, Mgh, O, K:) or the subst. therefrom: (Msb:) or [rather] it is also a subst. in the sense of taToliyqN ; (Mgh;) [whence,] TalaAqu AlmaroA^api signifies (assumed tropical:) The letting the wife go her way: (Lth, O:) and it has two meanings: one is [ the divorcing of the woman; i. e.] the dissolving of the wife's marriage-tie: and the other is the leaving, and dismissing, of the wife [either in an absolute sense or as is done by a single sentence of divorce]. (TA.)
