sourceDefinition: as syn. with A^agolaqa : see the latter. -A2- Also, inf. n. galoqN , He went away. (TA.) ― -b2- And galaqa fiY AlA^aroDi , aor. , inf. n. galoqN , He went far into the land; (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K, * TA;) as also falaqa , aor. , inf. n. faloqN . (Ibn-'Abbád, O, TA.) -A3- galiqa said of a door: see 7. ― -b2- [Hence,] galiqa Alr~ahonu , aor. , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, &c.,) inf. n. galaqN , (S, O, Msb,) or guluwqN , (IAar, TA,) or both, (Sb, TA,) (tropical:) The pledge was, or became, a rightful possession [i. e. a forfeit ] to the receiver of it (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) when not redeemed within the time stipulated; (S, O, K;) or so galiqa Alr~ahonu fiY yadi Almurotahini : (Sb, TA:) or galiqa Alr~ahonu means the pledge remained in the hand [or possession ] of the receiver of it, the pledger being unable to redeem it; (IAar, TA;) accord. to the Bári', it is when a man pledges a commodity and says, “ If I do not pay thee within such a time, the pledge shall be thine for the debt. ” (Msb.) This is forbidden in a trad. (S, Mgh, O, Msb, &c.) It is said in a trad. of the Prophet on this subject, laA yagolaqu bimaA fiyhi laka gunomuhu wuEalayoka guromuhu [meaning It shall not become a forfeit to the receiver with what is involved in it: (or, accord. to an explanation of the first clause in the Msb, it shall not become a rightful possession to the receiver for the debt for which it was pledged: ) to thee shall pertain the regaining of it, and its increase, and growth, and excess in value, if such there be, and upon thee shall be the obligation of the debt belonging to it, and the bearing of any unavoidable damage that it may have sustained ]: (O:) or lahu gunomuhu waEalayohi guromuhu i. e., accord. to A 'Obeyd, to him (the owner) it shall return, and to him shall pertain its increase [ if there be any ], and if it have become defective, or have perished, [ unavoidably, ] he shall be responsible for it and shall pay the debt to him to whom it is owed without being compensated by [ the remission of ] aught of the debt: (Msb:) or laka gunomuhu waEalayohi guromuhu , which means to thee (the pledger) shall pertain the increase of it (the pledge), and its growth, and its excess in value, [ if it have any, ] and upon him (the receiver of it) shall be the responsibility [ to make compensation ] for it if it perish [ through his fault, in his possession ], (O. [There are other, somewhat different, readings and explanations of this trad. in the Mgh &c.; but what I have here given, from the O and Msb, appear to me to be the most approvable. See also gunomN : and see art. rhn .]) Zuheyr says, wafaAraqatoka birahonK laA fakaAka lahu yawoma AlwadaAEi faA^amosaY Alr~ahonu qado galiqaA (assumed tropical:) [ And she separated herself from thee with a pledge for which there is nothing wherewith it may be redeemed, on the day of valediction, so the pledge has become a forfeit to its receiver ]: (S, Mgh, O, TA:) he means that she received his heart as a pledge, and went away with it. (Mgh, TA.) The saying of Ows Ibn-Hajar A^abuw galaqK fiY layolatayoni muw^aj~ali means (assumed tropical:) The owner of a pledge that has become a rightful possession [or forfeit ] to its receiver, the period for the release of which is two nights: to this he likens a captivated heart. (TA.) ― -b3- One says also, of a slave who has received permission to traffic, galiqato raqabatuhu biAld~ayoni (assumed tropical:) His raqabap [meaning person ] has become a rightful possession [or a forfeit to his creditor or creditors] by reason of debt, when he is unable to free it. (Mgh.) ― -b4- And galiqa signifies also (assumed tropical:) He was unransomed, or unredeemed; said of a captive, and of a criminal. (TA.) ― -b5- And (tropical:) He, or it, stuck fast: (S, O, TA:) thus in the saying, galiqa qalobuhu fiY yadi fulaAnapa [ His heart stuck fast in the possession of such a woman or girl ]: (TA:) and AiHotad~a fagaliqa fiY Hid~atihi [ He became excited by sharpness of temper, and stuck fast in his sharpness of temper ]: (S, O. TA:) and galiqa is said of anything that sticks fast in a thing, and cleaves to it: thus one says, galiqa fiY AlbaATili [ He stuck fast in that which was vain, or false ]: and the saying of El-Farezdak walawo kaAnuwA A^uwliY galaqK sigaAbaA means Had they been persons who had stack fast in poverty and hunger, cleaving thereto. (Sh, TA.) ― -b6- Also, (Msb, TA,) inf. n. galaqN , (Mgh, Msb,) (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, disquieted, (Mgh,) or disquieted by grief; (Mgh, Msb;) or angry, (Msb, TA.) and excited by sharpness of temper. (TA.) Hence yamiynu Algalaqi (assumed tropical:) The oath of anger; said by some of the lawyers to be so called because he who swears it closes thereby against himself a door preventing him from advancing or drawing back. (Msb.) And hence A_iy~aAka waAlgalaqa (assumed tropical:) Beware thou of, or avoid thou, the being disquieted, or disquieted by grief [or anger ]: or, as some say, the meaning is, Alt~aToliyqaAtu Hat~aY laA yaboqaY minohaA ↓ laA yugolaqu $aYo'N (assumed tropical:) [i. e. The sentences of divorce shall not be closed, or concluded, at once, by one's saying “ Thou art trebly divorced, ” so that there shall not remain of them aught ]; for one should divorce agreeably with the sun~ap : (Mgh:) [or, accord. to the TA, A_iy~aAka waAlgalaqa app. means beware thou of, or avoid thou, the state of straitness: ] and Algalaqu signifies also the being in a state of perdition: (TA:) and contractedness of the mind or bosom, (Mbr, JK, TA,) and paucity of patience. (Mbr, TA.) ― -b7- One says also, galiqati Aln~axolapu , (O. K, TA,) inf. n. galaqN , (TA,) : The palm-tree had worms in the bases of its branches and was thereby stopped from bearing fruit; (O, K, TA;) and so Eani AlA_ivomaAri ↓ A^ugoliqato . (TA.) ― -b8- And galiqa Zahoru AlbaEiyri , (S, O, K, TA,) inf. n. galaqN , (S, O, TA,) (tropical:) The back of the camel became galled with galls not to be cured; (S, O, K, TA;) the whole of his back being seen to be two portions of cicatrized skin, the results of galls that had become in a healing state, and the two sides thereof glistening: ISh says that in the case of the worst galls of the camel, the furniture, or saddle and saddle-cloth, cannot be [partially] raised from contact with him [so as to be bearable by him]. (TA.)

A_igolaAqN , (Mgh, K, &c.,) He made the door fast with a galaq , so that it could not be opened unless with a key; (Msb;) [i. e.] he locked the door; or bolted it: or he closed, or shut, it: (MA:) contr. of fataHahu : (O, K: *) and ↓ galaqahu , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. galoqN , (S, O, Msb,) signifies the same; (S, O, Msb, K;) mentioned by IDrd, on the authority of AZ; but rare; (Msb;) or a mispronunciation; (K;) or bad, (S, O, K,) and rejected; (S;) and galoqN is [said to be] the subst. from A^agolaqa ; (S, Mgh, K;) whence the saying of a poet, wabaAbK A_i*aA maA maAla lilogaloqi yaSorifu [ And a door that, when it turns to be locked, or closed, creaks ]: (S, O, Mgh: *) and one says, AlA^abowaAba ↓ gal~aqotu [ I locked, or closed, the doors ]; the verb being with teshdeed to denote multiplicity [of the objects]; (Sb, S, TA;) [and] it is so to denote muchness [of the action] or intensiveness, (O,) [for] one says also, AlbaAba ↓ gl~q , a chaste phrase; El-Isbahánee says that ↓ gal~aqotu signifies I locked, or closed, ( A^agolaqotu ,) many doors, or a door several times, or a door well or thoroughly; (TA;) and one says also A^agolaqotu AlA^abowaAba ; (S, O, TA;) said by Sb to be a good Arabic phrase; (TA;) but this is rare; (O;) El-Farezdak says, maA zilotu A^afotaHu A^abowaAbFA waA^ugoliquhaA Hat~aY A^atayotu A^abaA Eamoriw bona Eam~aAri [ I ceased not to open doors and to close them until I came to Aboo-'Amr Ibn-'Ammár ], meaning, as AHát says, Aboo-'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà. (S, O, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence] one says, A^ugoliqa Ealayohi AlA^amoru (assumed tropical:) The affair was [ as though it were closed against him; i. e., was made ] strait to him. (TA. [See also 10.]) ― -b3- And [hence] A_igolaAqN signifies (assumed tropical:) The act of constraining: (Mgh, O, TA:) whence the saying in a trad., laA TalaAqa walaA EataAqa fiY A_igolaAqK (assumed tropical:) [ There is no divorcement of a wife, nor liberation of a slave, in a case of constraint ]; (Mgh, * O, TA;) for the agent is straitened in his affair, (Mgh, TA,) as though the door were locked, or closed, against him, and he were imprisoned. (TA.) One says, A^agolaqahu EalaY $aYo'K (assumed tropical:) He constrained him to do a thing. (IAar, Mgh, TA.) ― -b4- See also 1, last quarter, in two places. ― -b5- One says also, Aglq Alr~ahona (tropical:) He made, or declared, the pledge to be due [or a forfeit to its receiver]. (IAar, TA.) And in like manner one says of the arrows termed magaAliq , [pl. of migolaqN ,] tugoliqu AlxaTara i. e. (tropical:) They make the stake, or wager, or thing playedfor, to be due [or a forfeit ] to the player (O, TA) who wins, or is successful. (TA.) ― -b6- And Aglq AlqaAtila (assumed tropical:) He delivered, or surrendered, the slayer to the heir, or next of kin, of the slain, that he might decide respecting his blood as he pleased. (O, TA.) And A^ugoliqa fulaAnN bijariyratihi (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one was delivered, or surrendered, to be punished for his crime ]. (TA.) And El-Farezdak says, A^asaAraY HadiydK A^ugoliqato bidimaA=y^ihaA (assumed tropical:) [ Captives in bonds of iron, delivered, or surrendered, to be punished for their bloods that they had shed]. (TA.) ― -b7- And A^ugoliqa fulaAnN (assumed tropical:) Such a one was angered. (TA.) ― -b8- And AlA_igolaAqu [or rather A_igolaAqu Zahori AlbaEiyri ] signifies (assumed tropical:) The galling of the back of the camel by heavy loads: (K, TA:) whence the phrase mano A^agolaqa Zahorahu [meaning (assumed tropical:) Such as has heavily burdened his back with sins ], applied, in a trad., to one of those for whom the Prophet will intercede; the sins that have burdened the back of the man being likened to the weight of the load of the camel: [but] it is also said that AlA_igolaAqu was a practice of the Time of Ignorance; that when the camels of any one of them amounted to a hundred, A^agolaquwA baEiyrFA , i. e. (assumed tropical:) They displaced the sanaAsin [pl. of sinosinN , q. v.] of one of the vertebræ of a camel, and wounded his hump, in order that he might not be ridden, and that no use might be made of his back; and that camel was termed muEan~FY [q. v. in art. Enw ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: is [said to be] the inf. n. of galaqa as syn. with A^agolaqa : (S, O, Msb:) and (S, K) the subst. from the latter verb [q. v.]. (S, Mgh, K.) -A2- As an epithet, (O, K,) applied to a man, or to a camel, (K,) or to each of these, (O,) Old, or advanced in age, and lean, meagre, or emaciated: (O, K, TA:) accord. to the “ Nawádir, ” it is applied to an old man [app. as meaning lean, meagre, or emaciated ]: (TA:) or red; (K;) or in this sense applied to a man, and to a skin for water or milk, and to leather: (Ibn-'Abbád, O:) or, accord. to AA, applied to a skin for water or milk, vitiated, or rendered unsound, in the tanning. (O.)

sourceDefinition: [part. n. of galiqa primarily signifying Being, or becoming, locked, or bolted; or closed, or shut. ― -b2- And hence,] (tropical:) A pledge being, or becoming, a rightful possession [i. e. a forfeit ] to the receiver of it, not having been redeemed within the time stipulated. (TA. [See also the verb.]) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) A captive, and a criminal, unransomed, or unredeemed. (TA.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) A narrow, or strait, place. (TA.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) A man evil in disposition: or much, or often, in anger; thus expl. by Aboo-Bekr: or narrow in disposition, difficult to be pleased. (TA.) ― -b6- And (tropical:) Speech, or language, [ difficult to be understood, ] dubious, or confused. (S, K, TA.) ― -b7- And naxolapN galiqapN (tropical:) A palm-tree having worms in the bases of its branches and thereby stopped from bearing fruit. (TA.) ― -b8- And galiqN applied to the back of a camel, (tropical:) Having incurable galls; the whole of it being seen to be two portions of cicatrized skin, and the two sides thereof glistening. (TA.)

(TA.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) A man evil in disposition: or much, or often, in anger; thus expl. by Aboo-Bekr: or narrow in disposition, difficult to be pleased. (TA.) ― -b6- And (tropical:) Speech, or language, [ difficult to be understood, ] dubious, or confused. (S, K, TA.) ― -b7- And naxolapN galiqapN (tropical:) A palm-tree having worms in the bases of its branches and thereby stopped from bearing fruit. (TA.) ― -b8- And galiqN applied to the back of a camel, (tropical:) Having incurable galls; the whole of it being seen to be two portions of cicatrized skin, and the two sides thereof glistening. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, O, K,) thus as heard by AHn from El-Bekree and others, (O,) and ↓ giloqapN (O, K) as heard by him from one of the Desert-Arabs of Rabee'ah, the former the more common, (O,) and ↓ galoqaY , (K,) A certain tree [or plant ] with which the people of Et-Táïf prepare hides for tanning by the treatment termed EaTonN : (ISk, S, TA: [see EaTana Aljiloda :]) accord. to information given to AHn by an Arab of the desert, (O,) a certain small tree, [or plant, ] (O, K, TA,) resembling the EiZolim [q. v.], (O, TA,) bitter (O, K, TA) in an intense degree, not eaten by anything: it is dried, then bruised, and beaten, with water, and skins are macerated in it, in consequence of which there remains not upon them a hair nor a particle of fur nor a bit of flesh; this being done when they desire to throw the skins into the tan, whether they be of oxen or of sheep or goats or of other animals; and it is bruised, and carried into the various districts or towns for this purpose: (O, TA:) it is found in El-Hijáz and Tihámeh: (K, TA:) AHn says, it is a tree [or plant ] not to be endured for pungency; the gatherer of it fears for his eyes from its exhalation or its juice: (TA:) it is of the utmost efficiency for tanning: (K, TA:) Lth says, (O, TA,) it is a bitter tree [or plant ]; (O;) and it is a poison; a mixture being made with its leaves for wolves and dogs, which kills them; and it is used also for tanning therewith: (O, TA:) and AHn says, (TA,) the Abyssinians poison weapons with it, (K, TA,) cooking it, and then smearing with it the weapons, (TA,) and it kills him whom it smiles. (K, TA.) [Accord. to Forskål, (Flora Ægypt. Arab. p. lxvi.,) the names of “ Harmal Hrml , and Ghalget ed dib glqt Aldyb , ” by which he means Haromal and galoqap Al*~iy^ob , are now applied to Peganum harmala. ]

definition: , (S, Msb, K, *) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, *) inf. n. tagoyiyrN , (Msb,) He made the thing other than it was; (K;) made it cease to have the quality which it had; (Msb;) altered it; changed it. (K.) He, or it, altered, or changed, the thing in odour, or otherwise, for the worse; corrupted, tainted, or infected, it; rendered it ill-smelling, stinking, fetid, rancid, rank, fusty, or frouzy. (The lexicons passim.) It is said in the Kur [viii. 55], *`lika biA^an~a A@ll~`ha lamo yaku mugay~irFA niEomapF A^anoEamahaA EalaY qawomK Hat~aY yugay~iruwA maA biA^anofusihimo [ This was because God changeth not favour which He hath conferred upon a people until they change what is in themselves: or] until they change what God hath commanded them to do. (Th, TA.) ― -b2- [And He exchanged the thing for another thing. ] ― -b3- gy~r Al$~ayoba He plucked out the white, or hoary, hairs. (TA.) ― -b4- gy~r Eano baEiyrihi He put down the saddle from his camel, and put it to rights, or adjusted it, or repaired it. (TA.) One says taraka Alqawoma yugay~iruwna He left the people putting to rights, or adjusting, or repairing, the camels' saddles. (S, TA.) -A2- See also 1, latter half.

sourceDefinition: signifies i. q. siwFY [ Other ]: and the pl. is A^agoyaArN : (S:) [but gayor itself often has a pl. meaning, as will be seen in what follows:] or [accord. to general usage, as will be seen below,] gayoru signifies i. q. siwaY [ other than; exclusively of; or not, as used before a substantive or an adjective]. (Msb, K: in the CK [erroneously] siwFY .) It is used to qualify a subst.; [governing (as a prefixed noun) the noun that follows it in the gen. case;] and when so used, it is put in the same case as the noun preceding it. (S.) It qualifies an indeterminate noun: (Mughnee, Msb:) you say jaA='aniY rajulN gayoruka [ A man, other than, or not, thou, came to me ]: (Msb:) and naEomalo SaAliHFA gayora A@l~a*iY kun~aA naEomalu [ We will in that case do good, other than, or not, what we used to do: (Kur xxxv. 34:)]: (Mughnee:) and mino maA='K gayori A=sinK [ Of water other than, or not, altered in taste and colour ]. (Kur xlvii. 16.) It is a noun necessarily prefixed, as to the sense, to a noun which it governs in the gen. case: but sometimes it is without the latter, when the meaning is understood and it is preceded by layosa , (Mughnee, K,) or by laA : (K:) [in which case it signifies Any other person or thing; any person or thing beside, or else: ] you say qabaDotu Ea$arapF layosa gayoruhaA [ I received ten; not other than they was received by me; i. e., not any other thing; or not anything beside, or else ]; (Mughnee, K;) the enunciative, maqobuwDFA , being suppressed: (Mughnee:) and lys gayorahaA , (Mughnee, K;) the noun [of lys ] being understood; i. e., layosa AlmaqobuwDu gayorahaA : (Mughnee:) and lys gayora ; in which the affixed noun [for AlmDAf , in the K, I read AlmDAf Alyh , as in the Mughnee,] is suppressed, and the noun [of lys ] is also understood: (Mughnee, K:) and lys gayoru ; (Mughnee, K;) in which, accord. to Mbr, and the later authors, gyr is indecl., being likened to qabolu and baEodu , so that it may be either the noun or the enunciative [of lys ] or, accord. to Akh, it is decl., because it is not a noun of time like qabolu and baEodu , nor of place like fawoqu and taHotu , but like kul~N and baEoDN , so that it is the noun [of lys ], and the enunciative is suppressed; (Mughnee;) or it may be either indecl. or decl., (Mughnee, K,) accord. to Ibn-Kharoof: (Mughnee:) and lys gayorFA , and lys gayorN ; (Mughnee, K;) in both which cases it is decl., as though the affixed noun were mentioned: (Mughnee:) and laA gayoru ; for the saying, [which we find in the Mughnee,] app. taken from a statement of Seer, that this is incorrect, is not good, since it occurs in the following verse, cited by Ibn-Málik; jawaAbFA bihi tanojuw A@Eotamido fawarab~inaA laEano EamalK A^asolafota laA gayoru tusoA^alu [ Aim thou at having an answer by which thou mayest be safe; for, by our Lord, respecting an action which thou shalt have done before, not any other thing, or not anything beside or else, thou wilt be asked ]. (K.) ― -b2- It does not become determinate by its being prefixed to another noun, because it is very vague: but it is also applied as an epithet to a determinate noun which is near to being indeterminate; as in SiraATa A@l~a*iyna A^anoEamota Ealayohimo gayori A@lomagoDuwbi Ealayohimo [ The way of those upon whom Thou hast conferred favour; the other than, or those who are not, the objects of anger; (Kur i. 6 and 7;)] because the noun rendered determinate by the art. Al denoting a genus is near to being indeterminate, and because when gyr occurs between two contraries its vagueness becomes weakened, (Mughnee, K, *) or altogether departs: (K:) or it is here applied as an epithet to a determinate noun because it resembles a determinate noun in its being prefixed to such a noun: (Msb:) Az says that gyr is here in the gen. case because it is an epithet to Al*yn ; and that it may be an epithet to [what is technically termed in this instance] a determinate noun [as having the article Al prefixed to it] because Al*yn has not [in itself] a direct meaning ( liA^an~a Al~a*iyna gayoru maSomuwdK Samoduhu ), [it being merely a conjunct noun, the meaning of which is determined by what follows it,] notwithstanding it has the art. Al prefixed to it: Abu-l-'Abbás says that Fr holds Al*yn to have the office of an indeterminate noun; and gyr to be an epithet of it; not of any other noun; but that gyr , accord. to some, may be an epithet relating to the nouns implied in AnEmt Elyhm , these not having a direct meaning: Akh says that gyr [with what follows] is a substitute [for Al*yn with what follows], as though the meaning were SiraATa gayori AlmagoDuwbi Ealayohimo [ the way of those who are not the objects of anger ]. (TA.) The reading gayora is also related, on the authority of Ibn-Ketheer, in the accus. case, as a denotative of state, [meaning they being not the objects of anger, ] relating to the pronoun governed in the gen. case by the prep. [in Elyhm ]; or by A^aEoniY [ I mean ] understood; or as an exceptive, [accord. to a usage to be explained below,] if the favours be interpreted as conferred in common upon the two classes of persons. (Bd.) ― -b3- As it resembles a determinate noun in its being prefixed to a determinate noun, [as AlmgDwb in the above-cited passage of the Kur,] some have presumed to prefix to it the article Al : but against this it may be urged, that its prefixion to a determinate noun is not to render the expression determinate, but for specification; and Al does not imply specification. (Msb.) ― -b4- In the following verse of Hassán, A^ataAnaA falamo naEodilo siwaAhu bigayorihi nabiY~N badaA fiY Zulomapi All~ayoli haAdiyaA the meaning is, [ A prophet came to us, who appeared in the darkness of night, a director in the right way, ] and we did not weigh another than him with another than the other, i. e., with him. (Mughnee.) ― -b5- [ wagayoru *`lika is a phrase of frequent occurrence, meaning Et cœtera. ] ― -b6- gayoru is also used in the sense of layosa [He, or it, is not ]; as in the phrase kalaAmu A@ll~`hi gayoru maxoluwqK [ The word of God is not created ], syn. layosa bimaxoluwqK . (Az, TA.) ― -b7- It is also used in the sense of laA [meaning Not, as used before a participle]; (S, K;) and then it is in the accus. case, as a denotative of state; (S;) as in the phrase famani A@DoTur~a gayora baAgK , (S, K,) in the Kur [ii. 168, and other places], (S,) i. e., jaAy^iEFA laA baAgiyFA [ But whosoever is necessitated, being hungry, not transgressing the due bounds ]. (S, K.) ― -b8- It is also used as an exceptive, (S, Mughnee,) in the sense of A_il~aA [ Except; save; or but ]; (Msb, K;) and then it is put in the same case in which the word following A_il~aA would be put in the same phrase, (S, Mughnee, Msb, K,) because it is originally a qualificative, and its use as an exceptive is adventitious: (S:) therefore you say jaA='a Alqawomu gayora zayodK [ The people came, except Zeyd ]; and maA jaA='aniY A^aHadN gayora zayodK and gayoru zayodK [ Not any one came to me, except Zeyd ]: (Msb, K:) or its case depends upon the governing words, so that you say maA qaAma gayoru zayodK [ No one stood, except Zeyd ], and maA raA^ayotu gayora zayodK [ I saw not any, except Zeyd ]: (Msb:) but Fr says that some of the Benoo-Asad and Kudá'ah put gyr in the accus. case, when used in the sense of A_il~aA , whether the phrase before it be complete or incomplete; saying maA jaA='aniY gayoraka [ Not any one came to me, except thou ], and mA jA'nY A^aHadN gayoraka [ Not any one came to me, except thou ]: (S, Msb:) and AA says that when gyr has the place of A_il~aA , it is put in the accus. case. (Msb.) In the saying laA A_il`ha gayoru A@ll~`hi [ There is no deity other than God ], gyr is in the nom. case because it is the enunciative of lA ; but it may be put in the accus. case, as meaning A_il~aA . (Msb.) When, as an exceptive, it is prefixed to an indecl. word [and not preceded by a prep.], it may be itself indecl., with fet-h for its termination; as in the following verse; lamo yamonaEi Al$~uroba minohaA gayora A^ano naTaqato HamaAmapN fiY guSuwnK *aAti A^awoqaAli [ Nought prevented the drinking from it, except that a pigeon cooed, upon branches having AwqAl , which app. means stumps of cut shoots ]. (Mughnee, K.) [See also an ex. (of gayora A^an~a ) in a verse cited voce bayoda .] ― -b9- [It is often used with a prep.; as in bigayori HisaAbK Without reckoning; (Kur ii. 208, &c.;) and mino gayori suwo'K Without leprosy. (Kur xx. 23, &c.)] -A2- gayorN (JK, K) and (JK) ↓ giyarN (JK, S) signifying The act of altering, or changing, i. q. tagoyiyrN , (JK,) are substs. from gay~arahu ; (S with respect to the latter, and K with respect to the former;) not inf. ns., as having no unaugmented verb. It is used to qualify a subst.; [governing (as a prefixed noun) the noun that follows it in the gen. case;] and when so used, it is put in the same case as the noun preceding it. (S.) It qualifies an indeterminate noun: (Mughnee, Msb:) you say jaA='aniY rajulN gayoruka [ A man, other than, or not, thou, came to me ]: (Msb:) and naEomalo SaAliHFA gayora A@l~a*iY kun~aA naEomalu [ We will in that case do good, other than, or not, what we used to do: (Kur xxxv. 34:)]: (Mughnee:) and mino maA='K gayori A=sinK [ Of water other than, or not, altered in taste and colour ]. (Kur xlvii. 16.) It is a noun necessarily prefixed, as to the sense, to a noun which it governs in the gen. case: but sometimes it is without the latter, when the meaning is understood and it is preceded by layosa , (Mughnee, K,) or by laA : (K:) [in which case it signifies Any other person or thing; any person or thing beside, or else: ] you say qabaDotu Ea$arapF layosa gayoruhaA [ I received ten; not other than they was received by me; i. e., not any other thing; or not anything beside, or else ]; (Mughnee, K;) the enunciative, maqobuwDFA , being suppressed: (Mughnee:) and lys gayorahaA , (Mughnee, K;) the noun [of lys ] being understood; i. e., layosa AlmaqobuwDu gayorahaA : (Mughnee:) and lys gayora ; in which the affixed noun [for AlmDAf , in the K, I read AlmDAf Alyh , as in the Mughnee,] is suppressed, and the noun [of lys ] is also understood: (Mughnee, K:) and lys gayoru ; (Mughnee, K;) in which, accord. to Mbr, and the later authors, gyr is indecl., being likened to qabolu and baEodu , so that it may be either the noun or the enunciative [of lys ] or, accord. to Akh, it is decl., because it is not a noun of time like qabolu and baEodu , nor of place like fawoqu and taHotu , but like kul~N and baEoDN , so that it is the noun [of lys ], and the enunciative is suppressed; (Mughnee;) or it may be either indecl. or decl., (Mughnee, K,) accord. to Ibn-Kharoof: (Mughnee:) and lys gayorFA , and lys gayorN ; (Mughnee, K;) in both which cases it is decl., as though the affixed noun were mentioned: (Mughnee:) and laA gayoru ; for the saying, [which we find in the Mughnee,] app. taken from a statement of Seer, that this is incorrect, is not good, since it occurs in the following verse, cited by Ibn-Málik; jawaAbFA bihi tanojuw A@Eotamido fawarab~inaA laEano EamalK A^asolafota laA gayoru tusoA^alu [ Aim thou at having an answer by which thou mayest be safe; for, by our Lord, respecting an action which thou shalt have done before, not any other thing, or not anything beside or else, thou wilt be asked ]. (K.) ― -b2- It does not become determinate by its being prefixed to another noun, because it is very vague: but it is also applied as an epithet to a determinate noun which is near to being indeterminate; as in SiraATa A@l~a*iyna A^anoEamota Ealayohimo gayori A@lomagoDuwbi Ealayohimo [ The way of those upon whom Thou hast conferred favour; the other than, or those who are not, the objects of anger; (Kur i. 6 and 7;)] because the noun rendered determinate by the art. Al denoting a genus is near to being indeterminate, and because when gyr occurs between two contraries its vagueness becomes weakened, (Mughnee, K, *) or altogether departs: (K:) or it is here applied as an epithet to a determinate noun because it resembles a determinate noun in its being prefixed to such a noun: (Msb:) Az says that gyr is here in the gen. case because it is an epithet to Al*yn ; and that it may be an epithet to [what is technically termed in this instance] a determinate noun [as having the article Al prefixed to it] because Al*yn has not [in itself] a direct meaning ( liA^an~a Al~a*iyna gayoru maSomuwdK Samoduhu ), [it being merely a conjunct noun, the meaning of which is determined by what follows it,] notwithstanding it has the art. Al prefixed to it: Abu-l-'Abbás says that Fr holds Al*yn to have the office of an indeterminate noun; and gyr to be an epithet of it; not of any other noun; but that gyr , accord. to some, may be an epithet relating to the nouns implied in AnEmt Elyhm , these not having a direct meaning: Akh says that gyr [with what follows] is a substitute [for Al*yn with what follows], as though the meaning were SiraATa gayori AlmagoDuwbi Ealayohimo [ the way of those who are not the objects of anger ]. The reading gayora is also related, on the authority of Ibn-Ketheer, in the accus. case, as a denotative of state, [meaning they being not the objects of anger, ] relating to the pronoun governed in the gen. case by the prep. [in Elyhm ]; or by A^aEoniY [ I mean ] understood; or as an exceptive, [accord. to a usage to be explained below,] if the favours be interpreted as conferred in common upon the two classes of persons. (Bd.) ― -b3- As it resembles a determinate noun in its being prefixed to a determinate noun, [as AlmgDwb in the above-cited passage of the Kur,] some have presumed to prefix to it the article Al : but against this it may be urged, that its prefixion to a determinate noun is not to render the expression determinate, but for specification; and Al does not imply specification. (S, K.) ― -b8- It is also used as an exceptive, (S, Mughnee,) in the sense of A_il~aA [ Except; save; or but ]; (Msb, K;) and then it is put in the same case in which the word following A_il~aA would be put in the same phrase, (S, Mughnee, Msb, K,) because it is originally a qualificative, and its use as an exceptive is adventitious: (S:) therefore you say jaA='a Alqawomu gayora zayodK [ The people came, except Zeyd ]; and maA jaA='aniY A^aHadN gayora zayodK and gayoru zayodK [ Not any one came to me, except Zeyd ]: (Msb, K:) or its case depends upon the governing words, so that you say maA qaAma gayoru zayodK [ No one stood, except Zeyd ], and maA raA^ayotu gayora zayodK [ I saw not any, except Zeyd ]: (Msb:) but Fr says that some of the Benoo-Asad and Kudá'ah put gyr in the accus. case, when used in the sense of A_il~aA , whether the phrase before it be complete or incomplete; saying maA jaA='aniY gayoraka [ Not any one came to me, except thou ], and mA jA'nY A^aHadN gayoraka [ Not any one came to me, except thou ]: (S, Msb:) and AA says that when gyr has the place of A_il~aA , it is put in the accus. case. sourceDefinition: Single; sole; only; one, and no more; syn. witora ; (S, A, L, Msb;) i. e. waAHidN : (Msb:) [and, used as a subst., a single, or an individual, person or thing: ] fem. farodapN and ↓ farodaYo [which latter is anomalous, as though fem. of farodaAnu ]: (Msb:) pl. A^aforaAdN and ↓ furaAdaY which latter is anomalous, as though pl. of furodaAnu (S, L, Msb) and of farodaYo , like as sukaAraY is pl. of sukoraAnu and of sakoraY . (Msb. See also furaAdN , below.) You say, Eadadotu Ald~araAhima A^aforaAdAF I counted the dirhems one by one. (T, A.) ― -b2- And Such as has no equal, or like: (Lth, M, L, K:) pl. A^aforaAdN (M, K) and furaAdaY [respecting which latter see above]. (K.) Alfarodu as an epithet applied to God means The Single; the Sole; the One; (T;) He who has no equal, or like; the Unequalled: (Lth, T, L:) but Az says, I have not found it so applied in the Sunneh; and no epithet should be applied to God except such as He has applied to Himself, or such as the Prophet has applied to Him. (L.) And one says sayofN farodN , (K,) and ↓ faradN , (T, L, K,) and ↓ furudN , (L, K,) and ↓ faridN , (K,) and ↓ farudN , (T, K,) and ↓ fariydN and ↓ farodadN , (K, but the third and fifth not in the text of the K as given in the TA,) A sword having diversified wavy marks, streaks, or grain; ( *uw firinodK , K, [in the TA wafirinodN , as though one said also sayofN firinodN , which is evidently a mistake,]) unequalled (T, L, K) in excellence. (T, L.) ― -b3- And The half [meaning one ] of a pair or couple. (M, L, K.) ― -b4- And Such as is alone, by himself or by itself, or apart from others; unconnected with, or unattended by, others; solitary, or separate; syn. mut~aHidN , (M, L, K,) or maA kaAna waHodahu ; (Lth, L;) unmixed with others; [in which sense it is] a word of more common application than witorN , and more special than waAHidN : (Kull p. 278:) pl. firaAdN (M, L, K) [and A^aforaAdN and furuwdN also, as will be shown below]: an ex. of the first of these pls. occurs in the saying, (cited by IAar, L,) taxal~ufa Als~aqori firaAda Als~irobi [ As the hawk's seizing, or carrying off by force, those that are apart from the others of the flock of birds ]. (M, L. See, again, furaAdN .) [Hence,] one says vaworN farodN , (S,) and $aYo'N farodN , (M, K,) and ↓ faridN , (S, M, K,) and ↓ faradN , and ↓ farudN , (M, K,) and ↓ furudN , (K,) and ↓ faAridN , (S, M, K,) and ↓ fariydN , (S, K,) and ↓ faruwdN , (M, K,) and ↓ farodaAnu , (K,) [and ↓ muforadN (see an ex. voce $aApN , in art. $wh ),] A bull, (S,) and a thing, (M, K,) that is alone, by itself, or apart from others; solitary, or separate from others. (S, M, K.) And ↓ sidorapN faAridapN A lote-tree apart from others. (S.) And $ajarapN ↓ faAridN , (M, K,) and faAridapN , (M, TA,) A tree apart from others. (M, K, * TA.) And ↓ ZaboyapN faAridN A gazelle apart, or separate, from the herd. (S, M, K.) And ↓ naAqapN faAridN , and ↓ miforaAdN , and ↓ faruwdN , A she-camel that goes away alone, apart from others, in the pasture, (M, L, K, *) and at the water; (M in explanation of the last, and L;) the epithet applied to the male being ↓ faAridN , only. (M, L.) And bih`*aA AlA^amori ↓ huwa faAridN He is alone in this affair. (A.) And it is said in a trad., ↓ lAa tuEad~u faAridatukumo , meaning Your ewe, or she-goat, that ye have set apart from the flock, or herd, that ye may milk her in the tent, or house, shall not be reckoned [among those for which ye are to pay the poorrate]: (A:) or the meaning is, what is over and above the fariyDap [or fixed number of camels, &c., to be given in payment of the poor-rate ] shall not be added to the latter and reckoned therewith. (L.) And in another it is said, ↓ lAa yagul~u faAridatukumo , expl. by Th as meaning Such of you as shall segregate himself, as, for instance, one or two, and gain spoil, shall resign it to the collective body, and not act unfaithfully by taking it for himself. (M, L.) And in another, faminokumu Almuzodalifu SaAHibu AlEimaAmapi Alfarodapi And of you is El-Muzdelif, he of the solitary turban: this was said of him because, when he rode, no one with him wore a turban, to show honour to him. (L.) ― -b5- laqiyotuhu farodayoni means I met him, we two being alone. (S, L, K.) ― -b6- A^aforaAdu Aln~ujuwmi , (S, M, L, K,) as also furuwduhaA , (K,) signifies The brightly-shining stars ( Ald~araAriYo'u ) in the horizon [ when other stars, there, are invisible ]: so called because they are apart from the other [visible] stars. (M, L.) And Alfuruwdu , (T, M, L, and so in some copies of the K,) in some copies of the K ↓ Alfuroduwdu , [and thus in the CK,] but the former is the right, (TA,) Certain stars, disposed in a row, behind the Pleiades; (K;) in some copies of the K, around the Pleiades: (TA:) certain bright stars around the Pleiades. (T, L.) And (L) Certain stars around HaDaAri [q. v.], which is one of the two stars called AlmuHolifaAni , (M, L, TA,) the other whereof is called Alwazonu ; (TA;) certain small stars with HaDaAri ; so called because situate apart from the latter, by its side. (Kitáb Anwá el- 'Arab, TA.) And Alfarodu is a name of The star (a) in the hinder part of the neck of Al$~ujaAE [the constellation Hydra; which star is also called Eunuqu Al$~ujaAEi ]. (Kzw in his description of Al$jAE .) ― -b7- farodN signifies also One side of a jaw: (M, L, K:) pl. A^aforaAdN . (M, L.) ― -b8- And A sandal such as is termed simoTN , not patched, nor having a second sole added to it; (K;) a sandal having a single sole; not having a sole composed of two pieces of leather sewed together, one beneath the other; thus in the saying, yaA xayora mano yamo$iY binaElK farodi [ O best of such as walk with a single-soled sandal ], meaning O best of the great men of the Arabs; for sandals were worn by the Arabs, exclusively of the foreigners; and thin sandals, only by the kings and chief persons of the former. (L.) ― -b9- Also, and ↓ faAridN , A bull [app. a wild bull ]. (Lth, T, L. [See also muforadN .]) ― -b10- [The pl.] AlA^aforaAdu as a conventional term in lexicology signifies What have been transmitted by only one of the lexicologists; what is thus transmitted, if the transmitter is a person of exactness (as Aboo-Zeyd and ElKhaleel and others), is admitted. (Mz, 5th nwE . [See also AlA=HaAdu , voce A^aHadN ; a similar, but less restricted, term: and see AlmafaAriydu .])

He broke it; namely, the seal (A, Mgh, Msb, K) of a letter; (A, K;) and any other thing; (TA:) he broke it asunder, or into several pieces; he dissundered it; (S, Mgh, O, K;) for instance, the seal from a letter. (S, O.) faS~a AlxaAtama is also a metonymical phrase, meaning (tropical:) Inivit: (TA.) [or rather, i. a. ] faD~ AlbakaArapa (tropical:) he destroyed the virginity: the virginity being likened to a seal, or this phrase is from faDaDotu All~uw^oluw^apa I bored, or perforated, the pearl. (Msb.) (TA,) you should not say ↓ yufoDiD ; (S, TA; [but in one copy of the S, I find yafoDiD ;]) though some allow it: and some say that A_ifoDaA' [evidently a mistake for A_ifoDaAD ] means the falling out of the teeth from above and below; but the former explanation is the more common. (TA.) ― -b2- He separated it; dispersed it; scattered it; broke it up; (S, A, Msb, TA;) namely, a thing; (Msb;) or a party of men; (S, O;) or a ring of men, (A, TA,) after they had collected together. (TA.) You say also, faD~a AlmaAla EalaY Alqawomi (Mgh, * TA) He distributed the property among the people, or party of men. (Mgh, TA. *) ― -b3- faDaDotu maA bayonahumaA I cut [ the tie, or bond, that was between them ]. (TA.) ― -b4- faD~a AlmaA='a , [aor. and] inf. n. as above, He poured out, or forth, the water; (TA;) and so Ald~umuwEa the tears. (Har p. 57.) [See also 8.] -A2- faD~a AlmaA='u , [aor., accord. to rule, yafiD~u ,] The water flowed: (TA:) and Ald~umuwEu ↓ AnfD~t The tears poured forth. (Har p. 57.)

definition: He devirginated her: (O, K:) and so AqtD~hA , with q .
sourceDefinition: He devirginated her: (O, K:) and so AqtD~hA , with q . (O, TA.) [See also 1, second sentence.] ― -b2- AftD~ AlmaA='a He poured out, or forth, the water by little and little, successively: (O, K:) or he obtained the water at the time of its coming forth (S, O, K,) from the spring or from the clouds. (TA.) [See also 1, near the end.] ― -b3- AftD~ti said of a woman, She broke [i. e. ended ] her Eid~ap , (O, K, TA,) meaning a widow's Ed~p [during which she may not marry again, nor use perfumes &c., and] which is a period of four months and ten nights, but was before the Prophet's time a year: (TA:) this she did by touching perfume, or by some other act, (K, TA,) such as paring the nail, or plucking out the hair from the face: (TA:) or she rubbed her body with [or against] a beast, (K, TA,) i. e. an ass, or a sheep or goat, (O in art. Hf$ ,) thereby to quit the state of the Ed~p : or it was customary with them for her to wipe her qubul with a bird, and to throw it away; in consequence of which it hardly ever, or never, lived: (K, TA:) she used to enter a Hifo$ [or small tent], and wear the worst of her clothing until a year passed, when a beast or bird was brought to her, and by means thereof she broke her Ed~p ; then she went forth, and a baEorap [or piece of camel's or similar dung] was given to her, and she threw it: (TA: [see 1 in art. bEr :]) she used not to wash herself, nor to touch water, nor to pare a nail, nor to pluck out hair from her face; then she would go forth, after the year, with the foulest aspect, and break her Ed~p by means of a bird, wiping her qubul with it, and throwing it away. (O, TA.) The verb, thus used, occurs in a trad., but, as some relate it, with q and b [i. e. saying taqobiDu instead of tafotaD~u ]; and Az mentions that EshSháfi'ee related this trad. [in like manner] pronouncing the word with q and D , from AlqbD . (TA.)

definition: What is separated, dispersed, or scattered;
sourceDefinition: What is separated, dispersed, or scattered; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ faDiyDN ; (O, K, TA;) of rain-water, and of hail, and of sweat: (TA:) and sprinkled: (K:) and particularly what is sprinkled, of water, when one performs ablution with it, (A, O, K,) and what flows upon the limbs on that occasion; (A;) as also ↓ faDiyDN . (TA.) [See also faD~N and fuDaADN .]

definition: A branch of a tree: (S, M, Msb, K:) or such as is of just proportion in length or in breadth: (T:) said to be syn.
sourceDefinition: A branch of a tree: (S, M, Msb, K:) or such as is of just proportion in length or in breadth: (T:) said to be syn. with guSonN ; but this latter signifies “ such as has been cut off ” i. q. qaDiybN meaning maqoDuwbN : (M:) pl. A^afonaAnN ; (T, S, M, Msb, K;) said by Sb to be its only pl.; (M;) occurring in the Kur lv. 48; where some explain it as pl. of fan~N , and meaning “ sorts, ” or “ species ”; others, as pl. of fananN : (T, Bd:) and A^afaAniynu is a pl. pl., (T, S, K,) i. e. pl. of A^afonaAnN . (T, S.) ― -b2- And as a branch shelters like as does darkness, a poet uses it metaphorically, saying, A^agaAva $ariydahumo fananu AlZ~alaAmi (tropical:) [ The shelter of the darkness aided him, or them, who fled ]. (M.) ― -b3- And [in like manner also] the pl. pl. is used in a trad. describing the inmates of Paradise, as meaning (tropical:) Locks of hair; these being likened to branches: and El-Marrár says, A^aEalaAqapF A^um~a Alwaliydi baEodamaA A^afonaAnu raA^osika kaAlv~agaAmi Almuxolisi (tropical:) [Dost thou feel attachment of love to Umm-ElWeleed after that the locks of thy head have become like the hoary thaghám? ]; meaning the locks of the hair of his head when he had become hoary. (T. [See vagaAmN .])

definition: , (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb,) or qabaDahu biyadihi , (O, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb,) or qabaDahu biyadihi , (O, K,) aor. , (A, Msb, K,) inf. n. qaboDN , (S, Msb,) He took it with his hand, (A, O, K,) by actual touch, or feel: (O:) or the former signifies he closed his hand upon it: (Lth:) [ he grasped it; griped it; clutched it; seized it: ] or he took it with the whole of his hand: (Bd, xx. 96:) or i. q. A^aja*ahu [ he took it in any manner: he took it with his hand: he took possession of it: and he received it ]: (S, M, Mgh, Msb:) and qabaDa Ealayohi , and bihi , (M,) or qabaDa Ealayohi biyadahi , (A, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M,) he grasped it, clutched it, laid hold upon it, or seized it, with his hand; syn. A^amosakahu : (A, K:) or he seized it ( A^anoHaY Ealayohi ) with the whole of his hand: (M:) or he closed, or contracted, his fingers upon it: (Mgh, Msb:) it is also said, by MF, that some assert qaboDN to signify the “ taking with the ends of the fingers; ” but this is a mistranscription, for qaboDN , with the unpointed S . (TA [in which it is said, in another place in this art., that ↓ taqobiyDN has also this last signification; but this is evidently, in like manner, a mistranscription, for taqobiyDN .]) You say, qabaDa AlmataAEa [ He took, or received, the commodity, or the commodities, or goods ]. (A.) And qabaDa minohu Ald~ayona [ He took, or received, from him the debt ]. (M, K, in art. qDY ; &c.). And it is said in the Kur, [xx. 96,] faqabaDotu qaboDapF mino A^avari Alr~asuwli , (M,) and, accord. to an extraordinary reading, ↓ qabiyDapF , (B,) meaning [ And I took a handful ] of the dust from the footstep of the hoof of the horse of the messenger [Gabriel]: (IJ, M:) and ↓ A_iqotabaDa mino A^atarihi qaboDapF signifies the same as qabaDa : and qabaSa [q. v.] is [said to be] a dial. form thereof. (TA.) And you say, qabaDa AlT~aAy^ira He collected, or comprehended, the bird in his grasp. (A.) And qabaDa EalaY Eurofi Alfarasi [ He grasped, or laid hold upon, the mane of the horse ]. (A.) ― -b2- It is also used metaphorically, to denote the having an absolute property in a thing, to dispose of it at pleasure, without respect to the hand; as in the phrase qabaDotu AlA^aroDa , and Ald~aAra , (tropical:) I had, or took, or got, possession of the land, and of the house. (TA.) And [in like manner] it is said in a trad., yaqobiDu A@ll~`hu AlA^aroDa , and Als~amaA='a , (assumed tropical:) God will comprehend, or collect together, [ within his sole possession, (see quboDapN ,)] the earth, and the heaven. (TA.) [In like manner] you say also, qabaDa EalaY gariymihi (tropical:) [ He arrested his debtor: used in this sense in the present day]. (A.) And qabaDa A@ll~`hu ruwHahu (tropical:) God took his soul. (TA.) And qabaDahu A@ll~`hu (tropical:) God caused him to die. (Msb.) And qubiDa (tropical:) He (a man, S, M, A) died: (S M, A, * K:) and also (assumed tropical:) he (a sick man) was at the point of death; in the state of having his soul taken; in the agony of death. (L, TA.) And qabaDotuhu Eani AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) I removed him from the thing, or affair. (Msb.) ― -b3- qabaDahu , aor. as above, (M, K,) and so the inf. n., (S, M, Mgh,) also signifies the (assumed tropical:) contr. of basaTahu ; (S, * M, Mgh, * K;) and so ↓ qb~Dhu , (IAar, M,) inf. n. taqobiyDN . (TA.) [As such, (assumed tropical:) He contracted it; or drew it together. ] You say, qabaDa rijolahu wabasaTahaA (tropical:) [ He contracted his leg, and extended it ]. (A.) And qabaDa kaf~ahu [ He clenched his hand ]. (S, Mgh, Msb, K, in art. brjm .). And qabaDa yadahu Eanohu (assumed tropical:) [ He drew in his hand from it: or] he refrained from laying hold upon it. (K.) Whence the saying in the Kur, [ix. 68,] wayaqobiDuwna A^ayodiyahumo , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ And they draw in their hands, or refrain, ] from expenditure, or from paying the [poor-rate called] zakaAp . (TA.) You say also, janaAHahu ↓ qb~D (assumed tropical:) He (a bird) contracted his wing: (M:) or qabaDa , or qabaDa janaAHahu , (assumed tropical:) he contracted his wing to fly. (TA.) And hence, (TA,) qabaDa , aor. as above; (S, K;) or qabuDa (M;) [or both;] inf. n. [of the former] qaboDN (S, K,) and [of the latter, as indicated in the M,] qabaADapN (S, M, A, K) and qabaADN ; (M;) (tropical:) He (a bird, S, K, and a horse, A, and a man, S, or other [animal], K,) was quick, (S, M, A, K,) in flight, or in going or pace. (K.) yaqobiDona , said of birds, in the Kur, [lxvii. 19,] is [said to be] an ex. of this signification. (S, K. *) You say also, qabaDati AlA_ibilu (tropical:) The camels were quick in their pace; at every spring therein, putting their legs together. (A.) And ↓ A_inoqabaDa (tropical:) He, or it, (a company of men, M,) went, or journeyed, and was quick. (Lth, M, K.) And fiY fulaAnN ↓ A_inoqabaDa HaAjatihi (tropical:) Such a one was quick, and light, or active, in accomplishing his want. (A.) And qaboDN also signifies i. q. nazowN (assumed tropical:) [The act of leaping, &c.]. (TA.) ― -b4- [Also, as contr. of basaTahu ,] (assumed tropical:) He collected it together. (Az.) And hence, (Az,) qabaDa AlA_ibila , (Az, M,) aor. , inf. n. qaboDN (Az, S, M) (assumed tropical:) He drove (Az, S, M) the camels violently, or roughly, (Az, M.) or quickly: (S:) because the driver collects them together, when he desires to drive them; for when they disperse themselves from him, the driving of them is difficult: (Az, TA:) and bihaA ↓ A_inoqabaDa [signifies the same, or, agreeably with an explanation given above, (tropical:) he went quickly with them ]. (M.) And AlEayoru yaqobiDu EaAnatahu (assumed tropical:) The he-ass drives away his she-ass. (M.) ― -b5- [As such also,] qabaDahu ; (A;) and ↓ qb~Dhu , (S, M, K,) inf. n. taqobiyDN ; (S;) (tropical:) He, or it, drew it, collected it, or gathered it, together; contracted it, shrank it, or wrinkled it. (S, M, A, * K.) You say, qabaDa wajohahu (tropical:) He, or it, contracted, or wrinkled, his face ]. (A.) And qabaDati Aln~aAru Aljilodapa (tropical:) [ The fire contracted, shrank, or shrivelled, the piece of skin ]. (A.) And ↓ qab~aDa maA bayoni Eayonayohi (assumed tropical:) He contracted, or wrinkled, the part between his eyes. (M, TA.) And ↓ yawomN yuqab~iDu maA bayona AlEayonayoni (assumed tropical:) [ A day that contracts, or wrinkles, the part between the eyes ]; a metonymical phrase, denoting vehemence of fear, or of war. (M, TA. *) And in like manner you say, AlHa$aY ↓ yawomN yuqab~iDu (assumed tropical:) [ A day that contracts the bowels ]. (M.) [And hence qabaDa , aor. and inf. n. as first mentioned, (assumed tropical:) It (a medicine, or food, &c.,) astringed, or constipated. And (assumed tropical:) It (food) was astringent in taste; as also ↓ taqab~aDa .] ― -b6- As such also, qabaDahu , signifies (assumed tropical:) He straitened it; scanted it; made it scanty. (Msb, TA.) You say, qabaDa A@ll~`hu Alrizoqa , aor. and inf. n. as first mentioned, (assumed tropical:) God straitened, scanted, or made scanty, the means of subsistence. (Msb.) And it is said in the Kur, [ii. 246,] waA@ll~`hu yaqobiDu wayabosuTu (assumed tropical:) And God straitens, or scants, or makes scanty, the means of subsistence, to some, (Bd, Msb, * TA, *) or withholds the means of subsistence from whom He will, (Jel,) and amplifies, enlarges, or makes ample or plentiful, the same, (Bd, Msb, Jel, TA,) to some, (Bd, TA,) or to whom He will. (Jel.) ― -b7- [As such also, (assumed tropical:) He abridged his liberty. ] You say, fulaAnN yabosuTu gabiydahu vum~a yaqobiDuhumo (tropical:) [ Such a one enlarges the liberty of his slaves; then abridges their liberty ]. (A.) ― -b8- [As such also, (tropical:) He, or it, contracted his heart; i. e. distressed him; grieved him. ] You say, A_in~ahu yaqobiDuniY maA yaqobiDuka wayabosuTuniY maA yabosuTuka (tropical:) Verily what distresses thee, or grieves thee, distresses, or grieves, me; and what rejoices thee rejoices me ]. (A.) [And it is related in a trad., that Mohammad said, faATimapu min~iY yaqobiDuniY maA qabaDahaA wayabosuTuniY maA basaTahAa (tropical:) [ Fátimeh is as though she were a part of me: what hath distressed her, or grieved her, distresses, or grieves, me; and what hath rejoiced her rejoices me ]. (TA.) Or the phrase A_in~ahu layaqobiDuniY maA qabaDaka , mentioned by Lth, means (assumed tropical:) Verily what hath annoyed and angered thee annoys and angers me. (Az, TA.) qaboDN and basoTN are terms applied by the investigators of truth among the Soofees to two contrary states of the heart, from both of which it is seldom or never free: the former being an affection of the heart withholding it from dilatation and joy; whether the cause thereof be known, as the remembrance of a sin or an offence, or of an omission, or be not known; and some of them make other divisions thereof. (TA.) [In like manner] you say also, Ean~aA famaA qabaDaka ↓ AinoqabaDotu (tropical:) [ Thou shrankest from us: and what made thee to shrink? ]. (A.) ― -b9- [As such also, (tropical:) He, or it, made him close-fisted, tenacious, or niggardly. ] You say, Alxayoru yaqobiDuhu waAl$~ar~u yabosuTuhu (tropical:) [ Wealth makes him close-fisted, tenacious, or niggardly; and poverty makes him open-handed, liberal, or generous ]. (A.)

(M, TA. *) And in like manner you say, AlHa$aY ↓ yawomN yuqab~iDu (assumed tropical:) [ A day that contracts the bowels ]. (M.) [And hence qabaDa , aor. and inf. n. as first mentioned, (assumed tropical:) It (a medicine, or food, &c.,) astringed, or constipated. And (assumed tropical:) It (food) was astringent in taste; as also ↓ taqab~aDa .] ― -b6- As such also, qabaDahu , signifies (assumed tropical:) He straitened it; scanted it; made it scanty. (Msb, TA.) You say, qabaDa A@ll~`hu Alrizoqa , aor. and inf. n. as first mentioned, (assumed tropical:) God straitened, scanted, or made scanty, the means of subsistence. (Msb.) And it is said in the Kur, [ii. 246,] waA@ll~`hu yaqobiDu wayabosuTu (assumed tropical:) And God straitens, or scants, or makes scanty, the means of subsistence, to some, (Bd, Msb, * TA, *) or withholds the means of subsistence from whom He will, (Jel,) and amplifies, enlarges, or makes ample or plentiful, the same, (Bd, Msb, Jel, TA,) to some, (Bd, TA,) or to whom He will. (Jel.) ― -b7- [As such also, (assumed tropical:) He abridged his liberty. ] You say, fulaAnN yabosuTu gabiydahu vum~a yaqobiDuhumo (tropical:) [ Such a one enlarges the liberty of his slaves; then abridges their liberty ]. (A.) ― -b8- [As such also, (tropical:) He, or it, contracted his heart; i. e. distressed him; grieved him. ] You say, A_in~ahu yaqobiDuniY maA yaqobiDuka wayabosuTuniY maA yabosuTuka (tropical:) Verily what distresses thee, or grieves thee, distresses, or grieves, me; and what rejoices thee rejoices me ]. (A.) [And it is related in a trad., that Mohammad said, faATimapu min~iY yaqobiDuniY maA qabaDahaA wayabosuTuniY maA basaTahAa (tropical:) [ Fátimeh is as though she were a part of me: what hath distressed her, or grieved her, distresses, or grieves, me; and what hath rejoiced her rejoices me ]. (TA.) Or the phrase A_in~ahu layaqobiDuniY maA qabaDaka , mentioned by Lth, means (assumed tropical:) Verily what hath annoyed and angered thee annoys and angers me. (Az, TA.) qaboDN and basoTN are terms applied by the investigators of truth among the Soofees to two contrary states of the heart, from both of which it is seldom or never free: the former being an affection of the heart withholding it from dilatation and joy; whether the cause thereof be known, as the remembrance of a sin or an offence, or of an omission, or be not known; and some of them make other divisions thereof. (TA.) [In like manner] you say also, Ean~aA famaA qabaDaka ↓ AinoqabaDotu (tropical:) [ Thou shrankest from us: and what made thee to shrink? ]. (A.) ― -b9- [As such also, (tropical:) He, or it, made him close-fisted, tenacious, or niggardly. ] You say, Alxayoru yaqobiDuhu waAl$~ar~u yabosuTuhu (tropical:) [ Wealth makes him close-fisted, tenacious, or niggardly; and poverty makes him open-handed, liberal, or generous ]. (A.)

sourceDefinition: quasi-pass. of qab~aDahu as contr. of basaTahu ; (M;) as also ↓ AinoqabaDa is of qabaDahu in the same sense, (S, * M, K, *) being contr. of AinobasaTa . (S, K.) [As such,] both signify (assumed tropical:) It became drawn, collected, or gathered, together; or it drew, collected, or gathered, itself together; or contracted; or shrank; syn. of the former, tajam~aEa ; (TA;) and of the latter, AinoDam~a [which also signifies it became drawn and joined, or adjoined, to another thing; &c.]. (O, K.) So the latter signifies in the phrase fiY HaAjatiY ↓ AnqbD (assumed tropical:) [ It became comprised in, or adjoined to, the object of my want ]. (O.) ― -b2- [As such also,] the former signifies (tropical:) It (a man's face, A, or the part between the eyes, M,) became contracted, or wrinkled; (M, A; *) and in like manner a piece of skin, in, or upon, a fire; meaning it became contracted, shrunken, or shrivelled; it shrank: (so in different copies of the S:) or it (skin, K, or the skin of a man, TA) became contracted, or shrunken; (K, TA;) and so an old man. (A.) ― -b3- [As such also,] taqb~D Eanohu (tropical:) He shrank, or shrank with aversion, from him, or it; (S, M, A, K;) as also Eanohu ↓ AinoqabaDa : (A:) [see an ex. of the latter near the end of 1.] ↓ AlAinoqibaADu Eani Aln~aAsi also signifies (assumed tropical:) The withdrawing, removing, or retiring, from men. (TA.) And Eani AlA^amori ↓ AinoqabaDa (assumed tropical:) He removed, or became removed, from the thing, or affair. (Msb.) ― -b4- tqb~D EalaY AlA^amori (tropical:) He paused, or waited, at the thing, or affair; syn. tawaq~afa . (M, A.) ― -b5- tqb~D A_ilayohi (assumed tropical:) He leaped, or sprang, towards him. (Sgh, K.) ― -b6- See also 1; last third of the paragraph.

definition: (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) [ A handful;
sourceDefinition: (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) [ A handful; ] what one takes with the hand, or grasps; (S, K;) mino ka*aA [ of such a thing ]; (Mgh;) as, for instance, mino sawiyqK [ of meal of parched barley ]; (S;) or mino tamorK [ of dates ]; (S, A, Msb;) i. e. kaf~AF ; (S;) as also ↓ qaboDapN ; (S, M, A, K;) but the former is the more common; (S, K;) and ↓ qabiyDapN : (B:) or the first is a subst. in the sense of maqobuwDN , and the second is a n. un.: (TA:) the pl. of the first is qubaDN . (TA.) You say also, kaf~iY ↓ h`*aA qaboDapu This is the quantity that my hand grasps. (M.) See two other exs. of the second word, and an ex. of the third, in 1, before the first break in the paragraph. It is also said in the Kur, [xxxix. 67,] waA@loA^aroDu jamiyEFA yawoma AlqiyaAmapi ↓ qaboDatuhu , i. e. quboDatuhu , for qaboDapN is an inf. n. [of un.] used as a subst., or is for *aAtu qaboDapK , (Bd,) and the literal signification is, [ And the earth altogether shall be ] his handful [ on the day of resurrection ]; (Bd, Jel;) meaning in his possession (Jel, TA) alone, (TA,) and at his free and absolute disposal: (Jel:) Th says, that this is like the phrase h`*ihi Ald~aAru fiY qaboDatiY , meaning as explained above, voce qaboDN ; but this opinion is not valid:) (M:) another reading is ↓ qaboDatahu , in the accus. case, (M, Bd,) as an adv. n.; that which is determinate being thus likened to what is vague; (Bd;) and this is allowed by some of the grammarians; but it is not allowed by any one of the grammarians of El-Basrah. (M.) It is also said, in the trad. of Bilál and the dates, fajaEala yajiYo'u bihi qubaDFA qubaDFA [ And he set about bringing them (the pronoun referring to Alt~amor the dates ) handfuls by handfuls ]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: Taking with the hand: [or in any manner: taking possession of: receiving: (see 1:)] grasping, clutching, or seizing, with the hand: and in like manner, [but in an intensive sense,] ↓ qab~aADN : (K:) or the latter is of the dial. of the people of El-Medeeneh, applied to him who [ grasps or] collects everything: (Aboo-'Othmán El-Mázinee:) and ↓ qb~aADapN [which is doubly intensive]; (K;) the p in this last not denoting the fem. gender. (M.) [See an ex. of the first, voce EaAy^iDF , in art. EwD .] ― -b4- [Applied to medicine, food, &c., (assumed tropical:) Astringent, or constipating. ]

definition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) which is [an appellation applied to The rainbow ] in the sky, (S,) i. e. certain streaks of an arched form appearing in the sky in the days of the [ season called ] rabiyE , after rain, red and yellow and green, (TA,) is imperfectly decl. [accord. to general usage], (S,) [that is to say,] it is a compound of two words whereof the latter is inseparable from the former, so that one may not say taA^am~alo quzaHa famaA A^aboyana qawosahu [ Consider thou Kuzah, for how plain is his bow! ], (TA,) and the latter word is said to be the name of a certain devil, as such, imperfectly decl., (TA, Msb,) assigned to the same class as zuHal , which, as Mbr says, is imperfectly decl. as being a proper name and deviating from its original form: (TA:) it is said in a trad., Say not ye qawosu quzaHa , for quzaHu is the name of a devil, but say qawosu A@ll~`hi : (Msb, TA:) or quzaHu is the name of a certain angel who is charged with the management of the clouds: or the name of a certain king of the 'Ajam [i. e. Persians or foreigners ]: (K: [but SM remarks upon this last saying as being very strange, deemed improbable by his sheykh (MF), and not found by himself in any book except the K:]) or quzaHu is the name of a mountain in El-Muzdelifeh, and the word qawos was prefixed to it because this was the first place over which the qws thus called appeared in the Time of Ignorance: (TA:) or quzaH thus used is from quzoHapN , (Msb, K, TA,) of which quzaHN is pl., (Msb,) and which signifies a streak of yellow and of red and of green, (Msb, K, TA,) which are the colours that are in the [said] qws ; (TA;) and if so, it is perfectly decl. [i. e. one says qawosu quzaHK ]: (Msb:) or it is from qazaHa signifying it was, or became, high, or elevated: (K, TA:) Dmr strangely asserts that qws qzH is a mistake, and that it is correctly qawosu qazaEK , from qazaEN signifying “ clouds. ” (MF, TA.)

definition: He made his [meaning his own] breast, or chest, to stick out.
sourceDefinition: He made his [meaning his own] breast, or chest, to stick out. (A.) ― -b2- He drew back, and became refractory, and made himself like him who has a hollow, or receding, back, and a protruding, or protuberant, breast, or chest. (Har, p. 17.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) He drew back; held back; or hung back. (S, K.) You say, tqAEs Eani AlA^amori (tropical:) He drew back, held back, or hung back, from the thing, or affair, and would not go forward in it; (S, TA;) as also ↓ qaEisa , inf. n. qaEasN ; and ↓ tqE~s : (TA:) in some copies of the S, instead of tqAEs , in this phrase, we find ↓ taqaEowasa . (TA.) And [in like manner,] ↓ AiqoEanosasa (assumed tropical:) He drew back; he receded, or went backwards. (S, K.) When a man draws water without a pulley, pulling the rope at the head of the well, his back pains him, and it is said to him, waA@jo*ibi Ald~alowa ↓ AiqoEanosiso (assumed tropical:) [ Go thou backwards, and pull the bucket ]. This verb is without idghám because it is quasi-coördinate to AiHoranojama . (S.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) He (a horse, S, K) drew back, or held back, and would not go forward: (S:) or would not submit to his leader; (K;) [as also ↓ AqEnss ; as appears from an explanation of its part. n., below.] You say also, Ald~aAb~apu ↓ tqE~st , meaning (assumed tropical:) The beast of carriage stood still, and would not move from its place. (TA.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) [ He (a man) and] it (might or strength) was, or became, firm, or steady, and resisted; [as also ↓ AqEnss ; as appears from an explanation of its part. n., below:] and ↓ AqEnss (assumed tropical:) he was, or became, firm, and did not bow his head: and qaEisa , inf. n. qaEasN , (assumed tropical:) he (a man) was, or became, inaccessible, or unapproachable, and mighty, or strong, and firm, or steady. (TA.) ― -b6- (tropical:) It (the night) was, or became, long, or protracted; as though it did not quit its place; like baraka . (A, TA.) See A^aqoEasu .

definition: Having a protruding, or protuberant, breast, or chest, and a hollow, or receding, back;
sourceDefinition: Having a protruding, or protuberant, breast, or chest, and a hollow, or receding, back; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ qaEisN (S, K) and ↓ mutaqaAEisN : (S:) [or the last rather signifies making his breast, or chest, to stick out: see its verb:] fem. of the first, qaEosaA='u ; (K;) applied to a woman [&c.]: and pl. quEosN : the dim. of the first is A^uqayoEisu . (TA.) [See A^ajonaA^u and A^afozaru .] ― -b2- Applied to a horse, Having the Sahowap [or place of the saddle ], (K,) or the spine in that part, (S,) depressed, and the qaTaAp [or part next behind ] elevated; (S, K;) [i. e., saddle-backed. ] ― -b3- Applied to a camel, Having the head and neck and back inclining: (K:) or having the head and neck inclining towards the back: (S:) the latter is the right explanation. (TA.) Hence the saying, Aibonu xamosK Ea$aA='u xalifaAtK quEosK , meaning, The tarrying of the moon five nights old until it sets is like the tarrying during the evening feed of pregnant camels having their heads and necks inclining towards their backs. (S, TA.) [See EatamapN .] The same epithet applied to a camel also signifies Having a shortness in the hind legs, and a sloping in the withers. (TA.) ― -b4- Also, the fem., qaEosaA='u , applied to an ant ( namolap ), Raising its breast and its tail: (K:) pl. quEosN and qaEosaAwaAtN . (TA.) ― -b5- And applied to a bow ( qawos ,) Having a bending outwards of its inner side, in its middle, and a bending inwards of its outer side. (TA.) ― -b6- Also A^aqoEasu , applied to a man, (assumed tropical:) Inaccessible, or unapproachable, (S, K, TA,) and mighty, or strong, and firm, or steady. (TA.) You say also, Eiz~N A^aqoEasu (A) and Eiz~apN qaEosaA='u (S, A) (tropical:) Firm might or strength. (S.) AirotafaEa : (S, Msb, TA:) all of which explanations are correct. (TA.) And qalaSato $afatuhu His lip became contracted; (S, M, Msb, K;) as also ↓ tql~St : (Msb:) or became contracted upwards. definition: A young, or youthful, she-camel;
sourceDefinition: A young, or youthful, she-camel; (S, M, Msb, K;) i. e. among camels (Mgh, Msb) the like of a jaAriyap among women: (S, Mgh, Msb:) or such as endures journeying; (Lth, K;) so called until her tush grows forth, [ in her ninth year, ] when she ceases to be so called: (Lth:) or a young, or youthful, Arabian camel: (TA:) or a she-camel from the time when first ridden, until she sheds the central incisor, [ in her sixth year, ] when she is called naAqapN ; (El-'Adawee, S, Sgh, K;) the he-camel during that period being called qaEuwdN , and then jamalN : (El-'Adawee, S, Sgh:) or any sh-camel from the time when she is ridden, whether she be a binotu labuwnK or a Hiq~ap , until she becomes a bakorap , or until her tush grows forth: (M:) or a she-camel in her sixth year: or in her second year: (M:) and sometimes a she-camel just born is thus called: (M:) the qlwS is so called because of the length of her legs, and her not being yet bulky in the body: (T, TA:) and a long-legged she-camel is so called, (S, K,) sometimes: (S:) the term is only applied to a female: (IDrd, K:) [dim. qulay~iSapN , of the pl. of which ( qulay~iSaAtN ) see an ex. in a verse cited in art. dh :] pl. qalaAy^iSu and quluSN (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K) and quloSaAnN (M, L) and (pl. pl., K, i. e. pl. of quluSN , S) qilaASN . sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. katobN and kitaAbN and kitaAbapN (S, K) and kitobapN ; (Msb;) the first of these inf. ns. agreeable with analogy; the second, anomalous; (TA;) or the latter of these two is a subst., like libaAsN ; (Lh;) or originally an inf. n., and afterwards used in the senses given below; (MF;) as also kitaAbapN , and kitobapN : (TA:) and ↓ kt~bhu (K) and ↓ Akttbhu ; (S, K;) He wrote it: (S, K:) or katabahu has this signification; and ↓ Akttbhu , as also ↓ Astktbhu , signifies he asked [one] to dictate it ( A_isotamolaAhu ): (K:) ↓ A_ikotatabahaA in the Kur, xxv. 6, signifies he hath written them (S) for himself: (Bd:) or he hath asked [one] to write them for him, or to dictate them to him. (TA, Bd.) ― -b2- kataba Eanohu [ He wrote what he had heard, or learned from him. ] A phrase of common occurrence in biographies. ― -b3- kataba [ He was a writer, or scribe, and a learned man. (Implied in the S, where we are referred to the Kur, lii. 41, and lxviii., 47, in illustration of kaAtibN as signifying “ a learned man. ”)] -A2- kataba , aor. , inf. n. kitaAbN , q. v., (assumed tropical:) He (God) prescribed, appointed, or ordained, (TA,) and made obligatory. (Msb.) kutiba Ealayokumu AlqiSaASu The law of retaliation is prescribed, appointed, or ordained, as a law of which the observance is incumbent on you. (Kur, ii. 173.] kutiba Ealayokumu AlS~iyaAmu Fasting is prescribed as incumbent on you. [Kur. ii. 179.] (TA.) ― -b2- kataba Ealayohi ka*aA (tropical:) He judged, passed sentence, or decreed, against him that he should do such a thing. (A.) ktb AlqaADiY biAln~afaqapi The judge gave sentence that the expenses should be paid. (Msb.) -A3- kataba , aor. , inf. n. katobN , He drew together; brought together; conjoined. (S.) ― -b2- Hence, kataba Albagolapa , aor. and , inf. n. katobN , He conjoined the oræ of the mule's vulva by means of a ring or a thong; (S;) as also kataba EalayohaA . (A.) kataba , aor. and , (K,) inf. n. katobN ; and kataba EalayohaA ; (TA;) He closed the camel's vulva, (K,) and put a ring upon it: (TA:) or he put a ring of iron or the like upon it, (K,) conjoining the oræ, in order that she might not be covered. (Lh.) See above. IAar says, I heard an Arab of the desert say, A^akotabotu fama ↓ Als~iqaA' falamo yasotakotibo I bound the mouth of the sqA' , but it did not become fast bound, or closed, because of its hardness and thickness. (TA.) -A4- kataba Aln~aAqapa He used art to make the she-camel take a liking to that which was not her own young one, and put something as a ring through her nostrils, lest she should smell the baw~ , (in some copies of the K, bawol ; but this is a mistake; TA,) and not have a fondness for it. (TA.) -A5- kataba (tropical:) He collected a katiybap . (TA.) See also 2.

definition: and ↓ takaAtubN are syn.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ takaAtubN are syn.: (S, K:) you say, kAtb Sadiyqahu He wrote to his friend: and ↓ tkAtbA They wrote, one to the other. (TA.) ― -b2- kAtbhu , inf. n. mukaAtabapN (Az, K, Msb) and kitaAbN , (Az, Msb,) (tropical:) He (a slave) made a written [or other] contract with him (his master), that he (the former) should pay a certain sum as the price of himself, and on the payment thereof be free: (K, &c.:) also he (a master) made such a contract with him (his slave): (Az, Msb, &c.:) and ↓ tkAtbA They two made such a contract, one with the other. (Msb.) The slave in this case is called mukaAtabN (S, Msb) and also mukaAtibN ; and so is the master; the act being mutual. (Msb.) [But the lawyers in the present day call the slave mukaAtabN only; and the master, mukaAtibN .] AlkitaAbapu , signifying “ what is written, ” is tropically used by the professors of practical law as syn. with AlmukaAtabapu , because the contract above mentioned was generally written; and is so used by them when nothing is written. It was thus called in the age of el-Islám, accord. to Az. These two words are said by Z to be syn.; but it is thought that he may have written the former by mistake for AlkitaAbu , adding the p by a slip of the pen. (Msb.)

(Msb.) Pl. kutubN and kutobN . (S.) ― -b3- A revealed scripture. (Msb.) [Whence A^aholu kitaAbK People having a revealed scripture: and A^aholu AlkitaAbi The people of the Bible. See also A^aholN .] AlktAb signifies The taworAp , or Pentateuch, or Mosaic Law: (K:) and the Gospel, or Book of the Gospels: the Scriptures of the Jews and Christians: (Expositions of the Kur, passim:) and the Kur-án. (TA.) ― -b4- See also 3. -A2- kitaAbN [inf. n., or subst.: see 1] Divine prescript, appointment, or ordinance: judgment, or sentence: fatal decree, or predestination. (S, K.) laA^aqoDiyan~a bayonakumaA bikitaAbi All~`hi I will assuredly determine, or judge, between you two according to the judgment, or sentence, of God, which hath been revealed in his book. A trad., not relating to the Kur-án. (TA.) El-Jaadee says, yaA A@bonapa Eam~iY kitaAbu All~`hi A^axorajaniY Eanokumo wahalo A^amonafan~a All~`ha maA faEalaA [ O daughter of my paternal uncle! the decree of God hath expelled me from you: and could I indeed forbid God to do what He hath done? ] (S.) [Hence,] AlkitaAbu AlA^aw~alu [ The first writing; meaning the register of God's decrees ]. (M and K voce maHobalN , q. v.) ― -b2- A receptacle for ink. (K).

A school; a place where the art of writing is taught: (S, K, &c.:) accord. to Mbr and F, the assigning this signification to the latter word is an error; it being a pl. of kaAtibN , and signifying, accord. to Mbr, the boys of a school: in the A it is said, this word is said to signify the boys; not the place: but Esh-Shiháb says, in the Sharh esh-Shifa, that it occurs in this sense in the classical language, and is not to be regarded as a postclassical word: it is said to be originally a pl. of kaAtibN , and to be fig. employed to signify a school. (TA.) Pl. of the former makaAtibu ; (TA;) and of the latter kataAtiybu . (S.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. takofiyrN : see 1, first signification, in three places. -A2- Hence, kaf~ara Al*~anoba It (war in the cause of God [or the like]) covered, or concealed, the crime or sin: (Mgh:) (or expiated it: or annulled it; for] tkfyr with respect to acts of disobedience is like A_iHobaATN with respect to reward. (S, K.) The saying in the Kur [v. 70.] lakaf~aronaA Eanohumo say~iy^aAtihimo means, We would cover, or conceal, their sins, so that they should become as though they had not been: or it may mean, We would do away with their sins; as is indicated by another saying in the Kur [xi. 116,] “ good actions do away with sins. ” (El-Basáïr.) kaf~ara A@ll~`hu Eanohu Al*~anoba signifies God effaced his sin. (Msb.) ― -b2- And kaf~ara Eano yamiynihi [ He expiated his oath; ] he performed, (Msb,) or gave, (K,) what is termed kaf~aArap [i. e. a fast, or alms, for the expiation of his oath ]: (Msb, K:) takofiyrN of an oath is the doing what is incumbent, or obligatory, for the violation, or breaking, thereof: (S:) kaf~ara yamiynahu is a vulgar phrase. (Mgh.) -A3- kaf~arahu as syn. with A^akofarahu : see 4. -A4- kaf~ara lahu , inf. n. takofiyrN , (A, Mgh, TA,) He did obeisance to him, lowering his head, or bowing, and bending himself, and putting his hand upon his breast: (Mgh:) or put his hand upon his breast and bent himself down to him: (TA:) or he made a sign of humbling himself to him; did obeisance to him: (A:) namely, an Eiloj [or unbeliever of the Persians or other foreigners] (A, Mgh) or a *im~iY~ [or free non- Muslim subject of a Muslim government, i. e., a Christian, a Jew, or a Sabian] (Mgh) to the king; (A, Mgh;) or a slave to his master, or to his dihoqaAn [or chief]: (TA:) and ↓ kafara , [aor. , accord. to the rule of of the K,] (TK,) inf. n. kaforN , (K,) he (a Persian, faArisiY~N , K, and so in the L and other lexicons, but in the TS faAris , without Y , which is probably a mistake of copyists, TA) paid honour to his king, (K, TA,) by making a sing with his head, near to prostration: (TA:) takofiyrN is a man's humbling himself to another, (S, K, TA,) bending himself, and lowering his head, nearly in the manner termed rukuwEN ; as one does when he desires to pay honour to his friend; (TA;) or as the Eiloj does to the dihoqaAn : (S:) and the tkfyr of the people of the scriptures [or Christians and Jews, and Sabians] one's lowering his head to his friend, like the tasoliym with the Muslims: or one's putting his hand, or his two hands, upon his breast: (TA:) and tkfyr in prayer is the bending one's self much in the state of standing, before the action termed rukuwEN ; the doing of which was disapproved by Mohammad, accord. to a trad. (TA.) It is said in a trad., A_i*aA A^aSobaHa A@bonu A=dama faA_in~a AlA^aEoDaA='a tukaf~iru kul~uhaA lil~isaAni When the son of Adam rises in the morning, verily all the members abase themselves to the tongue, (Mgh, TA,) and confess obedience to it, and humbly submit to its command. (TA.) ― -b2- takofiyrN also signifies The crowning a king with a crown, [because] when he, or it, is seen, obeisance is done to him ( A_i*aA ruy^iYa kuf~ira lahu ). (K.) ― -b3- See also takofiyrN below.

definition: He denied, or disacknowledged, to me my right, or just claim.
sourceDefinition: He denied, or disacknowledged, to me my right, or just claim. (A, Mgh, K.) Hence the saying of 'Ámir, A_i*aA A^aqar~a Einoda AlqaADiY bi$aYo'K vum~a kaAfara [ When he confesses a thing in the presence of the Kádee, then denies, or disacknowledges: kaAfara being thus used in the sense of kafara ]. But as to the saying of Mohammad [the lawyer], rjulN lahu EalaY A=xara dayonN fakaAfarahu bihi siniyna [ A man who owed to another a debt, and denied to him, in the case of it, for years ], he seems to have made it imply the meaning of AlmumaATalap , and therefore to have made it trans. in the same manner as AlmmATlp is trans. (Mgh.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Mgh, K,) and ↓ kf~rhu , (A, Mgh, Msb,) [the latter of which is the more common in the present day,] He called him a kaAfir [i. e. a disbeliever, an unbeliever, or an infidel ]: (S, Mgh, K:) he attributed, or imputed to him, charged him with, or accused him of, disbelief, or infidelity: (S, A, Msb:) or he said to him kafarota [ Thou hast become an unbeliever, or infidel, or Thou hast blasphemed: in this last sense, “ he said to him Thou hast blasphemed, ” kf~rhu , to which alone it is assigned in the Msb, is very commonly used in the present day]. (Msb.) Hence the saying, laA tukofiro A^aHadFA mino A^aholi qibolatika Do not thou attribute or impute disbelief or infidelity to any one of the people of thy kibleh; (S, TA;) i. e., do not thou call any such a disbeliever, &c.; or do not thou make him such by thine assertion and thy saying. (TA.) laA tukaf~iruwA A^ahola qibolatikumo is not authorized by the relation, though it be allowable as a dial. form. (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Also] A^akofarotuhu , inf. n. A_ikofaArN , I made him a disbeliever, an unbeliever, or an infidel; I compelled him to become a disbeliever, &c. (Msb.) And A^akofara fulaAnN SaAHibahu Such a one compelled his companion by evil treatment to become disobedient after he had been obedient. (Mgh.) And A^akofara Alr~ajulu muTiyEahu The man compelled him who had obeyed him to disobey him: (T, TA:) or he made him to be under a necessity to disobey him. (TA.) -A2- Akfr He (a man, TA) kept, or confined himself, to the kafor , (K,) i. e. qaroyap [ town or village ]; (TA;) as also ↓ Aktfr . (IAar, K.)

definition: The darkness and blackness of night;
sourceDefinition: The darkness and blackness of night; [because it conceals things;] as also, sometimes, ↓ kiforN . (S, K.) [See also kaAfirN .] See a verse cited voce *ukaA='u . -A2- Earth, or dust; because it conceals what is beneath it. (Lh.) -A3- [Hence also] A grave, or sepulchre: (S, K:) pl. kufuwrN . (S.) Whence the saying, A^all~hum~a A@gofiro liA^aholi Alkufuwri [ O God, pardon the people of the graves ]. (S.) -A4- [And hence, perhaps,] A town, or village; [generally the latter;] syn. qaroyapN : (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) a Syriac word, and mostly used by the people of Syria [and of Egypt]: or, accord. to El-Harbee, land that is far from men, by which no one passes: (TA:) pl. kufuwrN : (S, Msb:) in the present day, it is applied in Egypt to any small qaroyap [or village ] by the side of a great qaroyap [or town ]: they say Alqaroyapu AlfulaAniy~apu wakaforuhaA [ Such a town and its village ]: and sometimes one qaroyap has a number of kufuwr . (TA.) Hence the saying of Mo'áwiyeh, A^aholu Alkufuwri humo A^aholu Alqubuwri [ The people of the villages are the people of the graves ]; meaning, that they are as the dead; they do not see the great towns and the performance of the congregational prayers of Friday: (S, Mgh:) by Alkfwr he meant the villages ( AlquraY ) remote from the great towns and from the places where the people of science assemble, so that ignorance prevails among their inhabitants, and they are most quickly affected by innovations in religion and by natural desires which cause to err. (Az, TA.) Hence also the trad. (of Aboo-Hureyreh, TA), layuxorijan~akumu A@lr~uwmu minohaA kaforFA kaforFA [ The Greeks will assuredly expel you from them, town by town, or village by village ]; (S, * TA;) i. e. from the furFY of Syria. (S, TA.) ― -b2- kaforN EalaY kaforK also signifies One upon another; or one part upon another. (TA.)
